Also the limits of open access calls to the node of a machine, for one caller and for one org ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#who-can-call-them)). The service layer checks each limit before it writes, and a refused call commits nothing. | `resource_exhausted`                                     |
| An idempotency key that another call holds for more than 10 s                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `unavailable`                                            |
| A refusal of an edge server for too many open requests ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#listeners))                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | HTTP 429 or 503, which a client reads as `unavailable`   |
| An edge server that got no connection to the control role ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#forwarded-requests))                                                                                                                                                                                                      | HTTP 502, which a client reads as `unavailable`          |
| Each refusal of maintenance mode ([Maintenance mode](#maintenance-mode))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `unavailable`, or HTTP 503 on a route that is not a call |

Every other answer can follow a call that ran, also an `unavailable` answer. An example is a sign-in link whose mail failed after the server stored the link. A usage limit, such as the most orgs of one account, carries no header, because a retry soon after gets the same refusal.

Some refusals are not answers of a call, so they carry no header:

* The WebSocket endpoint `/api/ws/exec` reports an error with a close code and a reason ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#the-websocket-endpoint)).
* The MCP server reports the error of a tool call in the result of the tool ([the MCP server](/reference/mcp/#errors)).
* The limit of certificate renewals of a server answers on the control channel, not with an error of a call ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#certificate-renewal)).

```text
$ curl -si -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer hbx_unknown' -d '{}' \
    https://example.com/hopbox.v1.OrgService/ListOrgs
HTTP/2 401
hopbox-not-run: 1
...
{"code":"unauthenticated","message":"the credential is not valid"}
```

The message of an error that the service layer refuses, such as a bad domain, says which rule the request broke. Every other error gets a fixed message. So it never shows the internals of the server to a client, such as the address of the database:

| Code                  | Message                                                                                     |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deadline_exceeded`   | `the call ran out of time`                                                                  |
| `canceled`            | `the call was canceled`                                                                     |
| `internal`            | `internal error. The server log has the details under the request ID`                       |
| a code from a library | `the call failed with the code <code>. The server log has the details under the request ID` |

The server writes the cause of these errors only to its log, with the request ID ([Logs](#logs)).

Connect refuses some requests before any interceptor runs. Examples are a body that does not decode, a message larger than 4 MiB, and an unknown content type. These errors keep the text of Connect, such as `protocol error: incomplete envelope`, because the error mapping never sees them. Their text describes only the request, never the server. They count only in `hopbox_http_requests_total`, not in `hopbox_api_calls_total` ([Metrics](/reference/metrics/#metrics-of-the-api)). They get no `api call` log record.

### Enum names in JSON

In the JSON codec, an enum value is its full name, such as `VAR_SCOPE_PRIVATE`. A request with a name that the enum does not know gets `invalid_argument`, also a name in lowercase, such as `private`. The handler never runs. The message names the field and lists the values of the enum:

```text
unmarshal message: scope is "VAR_SCOPE_PRIVAT", which is not a value of VarScope. Use one of VAR_SCOPE_SHARED, VAR_SCOPE_PRIVATE, VAR_SCOPE_ALL
```

The JSON codec of Connect drops an unknown name, and the field then holds its unspecified value. For some fields, the unspecified value is the default. Examples are the shared scope of `SetVar` and `DeleteVar`, the member kind of `CreateAPIKey`, and the restart policy `always` of `CreateMachine`. So without the check, a typo runs the call with a choice that the client did not make. The API listener, the internal listener, and the admin socket all make this check.

The JSON codec still drops an unknown field, so a client with a newer schema keeps working. The unspecified value itself, or an enum number, passes the codec. The service layer takes the unspecified value as the default of the field, or refuses it where the field has no default. It refuses a number that the enum does not know. The binary protobuf codec carries numbers, not names, so it needs no such check.

The check runs in the codec, before the request gate, as for any body that does not decode. So an anonymous call with an unknown name gets `invalid_argument`, not `unauthenticated`. The same call with a known name gets `unauthenticated`. The refusal counts only in `hopbox_http_requests_total`, as the paragraph “Connect refuses some requests before any interceptor runs” in [Errors](#errors) says.

### When a listener stops

When a listener stops, it lets each running unary call finish. A unary call that still reads its request body gets 2 s more for the read. Then the read fails, so a stalled upload cannot hold the stop. A lifecycle call of a machine that waits for its machine ends its wait at once. It answers with the machine as it is and `done` false ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#the-wait)). A stream ends at once: the server cancels its context and ends every read of its request body. So a stream that waits for the client, such as a reflection stream, ends too ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run)). A shutdown of the HTTP server does not track a connection that a handler took over. So the listener ends each open WebSocket itself, with the close code 1001 and the reason `the server shuts down. Connect again`. A running tool call of the MCP server ends at once, as a stream does ([the MCP server](/reference/mcp/#when-the-listener-stops)).

Example:

```text
$ curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' \
    http://127.0.0.1:7080/hopbox.admin.v1.InstallConfigService/GetInstallConfig
{"code":"unauthenticated","message":"this call needs a credential"}
```

### Streams and their credential

The gate checks the credential of a call once, at its start. A stream can run for hours, so it checks its credential again while it runs. `Service.GuardStream` of `internal/service` gives each stream a context. The context ends with the credential:

* At the expiry of the credential ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/)). For a session, that is the end of its lifetime, or 7 days after its last use, whichever comes first ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/)). For a CLI token, it is the end of the newest live access token of its CLI sign-in. So a stream lives on while the CLI refreshes its tokens. For an API key, it is the expiry of the key.
* At the first check that finds the credential ended. Examples are a sign-out of a session, and the end of a CLI sign-in. The reuse of an old refresh token ends a CLI sign-in too, with its whole family. Others are the revoke of an API key, the leave of the account of a member key from its org, and an expiry. The check runs every 30 s (`service.DefaultCredentialRecheck`). A check that cannot reach the control store keeps the stream. It logs `the check of the credential of a stream failed` at level warn with `component=service` and `err`, and tries again at the next check.

The stream then ends with `unauthenticated` and the message `the credential of this stream ended. Sign in again: ...`. `WatchMachines`, `Exec`, `Upload`, `Download`, `StreamMachineLogs`, and the WebSocket of exec run under such a guard. A session, a CLI token, a member key, and an org key can hold a stream. Any other kind of caller gets `unauthenticated` at once.

## Maintenance mode

Maintenance mode stops every change of the install through the API and the control channels, so that `hopboxd admin db export` can copy a control store that no longer changes ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-maintenance-on)). It is a flag of the install config ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#install_config)). Only root on a control server turns it on or off, with `SetMaintenance` on the admin socket ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setmaintenance)). The code is in `internal/api/maintenance.go` and `internal/service/maintenance.go`.

In maintenance mode, every listener of the control role refuses each call that can change the control store: the API listener, the admin socket, and the internal listener, also for the requests that the edge servers forward. The maintenance gate sorts each call into one of three kinds:

* A call of gRPC health or of gRPC reflection ([Reflection and health](#reflection-and-health)), and `SetMaintenance`, pass as they are. The policy lets only `local_root` call `SetMaintenance`, so the admin socket always takes it. No other write could turn maintenance mode off.
* A call whose method has the option `(hopbox.v1.read_only)` ([API definitions](/reference/api-definitions/#hopboxv1read_only)) runs as a read call. Each write that it makes runs under the maintenance mode of the process, such as its audit entry, or the last use of a machine for its auto-delete timeout. In maintenance mode, the call fails at that write, before the write, with the refusal below. A read call that writes nothing works in maintenance mode.
* Every other call is refused before the request gate, so it reads no credential and changes nothing.

So these calls work in maintenance mode:

| Service                                | Calls                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `hopbox.v1.InstallService`             | `GetInstallInfo`                                                         |
| `hopbox.v1.AccountService`             | `GetAccount`, `ListSignInMethods`, `ListCLISignIns`                      |
| `hopbox.v1.AuditService`               | `ListAuditEntries`                                                       |
| `hopbox.v1.APIKeyService`              | `ListAPIKeys`                                                            |
| `hopbox.v1.MachineService`             | `GetMachine`, `ListMachines`, `ListMachineSizes`, `WatchMachines`        |
| `hopbox.v1.OrgService`                 | `GetOrg`, `ListOrgs`, `GetOrgUsage`, `ListOrgMembers`, `ListInvitations` |
| `hopbox.v1.SSHKeyService`              | `ListSSHKeys`                                                            |
| `hopbox.v1.VarService`                 | `ListVars`                                                               |
| `hopbox.admin.v1.InstallConfigService` | `SetMaintenance`                                                         |
| gRPC health and reflection             | every call                                                               |

Each other call is refused, also these reads: every read of the admin API, such as `GetInstallConfig` and `ListServers`, because it writes its audit entry ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/)), and `Download` and `StreamMachineLogs`, because each records a use of its machine. Their node channels are closed in maintenance mode anyway. The audit log thus never loses an access that it would have recorded.

Each refusal changes nothing. It has the code `unavailable`, the message `the install is in maintenance mode, so it takes only reads. Retry later`, and the headers `Hopbox-Not-Run: 1` and `Retry-After: 30`:

```text
$ curl -si -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"ann@example.org"}' \
    https://example.com/hopbox.v1.AuthService/RequestMagicLink
HTTP/2 503
hopbox-not-run: 1
retry-after: 30
...
{"code":"unavailable","message":"the install is in maintenance mode, so it takes only reads. Retry later"}
```

The plain HTTP routes that can change the install answer HTTP 503 with the same headers and message: the sign-in with GitHub and Google at `/auth/<provider>/start` and `/auth/<provider>/callback` ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/)), the sign-in of private machine URLs at `/auth/machine` ([the edge role](/reference/edge/)), and the WebSocket endpoint `/api/ws/exec`. The console, health, and the MCP endpoint keep serving. Each tool of the MCP server calls the API, so it gets the refusal of its call.

The last use of a session, an API key, an admin API key, or a CLI token is a write of the request gate too, but a lost time of a last use is harmless. So in maintenance mode, the request gate skips that write, and the call goes on ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#lifetimes)).

A read call can run while maintenance mode turns on. Each of its writes either ends before `SetMaintenance` returns, or is refused before it changes anything. So no write of a read call comes after the turn to on either. A stream such as `Download` that runs at the turn ends at its next record of the use of its machine.

When maintenance mode turns on, the control process ends each call without the option `(hopbox.v1.read_only)` that still runs: the unary calls, the streams such as `Exec`, and the control channels of the servers ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#maintenance-mode)). A call that maintenance mode ended gets `unavailable` with the message `the install went into maintenance mode, which ended this call. Retry later`, and no `Hopbox-Not-Run` header, because it can have changed something before its end. The leader also pauses its jobs ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#leader-jobs)). A turn to on with `SetMaintenance` succeeds only after each of these ended in every live control process of the install while maintenance mode stayed on, so no change of the API or of a server comes after it. The other control processes report this in their rows of `control_processes` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setmaintenance)). The call gives up with `unavailable` after at most 30 s, the deadline of the call, and maintenance mode stays on. If maintenance mode turns off during the wait, for example by a second root on the socket, the turn to on fails with `unavailable: unavailable: maintenance mode turned off while it waited for the calls, control channels, and leader jobs to end`, because the work runs again. `hopboxd admin db export` also reads the flag in the snapshot of its dump, and refuses a store out of maintenance mode.

The request gate checks a server certificate on the internal listener, also for health and reflection. The first use of a certificate, which retires the other certificates of its server, and the alarm of a retired certificate write to the store. In maintenance mode, the gate refuses such a call with the refusal above, before the write ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/)).

When maintenance mode turns off, the listeners take every call again, the servers dial their control channels again, and the leader runs its jobs again. Each control process reads the flag at its start, and again at each change event `install.maintenance_changed` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#events)). So a control process that starts on a store in maintenance mode, such as a copy of `hopboxd admin db export`, starts in maintenance mode too.

## Reflection and health

gRPC server reflection is on, so `grpcurl` can list and call the services. The server serves the reflection services `grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection` and `grpc.reflection.v1alpha.ServerReflection`. They list the services of their listener.

The health service is `grpc.health.v1.Health`, with the methods `Check` and `Watch`. A check can name the whole server, with an empty service name, or one service of the listener. It returns `SERVING` while the control store answers a ping within 2 s, and `NOT_SERVING` otherwise. A check of an unknown service gets `not_found`. `Watch` sends the status at once. Then it checks again every 5 s, and sends the status each time that it changes. Each listener serves at most 64 open `Watch` calls. One more gets `resource_exhausted`.

```sh
grpcurl -plaintext 127.0.0.1:7080 list
grpcurl -plaintext 127.0.0.1:7080 grpc.health.v1.Health/Check
```

## InstallService

`hopbox.v1.InstallService` describes the install to a client before it signs in. The generated reference is [Public API](/api/public/).

### GetInstallInfo

`GetInstallInfo` returns the facts that a client needs before its first call. It needs no credential. It has no side effects, so the Connect protocol also serves it with HTTP GET.

| Item              | Value                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.InstallService/GetInstallInfo` |
| Policy action     | `install.get_info`, every caller           |
| Idempotent option | no                                         |
| Audit entry       | none                                       |

The request `GetInstallInfoRequest` has no fields. The response `GetInstallInfoResponse` has these fields:

| Field             | Type                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `domain`          | string                  | The domain of the install, for example `example.com`. It is empty until an instance admin sets it with `UpdateInstallConfig` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#updateinstallconfig)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `sign_in_methods` | repeated `SignInMethod` | The sign-in methods that anyone can use on the install ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/#signinmethod)). `SIGN_IN_METHOD_EMAIL_LINK` is in the list while the install has an SMTP config ([SMTP config](/reference/smtp/)) or the file mail transport ([Mail](/reference/mail/#mail-transports)). `SIGN_IN_METHOD_GITHUB` and `SIGN_IN_METHOD_GOOGLE` are in it while the install has a domain and the client of the provider ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/#config)). The first-admin login link is never in it, because only root can make one. |
| `ssh_host_key`    | string                  | The public host key of the SSH front door, in the `authorized_keys` format, for example `ssh-ed25519 AAAA...`. The edge servers show it on every SSH port ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#keys)). It is empty until a control process made the keys of the front door, which needs a key-encryption key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `version`         | string                  | The version of `hopboxd` on the server that answered, for example `v0.1.0` ([the version command](/reference/version/#version-format)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `mail_to_files`   | bool                    | `true` on a dev or test install with the file mail transport ([Mail](/reference/mail/#mail-transports)). Then no magic link or invitation reaches its recipient by email. The console uses it to tell the person to ask the operator for the link.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

In the JSON codec, a field with its default value is left out, so an empty `domain` does not appear.

Example with the Connect protocol and HTTP GET:

```text
$ curl -s --http2-prior-knowledge \
    'http://127.0.0.1:7080/hopbox.v1.InstallService/GetInstallInfo?encoding=json&message=%7B%7D'
{"domain":"example.com","version":"v0.1.0"}
```

Example with gRPC:

```sh
grpcurl -plaintext 127.0.0.1:7080 hopbox.v1.InstallService/GetInstallInfo
```

## Logs

The API writes these records with `component=api`. The access log record covers every call, also refused ones.

| Message                       | Level | Fields                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `api call`                    | info  | `procedure`, `protocol`, `peer`, `caller`, `code`, `duration`, and `request_id`. `protocol` is `connect`, `grpc`, `grpcweb`, or `websocket` for the WebSocket endpoint of exec. `peer` is the address of the client, empty on the admin socket. `code` is `ok` or the error code. `caller` is the caller kind, or `unresolved` after the gate refused the credential. A call of a tool of the MCP server also has `mcp_request_id`, the request ID of its MCP request ([the MCP server](/reference/mcp/#logs)). |
| `api call failed`             | error | `procedure`, `err`, `request_id`. For an `internal` error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `api call failed`             | warn  | `procedure`, `err`, `request_id`. For a Connect error from a library, which keeps its code.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `api call stopped`            | info  | `procedure`, `err`, `request_id`. For `deadline_exceeded` and `canceled`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `api credential refused`      | info  | `err`, `request_id`. A resolver refused a credential.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `api credential check failed` | error | `err`, `request_id`. A resolver failed to check a credential.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `machine URL sign-in failed`  | error | `err`, `request_id`. `GET /auth/machine` failed with `500` ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#answers-of-authmachine)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `websocket upgrade failed`    | info  | `path`, `err`, `request_id`. The upgrade of a request to the WebSocket endpoint `/api/ws/exec` failed ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#the-websocket-endpoint)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

The HTTP server writes its own errors, such as a protocol error of a client, at level warn with `component=http`.

# API definitions

> The API definitions under proto/, the code generators and their versions, the generated outputs, the make targets, and the API checks in CI.

The API definitions of hopbox are protobuf files under `proto/`. buf checks them and runs the code generators that turn them into Go code, TypeScript code, MCP tools, and OpenAPI documents. This page lists the files, the generators, the outputs, the make targets, and the checks in CI. After a change to a proto file, run `make generate` and commit the generated code with the change (the build guide of the repo has an example).

## Packages and folders

The STANDARD lint rules require that the folder of a file matches its package.

| Package             | Folder                    | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hopbox.v1`         | `proto/hopbox/v1`         | The public API ([the API server](/reference/api/)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `hopbox.admin.v1`   | `proto/hopbox/admin/v1`   | The admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `hopbox.cluster.v1` | `proto/hopbox/cluster/v1` | The cluster API between the servers of an install and the control role: the enrollment and the control channel. Only the internal listener serves it ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/)). It is not part of the public API. The name is not `internal`, because Go forbids an import of `gen/hopbox/internal` from `internal/control`. |
| `hopbox.guest.v1`   | `proto/hopbox/guest/v1`   | The guest link between a node and the guest agent of a machine. [Guest link](/reference/guest-link/) describes it. It is not part of the public API.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

| File                                         | Services                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `proto/hopbox/v1/options.proto`              | none. It defines the options `(hopbox.v1.idempotent)` and `(hopbox.v1.read_only)`.               |
| `proto/hopbox/v1/install.proto`              | `hopbox.v1.InstallService`                                                                       |
| `proto/hopbox/admin/v1/install_config.proto` | `hopbox.admin.v1.InstallConfigService`                                                           |
| `proto/hopbox/admin/v1/keyring.proto`        | `hopbox.admin.v1.KeyringService`                                                                 |
| `proto/hopbox/admin/v1/server.proto`         | `hopbox.admin.v1.ServerService`                                                                  |
| `proto/hopbox/cluster/v1/enrollment.proto`   | `hopbox.cluster.v1.EnrollmentService` ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/)) |
| `proto/hopbox/cluster/v1/control.proto`      | `hopbox.cluster.v1.ControlService` ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/))          |
| `proto/hopbox/guest/v1/link.proto`           | `hopbox.guest.v1.LinkService`                                                                    |

## Definitions

### `(hopbox.v1.idempotent)`

File: `proto/hopbox/v1/options.proto`.

| Item         | Value                                        |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| Kind         | extension of `google.protobuf.MethodOptions` |
| Type         | `bool`                                       |
| Default      | `false`                                      |
| Field number | `51200`                                      |

A method with this option creates a resource, such as a machine or a fork. A client must send an `Idempotency-Key` header with each call of such a method. A client that retries the call sends the same key again. The server keeps each key for 24 hours. For a key that it knows, the server returns the first result and does not act again. [The API server](/reference/api/#idempotency-keys) says how the server handles the header. `hopbox.admin.v1.KeyringService.RotateKEK` has the option.

Example:

```proto
import "hopbox/v1/options.proto";


service MachineService {
  rpc CreateMachine(CreateMachineRequest) returns (CreateMachineResponse) {
    option (hopbox.v1.idempotent) = true;
  }
}
```

### `(hopbox.v1.read_only)`

File: `proto/hopbox/v1/options.proto`.

| Item         | Value                                        |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| Kind         | extension of `google.protobuf.MethodOptions` |
| Type         | `bool`                                       |
| Default      | `false`                                      |
| Field number | `51201`                                      |

A method with this option changes nothing on the server, such as a get, a list, or a watch call. A second run of the call does no harm. The request gate still records the last use of the credential of the call, such as an API key, at most once per minute, except in maintenance mode ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#lifetimes)). A second run only moves that time. So the Go client and the TypeScript SDK retry a unary call with it, also after a lost answer ([Go client](/reference/go-client/#retries)). They never retry a stream. In maintenance mode, the server lets a call with this option in, and refuses it at its first write, such as its audit entry, before the write ([the API server](/reference/api/#maintenance-mode)). So a read that writes nothing works in maintenance mode. The option itself does not say whether a call writes an audit entry: an audit entry of a read, such as the entry of each call of the admin API, does not count as a change for a retry. Give the option to each new call that only reads. Do not give it to a call that writes, also when its name starts with `Get`. For example, `GetDeviceAuthorization` counts each wrong code against a limit, so it has no option.

The standard option `idempotency_level` with the value `NO_SIDE_EFFECTS` says the same. But `buf breaking` with the FILE rules counts a change of `idempotency_level` as a break, so the read calls of v0.1.0 cannot get it. A new custom option passes `buf breaking`. The clients treat both options the same. `GetInstallInfo` has both.

These methods of `hopbox.v1` have the option:

| Service          | Methods                                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `InstallService` | `GetInstallInfo`                                                                                                       |
| `AccountService` | `GetAccount`, `ListSignInMethods`, `ListCLISignIns`                                                                    |
| `APIKeyService`  | `ListAPIKeys`                                                                                                          |
| `AuditService`   | `ListAuditEntries`                                                                                                     |
| `MachineService` | `GetMachine`, `ListMachines`, `ListMachineSizes`, and the streams `WatchMachines`, `Download`, and `StreamMachineLogs` |
| `OrgService`     | `GetOrg`, `ListOrgs`, `GetOrgUsage`, `ListOrgMembers`, `ListInvitations`                                               |
| `SSHKeyService`  | `ListSSHKeys`                                                                                                          |
| `VarService`     | `ListVars`                                                                                                             |

These methods of `hopbox.admin.v1` have the option:

| Service                | Methods                                               |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `InstallConfigService` | `GetInstallConfig`, `GetSMTPConfig`, `GetOAuthConfig` |
| `CertificateService`   | `GetCertificate`                                      |
| `KeyringService`       | `ListKEKs`                                            |
| `MailService`          | `ListMailFiles`, `GetMailFile`                        |
| `InstanceAdminService` | `ListInstanceAdmins`                                  |
| `AccountService`       | `ListAccountSignInMethods`                            |
| `ServerService`        | `ListServers`, `GetServer`                            |
| `OrgService`           | `ListOrgs`, `GetDefaultOrgLimits`                     |
| `AdminKeyService`      | `ListAdminKeys`                                       |
| `MachineService`       | `ListMachines`                                        |
| `ImageService`         | `ListImages`                                          |
| `PoolService`          | `GetPool`, `ListPools`                                |
| `SizeService`          | `GetSize`, `ListSizes`                                |

No method of `hopbox.cluster.v1` has the option.

Example:

```proto
import "hopbox/v1/options.proto";


service OrgService {
  rpc ListOrgs(ListOrgsRequest) returns (ListOrgsResponse) {
    option (hopbox.v1.read_only) = true;
  }
}
```

## Configuration files

| File                                      | What it sets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `buf.yaml`                                | buf configuration version `v2`. One module at `proto/`. Lint uses the `STANDARD` rules. Breaking-change checks use the `FILE` rules. The module has no dependencies, so buf never reads a registry.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `buf.gen.yaml`                            | The plugins, their options, and their output folders. Every plugin is local. `exclude_types` keeps `hopbox.admin.v1`, `hopbox.cluster.v1`, and `hopbox.guest.v1` out of the TypeScript SDK. The SDKs never include the admin API, only the servers of an install and the control role use the cluster API, and only a node and a guest agent use the guest link. `clean: true` deletes each output folder before buf writes to it. Managed mode sets `go_package` to the path of the file under `gen/` in the Go module of hopbox, so the proto files carry no Go options. |
| `proto/hopbox/v1/openapi.base.yaml`       | The `info` block of the OpenAPI document of `hopbox.v1`: its title, description, and version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `proto/hopbox/admin/v1/openapi.base.yaml` | The `info` block of the OpenAPI document of `hopbox.admin.v1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `tools/proto/go.mod`                      | The versions of buf and of the Go plugins, as `tool` directives.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `web/packages/sdk/package.json`           | The versions of `@bufbuild/protoc-gen-es` and its runtime `@bufbuild/protobuf`, and the other packages of the TypeScript SDK ([TypeScript SDK](/reference/ts-sdk/#package)). `pnpm-lock.yaml` locks them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Generators and outputs

`make generate` runs `buf generate`, which runs these plugins.

| Plugin                       | Version                                                                         | Runs on                                                                            | Output                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `protoc-gen-go`              | `google.golang.org/protobuf` v1.36.12                                           | every package                                                                      | `gen/<path>/*.pb.go`, Go package `<name><version>`, for example `hopboxv1`                                                                                                                                                              |
| `protoc-gen-connect-go`      | `connectrpc.com/connect` v1.21.1                                                | every package                                                                      | `gen/<path>/<name><version>connect/*.connect.go`, for each file with a service                                                                                                                                                          |
| `protoc-gen-go-mcp`          | `github.com/redpanda-data/protoc-gen-go-mcp` v0.0.0-20260729122341-6334690a62b6 | `hopbox.v1`                                                                        | `gen/hopbox/v1/hopboxv1mcp/*.pb.mcp.go`, one MCP tool for each unary method, for each file with a service. The plugin skips streaming methods. The MCP server in `internal/mcp` serves these tools ([the MCP server](/reference/mcp/)). |
| `protoc-gen-connect-openapi` | `github.com/sudorandom/protoc-gen-connect-openapi` v0.28.0                      | `hopbox.v1` and `hopbox.admin.v1`, one run each                                    | `docs/reference/api/hopbox.v1.openapi.yaml` and `docs/reference/api/hopbox.admin.v1.openapi.yaml`, one OpenAPI 3.1 document for each package                                                                                            |
| `protoc-gen-es`              | `@bufbuild/protoc-gen-es` 2.16.0                                                | every package except `hopbox.admin.v1`, `hopbox.cluster.v1`, and `hopbox.guest.v1` | `web/packages/sdk/src/gen/<path>/*_pb.ts`, TypeScript with `target=ts` and `import_extension=js`, so a relative import between generated files ends in `.js`, as Node.js ES modules require                                             |
| `protoc-gen-es`              | `@bufbuild/protoc-gen-es` 2.16.0                                                | `hopbox.admin.v1`, with the types of `hopbox.v1` that it uses                      | `web/apps/console/src/gen/<path>/*_pb.ts`, with the same options. The Admin area of the console calls the admin API with this code ([Console](/reference/console/#admin-area)). The SDK never includes the admin API.                   |

buf is `github.com/bufbuild/buf` v1.74.0.

The output folders are in git. Do not edit a file in them by hand. The next `make generate` writes over it, and CI rejects it. `.gitattributes` marks the folders as generated, so GitHub folds them in a diff.

[Public API](/api/public/) is the generated reference of the public API, and [Admin API](/api/admin/) is the generated reference of the admin API. The cluster API `hopbox.cluster.v1` and the guest link get no OpenAPI document and no MCP tools. [Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/) and [the control channel](/reference/control-channel/) describe the cluster API. Their paths come from the services, and their descriptions come from the comments in the proto files.

### Version rules

* A generator and the runtime that builds its output must have the same version. The test `TestGoGeneratorsMatchRuntimes` in `proto/generators_test.go` compares `google.golang.org/protobuf`, `connectrpc.com/connect`, and `github.com/redpanda-data/protoc-gen-go-mcp` in `go.mod` with the same modules in `tools/proto/go.mod`. It checks only the modules that `go.mod` requires. The test `TestESGeneratorMatchesRuntime` compares `@bufbuild/protobuf` with `@bufbuild/protoc-gen-es` in `web/packages/sdk/package.json`. It also rejects a range such as `^2.16.0` or `~2.16.0`, so each must be an exact version. `make test` runs both tests.
* To change a version, change it in both files, then run `make generate` and commit the result.
* `protoc-gen-go-mcp` has no release tags, so its version is a pseudo-version of one commit.
* `buf.gen.yaml` runs `protoc-gen-go-mcp` with `GOEXPERIMENT=nojsonv2`. The plugin writes each tool schema with Go’s `%#v` format. With the JSON v2 package of Go 1.27, a `json.RawMessage` prints as `jsontext.Value`, and the generated file does not import `jsontext`. With `nojsonv2`, the plugin prints `json.RawMessage`, and the output compiles.
* The generated MCP code imports `google.golang.org/grpc`. grpc uses `http2.TrailerPrefix` from `golang.org/x/net`. With Go 1.27, `golang.org/x/net` v0.54.0 does not define it, and the build fails with `undefined: http2.TrailerPrefix`. `golang.org/x/net` v0.55.0 defines it. So `go.mod` requires `google.golang.org/grpc` v1.83.1, which requires `golang.org/x/net` v0.55.0. The `go.mod` of `github.com/redpanda-data/protoc-gen-go-mcp` asks only for grpc v1.82.1. Do not move grpc below v1.83.1.

## Make targets

| Target           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `generate`       | Runs `buf generate`, then sqlc for the store queries ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#queries)). If `web/packages/sdk/node_modules/.bin/protoc-gen-es` is missing, it fails with a message. Run `corepack pnpm install` first.              |
| `check-generate` | Runs `make generate`. It then looks for a changed, added, or deleted file in `gen/`, `docs/reference/api/`, `web/packages/sdk/src/gen/`, `web/apps/console/src/gen/`, and `internal/store/db/`. If git sees one, it prints the changed files and fails. |
| `lint`           | Runs golangci-lint, then `buf lint`, then the docs check, which makes sure that the docs and the code agree.                                                                                                                                            |
| `breaking`       | Runs `buf breaking --against '.git#ref=<BREAKING_AGAINST>'`. If that ref has no `proto/` folder, it prints a message and passes. If the ref does not exist, it fails.                                                                                   |

| Variable           | Default                                      | Description                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `BUF`              | `$(GO) tool -modfile=tools/proto/go.mod buf` | The buf command.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `BREAKING_AGAINST` | `origin/main`                                | The git ref that `make breaking` compares `proto/` with. Run `git fetch` first, so that the ref is current. In a checkout without the `origin` remote, set it to `main`. |

The `breaking` target passes for a ref without `proto/`, so the first change that adds `proto/` can merge. After that change is on `main`, every later change is checked against it.

## Checks in CI

| Check            | Job    | Command                                      | Fails when                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Lint             | `lint` | `make lint`                                  | a definition breaks a `STANDARD` rule, for example a message name that is not PascalCase              |
| Breaking changes | `api`  | `make breaking BREAKING_AGAINST=origin/main` | a change breaks a `FILE` rule against `main`, for example a deleted extension or a changed field type |
| Drift            | `api`  | `make check-generate`                        | the generated code in git differs from the output of `make generate`                                  |
| Versions         | `test` | `make test`                                  | a generator and its runtime have different versions                                                   |
| Tidy             | `lint` | `go mod tidy -diff` in `tools/proto`         | `tools/proto/go.mod` or `tools/proto/go.sum` is not tidy                                              |

These outputs illustrate each failure. The `make lint` sample comes from a message that was added to `options.proto` only for the illustration.

```text
$ make lint
proto/hopbox/v1/options.proto:18:9:Message name "install_info" should be PascalCase, such as "InstallInfo".
proto/hopbox/v1/options.proto:19:10:Field name "Domain" should be lower_snake_case, such as "domain".


$ make breaking
proto/hopbox/v1/options.proto:15:3:Extension "51200" with name "hopbox.v1.idempotent" on message "google.protobuf.MethodOptions" changed type from "bool" to "string".


$ make check-generate
 M gen/hopbox/v1/options.pb.go
make: the generated code does not match the API definitions or the SQL queries. Run make generate and commit the result.
```

# Artifact format

> The artifact format version 1 for images: the files, artifact.json, the digest, the Go API, and tools/imageartifact.

An artifact is a folder that holds a disk and its metadata. Images, snapshots, and checkpoints share this format. Format version 1 has one kind, `image`. An image has no memory file. Snapshots and checkpoints come in phase 3, with a new format version.

The Go package `internal/artifact` reads, writes, and checks artifacts. It uses only the Go standard library, so the control role and the node role can both use it.

## Files

| File                | Required | What it holds                                                                      |
| ------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `artifact.json`     | yes      | The metadata.                                                                      |
| the disk file       | yes      | The disk, as raw bytes. The default image calls it `disk.raw`.                     |
| the compressed copy | no       | A zstd copy of the disk, for downloads. The default image calls it `disk.raw.zst`. |

The metadata names each file. Each file must be a regular file: the checks refuse a symlink. A file name is a plain name in the folder: it has no `/` or `\`, it does not start with a dot, and it is not `artifact.json`. So metadata can never point at a file outside the folder.

## The disk

| Item        | Rule                                                                                               |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Format      | Raw: the bytes of the block device, in a sparse file. A hole reads as zeros.                       |
| Partitions  | None. The file system fills the whole disk. Firecracker gives the disk to the guest as `/dev/vda`. |
| File system | ext4                                                                                               |
| Size        | A multiple of 512 bytes, the sector size of the virtio disk.                                       |
| sha256      | The sha256 of all bytes of the disk, with each hole read as zeros.                                 |

A node makes the disk of a machine from the image disk with a reflink copy, and makes the copy bigger. At boot, `systemd-growfs` in the guest grows the file system to fill the disk ([Default image](/reference/default-image/#disk)).

## artifact.json

`artifact.json` is a JSON object with these fields, in this order. Every field is required, apart from `disk.compressed`.

| Field                    | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `format_version`         | number | `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `kind`                   | string | `image`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `arch`                   | string | `x86_64`, the CPU architecture of the programs on the disk. A node refuses an artifact of another architecture.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `name`                   | string | The name of the artifact, for example `default`. It is 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, dots, and hyphens, and it starts and ends with a letter or digit. Each build of an image has the same name, so the name does not identify one build. The digest does. |
| `created_at`             | string | The build time, in RFC 3339 format in UTC with the suffix `Z`, for example `2026-10-16T00:00:00Z`. A time with an offset, also `+00:00`, is not valid. A reproducible build sets it from its `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`.                                               |
| `disk.file`              | string | The name of the disk file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `disk.format`            | string | `raw`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `disk.filesystem`        | string | `ext4`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `disk.size`              | number | The size of the disk in bytes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `disk.sha256`            | string | The sha256 of the disk, as 64 lowercase hex digits.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `disk.compressed.file`   | string | The name of the compressed copy. It differs from `disk.file`.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `disk.compressed.codec`  | string | `zstd`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `disk.compressed.size`   | number | The size of the compressed file in bytes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `disk.compressed.sha256` | string | The sha256 of the compressed file, as 64 lowercase hex digits.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `kernel.sha256`          | string | The sha256 of the guest kernel `vmlinux` that the image was built for and tested with ([Guest kernel](/reference/guest-kernel/#outputs)). A node refuses to boot the image with a kernel of another sha256.                                                     |
| `programs`               | list   | The program manifest: each program of the image with its version, sorted by name. An image lists at least one program.                                                                                                                                          |
| `programs[].name`        | string | The name of the program, for example `docker-ce`. Each name appears once.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `programs[].version`     | string | The version that the build installed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `programs[].source`      | string | Where the build got the program, for example `go.dev/dl`.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

A reader refuses these cases:

| Case                                                                            | Error                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| A `format_version` other than `1`                                               | `ErrUnsupportedVersion` |
| A field that the reader does not know, for example a `memory` field in an image | `ErrInvalid`            |
| A field name in another case, for example `Kind`                                | `ErrInvalid`            |
| A field name that appears twice in one object                                   | `ErrInvalid`            |
| A value that breaks a rule above                                                | `ErrInvalid`            |
| Data after the JSON object                                                      | `ErrInvalid`            |

A new field therefore needs a new format version. A new version can add the kinds `snapshot` and `checkpoint` with their memory files.

Example, shortened:

```json
{
  "format_version": 1,
  "kind": "image",
  "arch": "x86_64",
  "name": "default",
  "created_at": "2026-10-16T00:00:00Z",
  "disk": {
    "file": "disk.raw",
    "format": "raw",
    "filesystem": "ext4",
    "size": 3758096384,
    "sha256": "465579a3e137d8222d1bfde177cca61fb344791812203d628aa09777a1e26162",
    "compressed": {
      "file": "disk.raw.zst",
      "codec": "zstd",
      "size": 558547703,
      "sha256": "03ebe2e931f5521a445822065eb6b7a5ebcc5eb857542eec8d5288c609b07563"
    }
  },
  "kernel": {
    "sha256": "dfb03703bab6d4b590964f2d9473fdc82994ae94384cc5ed1c1b4a0430118a91"
  },
  "programs": [
    {
      "name": "containerd.io",
      "version": "2.4.2-2~ubuntu.26.04~resolute",
      "source": "download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Digest

The digest of an artifact is `sha256:` and the sha256 of the bytes of its `artifact.json`, for example `sha256:354fb767...`. The metadata holds the sha256 of each file, so the digest covers the whole artifact. A node that has the digest from the control plane checks `artifact.json` against it, then checks each file against `artifact.json`. An image cache with the compressed copy checks it with `VerifyCompressed`, unpacks it to the disk file, and runs `VerifyDisk`. After that check, the cache can delete the compressed copy. `VerifyDisk` alone then proves the disk. A node that downloads the compressed disk from the URL of an image gets no `artifact.json`. It checks the unpacked disk against the sha256 and the size that the control plane sends with the image ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/#the-image-cache)).

The writer encodes the metadata the same way each time: the field order above, two spaces of indent, `created_at` in UTC, and one newline at the end. So two builds with the same content have the same digest.

## Go API

| Function                              | Description                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Parse(data)`                         | Decodes and checks `artifact.json`.                                                                   |
| `Metadata.Validate()`                 | Checks the rules above.                                                                               |
| `Metadata.Marshal()`                  | Checks the metadata, then encodes it as `artifact.json`.                                              |
| `Digest(data)`                        | Returns the digest of the bytes of an `artifact.json`.                                                |
| `Read(dir)`                           | Reads and checks `dir/artifact.json`. Returns the metadata and the digest. It does not read the disk. |
| `Write(dir, metadata)`                | Writes `dir/artifact.json` in one rename. Returns the digest.                                         |
| `HashFile(ctx, path)`                 | Returns the size and the sha256 of a file.                                                            |
| `Metadata.VerifyDisk(ctx, dir)`       | Checks the size and the sha256 of the disk file.                                                      |
| `Metadata.VerifyCompressed(ctx, dir)` | If the metadata names a compressed copy, checks its size and its sha256.                              |
| `Verify(ctx, dir)`                    | `Read`, then `VerifyDisk` and `VerifyCompressed`.                                                     |

If a file does not match its metadata, the error is a `*MismatchError`. It holds the file name, the field (`size` or `sha256`), and both values.

## imageartifact

The build tool `tools/imageartifact` writes and checks the `artifact.json` of an image build. `make image` and `make check-image` run it ([Default image](/reference/default-image/#make-targets)).

```sh
go run ./tools/imageartifact write -dir DIR -name NAME -programs FILE -kernel-sha256 HEX -created UNIX
go run ./tools/imageartifact verify -dir DIR
```

| Command  | What it does                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `write`  | Hashes `DIR/disk.raw` and `DIR/disk.raw.zst`, and writes `DIR/artifact.json` with the programs of `FILE`, a JSON list of `{name, version, source}`. Prints the digest. |
| `verify` | Runs `Verify` on `DIR`. Prints the digest.                                                                                                                             |

| Flag             | Description                     |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `-dir`           | The artifact folder.            |
| `-name`          | The name of the artifact.       |
| `-programs`      | The program manifest.           |
| `-kernel-sha256` | The sha256 of the guest kernel. |
| `-created`       | The build time in Unix seconds. |

The exit status is 0 on success, 1 on an error, and 2 for a bad command line.

# The sign-in, account, and audit API

> The sign-in, account, audit, API key, and SSH key calls of the public API: AuthService with the device flow, AccountService, AuditService, APIKeyService, and SSHKeyService, with their audit entries.

These services of the public API `hopbox.v1` sign people in to the console and the hopbox CLI. They also manage the account of the caller with its API keys and SSH keys, and read the audit log. [The API server](/reference/api/) covers the parts that every call shares: the request gate, the policy check, and the error codes. [Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/) covers the session cookie, the check against cross-site requests, the links, and the rate limits. [Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/) covers the sign-in with GitHub and Google, which runs on browser endpoints, not on calls of this API. [CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/) covers the device flow, CLI tokens, API keys, and SSH keys. The generated reference is [Public API](/api/public/).

| Service                    | Calls                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hopbox.v1.AuthService`    | `RequestMagicLink`, `VerifyMagicLink`, `VerifyLoginLink`, `SignOut`, `StartDeviceAuthorization`, `GetDeviceAuthorization`, `ApproveDevice`, `PollDeviceAuthorization`, `RefreshCLIToken` |
| `hopbox.v1.AccountService` | `GetAccount`, `UpdateAccount`, `DeleteAccount`, `ListSignInMethods`, `RemoveSignInMethod`, `ListCLISignIns`, `EndCLISignIn`                                                              |
| `hopbox.v1.AuditService`   | `ListAuditEntries`                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `hopbox.v1.APIKeyService`  | `CreateAPIKey`, `ListAPIKeys`, `RevokeAPIKey`                                                                                                                                            |
| `hopbox.v1.SSHKeyService`  | `AddSSHKey`, `ListSSHKeys`, `RemoveSSHKey`                                                                                                                                               |

A call with the session cookie must carry the header `Origin` with the origin of the install, and the header `Connect-Protocol-Version: 1` ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#calls-with-the-cookie)). The examples on this page use curl against a laptop install with the domain `example.com`, as in [First sign-in on a new install](/guide/first-sign-in/). Each example of a call with the cookie uses these shell variables:

```sh
API=http://127.0.0.1:7080
COOKIE='__Host-hopbox_session=<token>'
browser() {
  curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Connect-Protocol-Version: 1' \
    -H 'Origin: https://example.com' -H "Cookie: $COOKIE" "$@"
}
```

## Messages

### Account

| Field             | Type                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`              | string                      | The UUID of the account.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `display_name`    | string                      | The name that the person chose. It can be empty.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `emails`          | repeated `AccountEmail`     | The emails of the account.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `instance_admin`  | bool                        | `true` for an instance admin.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `personal_org_id` | string                      | The UUID of the personal org of the account.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `version`         | int64                       | The version of the account. It starts at 1 and grows by 1 with each change.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `create_time`     | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the first sign-in.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `admin_notices`   | int32                       | The count of the open notices of an instance admin, which the Admin area lists ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#notices-to-instance-admins)). The console shows a banner while it is more than 0. It is 0 for any other account. |

### AccountEmail

| Field         | Type                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `email`       | string                      | The address, in lower case.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `verified`    | bool                        | `true` for an email that a sign-in method proved. Only a verified email links other sign-in methods to the account, and only while the account has no identity of GitHub or Google ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#what-a-sign-in-does)). The email of a login link stays unverified, until a link from a session proves it ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#link-a-new-sign-in-method)). |
| `verify_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the proof. It is unset for an email that is not verified.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

### SignInMethod

The enum `SignInMethod` names a kind of sign-in. `GetInstallInfo` lists the kinds that anyone can use ([the API server](/reference/api/#getinstallinfo)).

| Value                        | Meaning                                                                                                                                                | In `GetInstallInfo`                                                                                        |
