`machine delete` asks its question on the terminal. `env set NAME` reads the value from the terminal with no echo, as in a shell. Each of them reads its answer up to the first CR or LF, and no more. So a paste of `env set NAME`, a value, and a next command, each with its Enter, sets the value and then runs the command. A Ctrl-C at the question ends the command, and the prompt stays open.

At the prompt itself, the keys Ctrl-C and Ctrl-D are keys, not signals. A SIGINT, a SIGTERM, a SIGHUP, or a SIGQUIT that comes from another process closes the prompt, and puts the terminal back. For example, the close of the window of the terminal sends a SIGHUP. The line typed so far then does not run. The prompt prints a newline, and the CLI exits with 128 plus the number of the signal.

| Status | When                                                                                       |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 0      | `exit`, `quit`, or Ctrl-D on an empty line. The status of the last command does not count. |
| 80     | The prompt cannot open.                                                                    |
| 130    | A SIGINT from another process closed the prompt.                                           |
| 143    | A SIGTERM closed the prompt.                                                               |
| 129    | A SIGHUP closed the prompt.                                                                |
| 131    | A SIGQUIT closed the prompt.                                                               |
| 1      | The line editor did not start, or it failed to read a line.                                |

`hopbox prompt` opens [the prompt](#the-prompt), as `hopbox` without a command does. The help of the CLI does not list it.

### new

```sh
hopbox new [NAME] [flags]
```

Makes a machine in the org of the command with `CreateMachine` ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#createmachine)). The CLI adds the machine to the managed SSH block. Then it watches the machine with `WatchMachines` until the machine runs, and prints it as [machine show](#machine-show) does. `machine create` is the same command. Each try of the call carries the same idempotency key, so a retry never makes a second machine.

| Flag                    | Default                     | Description                                                                                          |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NAME`                  | a free name, such as `box1` | The name: a lowercase DNS label of 1 to 63 characters that starts with a letter.                     |
| `--size=SIZE`           | `default`                   | A size from [machine sizes](#machine-sizes).                                                         |
| `--image=IMAGE`         | `default`                   | The image.                                                                                           |
| `--restart=POLICY`      | `always`                    | The restart policy: `always` or `never`.                                                             |
| `--start-command=CMD`   | none                        | A command that the machine runs as `user` after each boot.                                           |
| `--auto-delete=TIMEOUT` | `off`                       | Deletes the machine after this time without use.                                                     |
| `--wait=DURATION`       | `5m`                        | The longest wait until the machine runs. `0` prints the new machine at once, in the state `pending`. |

JSON: the machine object of [Machines in commands](#machines-in-commands).

| Error                                                                                                           | Status | Cause                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `already_exists: already exists: the machine name "box1" is taken. A free name is "box2"`                       | 5      | Another machine holds the name, or another org holds it in reservation. The message names a free name, as the install suggests it. |
| `unavailable: ... no capacity: ...`                                                                             | 6      | No node has room for the machine ([Placement](/reference/placement/)).                                                             |
| `the machine <name> does not run after <wait>. It is <state>. hopbox machine show <name> shows its state later` | 6      | The wait ended first. The machine exists, and can still start.                                                                     |
| `the machine <name> failed to start. hopbox machine show <name> shows it`                                       | 1      | The machine reached the state `failed`.                                                                                            |

### list

```sh
hopbox list
```

Lists the machines of the org that you see, by name. `ls`, `machine list`, and `machine ls` are the same command. A state on its way shows both states, such as `stopped -> running`.

```text
NAME  STATE    SIZE     SHARED  URL                       SSH
box1  running  default  no      https://box1.example.com  box1.hop
```

The list also brings the managed SSH block up to date: the entries of the org on this install then match the list ([SSH files](#ssh-files)). JSON: an array of machine objects.

### connect

```sh
hopbox connect MACHINE
```

Opens the login shell of `user` in a running machine with `Exec`, with `tty` set and no `argv` ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#exec)). It needs no SSH key, and it uses only the port of the API, 443, so it works from networks with few open ports.

If stdin is a terminal, the CLI does these things:

1. It sends the size of the terminal and the env var `TERM`.
2. It puts the terminal in raw mode. Each key then goes to the shell, Ctrl-C, Ctrl-Z, and Ctrl-D too.
3. At each SIGWINCH, it sends the new size of the terminal.
4. When the shell ends, it puts the terminal back as it was. It does the same after an error and after a signal.

The exit status is the exit status of the shell, so `exit 3` in the shell ends `hopbox connect` with 3. A machine that does not run fails with `failed_precondition`, status 1. Phase 1 has no standby and no hibernate, so `connect` wakes no machine. `connect` has no JSON output: `--json` fails with status 80.

### exec

```sh
hopbox exec [flags] MACHINE [COMMAND [ARG...]]
```

Runs a command in a running machine with `Exec`, and exits with the exit code of the command.

The flags of `exec` go before the command. Each word from the command on belongs to the command, flags too. So `hopbox exec box1 ls -la` runs `ls -la`, and `hopbox exec box1 echo --json` prints `--json`. A `--` before the command also works. Without a command, the login shell of the user runs, and reads its commands from stdin. With `--tty` and no command, `exec` opens a shell, as `connect` does.

| Flag                       | Default                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-e`, `--env=NAME[=VALUE]` | none                     | An env var for the command, on top of the env of the machine. `NAME` alone takes the value of `NAME` on the laptop, also an empty value. If `NAME` is not set on the laptop, the command fails with status 80. Repeat the flag for more env vars. A value can hold commas. |
| `--timeout=DURATION`       | none                     | Ends the command after this time, 1 s to 24 h. The exit code is then 124.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `-t`, `--tty`              | `false`                  | Runs the command in a terminal. The command then sends all its output to stdout. If stdin is a terminal, the CLI handles it as `connect` does.                                                                                                                             |
| `-u`, `--user=USER`        | `user`                   | The Linux user that runs the command.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `-w`, `--dir=DIR`          | the home dir of the user | The working dir.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

The CLI sends its stdin to the command, as ssh does, and then the end of the input. The stdout of the command goes to stdout, and its stderr to stderr. A command in a shell loop that reads stdin takes the input of the loop. Give it `</dev/null` to stop that.

The exit status of `hopbox exec` is the exit code of the command:

| Exit code                  | When                                                                     |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| The code of the command    | The command ended by itself. A code out of 0 to 255 becomes 255.         |
| 124                        | `--timeout` ended the command.                                           |
| 126                        | The command did not start. The CLI prints `hopbox: <reason>` to stderr.  |
| 127                        | The program does not exist. The CLI prints `hopbox: <reason>` to stderr. |
| 128 plus the signal number | A signal ended the command, for example 130 for SIGINT.                  |

The statuses of [Exit status](#exit-status) apply only to a command that did not run. For example, a machine that does not exist gives 4, and a machine that does not run gives 1.

A Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a SIGTERM goes to the process group of the command, as the signal with the same name. The command can end, or go on. A second Ctrl-C or SIGTERM ends the exec. The API then ends the command with SIGTERM, and after 2 s with SIGKILL. The status is then 130 for SIGINT, or 143 for SIGTERM. With `--tty` and a terminal, Ctrl-C is a key for the command, as in `connect`.

With `--json`, the CLI keeps the output and prints one JSON object at the end:

```json
{"exit_code":3,"signal":"","error":"","timed_out":false,"stdout":"","stderr":"boom\n","stdout_truncated":false,"stderr_truncated":false}
```

| Field                                  | Type   | Description                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `exit_code`                            | number | The exit code of the command.                                                                                   |
| `signal`                               | string | The signal that ended the command, such as `SIGKILL`, or empty.                                                 |
| `error`                                | string | Why the command did not start, or empty.                                                                        |
| `timed_out`                            | bool   | Whether `--timeout` ended the command.                                                                          |
| `stdout`, `stderr`                     | string | The output. The CLI keeps at most 4 MiB of each (`cli.MaxJSONOutput`). A byte that is not UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD. |
| `stdout_truncated`, `stderr_truncated` | bool   | Whether the output had more than 4 MiB.                                                                         |

The exit status with `--json` is the exit code of the command too. `--json` with `--tty` fails with status 80, because a terminal sends all output to stdout.

### cp

```sh
hopbox cp [-r] [-u USER] SOURCE TARGET
```

Copies a file or a directory into a running machine with `Upload`, or out of it with `Download` ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#upload)). One of `SOURCE` and `TARGET` is in a machine, in the form `MACHINE:PATH`, such as `box1:app/main.go`. `MACHINE` is a machine name or UUID. A relative `PATH` starts at the home dir of the user. If a local path starts with a word and a colon, such as `notes:old`, write it as `./notes:old`.

| Flag                | Default | Description                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-r`, `--recursive` | `false` | Copies a directory. Its contents go into the target directory.                                    |
| `-u`, `--user=USER` | `user`  | The Linux user in the machine. It owns the new files, and a relative path starts at its home dir. |

A copy into a machine:

| `SOURCE`               | What the machine gets                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A file                 | The file `PATH`, with the permission bits of the local file.                                                                                                                                              |
| A directory, with `-r` | A tar stream of the contents of the directory. The machine extracts the contents into the directory `PATH`. It makes a missing `PATH` first. Symlinks stay symlinks. A socket or a device fails the copy. |
| `-`                    | stdin, as the contents of the file `PATH`. With `-r`, stdin is a tar stream, and the machine extracts it into the directory `PATH`.                                                                       |

An empty `PATH`, or a `PATH` that ends with `/`, gets the base name of `SOURCE`. So `hopbox cp run.sh box1:bin/` writes `bin/run.sh`, and `hopbox cp -r app box1:` writes the directory `app`. stdin has no name, so `-` needs a `PATH`. If the read of the local file fails, the CLI cancels the upload, so the machine keeps no file of a clean end.

A copy out of a machine:

| `TARGET`                                              | What the laptop gets                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A path                                                | The file, with the permission bits of the file in the machine. A temporary file in the same dir takes the data first, so a failed copy leaves no half file. |
| A directory that exists, or a path that ends with `/` | The file in that directory, with the base name of `PATH`.                                                                                                   |
| A directory, with `-r`                                | The contents of the directory `PATH`. The CLI makes a missing `TARGET` first.                                                                               |
| `-`                                                   | The data on stdout: the file, or with `-r` the tar stream of the directory.                                                                                 |

The CLI keeps the whole tar stream of a directory in a temporary file first. It extracts the stream only after the download ended well. Before the first write, it checks the name of every entry. A name with `..` that leads out of `TARGET`, or an absolute name, fails the copy, and the copy writes nothing. Then the CLI writes each entry through an `os.Root` of `TARGET`, so a write through a symlink that leads out of `TARGET` fails too. A symlink in the archive keeps its target as it is, also a target outside `TARGET`, as `tar` does. Only the writes of the copy stay inside `TARGET`. The CLI skips an entry that is not a file, a directory, or a link, and logs a warning. A download to a laptop has at most 4 MiB ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#limits)). A larger one fails with `failed_precondition`, status 1.

| Error                                                                               | Status |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| `both paths are in a machine. Copy through this laptop, in two steps`               | 80     |
| `neither path is in a machine. Write one as MACHINE:PATH, such as box1:app/main.go` | 80     |
| `<path> is a directory. Copy it with -r`                                            | 80     |
| `stdin has no name. Give the target path in the machine, such as box1:notes.txt`    | 80     |
| `the archive holds the path "<name>", which leaves the directory`                   | 1      |

On success, `cp` prints nothing, as cp does. JSON fields: `source`, `target`, `bytes` (the bytes that the copy moved), and `archive` (whether the data was a tar stream).

### logs

```sh
hopbox logs MACHINE [-f] [-n N] [--since=WHEN]
```

Prints the log of the start command of a machine with `StreamMachineLogs` ([Machine logs](/reference/machine-logs/)). A line from the stdout of the start command goes to stdout, and a line from its stderr goes to stderr. The machine can be stopped. When the node lost lines, the CLI prints `hopbox: <count> lines of the log were lost here` to stderr.

| Flag             | Default        | Description                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `-f`, `--follow` | `false`        | After the old lines, prints each new line as it comes. Ctrl-C ends it with status 130.                 |
| `-n`, `--tail=N` | `0`, all lines | Prints only the last `N` lines, at most 10000.                                                         |
| `--since=WHEN`   | all lines      | Prints only the lines from this time on: a duration back from now, such as `10m`, or an RFC 3339 time. |

With `--json`, the CLI prints one JSON object for each line, on a line of its own (JSON Lines). It prints no array, so `--follow` works with it. Each object has `time`, `stream` (`stdout` or `stderr`), `data`, and `dropped` (the count of lines lost before this one).

### machine show

```sh
hopbox machine show MACHINE
```

Prints one machine, as [Machines in commands](#machines-in-commands) shows.

### machine start

```sh
hopbox machine start MACHINE
```

Starts a stopped machine with `StartMachine`, and waits until it runs.

```text
Started the machine box1 in 1.204s.
```

The install waits for the machine for up to 60 s ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#the-wait)). If the machine is not there at the end of the wait, the command fails with status 6: `the machine <name> is not <state> after <time>. It is <state>. hopbox machine show <name> shows its state later`. The machine keeps its target, so it can still get there. The commands `machine stop`, `machine reboot`, `machine rename`, and `machine delete` work in the same way.

JSON fields of each of these commands: `machine`, the machine object, `duration_seconds`, how long the call took, and `done`, which is always `true`.

### machine stop

```sh
hopbox machine stop MACHINE
```

Stops a machine with `StopMachine`, and waits until it stops. Its disk stays.

### machine reboot

```sh
hopbox machine reboot MACHINE
```

Boots a running machine again with `RebootMachine`, and waits for the new boot.

### machine rename

```sh
hopbox machine rename MACHINE NAME
```

Gives a machine the new name `NAME` with `RenameMachine`. A running machine reboots, and the command waits for the new boot. The old name stays reserved for the org for 7 days. The CLI moves the machine to its new alias in the managed SSH block. A taken name fails with status 5, as at [new](#new).

### machine delete

```sh
hopbox machine delete MACHINE [--yes]
```

Deletes a machine and its disk with `DeleteMachine`, and waits until it is gone. `machine rm` is the same command. Its name and its SSH port stay reserved for 7 days. The CLI removes the machine from the managed SSH block.

Before the delete, the CLI asks on stderr: `Delete the machine <name> and its disk? Its name stays reserved for 7 days. [y/N]`. The answer ends at the first CR or LF. Only `y` or `yes` deletes. Another answer changes nothing, and fails with `nothing changed`, status 5. A Ctrl-C at the question deletes nothing, and ends the command with status 130. If stdin is not a terminal, or with `--json`, the CLI cannot ask. The command then needs `--yes`, or it fails with status 80.

| Flag          | Default | Description                   |
| ------------- | ------- | ----------------------------- |
| `-y`, `--yes` | `false` | Deletes without the question. |

### machine share

```sh
hopbox machine share MACHINE
```

Opens a private machine to the whole org with `ShareMachine`, and prints the machine. Only its creator can. If the env of the machine as a shared machine does not resolve, for example because a secret of the org does not open, the share fails, and the machine stays private ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#sharemachine)).

### machine unshare

```sh
hopbox machine unshare MACHINE
```

Makes a shared machine private to its creator again with `UnshareMachine`, and prints the machine. Only its creator can.

### machine update

```sh
hopbox machine update MACHINE [--restart=POLICY] [--start-command=CMD] [--auto-delete=TIMEOUT]
```

Changes the config of a machine with `UpdateMachine`, and prints the machine. A flag that you leave out keeps its value. Without a flag, the command fails with status 80.

| Flag                    | Description                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--restart=POLICY`      | The new restart policy: `always` or `never`.                                              |
| `--start-command=CMD`   | The new start command. An empty value removes it. The machine runs it from its next boot. |
| `--auto-delete=TIMEOUT` | The new auto-delete timeout, or `off`. A new timeout counts from now.                     |

### machine sizes

```sh
hopbox machine sizes
```

Lists the sizes that a machine can have, smallest first, with `ListMachineSizes` ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#listmachinesizes)). The list leaves out the retired sizes. An instance admin adds and retires sizes ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#sizeservice)).

```text
NAME     VCPUS  MEMORY  DISK
default  2      8 GiB   100 GB
```

JSON: an array of objects with `name`, `vcpus`, `memory_bytes`, and `disk_bytes`.

### url port

```sh
hopbox url port MACHINE PORT
```

Sets the port in the machine that its URL reaches, 1 to 65535, with `SetMachineURLPort`. Only the creator of the machine can. The command prints the URL:

```text
https://box1.example.com (private, port 3000)
```

JSON: the machine object.

### url public

```sh
hopbox url public MACHINE
```

Lets anyone open the URL of the machine, without an account, with `SetMachineURLVisibility`. Only the creator of the machine can. It prints the URL as `url port` does.

### url private

```sh
hopbox url private MACHINE
```

Lets only signed-in accounts with access to the machine open its URL. Only the creator of the machine can. A new machine is private.

### env list

```sh
hopbox env list
```

Lists the env vars and secrets of the org that you see, by name, with `ListVars` ([the env var API](/reference/vars-api/)). `env ls` is the same command. A secret shows `(secret)` and no value. A value with a newline shows its first line and `...`.

```text
NAME   SCOPE  SECRET  VALUE     UPDATED
TOKEN  all    yes     (secret)  2026-10-21T10:57:09Z
```

JSON: an array of objects. Each has `id`, `org_id`, `name`, `scope`, `secret`, and `value`, which is empty for a secret. Each also has `owner_account_id`, `updater_account_id`, `create_time`, and `update_time`.

### env set

```sh
hopbox env set NAME[=VALUE] [--secret] [--scope=SCOPE]
```

Sets an env var or a secret in the org of the command with `SetVar`. The machines get it at their next boot and in each new login shell. The CLI first checks the name with the rules of [the env var API](/reference/vars-api/) for the scope. A bad name fails with status 80, before the CLI reads any value.

Without `=VALUE`, the value comes from stdin, so a secret stays out of the shell history:

* If stdin is a terminal, the CLI writes `Value of NAME: `to stderr. Then it reads one line with no echo, so the value never shows on the screen. The line ends at the first CR or LF, and the CLI reads nothing after it. So in a paste, the next line stays for the next reader, such as [the prompt](#the-prompt). A Ctrl-C at this question turns the echo back on, and ends the command with status 130.
* Else it reads all of stdin, up to 64 KiB, and drops one newline at its end, as in `hopbox env set TOKEN --secret < token.txt`.

| Flag            | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--secret`      | `false`  | Seals the value. No call returns it again. A secret needs a key-encryption key on the install ([Sealing](/reference/sealing/)).                                                    |
| `--scope=SCOPE` | `shared` | `shared`: the shared machines of the org. `private`: your own private machines. `all`: every machine of the org. A personal org refuses `shared`, so use `private` or `all` there. |

```text
Set the secret TOKEN in the scope all.
```

JSON: the object of [env list](#env-list).

### env unset

```sh
hopbox env unset NAME [--scope=SCOPE]
```

Removes the value `NAME` of a scope with `DeleteVar`. `env rm` is the same command. A name without a value fails with status 4. JSON fields: `name` and `scope`.

| Flag            | Default  | Description                                            |
| --------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--scope=SCOPE` | `shared` | The scope of the value: `shared`, `private`, or `all`. |

### login

```sh
hopbox login [--url=URL]
```

Signs in the profile of the command with the device flow, as [Sign-in and tokens](#sign-in-and-tokens) describes. The command waits until a person approves the code in the console, the code ends after 10 minutes, or you press Ctrl-C.

| Flag        | Env var      | Default                | Description                                     |
| ----------- | ------------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `--url=URL` | `HOPBOX_URL` | the URL of the profile | The URL of the install. A new profile needs it. |

A URL that differs from the URL of the profile also drops the active org of the profile. That org belongs to the other install.

The command prints the code to stderr:

```text
To sign in, open this page in a browser and approve the code KWJQ-LBZV:


  https://example.com/device?code=KWJQ-LBZV


Waiting for the approval. Press Ctrl-C to stop.
```

Then the CLI prepares `~/.ssh` for the SSH front door ([SSH files](#ssh-files)). `--no-ssh-config` skips these steps:

1. It writes the host key of the install into `~/.ssh/known_hosts`, once the install has an SSH front door.
2. If the account has no SSH key, it adds the public key of `~/.ssh/hopbox_ed25519` to the account. For a missing file, it makes a new ed25519 key pair first. The key gets the name `hopbox CLI on <host name of the laptop>`. An account with a key keeps its keys as they are. `ssh-key add` adds more.

A failure of these steps does not fail the login. The CLI logs a warning, and the next command works. Then it prints the result to stdout:

```text
Signed in to https://example.com as ann@example.org. The profile default is active.
Added the SSH key ~/.ssh/hopbox_ed25519 (SHA256:rkEGrocWsFODhePtstCZFcyj1D0BUmGYu1rexwam/mo) to your account.
```

Only a login that added a key prints the second line. JSON fields: `profile`, `url`, `account`, the account object of [whoami](#whoami), and `ssh_key`. `ssh_key` is the key that the login added, as [ssh-key add](#ssh-key-add) prints it, or `null`.

| Error                                                                                             | Status   | Cause                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `the profile <name> has no install yet. Give its URL: hopbox login --url https://hop.example.org` | 80       | The profile has no URL, and the command gives none.                    |
| `the install URL is not valid: ...`                                                               | 80       | The URL breaks a rule of [URLs of an install](#urls-of-an-install).    |
| `start the sign-in at <url>: failed_precondition: ...`                                            | 1        | The install has no domain, so it has no console page for the approval. |
| `the code expired before its approval. Run hopbox login again`                                    | 1        | Nobody approved the code in 10 minutes.                                |
| `wait for the approval: ...`                                                                      | per code | A poll failed.                                                         |

### logout

```sh
hopbox logout
```

Ends the CLI sign-in of the profile with `SignOut`, and deletes its tokens from `credentials.toml`. The call goes to the install that issued the tokens: the `url` of the tokens in `credentials.toml`. The profile can name another install by now. The profile keeps its URL and its active org. If the install does not answer, the CLI still deletes the tokens. It then logs `the install did not end the CLI sign-in, so only the local tokens go. End it in the console` at level warn. A profile that is not signed in is no error.

```text
Signed out the profile default.
```

JSON fields: `profile` and `signed_out`. For a profile that was not signed in, `signed_out` is `false`.

### whoami

```sh
hopbox whoami
```

Prints the profile, the URL of the install, the account, and the org of the command.

```text
profile         default
url             https://example.com
account         01a14a7c-813f-7a14-b6bc-44a4e57ac6ff
name            -
emails          root@example.org (unverified)
instance admin  yes
org             acme (01a14a7c-be1e-74cc-9748-ff40254c5d55)
role            owner
```

The line `instance admin` shows only for an instance admin. JSON fields:

| Field                     | Type           | Description                                                         |
| ------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `profile`                 | string         | The profile of the command.                                         |
| `url`                     | string         | The URL of the install.                                             |
| `account`                 | object or null | The account. It is `null` for an org API key, which has no account. |
| `account.id`              | string         | The UUID of the account.                                            |
| `account.display_name`    | string         | The display name, or empty.                                         |
| `account.emails`          | array          | The emails: `email`, `verified`, and `verify_time`.                 |
| `account.instance_admin`  | bool           | Whether the account is an instance admin.                           |
| `account.personal_org_id` | string         | The UUID of the personal org.                                       |
| `account.version`         | number         | The version of the account.                                         |
| `account.create_time`     | string         | The time of the first sign-in.                                      |
| `org`                     | object or null | The org of the command, as [org show](#org-show) prints it.         |

The active org of the profile can stop being one of your orgs. Then `whoami` prints the rest with `org` as `null`, and logs `the active org of the profile is not one of your orgs. Pick another with hopbox org use` at level warn. Other commands in that org fail until you run `hopbox org use`.

### org list

```sh
hopbox org list
```

Lists your orgs: the personal org first, then the others, oldest first. A star marks the active org.

```text
   ID                                    NAME      ROLE   PERSONAL  SUSPENDED
   01a14a7c-813f-7a1c-946b-db123b23c342  Personal  owner  yes       no
*  01a14a7c-be1e-74cc-9748-ff40254c5d55  acme      owner  no        no
```

JSON: an array of org objects. Each has the fields of [org show](#org-show).

### org show

```sh
hopbox org show [ORG]
```

Prints one org: `ORG`, by name or UUID, else the org of the command.

```text
id         01a14a7c-be1e-74cc-9748-ff40254c5d55
name       acme
role       owner
personal   no
active     yes
suspended  no
created    2026-10-17T15:30:51Z
```

A suspended org shows `suspended yes, since <time>: <reason>`. JSON fields:

| Field            | Type           | Description                                    |
| ---------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `id`             | string         | The UUID of the org.                           |
| `name`           | string         | The name of the org.                           |
| `personal`       | bool           | Whether it is the personal org of the account. |
| `role`           | string         | Your role: `member`, `admin`, or `owner`.      |
| `suspended`      | bool           | Whether an instance admin suspended the org.   |
| `suspend_time`   | string or null | The start of the suspension.                   |
| `suspend_reason` | string         | The reason of the suspension, or empty.        |
| `version`        | number         | The version of the org.                        |
| `create_time`    | string         | The creation time of the org.                  |
| `active`         | bool           | Whether it is the active org of the profile.   |

### org create

```sh
hopbox org create NAME [--use]
```

### org join

```sh

```

Joins the org of an invitation. `LINK` is the whole link, or the token after `#token=` in it. Your account must hold the email of the invitation as a verified email.

The token of the link is a secret of its install. So the host of a whole link must be the host of the URL of the profile. A profile on a loopback address, such as `http://127.0.0.1:7080`, also takes the domain that `GetInstallInfo` returns, because its links name that domain. For another host, the command fails with status 80:

```text
the invitation is for the install at <host>, but the profile <name> signs in to <url>. Use the profile of that install with --profile
```

A bare token gets no such check.

| Flag    | Default | Description                                       |
| ------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `--use` | `false` | Also makes the org the active org of the profile. |


JSON: the org object of [org show](#org-show).

### api-key create

```sh

```

Makes an API key named `NAME` in the org of the command ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#api-keys)). Without `--json`, the secret alone goes to stdout, and a note goes to stderr. So `KEY=$(hopbox api-key create ci)` works.

| Flag             | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--kind=KIND`    | `member` | `member` acts as you in the org. `org` is a key of the org itself. Only org admins and owners make org keys.                                                                |
| `--expires=WHEN` | `90d`    | The end of the key: `30d`, `90d`, `365d`, a date such as `2027-01-31`, or an RFC 3339 time. A date means midnight UTC at its start. A custom end is at most 365 days ahead. |

The secret goes to stdout:

```text
hbx_<key>
```

The note goes to stderr:

```text
The member key 01a14a7c-beb0-7c35-a4c4-5c81288a9055 (ci) works until 2026-11-16T15:30:51Z. This is its only copy.
```

JSON fields: `key`, with the fields of [api-key list](#api-key-list), and `secret`. The install keeps no copy of the secret. A retry of the call with the same idempotency key fails with `already_exists`, so the CLI never prints a secret twice.

## Exit status

| Status | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0      | The command succeeded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 1      | The command failed for another reason, for example `invalid_argument` or `failed_precondition`.                                                                                                                                         |
| 2      | Not signed in: the profile has no CLI sign-in, the sign-in ended, or the install refused the credential (`unauthenticated`).                                                                                                            |
| 3      | The install refused the call: `permission_denied`.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 4      | Something is not there: `not_found`, an org or a member that a name does not match, or a profile that does not exist.                                                                                                                   |
| 5      | A conflict: `already_exists` or `aborted`. Also an answer other than `y` to the question of `machine delete`.                                                                                                                           |
| 6      | The install cannot serve the call now, after the retries: `unavailable`, `resource_exhausted`, or `deadline_exceeded`. Try again later. Also a machine that did not reach its state within the wait of `new` or of a lifecycle command. |
| 80     | The command line is not valid, for example an unknown command, an unknown flag, a bad profile name, or a bad URL. Also a command that deletes data without `--yes` and without a terminal for its question.                             |
| 130    | You stopped the command with Ctrl-C (SIGINT). The command then ends its work. A second Ctrl-C ends the process at once.                                                                                                                 |
| 143    | SIGTERM stopped the command.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

The prompt has statuses of its own ([Commands and signals in the prompt](#commands-and-signals-in-the-prompt)). `exec` and `connect` exit with the exit code of the command in the machine, once the command ran ([exec](#exec)). So for them, a status such as 1 or 4 can also come from the command. Use `exec --json` to tell the two apart: its object holds the exit code of the command.

# Cold move

> The cold move of a machine to another node. Its steps, and the disk listener on port 7444 of the mesh address. The stream and its digest, a resumed pull, a failed move, old copies, two releases, metrics, and logs.

A cold move takes one machine from its node to another node (step 4 of a drain). The source node stops the machine. Then the target node pulls the disk of the machine from the source node over the mesh. If the target of the machine is `running`, the target node boots it. The machine loses its memory, and keeps its disk, its name, its URL, its SSH port, and its address. The disk travels in one copy format for every moving state: a stream of the blocks that hold data, with a digest of the whole disk.

An instance admin starts a move with `MoveMachine` of the admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#movemachine)) or `hopboxd admin machine move` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-machine-move)). `CancelMove` or `hopboxd admin machine move --cancel` ends a move that runs. With `--give-back`, it also asks the target node to give back a machine that a failed move left there ([Give-back](#give-back)). The drain of a node moves each machine of the node the same way ([Drain of a node](#drain-of-a-node)).

The control side is in `internal/service/moves.go` and the leader job of `internal/control`. The node side is in `internal/node/transfer` (the disk listener and the pull), `internal/node/executor` (`move.go`), and `internal/node/machines`.

## Values

| Item                           | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Disk listener                  | Port `7444` (`transfer.Port`) of the mesh address of the node, with TLS 1.3 ([the mesh](/reference/mesh/))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Block                          | 4096 bytes (`transfer.BlockSize`). A block of zeros is a hole.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Frame                          | At most 1 MiB of data                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Idle timeout of a pull         | 30 s without a byte (`transfer.DefaultIdleTimeout`), counted only while the target waits for the source. The timer counts each wait for the next bytes, so one frame can take longer than 30 s. A save of the progress and the wait of a rate limit do not count. A source that keeps sending bytes holds a pull until the action timeout. If no frame completes, the pull reports no `pull_received`, so the pull deadline ends the move. |
| Write timeout of the listener  | 30 s for each frame (`transfer.DefaultWriteTimeout`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Save of the progress of a pull | Every 64 MiB, and at each stop of the pull                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Length of one pull             | At most 5 min, the timeout of an action of the executor (`executor.DefaultActionTimeout`). A larger disk arrives over several pulls.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Wait between two pulls         | 1 s after a pull that got bytes. After a pull without a byte, 2 s, then twice the wait each time, up to 30 s.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Pulls that fail for good       | 3 in a row (`maxPullFailures`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Stop timeout                   | 10 min (`domain.MoveStopTimeout`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Pull deadline                  | 30 min without progress (`domain.MovePullTimeout`): from the hand-off, or from the last pull that wrote bytes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Step of the leader job         | Every 2 s (`control.MoveEvery`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

## The steps of a move

| State of the move | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Current state of the machine             |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `stopping`        | `MoveMachine` checks the machine, picks the target, and records the move. The spec of the machine on its node then has the target `stopped`, so the executor stops it. The machine row keeps its own target.                                                                                                                     | `running`, then `stopped`                |
| `pulling`         | Once the machine is `stopped`, the leader hands it to the target node in one transaction. The source loses its lease. The target gets a new grant and a new row of `placements`. The machine and its address go to the target node with the current state `moving`. The target node pulls the disk from the source node.         | `moving`                                 |
| `done`            | The disk on the target is whole, and its digest matches. The executor of the target reports `stopped` with the proof of the pull, the ID of the move. If the target of the machine is `running`, the executor boots it after the control role accepts that report. The source node then removes its old copy.                    | `stopped`, then `starting` and `running` |
| `failed`          | The pull failed, the pull deadline passed, or an instance admin canceled the move. The machine stays on the source node, or goes back there, with its disk. A machine that is no longer in `moving` on the target stays there ([A step that an older control process accepted](#a-step-that-an-older-control-process-accepted)). | `stopped`                                |

The control role writes the current state `moving` itself, and also `stopped` after a failed pull. In both cases, no executor holds the lease of the machine at the time of the write ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#cold-moves)).

### Start of a move

`MoveMachine` locks the machine as a lifecycle call does, and refuses these cases with `failed_precondition`:

| Case                                                                                                                                                                                    | Message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The machine never booted, has the current state `hibernated`, `standby`, `moving`, or `deleted`, or a target other than `running` and `stopped`                                         | `a cold move needs a machine that booted, with the target running or stopped. This one is <state>, with the target <target>`                                                                                                                                                                |
| The machine moves already, or a node still holds an old copy of its files                                                                                                               | `the machine moves already, or a node still removes the files of its last move. Retry later`                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| A failed move left the machine on its target, and its source keeps a copy of its disk ([A step that an older control process accepted](#a-step-that-an-older-control-process-accepted)) | `a failed move left the machine on its node, and the node <id> keeps a copy of its disk. The node of the machine can lack a whole disk of it, so it does not move again. Give it back with hopboxd admin machine move --cancel --give-back, or delete the machine (reference/cold-move.md)` |
| The node of the machine serves no disk                                                                                                                                                  | `the node <id> of the machine serves no disk for a cold move. It needs a hopboxd that knows cold moves, and an address in the mesh`                                                                                                                                                         |
| The named target fails a filter of placement                                                                                                                                            | `the node <id> cannot take the machine: it <reason>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| A live control process runs a release of the schema version 44 to 49 ([Two releases](#two-releases))                                                                                    | `the control process <id> on <host> (hopboxd <release>) knows the migrations up to <version>, and only a hopboxd that knows migration 50 moves machines. Upgrade it first`                                                                                                                  |

A named target that is the node of the machine fails with `invalid_argument`. An unknown named target fails with `not_found`. Without a named target, placement picks one ([Placement](/reference/placement/#hard-filters)). It takes the size, the pool, and the labels of the size of the machine, and leaves out the node of the machine. A move needs no compatibility class, because it carries no memory. When no node takes the machine, the call fails with `unavailable` and the message of [Placement](/reference/placement/#when-no-node-has-room).

The start of a move writes the audit entry `machine.move` with `move`, `source`, `target`, and `old_target`.

### Hand-off to the target

The leader job runs every 2 s. For each move in `stopping`, it locks the machine row, then the move row, and does one of these things:

| Machine                                                                             | What the job does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stopped`, and its node is `ready`, `cordoned`, `draining`, or `shutting_down`      | It hands the machine to the target node. It locks the row of the target node as a placement does ([Placement](/reference/placement/#the-steps-of-a-placement)). A target that has no room any more gives way to another node that placement picks, unless the instance admin named it. |
| `stopped`, and its node is `unresponsive`                                           | It waits, because the source node must serve the disk.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `stopped`, and a live control process runs a release of the schema version 44 to 49 | It waits. 10 min after the start of the move, the move fails with `a control process runs a hopboxd that does not know the moves`.                                                                                                                                                     |
| deleted, or its target is `deleted`                                                 | The move fails with `the machine was deleted during the move`. A delete wins over the stop of a move.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| not `stopped` after 10 min, or its node is unresponsive after 10 min                | The move fails. The spec gives the machine its own target again.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

### The pull

The spec of a moving machine names the move, the source node, and the disk listener of the source ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#machinemove)). The executor of the target never boots such a machine before its disk is whole. A boot without the disk makes a new disk from the image. It pulls the disk first, whatever the target. A target `deleted` only removes what arrived.

The executor writes the move in its node-local state, as `pending_move`, before the first pull ([the node executor](/reference/executor/#node-local-state)). The machine never boots on the node until the control role accepted the proof of the pull of that move. The executor keeps that move as `acked_move`. This rule holds after a restart of `hopboxd`. It also holds for a spec that names another state or no move. A control role of the schema version 44 to 49 sends such a spec, because it does not know the moves.

The source node serves the disk once its next heartbeat brings the `DiskTransfers` of the control role ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#disk-transfers)). Until then, the source answers `403`. While its executor still holds the lease or the microVM runs, it answers `409`. The target tries again in both cases.

A pull runs in slices. One pull lasts at most 5 min, the timeout of an action of the executor. A pull that gets no byte for 30 s ends, and so does a cut link. The bytes that arrived stay in the partial copy, with the state of their digest, and the next pull resumes from the last whole frame. A restart of `hopboxd` on the target resumes too, from the last saved progress. So a large disk arrives over several pulls, and no step reads the whole copy again. After a pull that wrote bytes and did not end, the executor reports its state again with `pull_received`, the bytes of that pull. That report holds off the pull deadline. These causes count toward the 3 failures in a row that end the move:

* The source has no disk of the machine (`404`).
* The copy has another digest than the disk of the source.
* The target cannot write the copy, such as a full disk.

Any other failure, such as a cut link, a refusal, or a timeout, makes the executor try again until the pull ends. After the third failure, the executor reports `failed` from `moving`, with the error `pull the disk from node <id>: ...`, and stops acting with its lease.

### Pull deadline and cancel

If the target pulls no part of the disk for 30 min (`domain.MovePullTimeout`), a move in `pulling` fails with the error `the target node pulled no part of the disk for 30m0s`. The 30 min count from the hand-off, and again from each report with `pull_received`. So a large disk on a busy link keeps its move while it makes progress. The leader job checks the deadline at each step. A resumed pull can wait for the digest job of the source, and that wait writes no bytes. So the digest of a disk must take less than 30 min. An instance admin can also end a move that runs, with `CancelMove` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#cancelmove)) or `hopboxd admin machine move --cancel` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-machine-move)). The move then fails with the error `an instance admin canceled the move`, and the service logs `an instance admin canceled the move of a machine`.

| State of the move | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `stopping`        | Only a cancel ends it. The spec gives the machine its own target again on its node.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `pulling`         | The result of a failed pull ([End of a move](#end-of-a-move)). The machine goes back to the source node with its disk, stopped. A machine with the target `deleted` goes back with that target. A machine that is no longer in `moving` on the target stays there. |

The next heartbeat of the source node withdraws the disk from its listener, and the listener ends the streams of that disk at once. The target node then removes what it pulled.

### End of a move

`ReportMachine` reads the move of the machine in the transaction of each report of the target node while the move is `pulling`. Only a report that names the move in `pulled_move_id` proves that the target has the whole disk ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#machinereport)). Once the disk is here, the executor names the move in each report:

| Report                                                              | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Any state but `failed`, with the ID of the move in `pulled_move_id` | The move is `done`. The source node must remove its old copy. The service logs `a machine moved to another node`. A report of the same state ends the move too.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| The same state, without the proof                                   | Nothing ends. A report with `pull_received` above 0 holds off the pull deadline.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `failed`                                                            | The move is `failed`, with the error of the report. The control role ends the lease of the target. It gives the machine and its address back to the source node, with the current state and the target `stopped`. The target node must remove what it pulled. The service logs `the target node could not pull the disk, so the machine stays stopped on its source node`. |
| Any other step                                                      | The same result as `failed`, with the error `the target node left the state <state> with <new state>, without the whole disk of the move`. An executor of an older release gives such a report, because it boots a new disk from the image.                                                                                                                                |

The executor of the target boots the machine only after the control role accepted the report with the proof. If the move ended before, such as through a cancel, the control role refuses that report, because the lease of the target ended. So the machine never boots on the target.

An executor of an older release on the target can boot a new disk from the image before its report. The move fails, and the machine goes back to the source. That executor loses its lease, but its microVM of the new disk keeps running on the node until the node upgrades. After the upgrade, the node gets the removal of the files of the machine. The files stay while that microVM runs, and the node logs `the control plane asks this node to remove the files of a machine that it still acts on, so they stay for now`. An operator stops the systemd unit of that machine on the node.

The next heartbeat of the source node grants it the machine again. The machine stays stopped there with its disk. A start boots it from that disk.

The end of a move writes the audit entry `machine.move` with the actor `system` and `move`, `result`, and for a failure `error`. A failure that leaves the machine on its target adds `stayed`, the state of the machine.

### A step that an older control process accepted

A control process of the schema version 44 to 49 can take the channel of the target node during a pull. It accepts a step of the target out of `moving`, such as `failed`, and does not end the move. The move then stays `pulling`, and the machine is on the target in another state. The executor still waits for the proof, and pulls the disk again once a spec names the move.

A cancel, the pull deadline, or a step of the target without the proof then fail the move, and leave the machine where it is. The target can already run the machine with the pulled disk. So the control role never takes the machine back by itself, and no two microVMs run it. The move gets no `cleanup_server_id`, and the source keeps its copy of the disk. The service logs `a cold move failed while its machine was not in the state moving on the target node, so the machine stays there. The source node keeps its copy of the disk` at level warn, with `state` and `err`. An operator decides about that copy with a give-back ([Give-back](#give-back)) or a delete. If the target has no whole disk, the machine never boots there, and a delete removes it. The machine does not move again while the source keeps the copy, because a move from the target could make a partial or a blank disk the machine. `MoveMachine` and a drain refuse it. The source never counts as empty for a drain, and `DecommissionServer` refuses it, also after a later move of the machine from another node. Only a give-back or a delete of the machine ends the copy.

### Give-back

The owner approved the give-back on 2026-10-29 (plan question Q102). `CancelMove` with `give_back` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#cancelmove)) or `hopboxd admin machine move --cancel --give-back` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-machine-move)) asks the target node of a move to give the machine back to the source node. It applies to a machine that the move left on its target while the source keeps a copy of its disk ([A step that an older control process accepted](#a-step-that-an-older-control-process-accepted)). The call takes these cases:

| Case                                                                                                  | What the call does                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The move is `pulling`, and the machine is no longer in `moving` on the target                         | It fails the move as a cancel does, and asks for the give-back, in one transaction.                                                                         |
| No move runs, and the newest failed move left the machine on its target while the source keeps a copy | It asks for the give-back. A second call asks again.                                                                                                        |
| The move is `stopping`, or the machine is in `moving` on the target                                   | It cancels the move as `CancelMove` does. The machine stays on its source, or goes back there, so it needs no give-back.                                    |
| Any other case                                                                                        | It fails with `failed precondition: the machine has no move that runs, and no failed move left it on its node while another node keeps a copy of its disk`. |

A refusal of the give-back changes nothing, also the cancel of a move that the same call asks for. Cancel without the give-back to end such a move alone.

Only the target node knows whether a control process of an older release accepted the proof of the pull, so the target node decides. The request sets `give_back` of the move to `requested` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#machine_moves)), and gives the machine a new version of its spec. The spec of the machine on the target then names the move in `give_back_move_id` ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#machinespec)). For each new version of the spec, the executor of the target answers once, in a report of the state that the control role holds:

| Node                                                                                                                                          | Answer                                                   | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| It never proved the pull of the move, holds no disk file of the machine, and runs no microVM of it. A partial copy of a pull is no disk file. | `released_move_id`                                       | `give_back` turns `done`. The control role ends the lease of the target, and gives the machine and its address back to the source, with the current state and the target `stopped`. A machine with the target `deleted` goes back with that target. The target removes what it pulled (`cleanup_server_id` is the target). The machine never boots on the target, because its executor boots it only after a control role accepted the proof of the pull, and the lease of the target ended. |
| It proved the pull, or holds the whole disk of the move                                                                                       | `kept_move_id`                                           | `give_back` turns `kept`. The machine stays on the target, whose disk is the current one. The source removes its copy (`cleanup_server_id` is the source). The machine can move again once the source removed it, because a kept give-back ends the copy: `MoveMachine`, a drain, and `DecommissionServer` no longer count it.                                                                                                                                                               |
| A microVM of the machine runs on it                                                                                                           | none                                                     | The node logs `the control plane asks for the give-back of a machine whose microVM runs on this node, so the node keeps it` at level warn. Stop the machine, then ask again. After the stop, the other rows decide: with the proof and the disk file, the node keeps the machine. Without the proof, the node withholds its answer, because the machine booted a disk file of the node.                                                                                                      |
| It holds a disk file of the machine without the proof of the pull of the move, such as after a loss of its node-local state                   | `withheld_move_id`, with the reason `disk without proof` | The disk file can hold the newest writes, and a release would remove it. The give-back stays `requested`. The node logs `the control plane asks for the give-back of a machine whose disk is on this node without the proof of the pull of the move, so the node does not answer, and an operator decides` at level error.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| It proved the pull, but its disk file is gone                                                                                                 | `withheld_move_id`, with the reason `proof without disk` | A keep would remove the only whole copy on the source. The give-back stays `requested`. The node logs `the control plane asks for the give-back of a machine whose pull this node proved, but its disk is not here, so the node does not answer` at level error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| It cannot read the disk file of the machine                                                                                                   | `withheld_move_id`, with the reason `disk unreadable`    | The disk file can hold the newest writes. The give-back stays `requested`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

A withheld answer writes the note of its reason to `give_back_note` of the move, and the control role logs `the target node withholds its answer to the give-back of a machine` at level warn, once for each new note. `hopboxd admin machine moves` shows the note ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-machine-moves)):

| Reason             | Note                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
