| disk without proof | `the target node holds a disk file of the machine without the proof of the pull of the move, so a release could drop the newest disk, and it does not answer` |
| proof without disk | `the target node proved the pull of the move, but its disk file is gone, so a keep would remove the only whole copy on the source, and it does not answer`    |
| disk unreadable    | `the target node cannot read the disk file of the machine, so it does not answer`                                                                             |

A give-back that the node withholds has these exits today:

* Withdraw it with `CancelMove` with `withdraw_give_back`, or `hopboxd admin machine move --withdraw-give-back`. The move gets back its state from before the request: no `give_back`, no note. The spec of the target no longer names the move, and an answer that comes later changes nothing. The audit entry is `machine.cancel_move` with `give_back` `withdrawn`. The machine stays on the target, and the source keeps its copy.
* Wait. Each new version of the spec, such as a second request, gets a new answer. If the reason ends, such as a disk file that the node can read again, the node answers then.
* Delete the machine. A delete removes the disk file on the target and the copy on the source, so it loses both copies. Read both copies first, and keep the one that you need outside of hopbox. Each copy is `<data_dir>/machines/<machine id>/disk.raw` on its node, `/var/lib/hopbox/machines/<machine id>/disk.raw` with the default `data_dir` ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/#files-of-a-machine)). While the machine is stopped, copy each file with `cp --sparse=always`, so the holes of the disk stay holes.

No call takes the copy on the source while the target holds a disk file without the proof, and no call keeps the copy on the target in that case. The owner decides whether hopbox adds such a call.

The answer writes the audit entry `machine.move` with the actor `system`, `move`, and `give_back` (`done` or `kept`). It also drops the strands of the machine in each drain, because their reason named the copy. So the next step of a drain of the source or the target looks at the machine again, and moves it once no old copy waits for its cleanup. A step of a drain that wrote such a strand while the answer ran drops it at its next step, because the copy no longer exists. The removal of the node role keeps its strands until its cancel. The request writes the entry `machine.cancel_move` with `give_back` `requested`.

The call refuses with `failed_precondition` in two more cases. The heartbeats of the target node name no feature `give-back` ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#heartbeat)): `the node <id> runs hopboxd <version>, whose heartbeats name no feature give-back. Upgrade it first, or cancel without the give-back`. Or a live control process runs a release of the schema version below 59: `the control process <process> knows the migrations up to <n>, and only a hopboxd that knows migration 59 gives machines back. Upgrade it first`. Such a control role sends no give-back to a node, and accepts an answer without the give-back. If one starts after the request and takes the channel of the target, the answer can get lost. Ask again: the new version of the spec gets a new answer.

### Old copies

`cleanup_server_id` of a move names the node that still holds an old copy of the files of the machine: the source after `done`, the target after `failed`. The `DiskTransfers` of that node lists the machine in `remove`, once the machine is on another node or its row is gone. The executor of the node removes the files once it holds no valid lease of the machine and the microVM does not run: the disk, the partial copy, the node-local state, and the log. Then the next heartbeats name the machine in `removed_machines`, and the control role clears `cleanup_server_id`. A new move of the machine waits until then.

## Drain of a node

A drain takes every machine off a node, so that the node can leave the install. `DrainServer` of the admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#drainserver)) or `hopboxd admin server drain` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-server-drain)) starts it. The guide [Drain a node](/guide/drain-a-node/) shows it step by step. The drain cordons the node and sets its state to `draining` ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#server-states)). Then a leader job moves each machine of the node cold to another node. A drain never deletes a machine. Every machine keeps its disk.

The code is in `internal/service/drains.go`. The leader job calls `service.AdvanceDrains` every 5 s (`control.DrainEvery`).

| Item                          | Value                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Moves from the node at once   | At most 2 (`service.DrainMoves`). The count includes the moves that an admin started. |
| Empty checks in a row         | 3 (`service.DrainEmptyChecks`)                                                        |
| Time between two empty checks | 1 min (`service.DrainCheckEvery`)                                                     |
| Step of the leader job        | Every 5 s (`control.DrainEvery`)                                                      |

### Start

`DrainServer` locks the server, and does these things in one transaction:

1. It writes a row of `server_drains` for the node ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#server_drains)), with `cordoned_before`, the cordon flag of the node before the drain. A second call finds the row. It clears the stranded machines, restarts `started_at`, and counts the empty checks from zero. It keeps `cordoned_before`. This is a retry.
2. It sets the cordon flag. A node in `ready` or `cordoned` turns `draining`.
3. It writes the audit entry `server.drain` with the target kind `server` and the details `old_state`, `state`, and `retry` (`true` or `false`).

A node in `unresponsive` stays `unresponsive` with the cordon flag set. It turns `draining` at its next heartbeat, because a node with a row in `server_drains` comes back as `draining`, before the cordon rule. `UncordonServer` refuses a node that drains, with `failed precondition: the server <id> drains, and stays cordoned until the drain decommissions it. To keep the server, cancel the drain with hopboxd admin server cancel-drain <id>`. `CordonServer` during the drain sets `cordoned_before`, so a cancel keeps that cordon ([Cancel of a drain](#cancel-of-a-drain)). Placement takes only `ready` nodes, so a draining node takes no new machine.

`DrainServer` refuses these cases:

| Case                                                                                                                               | Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The ID is not valid                                                                                                                | `invalid_argument`                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| No server has the ID                                                                                                               | `not_found`                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| The server left the install                                                                                                        | `failed precondition: the server <id> is decommissioned`                                                                                                                                                                           |
| The server has no role `node`                                                                                                      | `failed precondition: the server <id> has no role node, so it holds no machine to move. Decommission it instead`                                                                                                                   |
| An admin session drains a server that shares its host with a live control process, or with the control process that takes the call | `permission denied: the server <id> hosts a control process, so only root on a control server or an admin API key drains it`. A drain ends in a decommission, and a control server goes only by root or by the Terraform provider. |
| A live control process runs a release of the schema version below 51 ([Two releases](#two-releases))                               | `failed precondition: the control process <process> knows the migrations up to <n>, and only a hopboxd that knows migration 51 drains servers. Upgrade it first`                                                                   |

### The machines of the node

Each run, the job reads the machines of the node in the order of their IDs. A machine that its executor has deleted does not count. For each machine, it does the first case that fits:

| Machine                                                                                                                      | What the job does                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A move of the machine runs                                                                                                   | It waits.                                                                                                                                                              |
| The target is `deleted`                                                                                                      | It waits, with the reason `the machine <name> waits for its delete`. The delete goes by itself.                                                                        |
| The current state is `pending`, and the target is `running`                                                                  | It waits until the machine boots, with the reason `the machine <name> has not booted yet, and moves once it runs`. Then it can move.                                   |
| The machine cannot move cold: it never booted with the target `stopped`, is `hibernated` or `standby`, or has another target | The machine is stranded, with the reason `a cold move needs a machine that booted, with the target running or stopped. This one is <state>, with the target <target>`. |
| The newest move of the machine from the node since the start of the drain failed                                             | The machine is stranded, with the reason `its move failed: <error of the move>`. It stays stopped with its disk on the node.                                           |
| Otherwise                                                                                                                    | A move starts, if fewer than 2 moves run from the node.                                                                                                                |

A move starts as `MoveMachine` starts it ([Start of a move](#start-of-a-move)), with a target that placement picks. The audit entry is `machine.move` with the actor `system`, the same details, and the detail `drain`, the ID of the server. A machine whose last move still waits for the cleanup of an old copy waits too, with the reason `the machine <name> waits until the node <id> (<state>) removes the old copy of its last move`. The state shows a node that cannot do the cleanup now, such as an `unresponsive` one. A start that fails with `failed_precondition` or with no capacity strands the machine. Its reason is the message of that error, such as `no capacity: no node has room for a machine of size ...`.

A machine that cannot move stays on the node with its disk: a running machine with no room keeps running, a machine whose move failed stays stopped. The stop is part of the cold move, and an early stop of a machine with no room elsewhere only adds downtime.

A machine that no node had room for gets the time of a next try, 1 min later (`service.DrainRetryEvery`, plan question Q102). At that time, the drain takes the machine as a machine that is not stranded. If a move of it starts, the machine leaves the stranded list. If no node has room again, the reason and the time of the next try change, and the drain logs `the drain tried a stranded machine again, and it still cannot move` at level debug. Any other reason ends the tries. The tries count toward the 2 moves at once, so a node that gets room takes the machines one step at a time. A machine stranded for another reason is not tried again until `DrainServer` runs again, because its reason needs a change by an operator. The removal of the node role does not try its stranded machines again. The drain also strands a machine whose disk copy a failed move left on this node ([A step that an older control process accepted](#a-step-that-an-older-control-process-accepted)). The machine is on another node. Its reason is `a failed move left the machine <state> on the node <id>, and this server keeps a copy of its disk. Give the machine back with hopboxd admin machine move --cancel --give-back, or delete it (reference/cold-move.md)`. A delete of that machine ends the reason.

The drain is stuck when no move runs, every machine left on the server is stranded, and a machine is stranded or the decommission was refused. A stuck drain waits for an operator. The operator fixes the reason, then runs `DrainServer` again. For a machine without room, room is enough: the next try moves it.

### Empty checks and the decommission

The `error` of the drain says why the drain waits now: an older control process, a node without heartbeats, the first wait of the table above, an old copy on the node, or a refused decommission. So a drain that starts no move always shows its reason. The control store keeps the time of the empty checks, so a new leader with another clock keeps the gap of 1 min.

After the moves, the job checks the node. The node counts as empty when all these things hold:

* The state is `draining` or `shutting_down`, so the node answers its heartbeats.
* No machine is on the node in the control store, except machines that their executor has deleted.
* The last heartbeat of the node lists no allocation.
* No move runs from or to the node.
* No old copy waits for the node to remove it (`cleanup_server_id`). While one waits, the reason is `the server still removes the old copy of the machine <name>`.
* The node keeps no copy of a disk after a failed move.
* No live control process runs a release of the schema version below 51.

The first empty check turns the state to `shutting_down`. It writes the audit entry `server.mark_shutting_down` with the actor `system` and the details `old_state` `draining`, `state` `shutting_down`, and `checks` `1`. The later checks change no state and write no such entry. The checks are 1 min apart, and the third one decommissions the node with all the checks of `DecommissionServer` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#decommissionserver)). The audit entry is `server.decommission` with the actor `system` and the details `old_state` `shutting_down`, `state` `decommissioned`, and `drain` `true`. The row of `server_drains` goes with the decommission.

| Event                                                                                                                     | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A check finds the node not empty                                                                                          | The state goes back to `draining`, and the empty checks restart from zero. The audit entry is `server.mark_draining` with the actor `system` and the details `old_state` `shutting_down`, `state` `draining`, and `reason`: `the node is not empty`, or why the drain waits.     |
| `DrainServer` runs again                                                                                                  | The state goes back to `draining`, and the empty checks restart from zero.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| The node sends no heartbeat for 20 s                                                                                      | The state turns `unresponsive`, and the audit entry is `server.mark_unresponsive`. The leader job marks `draining` and `shutting_down` nodes too. The error of the drain is `the server sends no heartbeat, so the drain waits for it`. The drain goes on at the next heartbeat. |
| The third check meets a refusal of the decommission, such as `... shares its host with the last live control process ...` | The error of the drain holds the message. The empty checks stay at 3, and the next check one minute later tries again.                                                                                                                                                           |
| A live control process runs a release of the schema version below 51                                                      | The error holds the refusal message of `DrainServer`. The drain starts no move and runs no check.                                                                                                                                                                                |

`DecommissionServer` still works on a `draining` or `shutting_down` node that is empty. Its refusals now name the cause: the machines, the move, or the kept copy ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#decommissionserver)). A decommission also drops the old copies that the server still had to remove. It clears `cleanup_server_id` of those moves, so that a new move of those machines does not wait.

### Cancel of a drain

`CancelDrain` of the admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#canceldrain)) or `hopboxd admin server cancel-drain` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-server-cancel-drain)) ends a drain. The owner approved it on 2026-10-29 (plan question Q102). The call does these things in one transaction:

1. It ends each move from the node that started since the first start of the drain and is still `stopping`, as `CancelMove` ends it, with the error `an instance admin canceled the drain of the server`. A move that an admin started during the drain counts too, and a move that started before the drain does not. The machine keeps its own target on the node, so a running machine boots there again.
2. It leaves each move in `pulling`. That machine stopped already, and a cancel of the pull leaves it stopped on the source ([Pull deadline and cancel](#pull-deadline-and-cancel)). The move ends `done` on the target, or fails by the rules of [End of a move](#end-of-a-move).
3. It deletes the row of `server_drains`, with its stranded machines.
4. It gives the node the cordon flag of `cordoned_before`. A `draining` or `shutting_down` node turns `cordoned` or `ready`. An `unresponsive` node keeps its state, and its next heartbeat gives it the state of its cordon. A row of a release of the schema version 57 or 58 has no `cordoned_before`, so the node stays cordoned.
5. It writes the audit entry `server.drain_cancel` with `old_state`, `state`, `cordoned`, `moved`, `canceled_moves`, and `pulling`.

Each move of a drain starts only under a key share lock of the server row and a shared lock of the row of the drain. The cancel locks the server row and then the row of the drain. `DrainServer` and `CordonServer` take the two rows in the same order. So no move of the drain starts after the cancel, and none of these calls ends in a deadlock with a move. The empty check takes the lock of the server registry before the server row, because its last check can decommission the node. If a move starts between the first read of the cancel and its lock, the cancel tries again, at most 3 times. Then it fails with `conflict: moves from the server <id> kept starting during the cancel. Retry`.

A heartbeat that brings a node back from `unresponsive` during a cancel can still read the old row of the drain, and set `draining`. So each step of the drain job first gives each `draining` or `shutting_down` node without a drain the state of its cordon. It locks the server row, and reads the drain again under the lock, so a `DrainServer` that committed meanwhile keeps its state. It writes the audit entry `server.mark_undrained` with the actor `system` and the details `old_state`, `state`, and `reason` `the server has no drain`.

The cancel refuses while a live control process runs a release of the schema version below 59. Such a leader does not know the cancel. Its step of the drain can set the cordon and the state `draining` again on a node whose drain the cancel ended.

### Logs of the drain

The control role logs with `component=service`:

| Message                                                                                  | Level | Fields                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `the drain of a server starts`                                                           | info  | `server`, `retry`                                       |
| `the drain of a server moves a machine`                                                  | info  | `server`, `machine`, `move`, `target`                   |
| `the drain of a server cannot move a machine, so the machine stays with its disk`        | warn  | `server`, `machine`, `reason`                           |
| `the drain tried a stranded machine again, and it still cannot move`                     | debug | `server`, `machine`, `reason`                           |
| `a step of the drain of a server failed. The next run tries again`                       | warn  | `server`, `err`                                         |
| `the drain found a server empty`                                                         | info  | `server`, `checks`                                      |
| `the drain decommissioned a server`                                                      | info  | `server`                                                |
| `the drain cannot decommission a server that it found empty`                             | warn  | `server`, `err`                                         |
| `an instance admin canceled the drain of a server`                                       | info  | `server`, `state`, `moved`, `canceled_moves`, `pulling` |
| `a server without a drain was in a state of a drain, so it gets the state of its cordon` | warn  | `server`, `state`                                       |

The leader logs `taking the drains on failed` at level warn with `err`, with `component=leader`.

### The subnet of a decommissioned node

The leader sweep frees the subnet of a decommissioned node, with the other sweeps ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#node_subnets)). A subnet is free once no machine address of it is held. An address is held when `held_until` is null or in the future. A moved machine keeps the address of its first node, so the subnet stays taken while such a machine lives. The next node that gets its first machine takes the first free subnet, which can be the freed one ([the node network](/reference/node-network/)). The sweep log `freed reserved machine names and ports` has the field `subnets` for the count.

## Removal of the node role

The removal of the role `node` from a running server moves its machines off as a drain does. But the server stays in the install with its other roles. An example is an edge server that keeps `edge`. `RemoveServerRoles` of the admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#removeserverroles)) or `hopboxd admin server remove-role <server> node` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-server-remove-role)) starts it. The call cordons the server, and the state turns `cordoned`, not `draining`.

The code is in `internal/service/removals.go`. The leader job calls `service.AdvanceRemovals` every 5 s, after `service.AdvanceDrains`. Each run does what a drain does with the machines of the node ([The machines of the node](#the-machines-of-the-node)): at most 2 moves at once, the same waits, and the same reasons of a stranded machine. The rows of `removal_strands` name the stranded machines, and `removal_error` says why the removal waits ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#removal_strands)). The audit entry of each move is `machine.move` with the actor `system` and the detail `removal`, the ID of the server. Each run also sets the cordon again, when a control process of an older release lifted it.

These things differ from a drain:

* No empty check and no decommission come at the end. The removal is ready once the server holds no machine, no allocation, and no move from or to it. It must also hold no old copy of a moved machine, and no copy of a disk that a failed move left. An enrollment of the server with the roles that stay then ends the removal ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#remove-roles-from-an-enrolled-server)).
* A stranded machine stays stranded until the cancel of the removal. A second `RemoveServerRoles` with the same roles returns the pending removal, and changes nothing.
* `CancelRoleRemoval` ends a removal that cannot finish. Each move from the server that started with the removal and still runs ends as `CancelMove` ends it, with the error `an instance admin canceled the removal of the node role`. A machine that moved stays on its new node ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#cancelroleremoval)).
* The server keeps its row in `node_subnets`, because each moved machine keeps the address of its first node ([the node network](/reference/node-network/)).

### Logs of the removal

The control role logs with `component=service`:

| Message                                                                                  | Level | Fields                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `the removal of roles from a server starts`                                              | info  | `server`, `roles`, `cordoned_before`         |
| `the removal of the node role moves a machine`                                           | info  | `server`, `machine`, `move`, `target`        |
| `the removal of the node role cannot move a machine, so the machine stays with its disk` | warn  | `server`, `machine`, `reason`                |
| `a step of the removal of the node role failed. The next run tries again`                | warn  | `server`, `err`                              |
| `an instance admin canceled the removal of roles from a server`                          | info  | `server`, `roles`, `moved`, `canceled_moves` |

The leader logs `taking the removals of the node role on failed` at level warn with `err`, with `component=leader`.

## What the machine keeps

| Item                | After the move                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Disk                | The same bytes, with the same holes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Memory              | Lost. A running machine boots again on the target.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Name, URL, SSH port | The same.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Address             | The same address of the subnet of its first node, and the same IPv6 address. The target node routes the `/32` and the `/128` to the tap device of the machine. The mesh peer of the target allows both ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#moved-machines), [the mesh](/reference/mesh/#allowed-ips)). |
| Route record        | Dropped at the stop, and written again with the lease of the target at the report of `running`. So no traffic goes to the source after the move.                                                                                                                                                                |
| Target state        | The same. During the stop, the spec of the source has the target `stopped`, and the machine row keeps its own target. So the usage of its org and of its node stay as they are.                                                                                                                                 |
| Lifecycle calls     | They change the machine row as usual. During the stop, the spec stays `stopped`, apart from a delete. On the target, the machine reaches the target of the row once its disk is whole.                                                                                                                          |

## The disk listener

Three things let a node run the disk listener on port `7444` of its mesh address. Its driver keeps its disks in files, and the node has an identity and a mesh address. Once the node knows its mesh address, the listener listens on it. A check every 2 s finds a new address, and the listener then listens on it.

### Access to a disk

Both sides of a pull use their server certificates of the install CA ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/)):

1. The listener asks each client for its certificate. The certificate must chain to the install CA, have the usage client auth, and name a server with the role `node`. Any other client fails the TLS handshake.
2. The target checks the certificate of the listener the same way, and checks that it names the source node of the spec. The mesh address of a node is in no certificate, so this check replaces the check of the host name.
3. The listener serves the disk of a machine only to one node, and only with one of its certificates. That node is the target in `serve` of the last `DiskTransfers` of the control role. The serial of the certificate must be in `target_serials` of that entry. The control role lists a disk there only while its move is `pulling`, with the target of that move. `target_serials` holds the serials of the certificates of the target that are not retired and not expired.

So a node can pull only the disk of a machine whose lease the control role granted to it for a move. A pull of another machine, a pull by another node, or a pull with a retired certificate gets `403`. When the next `DiskTransfers` no longer lists a disk, the listener ends each stream of that disk at once. The listener never serves the disk of a machine whose executor holds a valid lease or whose microVM runs.

### Requests

```text
GET https://<mesh address>:7444/v1/disks/<machine ID>?offset=<bytes>
```

| Status | When                                                                                                                      |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `200`  | The stream of the disk from `offset` follows.                                                                             |
| `400`  | The path names no machine, or `offset` is not a byte offset.                                                              |
| `401`  | The request has no certificate of a node.                                                                                 |
| `403`  | The control role names another node, or none, for the disk, or the certificate of the request is not in `target_serials`. |
| `404`  | The node has no disk of the machine.                                                                                      |
| `409`  | The machine still runs on the node, or its executor holds its lease.                                                      |
| `416`  | `offset` is past the end of the disk.                                                                                     |
| `500`  | The node cannot read the disk.                                                                                            |
| `503`  | The node has no identity yet.                                                                                             |

| Header of `200`       | Value                                                                  |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Content-Type`        | `application/vnd.hopbox.disk`                                          |
| `Hopbox-Disk-Size`    | The size of the disk in bytes.                                         |
| `Hopbox-Disk-Version` | The version of the disk file: `<inode>-<time of change in ns>-<size>`. |
| `Trailer`             | `Hopbox-Disk-Digest`                                                   |

| Trailer of `200`     | Value                                                                                                               |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Hopbox-Disk-Digest` | The digest of the whole disk, `sha256:<hex>`. It comes after the end frame. A stream that ends early has no digest. |

The listener sends the headers at once, before it reads the disk. So no digest delays the start of a stream.

### The stream

The body is a list of frames. Each frame is a header of 12 bytes, then its data:

| Bytes   | Value                                              |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| 0 to 7  | The offset of the data in the disk, big-endian.    |
| 8 to 11 | The length of the data, at most 1 MiB, big-endian. |

The frames come in the order of their offsets, from `offset` rounded down to a block. Each frame holds blocks that are not all zeros, so the holes of the disk and its blocks of zeros never cross the mesh. The listener skips the holes that the file system reports with `SEEK_DATA` and `SEEK_HOLE`, and reads the rest. A frame with the length 0 and the offset of the size of the disk ends the stream. A stream without it was cut.

The target writes each frame at its offset in the partial copy `<disk>.pull`, which it first makes the size of the disk. So the copy keeps the holes. The file `<disk>.pull.json` holds the progress. It has the move, the version of the disk file of the source, and the size. It also has the offset up to which the copy is on disk, and the digest state of the copy at that offset. A pull of another move, or a source whose size or version changed, starts again from zero.

### Digest

The digest of a disk is one sha256. It takes each block that holds a byte other than zero, as its offset in 8 bytes big-endian and then its bytes. Then it takes the size of the disk in 8 bytes big-endian. A hole and a block of zeros give the same digest, so both nodes agree whatever their file systems allocate.

A stream from offset 0 computes the digest of the source while it sends the frames. A stream from another offset needs the digest of the whole disk. For such a stream, the source starts a digest job apart from the request. When the job ends, the source sends the trailer. The job outlives the request, so a pull that stops early finds the digest later. The source keeps each digest for the version of its disk file while the control role lists the disk.

The target adds each frame to the digest of its copy as it writes it, and keeps the state of that digest with the progress. After the end frame, the target waits for the trailer without an idle timeout. When both digests match, it renames the copy to the disk file of the machine, and syncs the dir. Otherwise, it drops the copy.

## Two releases

If the heartbeats of a node say `disk_transfer`, the node takes part in moves ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#heartbeat)). The control role keeps the version of `hopboxd` of the last such heartbeat in `servers.disk_transfer_version` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#servers)). A node is a source or a target only while two things hold. That version is the current version of the node, and the node is in the mesh. So a node that went back to a release without moves takes no move.

A release of the schema version 44 to 49 runs beside migration 0050 ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#machine_moves)). Such a control role sends the spec of a moving machine without `move`. Its lifecycle calls do not know the moves. Two checks keep the disk of a machine safe in that case:

1. A live row of `control_processes` can have a `schema_version` below 50 (`service.MovesSchema`, [Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#control_processes)). While it does, the control role refuses `MoveMachine` and holds the hand-off of each move. A control process of a release before migration 0045 writes no row, so upgrade every control server before the first move.
2. The target node keeps the move in its node-local state. It never boots the machine until it has the whole disk of that move, whatever the spec says ([The pull](#the-pull)).

An executor of an older release on the target can boot a new disk from the image, and report `stopped` or `running`. That report has no `pulled_move_id`, so the move fails and the source keeps the disk ([End of a move](#end-of-a-move)).

The drain needs migration 0051 (`service.DrainsSchema`, [Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#server_drains)). A release of the schema version 44 to 50 runs beside it. It never reads the new tables, runs no drain job, and shows `draining` and `shutting_down` as unknown. It places nothing on such a node. It keeps the state in its heartbeats and never marks such a node unresponsive. Its uncordon can clear the cordon flag, which the next step of the drain sets again. Its hand-off of a move from a draining source waits and fails after 10 min. So while such a control process is live, `DrainServer` refuses, and the drain job starts no move, runs no check, and decommissions nothing ([Start](#start)).

The cancel of a drain needs migration 0059 (`service.DrainCancelSchema`, [Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#server_drains)). A release of the schema version 57 or 58 runs beside it. It never reads the new columns, and its drains write no `cordoned_before`, so their cancel keeps the cordon. While such a control process is live, `CancelDrain` refuses ([Cancel of a drain](#cancel-of-a-drain)).

The removal of a role needs migration 0056 (`service.RemovalsSchema`, [Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#removal_strands)). A release of the schema version 44 to 55 runs beside it. It never reads the removal, and its enrollment refuses a list that drops a role. Its uncordon can clear the cordon of a removal of `node`, which the next step of the removal sets again. So while such a control process is live, `RemoveServerRoles` refuses, and the removal job starts no move.

| Metric                             | Type    | Labels      | Description                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------- | ------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hopbox_disk_transfer_bytes_total` | counter | `direction` | The bytes of disk data of the pulls. `sent` counts what the node sent to other nodes. `received` counts what it pulled from another node. |

The pulls count in `hopbox_executor_actions_total` with the action `pull` ([the node executor](/reference/executor/#metrics)).

## Errors

| Error                                                                                | Cause                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `transfer: the source node does not serve the disk now: ...`                         | `403` or `409`. The executor tries again.                                                                  |
| `transfer: the source node has no disk of the machine: ...`                          | `404`. It counts toward the end of the move.                                                               |
| `transfer: the copy of the disk has another digest than the disk of the source: ...` | The copy is dropped. It counts toward the end of the move.                                                 |
| `transfer: cannot write the copy of the disk on this node: ...`                      | A local failure, such as a full disk. It counts toward the end of the move.                                |
| `transfer: the peer is not a node of this install: ...`                              | A certificate that does not chain to the install CA, names no node, or names another node than the source. |
| `transfer: the source sent nothing for 30s`                                          | The idle timeout of a pull.                                                                                |
| `transfer: the source sent no valid size or version of the disk`                     | The headers of the source have no size or no version. The executor tries again.                            |
| `transfer: the source sent no digest of the disk`                                    | The stream ended without the trailer. The executor tries again from the saved progress.                    |

# Console

> The console: its pages and their calls, its headers, its build, and its tests.

The console is the web app of an install. People use it in a browser to sign in, to manage their machines, and to open a shell in a machine. It is a single-page app in React and TypeScript, and `hopboxd` holds its build. This page gives its pages, its calls, its headers, its build, and its tests. The code is in `web/apps/console` and `internal/console`. [Use the console](/guide/console/) shows how to use it.

The first console holds the parts of phase 1:

* sign-in
* the list of machines, with the live state of each one
* the create, stop, start, and delete actions
* the switch that makes a URL public
* the web terminal

It also has the pages that the links of the API open, the account page, and the pages of an org. Phase 2 adds the Admin area for instance admins ([Admin area](#admin-area)).

## Where hopboxd serves it

The API listener of the control role serves the console at the domain of the install, next to the API ([the API server](/reference/api/#listener)). Each public handler of the control role holds the console, so the console also answers behind the edge. So the console calls the API from its own origin, and the browser needs no CORS rules.

The console takes every path that no API route takes:

| Request                                                                                          | Who answers                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `POST /hopbox.v1.<Service>/<Method>` and the other API calls                                     | the API                                                                                            |
| `GET /auth/github/start`, `/auth/github/callback`, `/auth/google/start`, `/auth/google/callback` | the sign-in with GitHub and Google ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/#endpoints)) |
| `GET /api/ws/exec`                                                                               | the WebSocket endpoint of exec ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/))                        |
| any other `GET` or `HEAD` request whose first path segment has no dot                            | the console                                                                                        |
| any other request, such as `GET /hopbox.v1.NoSuchService/Get` or `GET /index.html`               | the API, with `404 Not Found`, so a Connect or gRPC client reads an unknown procedure              |

The console needs HTTPS at `https://<domain>`. The session cookie has the `__Host-` prefix and the `Secure` flag, and each call with the cookie must carry the `Origin` header `https://<domain>` ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#calls-with-the-cookie)). Thus the console works only behind a front that ends TLS for the domain of the install, such as the edge. Over plain HTTP, the pages load, but no sign-in works.

A page that needs a session sends a browser without one to `/signin?return_to=<path>`, and the sign-in then returns to the page.

Every page of an org also calls `GetOrg`. Each page shows the actions that the role of the account allows. The service layer still decides each call ([the API server](/reference/api/)), and the page shows its error.

A form, or the question before a delete or another action that cannot be undone, opens in a modal dialog. The dialog keeps the focus inside it. The title of the dialog is its accessible name. The Cancel button, the Escape key, and a click on the dark backdrop close it. A click inside the dialog, or a drag that starts inside it, does not close it.

A path with no page shows “Page not found”. A path with a file extension, or under `/assets/`, that names no file of the build gets `404` with the text `the console has no file <path>`.

## Admin area

The Admin area is the part of the console for instance admins. [Use the Admin area](/guide/admin-area/) shows how to use it. The code is in `web/apps/console/src/admin`.

Only an instance admin sees the link “Admin” at the top right. While `admin_notices` of `GetAccount` is more than 0, each page that needs a session also shows a banner under the top bar, such as “2 security notices for the instance admins”. Its link “See the notices” opens `/admin/notices`. The banner reads the count with `GetAccount`, which needs no recent sign-in, so it shows also after 10 minutes. The routes under `/admin` read `instance_admin` of `GetAccount` before they load. For any other account, each of them shows “Page not found”. This only hides the pages. The server decides each call: the admin API takes a session only from an instance admin with a sign-in within the last 10 minutes ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#admin-sessions)).

| Path                           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Calls                                                                                                                                                  |
