### Drain of a server

The server page has the button “Drain” in the danger style. It opens the dialog “Drain ” ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#drain-of-a-node)). The dialog says these things:

* The drain cordons the server and moves each machine to another node, at most 2 at once.
* A running machine stops, moves, and boots again, so it loses its memory.
* Each machine keeps its disk, name, URL, SSH port, and address.
* Once the server holds nothing, the drain decommissions it.
* “Until then, Cancel drain ends the drain and keeps the server.”
* If Terraform manages the server, run terraform destroy instead, because the next refresh of Terraform drops a drained server from its state.

A server without the role `node` has no button “Drain”, because it holds no machine and the install refuses its drain. An admin session cannot drain a server that hosts a control process: the call fails with `permission_denied` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#drainserver)).

While the server drains, the page changes:

* The button reads “Drain again”. It starts the drain again, to try the stranded machines again. Its dialog says that the drain tries each stranded machine again and counts its empty checks from zero.
* The buttons “Cordon” and “Uncordon” are hidden, because a drain keeps the server cordoned.
* The button “Cancel drain” calls `CancelDrain` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#canceldrain)) after the dialog “Cancel the drain of ”. The dialog says that no new move starts, that a move whose machine still stops ends, and that a move whose disk copies already goes on to its end. It names the state that the server gets back: cordoned or ready.
* The section “Drain” shows these facts: Started, Moves, Empty checks (`n of 3`, and how long ago the last one ran), and Waits, the error of the drain.
* A notice says that the drain cannot go on by itself when the drain is stuck. It says that a machine without room moves once a node has room, and that a cancel keeps the server.
* A table lists each stranded machine with its reason. A machine whose disk copy a failed move left on this server shows “on another node” under its name.

The admin API has no stream of servers. So the list of servers and the page of a server read again every 2 s while a drain runs.

The calls of the admin API go to the services `hopbox.admin.v1.*`. Each read of the admin API writes an audit entry. So each load of a page of the Admin area adds entries to the audit log ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#where-the-admin-api-is-served)).

The Admin area keeps the rules for instance admins:

* It has no shell, no web terminal, and no file access for a machine. The machine list has no link to the page of a machine.
* It shows no secret value. No call of the admin API returns the SMTP password, an OAuth client secret, or key material. No call returns the secret of an admin key after its create. The forms of a password and a client secret are write-only: they start empty, and an empty field keeps the value that is set now. After a save, the page empties the field, and the cache of the console drops the request.
* The secret of a new admin key shows once, as `hopboxd admin admin-key create` prints it once. When the page closes, the cache of the console drops it.

Each call needs a sign-in within the last 10 minutes. After an older one, a call fails with `permission_denied` and the detail `RecentSignInRequired`. The page then shows “This step needs a sign-in within the last 10 min” and the button “Sign in again” ([Sign-in](#sign-in)).

## Look

The console has the look of the public site [hopbox.dev](https://hopbox.dev). It uses the same colors, fonts, buttons, cards, and icon:

| Part       | Value                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Background | `#0A0E0B`, with panels in `#111712`                                                                                                              |
| Text       | `#ECF2EC`, and `#A3B1A5` for secondary text                                                                                                      |
| Accent     | lime `#C4F05A`, for links, the main button, the focus ring, and the state `running`                                                              |
| Warning    | amber `#FFB443`, for a public URL, a state that changes, the `not verified` tag of an email, and the banner and the notices of an instance admin |
| Error      | `#FF7A6B`, for errors and the delete buttons                                                                                                     |
| Text font  | Bricolage Grotesque                                                                                                                              |
| Code font  | JetBrains Mono, for names, URLs, and the web terminal                                                                                            |

The console has a dark theme only, as the site has. It does not follow the light or dark setting of the system.

The look keeps the console accessible:

* Text has a contrast of at least 4.5:1 on its background (WCAG 2.2 level AA). A disabled control is the only exception.
* The control that has the keyboard focus shows a lime ring.
* Each state has a word next to its color, such as `running` or `Public URL: public`.
* A link inside a sentence has an underline, so it differs from the text by more than its color.

The web terminal takes its colors from the same values. If a program picks a text color with a contrast below 4.5:1, xterm.js makes it lighter.

## Browsers

The console works in these browsers:

| Browser         | Version       |
| --------------- | ------------- |
| Chrome and Edge | 111 or later  |
| Firefox         | 114 or later  |
| Safari          | 16.4 or later |

Vite builds the code for this set, its default build target of Baseline Widely Available browsers.

The terminal page fills the height of the window with the CSS selector `:has()`. Firefox supports it from version 121. In Firefox 114 to 120, the terminal and its bar are 360 pixels high together, and do not fill the window. Rows of a table with actions also do not light up on hover there, because that rule uses `:has()` too. The other parts of the console work the same.

On a short window, such as a phone in landscape, the terminal gets smaller, until it and its bar are 360 pixels high together. Then the page scrolls. The head and the tabs of the org keep their height.

## Sign-in

The sign-in page asks `GetInstallInfo` for the sign-in methods:

* For GitHub and Google, it shows a link to `/auth/<provider>/start?return_to=<path>`. The browser opens that link, and the API sends it on to the provider ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/#start)). The console encodes the path once with `encodeURIComponent`, and never decodes it ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/#return-path)).

* For magic links, it shows an email form, which calls `RequestMagicLink`. After the call, it says that the link went to the email. With `mail_to_files` in `GetInstallInfo`, it says instead that the install writes each email to a file on its server. An operator then reads the link with `sudo hopboxd admin mail show` ([Mail](/reference/mail/#read-the-mail)).

* Without a method, it shows the command that makes a first-admin login link: `sudo hopboxd admin login-link --email <email>`.

A magic link or a login link opens its own page, often in a new tab. So the sign-in page keeps its return path in the local storage of the browser for 15 minutes, the lifetime of a link. The page of the link then opens that path.

Some steps need a recent sign-in, at most 10 minutes old ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#recent-sign-in)). In the console, these steps are the approval of a CLI sign-in on `/device` and the link of a sign-in method on `/account`. Each call of the Admin area is such a step too. A link of GitHub or Google starts on the browser endpoint, which sends an older session to `/signin?again=1&return_to=/account` itself ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/#link-to-a-signed-in-account)). A call of such a step with an older session fails with `permission_denied` and the detail `RecentSignInRequired`. The page then links to `/signin?again=1&return_to=<path of the page>`. With `again=1`, the sign-in page shows the methods to a person who is signed in already. The new sign-in replaces the session of the browser, and the page of the step opens again.

The console checks a return path with the rules of the server. A good path has these properties:

* It is one path on the install, with at most 512 characters.
* It starts with one `/`.
* It has no backslash, no space, and no control character.
* It has no `.` or `..` segment.

The console drops any other return path, and opens `/`.

The pages of the links read the token from the fragment, then remove the fragment from the address bar and the history before the call. A browser never sends a fragment to a server, so the token never reaches a log or a `Referer` header.

The page of an invitation keeps its token in the session storage of the tab while the person signs in. A sign-in with GitHub or Google in the same tab then comes back to it. A magic link opens in another tab without the token. Go back to the first tab. When the tab gets the focus, it reads the account again and shows the accept button.

A call that fails with `unauthenticated` on a page that needs a session sends the browser to the sign-in page. “Sign out” calls `SignOut`, which ends the session and clears the cookie.

## Calls

The console calls the API with the TypeScript SDK `@hopbox/sdk` of the workspace, in its browser runtime ([TypeScript SDK](/reference/ts-sdk/)). The session cookie authenticates each call, so the client has no credential. Each call is a Connect `POST` with the binary format.

The SDK never includes the admin API. So the Admin area has its own generated code of `hopbox.admin.v1` in `web/apps/console/src/gen` ([API definitions](/reference/api-definitions/#generators-and-outputs)). It calls the admin API on the same transport of the SDK, with the same retries and idempotency keys.

The pages read and change data with TanStack Query and connect-query on the transport of the SDK. The transport already retries a call that is safe to run again, and puts an idempotency key on each create. A read call gets a retry after `unavailable`, `resource_exhausted`, or `deadline_exceeded`. A change without an idempotency key gets one only after an answer with `Hopbox-Not-Run: 1`, because `fetch` does not tell a refused connection from a lost answer ([TypeScript SDK](/reference/ts-sdk/#retries)). So TanStack Query never retries a call itself. A read stays fresh for 15 seconds. A change reads the data of its service again.

## Live machine list

Each page of an org follows the machines of the org with the stream `WatchMachines`. The stream sends each machine, then a `synced` message, then each change. The console shows the first list at the `synced` message. A machine in the state `deleted`, or a `gone_machine_id`, leaves the list.

When the stream breaks, the console keeps the old list on show. It opens the stream again after 1, 2, 5, 10, and then 30 seconds. The new first list replaces the old one at its `synced` message, so a machine that went away in the meantime leaves the list then. The head of the org shows the state of the stream: `connecting`, `live`, or `reconnecting`. An `unauthenticated` error ends the stream and opens the sign-in page.

## Web terminal

The web terminal opens the login shell of the main user of a running machine, as `hopbox connect` does. It runs exec over the WebSocket endpoint `/api/ws/exec` with these start fields ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/)):

| Field     | Value                                    |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `machine` | the name of the machine                  |
| `argv`    | empty, for the login shell               |
| `tty`     | true                                     |
| `size`    | the rows and the columns of the terminal |
| `term`    | `xterm-256color`                         |

The terminal is xterm.js. Each key goes to the shell as stdin, and each change of the size of the page sends a resize. The output of the shell goes to the terminal. When the shell ends, the terminal shows how it ended, such as `the shell ended with exit code 2`, and offers “Open a new shell”. The button “Open terminal” needs the state `running`.

The browser sends the session cookie with the WebSocket, and the server checks its `Origin` header against `https://<domain>` ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#calls-with-the-cookie)). A page of a machine URL thus cannot open a shell with the cookie of a person.

## Browser storage

The console keeps no credential in the storage of the browser. It keeps these keys:

| Key               | Storage | Value                                                   | Lifetime                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hopbox.lastOrg`  | local   | the ID of the org that the browser opened last, for `/` | until “Sign out”                                                                            |
| `hopbox.returnTo` | local   | the return path of the last sign-in page, with its time | 15 minutes, and one read                                                                    |
| `hopbox.invite`   | session | the token of an invitation that waits for a sign-in     | until the accept, “Not now”, an accept error that a retry cannot fix, or the end of the tab |

A browser without storage loses only these conveniences.

## Headers

Each response of the console has these headers:

| Header                         | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Content-Security-Policy`      | `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; manifest-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'` |
| `X-Content-Type-Options`       | `nosniff`                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `X-Frame-Options`              | `DENY`                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Referrer-Policy`              | `no-referrer`                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`   | `same-origin`                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` | `same-origin`                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Permissions-Policy`           | `camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=()`                                                                                                                                                         |

The policy allows scripts only from the console itself: no inline script, no `eval`, and no other site. The build has no inline script and no data URL. The console loads nothing from a CDN. No site can show the console in a frame.

The fonts are files of the build, so `font-src 'self'` covers them. Each file is a variable font in WOFF2, so one file gives every weight that the console uses:

| Font                 | Characters                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Size   |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| Bricolage Grotesque  | the Latin subset that hopbox.dev uses                                                                                                                                                                           | 75 KiB |
| Bricolage Grotesque  | the Latin Extended subset that hopbox.dev uses, such as `ł` and `ő`. The browser gets this file only for a page that shows such a character.                                                                    | 30 KiB |
| JetBrains Mono 2.304 | the Latin and Latin Extended-A characters, arrows, geometric shapes, dingbats such as `✓` and `❯`, box-drawing and block characters, and the Powerline symbols, for terminal programs such as `htop` and `tmux` | 45 KiB |

The policy allows inline styles. xterm.js writes style elements and style attributes while it runs, for the size of the cells and the colors of the text. Without inline styles, the terminal shows the text without its colors and its layout. An inline style cannot run code.

The cache headers depend on the file:

| File                                                              | `Cache-Control`                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `index.html`, and each page of the app                            | `no-cache`                            |
| a file under `/assets/`, whose name holds the hash of its content | `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` |
| a file that does not exist                                        | `no-store`                            |

Each file has an `ETag` from its SHA-256, and a request with a matching `If-None-Match` gets `304 Not Modified`. A file of text, script, JSON, or SVG of at least 1 KiB also has a gzip copy. A request with `Accept-Encoding: gzip` gets that copy with `Content-Encoding: gzip` and `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, unless it asks for a range.

## Build

`make console` builds the console:

1. It builds the SDK into `web/packages/sdk/dist/` with `tsc`.
2. It type-checks the console with `tsc`.
3. Vite writes the build to `internal/console/dist/`: `index.html`, and the hashed files under `assets/`, the icon and the two fonts among them. The terminal and xterm.js load in a chunk of their own, only on the terminal page. When an instance admin opens a page of the Admin area, the page loads in a chunk of its own.

`make build` runs `make console` first, so each `hopboxd` holds the console of its own commit. `tools/bundle` refuses a `hopboxd` without the console, so no release ships without it ([Release bundle](/reference/release-bundle/)). `internal/console` embeds `internal/console/dist/` with `go:embed`. Git ignores the build, apart from the empty file `.gitkeep`, which `go:embed` needs. The same lockfile gives the same files, so the build is reproducible.

A `hopboxd` built without `make console`, for example with `go build`, holds no console. Its API listener answers each path of the console with `404`. The text is `This hopboxd has no console. Build it with make console, then make build.` At its start, `hopboxd run` logs the record `this hopboxd has no console. Build it with make console, then make build` at level warn.

The console pins each package to an exact version in `web/apps/console/package.json`:

| Package                     | Version  |
| --------------------------- | -------- |
| `react`, `react-dom`        | 19.3.1   |
| `@tanstack/react-router`    | 1.170.45 |
| `@tanstack/react-query`     | 5.104.5  |
| `@connectrpc/connect-query` | 2.3.1    |
| `@xterm/xterm`              | 6.0.0    |
| `@xterm/addon-fit`          | 0.11.0   |
| `vite`                      | 8.3.4    |
| `typescript`                | 7.0.2    |
| `vitest`                    | 5.0.5    |
| `@playwright/test`          | 1.64.1   |

## Tests

| Test                                                 | What it checks                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Command                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `web/apps/console/test/*.test.ts`                    | With vitest: the rules of the return path and the browser storage, the live machine list, the labels, and the error texts. Also the clicks that close a dialog, and the colors that the web terminal takes from the tokens. For the Admin area: the form of labels and of amounts, the labels of the server states, the copy of the machine states, and the actor and the count of the notices. | `make test-console`, or `node_modules/.bin/vitest run` in `web/apps/console` |
| `internal/console`                                   | the routes, the headers, the cache, gzip, and the page of a binary without the console                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `make test`                                                                  |
| `TestConsoleTakesOnlyTheFreePaths` in `internal/api` | that the console hides no API route                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `make test`                                                                  |
| `TestConsole` in `internal/control`                  | the whole console in Chromium with Playwright, `web/apps/console/e2e`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `make test-console` only                                                     |

`TestConsole` runs a control role with a node that runs machines with the real guest agent. It serves the API with the console of the test binary at `https://hop.example.org`. An HTTP proxy of the test sits in front, and ends TLS with a certificate that the test makes. Chromium reaches the console through that proxy. The suite:

1. Checks the headers and the sign-in page without a session, and checks that both fonts load under the policy.
2. Signs in with a login link, comes back to the page that asked for the sign-in, and finds `box1` running. It checks that the scrolling row of tabs does not cut off the focus ring of a tab or the underline of the current tab.
3. Creates, stops, starts, and deletes a machine, and checks the name suggestion of a taken name.
4. Makes the URL of `box1` public, then private.
5. Runs `echo` in the web terminal, then `exit`. Before that, it checks at 844 by 390 and 1280 by 560 pixels that the tabs of the org keep their height.
6. Adds and removes an SSH key, creates an API key, and sets an env var.
7. Opens each dialog, and checks it at a desktop and a phone width. The title starts at the left edge, the text stays inside the dialog, and the buttons sit at the bottom right. The dialogs are “New machine”, “Delete box1”, “Revoke the API key”, “Remove the SSH key”, “Remove the member”, “Leave Team”, and “Delete Team”.
8. Checks that a click on the backdrop and the Escape key close a dialog, and that a click or a drag inside it does not.
9. Creates an org, and finds it in the org switcher.
10. Signs out, and checks that each page then asks for a sign-in.
11. Drops the cookies of the browser, and opens `/device?code=<code>` without a session. It signs in with a new login link, comes back to the code, and approves it.
12. Signs in, makes the session 11 minutes old, and opens `/device?code=<code>` with a second code. The approval fails and asks for a sign-in again. The suite signs in with a new login link, comes back to the code, and approves it. After the run, the Go test polls both device sign-ins and gets the CLI tokens of the account.
13. Opens a second browser with the session of `user1@example.org`, who is not an instance admin. The console shows no “Admin” link, and each page under `/admin` shows “Page not found”. A call of the admin API from that page gets `permission_denied` without the detail `RecentSignInRequired`.
14. Opens the Admin area. It cordons and uncordons the server of the test, and sets its labels. A label without `=` shows an error.
15. Creates a pool and a size in it, retires the size, deletes the pool, and finds the image `default`.
16. Sets the limits of the org `Team`, suspends it with a reason, and unsuspends it. It checks both dialogs at a desktop and a phone width. It finds `box1` in the machine list with its address, finds no link or button of a terminal or a shell, and stops `box1`.
17. Makes `user1@example.org` an instance admin, and revokes the role. Creates an admin key, which shows its secret once: after a visit to another page, the page no longer holds the secret. Then it revokes the key.
18. Finds the banner of the notices, and opens `/admin/notices` from it. The notices hold the admin key `notice1`, which the Go test registered as root, and the login-link grants of the setup. The suite clicks “Dismiss all”, and the banner goes on each page.
19. Sets the SMTP server and the GitHub app with a password and a client secret. The fields empty after the save, and the page says only that each secret is set. The page and the audit log never hold either secret.
20. Checks that each page of the Admin area fits a phone width of 360 pixels without a horizontal scroll.
21. Makes the session 11 minutes old, and clicks “Cordon”. The action fails and asks for a sign-in again, and the server stays `ready`. The suite signs in with a new login link, comes back to `/admin/servers`, and the cordon works. After the run, the Go test reads the audit log: each action of the Admin area has the actor kind `session`. The test also finds the new SMTP server of the install.
22. Turns on the file mail transport, and links the email `ann.work@example.org` on `/account`. It opens the link from the mail file, and finds the email link in the sign-in methods. Then it makes the session 11 minutes old, and checks that a second link asks for a sign-in again.
23. Drains a second server of the test, which holds no machine, from its page. The empty checks of the test come 2 s apart. The badge shows `draining` or `shutting down`, the section “Drain” shows, and the button “Uncordon” is gone. Then the badge shows `decommissioned`, and the page has no drain button and no button “Cancel drain”. The audit log has `server.drain` with the actor kind `session`, and `server.decommission` with the actor `system`. The Playwright test is “the drain button drains a server, which then leaves the install”.
24. Checks that no page error and no policy violation happened.

Steps 12, 14 to 23 each start with a new sign-in through a login link, and step 11 starts without cookies. So they need no session from the steps before them, and their order does not matter. Each sign-in goes through the page of the link and the real sign-in of the API, as for a person.

`TestConsole` gives Playwright the install in env vars, so you do not set them yourself. `HOPBOX_E2E_PROXY` is the proxy that serves the console and the API. `HOPBOX_E2E_LOGIN_LINK` is the first login link of `ann@example.org`, the account of the suite and an instance admin. A `POST` to `HOPBOX_E2E_LOGIN`, a URL on loopback, returns a new login link of that account. `HOPBOX_E2E_USER_COOKIE` is the session token of `user1@example.org`, an account with a verified email that is not an instance admin. `HOPBOX_E2E_USER_CODE` and `HOPBOX_E2E_USER_CODE_2` are the codes of the two device sign-ins. A `POST` to `HOPBOX_E2E_AGE_SESSIONS`, a URL on loopback, makes every session of `ann@example.org` 11 minutes old. A `POST` to `HOPBOX_E2E_MAIL`, a URL on loopback, turns on the file mail transport. A `GET` of it returns the link in the newest mail file. `HOPBOX_E2E_TEAM_ORG` is the ID of the org `Team`, where `bob@example.org` is a member of the account of the suite. `HOPBOX_E2E_DRAIN_SERVER` is the ID of a second server, cordoned and without machines, which the suite drains. `HOPBOX_E2E_PEER_ADDRESS` is the peer address of the first server, which the server page shows. The others are `HOPBOX_E2E_URL`, `HOPBOX_E2E_SSH_KEY`, and `HOPBOX_E2E_MACHINE`.

Without `HOPBOX_TEST_CONSOLE`, `TestConsole` skips. `make test-console` sets the variable, and `make test` does not, so `make test` needs no browser. The test needs `corepack pnpm install`, a build of the console, and the Chromium of Playwright: run `web/apps/console/node_modules/.bin/playwright install chromium` once. If one of them is missing, the test fails.

# The control channel

> The control channel of a server: its messages, heartbeats, certificate renewal, the reverse-attach data streams and their windows, the machine streams of exec, file copy, and logs, server states, and logs.

The control channel is the stream that each enrolled server keeps open to the control role. It carries the heartbeats of the server and the commands of the control role. This page covers the protocol `hopbox.cluster.v1.ControlService`, the heartbeat, the server states, the certificate renewal, the DNS zones, the mesh, the data streams, and the forwarding of data streams between control processes. The code is in `internal/control/channel` (the control side) and `internal/node` (the server side).

A server enrolls first ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/)). Both calls of the channel run on the internal listener, over TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2, with the certificate of the server ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/)).

## The server always dials

The server opens every connection. It opens `Channel` and keeps it open. When the control role needs a data stream to the server, it sends `OpenStream` on the channel, and the server opens `AttachStream` for it. This is the reverse-attach pattern. HTTP/2 carries the channel and every data stream on one connection, so hopbox needs no other multiplexer.

On a server with the control role and a role that enrolls, the control role runs in the same `hopboxd` as the `channel` unit. The `channel` unit still connects over mutual TLS.

Each server keeps one channel, whatever its roles. The node role, the DNS role, and the edge role use the same channel of their server. The DNS role gets its zones on it ([DNS zones](#dns-zones)). The edge role gets its certificate, its routes, and the access changes on it ([Edge pushes](#edge-pushes)). The mesh device of the server gets its peers on it ([Mesh pushes](#mesh-pushes)). Every server gets the URLs of the live control servers on it ([Control URLs](#control-urls)). Today, `node`, `dns`, and `edge` are the roles that enroll.

## ControlService

| Procedure                                        | Kind        | Description                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `/hopbox.cluster.v1.ControlService/Channel`      | bidi stream | The control channel.                             |
| `/hopbox.cluster.v1.ControlService/AttachStream` | bidi stream | One data stream that the control role asked for. |

Both calls need the certificate of a server. The policy lets a server act only for itself ([the API server](/reference/api/#callers-and-policy)):

| Action                         | Operation                                                                                                          | Allowed caller                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `server.channel`               | open `Channel`                                                                                                     | the server that the certificate names                            |
| `server.heartbeat`             | record a heartbeat                                                                                                 | the same server                                                  |
| `server.renew_certificate`     | sign a new certificate                                                                                             | the same server                                                  |
| `server.attach_stream`         | open `AttachStream`                                                                                                | the server of which the control role asked the stream            |
| `server.read_dns_zones`        | read the zones that the server serves, before a push of `dns_zones`                                                | the same server, with a certificate that carries the role `dns`  |
| `server.read_mesh_peers`       | read the mesh as the server sees it, before a push of `mesh_peers`                                                 | the same server                                                  |
| `server.read_control_urls`     | read the internal listeners of the live control processes on their peer addresses, before a push of `control_urls` | the same server                                                  |
| `server.read_disk_transfers`   | read the part of the server in the cold moves, before a push of `disk_transfers`                                   | the same server, with a certificate that carries the role `node` |
| `server.read_edge_certificate` | read the certificate of the install with its key, before a push of `edge_certificate`                              | the same server, with a certificate that carries the role `edge` |
| `server.read_edge_routes`      | read the routes of the machine URLs, before a push of `edge_routes`                                                | the same server, with a certificate that carries the role `edge` |

### ChannelRequest

Each message from the server holds one of these fields:

| Field                 | Type                 | When                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `heartbeat`           | `Heartbeat`          | The first message of each channel, then one every 5 seconds.                                                                        |
| `certificate_renewal` | `CertificateRenewal` | Once the certificate is 20 days old.                                                                                                |
| `stream_refused`      | `StreamRefused`      | The answer to an `OpenStream` that the server does not serve.                                                                       |
| `machine_report`      | `MachineReport`      | A step of the current state of a machine, from its executor ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#machinereport)). |

### ChannelResponse

Each message from the control role holds one of these fields:

| Field                   | Type                  | When                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `heartbeat_ack`         | `HeartbeatAck`        | The answer to each heartbeat.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `certificate_issued`    | `CertificateIssued`   | The answer to a `CertificateRenewal` that the control role grants.                                                                                                                          |
| `open_stream`           | `OpenStream`          | A request for a data stream.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `certificate_refused`   | `CertificateRefused`  | The answer to a `CertificateRenewal` that the control role does not grant now.                                                                                                              |
| `dns_zones`             | `DNSZones`            | Every zone that the DNS role of the server serves. Only a server with the DNS role gets it ([DNS zones](#dns-zones)).                                                                       |
| `reconcile_machine`     | `ReconcileMachine`    | What a machine of the server must become, with the lease of its executor ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#reconcilemachine)).                                         |
| `machine_report_result` | `MachineReportResult` | The answer to each `MachineReport` ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#machinereportresult)).                                                                            |
| `edge_certificate`      | `EdgeCertificate`     | The certificate of the install with its key. Only a server with the edge role gets it ([Edge pushes](#edge-pushes)).                                                                        |
| `edge_routes`           | `EdgeRoutes`          | Every machine that a machine URL can name, with the target of each running one. Only a server with the edge role gets it.                                                                   |
| `edge_lease_renewals`   | `EdgeLeaseRenewals`   | The rest of the lease of each target, in place of routes that stay the same. Only a server with the edge role gets it.                                                                      |
| `edge_access_changed`   | `EdgeAccessChanged`   | A change of the access to machines. Only a server with the edge role gets it.                                                                                                               |
| `edge_ssh_keys`         | `EdgeSSHKeys`         | The keys of the SSH front door. Only a server with the edge role gets it.                                                                                                                   |
| `mesh_peers`            | `MeshPeers`           | The mesh address of the server and the other servers of the mesh. Only a server whose heartbeat holds `mesh` gets it ([Mesh pushes](#mesh-pushes)).                                         |
| `disk_transfers`        | `DiskTransfers`       | The disks that the node serves to other nodes, and the machines whose old files it removes. Only a server whose heartbeat says `disk_transfer` gets it ([Disk transfers](#disk-transfers)). |
| `control_urls`          | `ControlURLs`         | The internal listeners of the live control processes on their peer addresses. Every server gets it ([Control URLs](#control-urls)).                                                         |

A message without a known field ends the channel with `invalid_argument`. A server that gets a message that it does not know logs `the control plane sent a message that this hopboxd does not know. Upgrade hopboxd` and goes on.

### Messages of two releases

An install can run release N and release N-1 at the same time ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#two-releases-on-one-store)). A rolling upgrade moves the control servers first, then the edge and DNS servers, then the nodes. So during the upgrade, a control role of N serves the channels of servers of N-1. A rollback of one server can also put a server of N on a control role of N-1. These rules keep the channel working in both cases:

* A message keeps the number and the type of each field. A new field gets a new number. `make breaking` checks this against `main` ([API definitions](/reference/api-definitions/)).
* Each release reads every message of the release before it. A field that N-1 does not send has its zero value, and N reads that value as N-1 meant it.
* A new field of a message that N-1 reads must not change what N-1 does with the other fields, because N-1 drops the new field.
* A new field of `ChannelRequest` comes from servers only in the release after the one whose control role reads it. A control role of N-1 ends each channel that sends a message without a field that it knows.
* A new field of `ChannelResponse` reaches the servers of N-1, which drop it with a warning. So the control role sends it only when the drop does no harm, or only to a server whose `hopboxd_version` of the [heartbeat](#heartbeat) knows the field.
* A new value of an enum is the same: a release that does not know it reads it as the zero value. The control role sends a new value only to a server of a release that knows it.

### Heartbeat

The heartbeat holds these values.

| Field                 | Type                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Limit                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `status`              | `ServerStatus`              | `SERVER_STATUS_OK` or `SERVER_STATUS_DEGRADED`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `SERVER_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED` is refused.                                                                                 |
| `problems`            | repeated string             | The failed checks of the server, one line each, in the form `<check>: <error>`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | at most 32, each at most 1024 bytes of UTF-8                                                                            |
| `cpu`                 | `CPUFingerprint`            | The CPU fingerprint.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | each string at most 256 bytes                                                                                           |
| `compatibility_class` | string                      | The compatibility class.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | at most 256 bytes                                                                                                       |
| `labels`              | map of string to string     | The labels of the server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | the label rules below                                                                                                   |
| `hopboxd_version`     | string                      | The version of `hopboxd`, such as `v0.1.0`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | at most 256 bytes                                                                                                       |
| `kernel_release`      | string                      | The release of the host kernel, as `uname -r` prints it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | at most 256 bytes                                                                                                       |
| `capacity`            | `Capacity`                  | What the server has for machines.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | each value fits a signed 64-bit number. `cpu_threads` fits a signed 32-bit number.                                      |
| `allocations`         | repeated `Allocation`       | The resources that the running machines of the server hold, from its executors.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | at most 4096                                                                                                            |
| `actions`             | repeated `ActionInProgress` | The actions that the executors of the server run now, such as `boot` ([the node executor](/reference/executor/#metrics)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | at most 4096, each name at most 256 bytes                                                                               |
| `sequence`            | uint64                      | Numbers the heartbeats of one channel, from 1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |                                                                                                                         |
| `executor`            | bool                        | Tells that the server runs machine executors.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |                                                                                                                         |
| `leases`              | repeated `MachineLease`     | The machine leases that the executors hold. The control role renews them ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#renewals)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | at most 4096                                                                                                            |
| `mesh`                | `MeshMember`                | The part of the server in the mesh: the public key of its WireGuard device. It is absent while the server has no device with a key ([the mesh](/reference/mesh/#which-servers-join)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | the key has 32 bytes. A part that breaks this limit ends no channel: the control role records the heartbeat without it. |
| `dns_zone_serial`     | optional uint32             | The serial of the zones that the DNS role of the server serves, also the zones on its disk after a restart ([the DNS role](/reference/dns/#zones-on-the-disk)). It is absent on a server without the DNS role, and before its first zones. The control role records it in `servers.dns_zone_serial`. A heartbeat without it clears the column.                                                                 | none                                                                                                                    |
| `inbound_machines`    | repeated string             | The IDs of the machines of the server with inbound traffic since the last heartbeat. The control role sets `last_activity_at` of each machine of the server in this list, at most once a minute for each machine ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#inbound-traffic-as-a-use)). The IDs of other servers change nothing.                                                                             | at most 4096, each a UUID                                                                                               |
| `disk_transfer`       | bool                        | Tells that the server serves and pulls the disks of the cold moves ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#two-releases)). The control role records the `hopboxd_version` of the heartbeat with it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |                                                                                                                         |
| `removed_machines`    | repeated string             | The IDs of the machines of the last `remove` of `DiskTransfers` whose old files the server removed ([Disk transfers](#disk-transfers)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | at most 4096, each a UUID                                                                                               |
| `egress_exit`         | bool                        | Tells that the server takes the egress of the machines of the other nodes. It is true on an edge server whose egress tunnel `hbe0` is ready and whose uplink works ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/#egress-edges)). The control role records the `hopboxd_version` of the heartbeat with it, in `servers.egress_exit_version`. A server of a release before the egress tunnels never sends it. |                                                                                                                         |
| `features`            | repeated string             | The features of the `hopboxd` of the server, as `hopboxd version --json` lists them, such as `remove-role` or `give-back` ([the version command](/reference/version/)). The control role records them in `servers.features`, with the `hopboxd_version` of the heartbeat in `servers.reports_version`. A server of a release before the field sends none.                                                      | at most 64, each from 1 to 64 bytes of UTF-8                                                                            |
| `addresses`           | repeated string             | The public addresses on the interfaces of the server: each global unicast address that is not private, such as its peer address and the floating addresses on its uplink. The control role records them in `servers.addresses`. The removal of a role from the server checks that the public addresses of the install name none of them.                                                                       | at most 64, each an IP address                                                                                          |
| `floating_addresses`  | repeated string             | The floating addresses of the bootstrap config of an edge server: `edge.public_ipv4`, `edge.floating_addresses`, and `edge.public_ipv6` ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). A server without the edge role sends none. The control role records them in `servers.floating_addresses`.                                                                                        | at most 64, each an IP address                                                                                          |

`CPUFingerprint`:

| Field          | Type   | Description                                                                   |

| `cpu_template` | string | The Firecracker CPU template. Always `none` in phase 1.                       |

A label key has 1 to 63 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, and `-`, and starts with a letter. A label value is UTF-8 of at most 255 bytes without control characters. A server has at most 64 labels.

A heartbeat that breaks a limit ends the channel with `invalid_argument` and a message such as `invalid argument: the heartbeat: 33 problems, more than 32`. The registry keeps the last valid heartbeat.

## The heartbeat

At the start of the channel, the server sends a heartbeat. Then it sends one every 5 seconds. The control role writes the facts to the server registry in the control store ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#servers)) and answers with `HeartbeatAck`. The admin calls `ListServers` and `GetServer` show the facts ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#serverservice)).

The control role writes at most one heartbeat of a channel every 2.5 seconds, half the interval. A heartbeat that comes sooner gets the answer of the last one, with its state, and no write. So a server that sends too fast cannot load the control store.

Sometimes the write of a heartbeat fails, for example because the control store does not answer for a moment. Then the control role logs `recording a heartbeat failed` at level warn, with the fields `server` and `err`. It sends no `HeartbeatAck`, and keeps the channel open. The next heartbeat tries again. So a short outage of the control store does not drop the channels of the whole fleet. Only a refused heartbeat ends the channel: one with a bad field (`invalid_argument`), or one of a server that the registry no longer serves (`unauthenticated`).

On a server, the `Collector` of `internal/node` gathers the facts. It reads some facts once, at the first heartbeat of the process, and others at each heartbeat:

| Fact                                           | Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | When           |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `problems` from the checks                     | the preflight check ([the preflight check](/reference/preflight/)): one line `<check>: <error>` for each failed check, of either severity                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | once           |
| `status`                                       | A failed check of severity `fail` gives `SERVER_STATUS_DEGRADED`. Else the status is `SERVER_STATUS_OK`. A warning alone, such as a kernel that is not the tested one, leaves the status `ok`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | once           |
| `kernel_release`                               | `uname`. A failure adds the problem `host: <error>`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | once           |
| `cpu`                                          | the first processor of `/proc/cpuinfo`. A failure adds the problem `cpu: <error>`, and the fingerprint then holds only the architecture and the template `none`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | once           |
| `compatibility_class`                          | the formula below, with the snapshot format version that `firecracker --snapshot-version` prints. The VMM driver of the node runs the Firecracker of `vmm.firecracker` ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)), for at most 5 seconds ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/#capabilities)). It never runs a `firecracker` of `PATH`. If it fails, the version is `unknown`, and the problem `firecracker: <error>` appears. | once           |
| `capacity`                                     | the CPU threads of the process, `/proc/meminfo`, and `statfs` of `data_dir`. A failure on Linux adds the problem `capacity: <error>`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | each heartbeat |
| `labels`                                       | `channel.labels` of the bootstrap config ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). Once `SetServerLabels` of the admin API set the labels of the server, the registry keeps those and ignores this field ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setserverlabels)).                                                                                                                                                                              | each heartbeat |
| `hopboxd_version`                              | the version of `hopboxd`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | each heartbeat |
| `allocations`, `actions`, `leases`, `executor` | the executors of the node ([the node executor](/reference/executor/)). A server with the node role runs the executors. A server without it sends empty lists and `executor` false.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | each heartbeat |
| `inbound_machines`                             | the inbound counters of the table `inet hopbox_node` ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#counters)). A server without the node role sends an empty list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | each heartbeat |
| `disk_transfer`, `removed_machines`            | the disk listener and the executors of the node ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/)). A node whose driver keeps no disk in files, and a server without the node role, send false and an empty list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | each heartbeat |
| `dns_zone_serial`                              | the serial of the zones that the DNS role serves, the value of `hopbox_dns_zone_serial` ([the DNS role](/reference/dns/#metrics)). A server without the DNS role, or without zones, leaves it out.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | each heartbeat |
| `egress_exit`                                  | the last check of the egress tunnel `hbe0` of an edge server, and the state of its uplink after the hold-down ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/#the-uplink-of-an-egress-edge)). A server without the edge role sends false.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | each heartbeat |
| `features`                                     | the features of `hopboxd`, as `hopboxd version --json` lists them                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | each heartbeat |
| `addresses`                                    | the addresses of the network interfaces of the host. A failed read sends none.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | each heartbeat |
| `floating_addresses`                           | `edge.public_ipv4`, `edge.floating_addresses`, and `edge.public_ipv6` of the bootstrap config. A server without the edge role sends none.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | each heartbeat |

A server without the node role runs no machine. So it skips the preflight checks and the snapshot version. Its `status` is always `SERVER_STATUS_OK`, its `problems` come only from the host, the CPU, and the capacity, and its `compatibility_class` is empty.

Off Linux, the CPU, memory, and disk facts are not available. The capacity then stays 0 without a problem line, and the preflight problems already say why.

### Compatibility class

The compatibility class names the servers that can restore the memory state of each other. It is `cc-` and 16 lowercase hex digits:

```text
cc-<first 8 bytes of SHA-256(arch NUL model NUL kernel_series NUL snapshot_version), in hex>
```

| Part               | Value                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `arch`             | The CPU architecture, such as `amd64`.                                                                                                                                 |
| `model`            | The CPU template. For the template `none`, it is `<vendor>/<family>/<model>/<stepping>`, such as `GenuineIntel/6/79/1`. The model name and the microcode do not count. |
| `kernel_series`    | The first two numbers of the kernel release, such as `6.18` for `6.18.57-hopbox1`.                                                                                     |
| `snapshot_version` | The output of `firecracker --snapshot-version`, such as `v12.0.0`, or `unknown`.                                                                                       |

## Silence

Both sides watch the channel:

| Side         | Rule                                                       | Then                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Control role | No message for 20 seconds, which is 4 heartbeat intervals. | It ends the channel with `deadline_exceeded`, and logs `control channel closed` with the error `the server sent nothing for 4 heartbeat intervals`. |
| Server       | No `HeartbeatAck` for 4 heartbeat intervals.               | It drops the channel with the error `the control plane answered no heartbeat for 4 intervals`, and dials again.                                     |

A new channel of a server replaces the open one of the same server. The control role ends the old channel with `aborted`, and the cause `a newer channel of the same server replaced this one` goes to its log.

When the control side ends a channel, the server gets the code and the cause: `deadline_exceeded` with `the server sent nothing for 4 heartbeat intervals`, `aborted` with `a newer channel of the same server replaced this one`, `permission_denied` with `the control plane ended the channel of this server` after `Hub.Disconnect`, `unavailable` with `the install went into maintenance mode, which ended this call. Retry later` ([Maintenance mode](#maintenance-mode)), or `invalid_argument` with `the message has no known content. Upgrade hopboxd on the control servers`. An error of the service layer, such as a refused heartbeat, keeps its code and message as in [the API server](/reference/api/#errors).

## Maintenance mode

In maintenance mode, the control role serves no control channel ([the API server](/reference/api/#maintenance-mode)):

* When maintenance mode turns on, each control process ends every open channel and every data stream with `unavailable` and the message `the install went into maintenance mode, which ended this call. Retry later`. `SetMaintenance` returns only after each channel of every live control process ended, so no heartbeat, report, or lease renewal comes after it. The other control processes report this in their rows of `control_processes` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setmaintenance)).
* A new `Channel` or `AttachStream` gets `unavailable` with the message `the install is in maintenance mode, so it takes only reads. Retry later`, and the headers `Hopbox-Not-Run: 1` and `Retry-After: 30`. The server dials again with its backoff of up to 30 s ([The agent](#the-agent)).
* The calls of `EdgeService` and `EnrollmentService` get the same refusal. So the edge role cannot sign anyone in to a machine URL or to the SSH front door.

The machines keep running on their nodes. Their leases are not renewed, so 30 s later each executor holds no valid lease and takes no action, but its microVM keeps running ([the node executor](/reference/executor/)). The edge role counts the lease of each target from its last routes, so within 30 s each machine URL answers `503 Service Unavailable` ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#routing)). The leader does not mark the silent servers `unresponsive` in maintenance mode ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#leader-jobs)). When maintenance mode turns off, the servers dial again. Their heartbeats bring new grants of the leases, with new epochs, and the routes of the edge servers come back. The leader gives the servers 20 s to dial before its first check of silent servers.

## Server states

A server is in one of these states. The drain of a node sets `draining` and `shutting_down` ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#drain-of-a-node)). Both states exist in `hopbox.admin.v1.ServerState` and in `hopbox.cluster.v1.ServerState` as `SERVER_STATE_DRAINING = 5` and `SERVER_STATE_SHUTTING_DOWN = 6`.

| State            | Meaning                                                                                           |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ready`          | The server sends heartbeats and takes new machines.                                               |
| `cordoned`       | An instance admin cordoned it. It keeps its machines but takes no new one.                        |
| `unresponsive`   | It sent no heartbeat for 20 seconds, or none since its enrollment. Its machines stay on it.       |
| `draining`       | A drain cordoned it, and moves its machines to other nodes. It takes no new machine.              |
| `shutting_down`  | A drain found it empty. After 3 empty checks in a row, the drain decommissions it.                |
| `decommissioned` | It left the install. The control role refuses its certificates, its heartbeats, and its renewals. |

The registry also keeps the flag `cordoned`, which is the choice of the instance admin. The flag stays while the server is unresponsive, so the server comes back cordoned. A server with a drain comes back `draining`, before the cordon rule.

| From                                                                | Event                                                | To                                                                            | Audit entry                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| none                                                                | `Enroll`                                             | `unresponsive`                                                                | `server.enroll` ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#enroll))                                        |
| `unresponsive`                                                      | a heartbeat, flag not set                            | `ready`                                                                       | `server.heartbeat`, actor `server`                                                                                       |
| `unresponsive`                                                      | a heartbeat, flag set                                | `cordoned`                                                                    | `server.heartbeat`, actor `server`                                                                                       |
| `ready`                                                             | `CordonServer`                                       | `cordoned`                                                                    | `server.cordon`                                                                                                          |
| `cordoned`                                                          | `UncordonServer`                                     | `ready`                                                                       | `server.uncordon`                                                                                                        |
| `unresponsive`                                                      | `CordonServer` or `UncordonServer`                   | `unresponsive`, with the flag set or cleared                                  | `server.cordon` or `server.uncordon`                                                                                     |
| `unresponsive`                                                      | a heartbeat, the server has a drain                  | `draining`                                                                    | `server.heartbeat`, actor `server`                                                                                       |
| `ready` or `cordoned`                                               | `DrainServer`                                        | `draining`                                                                    | `server.drain`                                                                                                           |
| `unresponsive`                                                      | `DrainServer`                                        | `unresponsive`, with the flag set.
