The `Manager` of a node runs one goroutine for each machine that the control role names, and for each machine of the node-local state. The goroutine does one action at a time, so a stop and a delete that come at once run one after the other. The executor reads the newest spec before each action.

The executor acts only with a valid lease. A lease is valid while all of these hold:

* The control role named the grant in a `ReconcileMachine`, or a heartbeat renewed it.
* The control role did not refuse it. A refusal is a heartbeat answer that did not renew it, or a report with the outcome stale.
* Its time did not run out. The time is the arrival of the spec plus `lease_remaining`, or the send time of the last heartbeat that renewed it plus 30 s. In both cases, the executor stops 3 s early (`LeaseMargin`).

Without a valid lease, the executor takes no action and sends no report. An action that runs at the loss of the lease ends at once. A boot that ends this way leaves no microVM. A stop that ends this way kills the microVM at once, as the end of the context of `Instance.Stop` asks the driver ([the VMM driver interface](/reference/vmm/#instance)). A microVM that runs keeps running. A new grant lets the executor act again. It then starts from the current state that the control role sends with the grant.

| Log message                                                           | Level | Fields                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ---------------------------- |
| `acting with a new lease`                                             | info  | `machine`, `epoch`           |
| `lost the machine lease, so the executor stops acting`                | warn  | `machine`, `epoch`, `reason` |
| `the machine lease expired, so the executor stops acting`             | warn  | `machine`, `epoch`           |
| `the control plane sent a machine spec without a valid lease or spec` | warn  | `err`                        |

Every log record of the executor has `component=executor`, apart from the records of the guest link server (see [The guest link](#the-guest-link)). Each record of the executor of one machine also has the field `machine`. The records of the `Manager`, such as a spec without a valid lease, have no such field. No record holds the spec, because the spec holds the secrets of the machine.

## Actions

| Target                                | What the node holds                                                                              | Action                                                                                                  | Reports                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `running`                             | no microVM, no memory file                                                                       | boot                                                                                                    | `starting`, then `running`                                                                                                |
| `running`                             | no microVM, a memory file                                                                        | wake: a boot from the memory file                                                                       | `starting`, then `running`                                                                                                |
| `running`                             | a microVM, and a reboot that a request asked for                                                 | reboot: a stop, then a boot                                                                             | `starting`, then `running`                                                                                                |
| `running`                             | a microVM without a served guest link, after a restart of `hopboxd`                              | attach the guest link with a new key                                                                    | `running`. The report goes only for another state in the control store.                                                   |
| `stopped`                             | a microVM                                                                                        | stop                                                                                                    | `stopped`                                                                                                                 |
| `stopped`                             | no microVM, and the state `pending`, `starting`, or `failed`                                     | none                                                                                                    | `stopped`. A memory file stays.                                                                                           |
| `stopped`                             | the state `hibernated`                                                                           | none                                                                                                    | none. A hibernated machine never steps to `stopped`, because that step drops its memory file.                             |
| `deleted`                             | anything                                                                                         | delete: a stop of the microVM, then the removal of the disk and the memory file                         | `deleted`                                                                                                                 |
| `hibernated`                          | a microVM, and a driver with the capability snapshot                                             | hibernate                                                                                               | `hibernated`                                                                                                              |
| `hibernated` or `standby`             | a driver without the capability                                                                  | none                                                                                                    | none. The executor logs `the executor cannot reach the target` at level warn, with `target` and `reason`.                 |
| any but `deleted`                     | a move in `pending_move` whose disk is not here yet, and a spec with `move`                      | pull: a copy of the disk from the source node of the move ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#the-pull)) | none, or `failed` after 3 pulls that fail for good                                                                        |
| `running`                             | the disk of the move in `pending_move` is here, without the proof that the control role accepted | report the proof of the pull, then boot once the control role accepted it                               | `stopped` with `pulled_move_id`, then `starting` and `running`                                                            |
| `stopped`, `hibernated`, or `standby` | the same                                                                                         | report the proof of the pull                                                                            | `stopped` with `pulled_move_id`. A machine that the control store has `stopped` already gets a report of `stopped` again. |
| `deleted`                             | the state `moving`                                                                               | delete: the removal of what arrived                                                                     | `stopped`, then `deleted`                                                                                                 |
| any but `deleted`                     | a move in `pending_move` whose disk is not here yet, and a spec without `move`                   | none                                                                                                    | none. The executor logs `the executor cannot reach the target` at level warn, with `target` and `reason`.                 |

The executor never boots a machine of a move before its disk is whole. A boot without the disk makes a new disk from the image. The move stays in `pending_move` of the node-local state until the control role accepted a report with the proof of its pull, `pulled_move_id`. The executor then writes the move in `acked_move`. Until then, the machine never boots on the node, whatever its current state. This rule holds after a restart of `hopboxd`, and on a spec of a control role that does not know the move. It also holds after such a control role accepted a step out of `moving`. If the control role ended the move before it accepted the proof, it refuses that report, and the machine never boots on the node. Once the disk is here, each report of the executor names the move in `pulled_move_id`. A pull can write bytes and end early. The executor then reports its current state again with `pull_received`, which holds off the pull deadline of the move. After a pull that failed for good, the executor reports `failed` and acts no more with its grant: the control role gives the machine back to its source node.

A boot or a wake starts only after the control role answered each report that waits in the queue. Such an answer can find the grant stale, for example the answer to the report of a crash. A boot with a stale grant can run the machine beside the executor of the live grant. So a restart after a crash waits for the answer to `failed`. If the control channel is down at the crash, the machine does not restart on the node until the channel is back. When the answer arrives, the machine restarts with the same grant. If the lease ended in the meantime, the machine waits for the next grant, and restarts with it. The wait for that grant can add up to the rest of the lease, about 30 s (`domain.MachineLeaseTTL`). A boot or a wake succeeds once the guest agent applied the configuration of the machine on an authenticated guest link ([Guest link](/reference/guest-link/#node-api)). Only then does the executor report `running`. A boot that fails reports `failed` with the error. If the microVM runs but its guest agent does not come up, the executor stops the microVM first.

When a report needs a step that the lifecycle does not allow, the executor reports through one state between. For example, a delete of a machine in `starting` reports `stopped`, then `deleted` ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#steps-between-current-states)).

Each action has a timeout of 5 min (`DefaultActionTimeout`). An action that fails without a state to report, such as a delete that the driver refuses, runs again 5 s later.

| Log message                                                                                    | Level | Fields                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `machine state changed`                                                                        | info  | `from`, `to`, `boot_generation`                                                                         |
| `a machine action failed`                                                                      | warn  | `boot_generation`, `err`                                                                                |
| `stopping the machine failed`, `deleting the machine failed`, `hibernating the machine failed` | warn  | `err`                                                                                                   |
| `the guest agent of the running machine did not come back`                                     | warn  | `err`                                                                                                   |
| `cannot read the machine from the VMM driver`                                                  | warn  | `err`. Before its first action, the executor asks the driver for the microVM. It tries again 5 s later. |
| `cannot stop a machine whose guest agent did not come up`                                      | error | `err`                                                                                                   |
| `stopping the machine for its delete failed`                                                   | warn  | `err`. The delete runs again 5 s later.                                                                 |
| `the VMM driver declares the capability snapshot but cannot snapshot`                          | error | `driver`. The hibernate runs again 5 s later.                                                           |
| `the lifecycle has no steps between two states`                                                | error | `from`, `to`. The executor sends no report.                                                             |

## The guest link

Each boot gets its own link key of 32 random bytes. The executor serves the guest link on the socket that the driver names. The driver puts the key in the metadata service of the microVM ([Guest link](/reference/guest-link/#link-key)). The configuration of the guest link comes from the spec:

| Configuration            | From                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hostname`               | `name`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `env`                    | `env`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `authorized_keys`        | `authorized_keys`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `start_command`          | `start_command`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `network`, `nameservers` | `network`. Without an address, the guest agent leaves the network as it is. A spec with an address and without resolvers gets the resolvers of the node, from `Config.Nameservers` ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#the-resolvers-of-the-machines)). |

The executor also reports the SSH host keys of the guest with `running`. After a change of the keys, it reports `running` again. The SSH front door accepts only these keys ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#connection-to-the-machine)). The guest agent leaves out an env value whose name breaks its rules, and counts it in its answer. The executor logs `the guest agent left env values out of the machine` at level warn, with `count`, and reports the count with `running` ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#machinereport)). The machine API shows it as `skipped_env_vars`. A running machine gets new env vars and new authorized keys at once: the executor pushes them to the guest agent, and logs `pushed a new configuration to the guest agent`. A share of the machine can change its env vars, for example. A new start command and a new host name apply at the next boot. A new restart policy applies at once. After a restart of `hopboxd`, the executor serves the guest link again with the current spec and a new key. It gives the new key to the metadata service first. The guest agent reads the key before each handshake, so it connects again.

| Log message                                            | Level | Fields                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cannot push the new configuration to the guest agent` | warn  | `err`. The push runs again 5 s later.                                 |
| `cannot give the machine a new link key`               | warn  | `err`. After a restart of `hopboxd`, the attach runs again 5 s later. |
| `cannot serve the guest link`                          | warn  | `err`. After a restart of `hopboxd`, the attach runs again 5 s later. |
| `the guest link stopped`                               | warn  | `err`. The server of the guest link ended with an error.              |

The server of the guest link, `internal/node/guestlink`, writes these records with `component=guestlink` and `machine`. They have no `component=executor`. Each record has one `component` key, so every JSON reader gets the same value.

| Log message                                                 | Level | Fields                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | -------------------------- |
| `guest link up`                                             | info  | `version`, `agent_version` |
| `guest link handshake failed`                               | warn  | `err`                      |
| `guest link down`                                           | warn  | `err`                      |
| `push the configuration`                                    | warn  | `generation`, `err`        |
| `the guest agent failed to apply the configuration`         | error | `generation`, `err`        |
| `ignored a guest link message that this node does not know` | debug |                            |

## Exec, file copy, and logs

The executor serves the exec and the file copy of the machine API on the guest link ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#access-calls)). `Manager.Guest(id)` returns the guest link of a machine. The handlers of the machine streams call it ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#machine-streams)). It returns the link only in these cases:

| Case                                                              | Result                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The executor has no machine with the ID.                          | `executor.ErrNoMachine`: `this node does not run the machine` |
| The executor holds no valid lease of the machine.                 | an error that wraps `ErrNoMachine`                            |
| The machine does not run, or its guest agent did not come up yet. | `executor.ErrNotRunning`: `the machine is not running`        |
| The machine runs, and its guest agent came up.                    | the guest link of the boot                                    |

The executor withdraws the link before it closes it, at each stop, crash, reboot, hibernate, and delete. A call on a link that closes ends with an error.

The guest agent sends each line of output of the start command over the guest link. The executor hands each line to `Config.Logs`, such as a `machinelog.Store`, and never waits for it ([Machine logs](/reference/machine-logs/)). The executor drops the log of a machine once the control role accepted its delete.

On a server with the node role, `hopboxd run` sets `node.Agent.Handlers` to `access.Handlers{Guests: manager, Logs: store}.Map()`, with the logs in `<data_dir>/logs`. `machines.Machines` of `internal/node/machines` builds both, and its unit runs the executors and the logs. The unit writes these records, without a component:

| Log message                                                      | Level | Fields                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `the kernel cache has the guest kernel of the release`           | info  | `kernel`, `sha256`                                                               |
| `cannot add the guest kernel of the release to the kernel cache` | warn  | `kernel`, `err`. The node still boots the machines whose kernel is in the cache. |
| `the executors stopped`                                          | error | `err`                                                                            |
| `the machine logs stopped`                                       | error | `err`                                                                            |

## Restart policy

A machine can stop by itself: a crash, a shutdown or a reboot from inside, or a boot that failed. With the target `running`, the restart policy then decides.

| Event                                         | `always`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `never`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A crash                                       | The executor reports `failed`, waits for the backoff, and boots again.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | The executor reports `failed`. The machine stays down. A start asks for a new boot ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#startmachine)).                                                                                                     |
| A shutdown from inside                        | The executor reports `stopped`, waits for the backoff, and boots again.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | The executor reports `stopped` with `stopped_by_itself`. The control role then sets the target to `stopped`. The machine stays down until a request. A later start asks for a new boot ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#startmachine)). |
| A failed boot or wake                         | The executor reports `failed`, waits for the backoff, and tries again.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | The executor reports `failed`. The machine stays down until a start.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| A node reboot                                 | The node shuts the guest down cleanly after the stop of `hopboxd`, so the executor sees nothing and reports nothing ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/#a-stop-through-systemd)). The microVM does not run after the restart of `hopboxd`, so the executor boots the machine. | The same. The target `running` asks for it.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| A `systemctl stop` of the unit of the machine | If the guest shut down in time, the same as a shutdown from inside. If systemd had to kill Firecracker, the same as a crash.                                                                                                                                                                       | The same.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| An exit of the start command                  | The executor waits for the backoff, and asks the guest agent to run the command again.                                                                                                                                                                                                             | The command stays stopped.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

The backoff starts at 1 s and doubles after each restart, up to 5 min (`domain.RestartBackoff`). A run of at least 5 min starts the count again (`DefaultStableRun`). The start command has a count of its own. A request that asks for a boot skips the backoff. Such a request is a reboot, or a start of a failed machine. A change of the target also ends the backoff.

| Log message                                                | Level | Fields                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------ |
| `the machine crashed`                                      | warn  | `err`                          |
| `the machine shut down from inside`                        | info  |                                |
| `the machine starts again after a backoff`                 | info  | `restart`, `wait`              |
| `the start command exited, and runs again after a backoff` | info  | `exit_code`, `restart`, `wait` |
| `ran the start command again`                              | info  |                                |
| `cannot run the start command again`                       | warn  | `err`                          |

## Saved state

A failure never deletes saved state. The executor follows the contract of [Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#executor-contract-after-a-failed-wake):

1. A wake that fails reports `failed`. The memory file stays.
2. A stop then steps from `failed` to `stopped`. The memory file stays.
3. A later start wakes the machine from the kept memory file.
4. Only a delete drops the memory file.

## Node-local state

The executor keeps one file per machine in its state dir, `<dir>/<machine ID>.json`, with mode `0600`. The file exists only so that a restarted `hopboxd` can attach to its microVMs again and clean up after them. The control store stays the source of truth. The file holds no secret.

| Field             | Description                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `machine_id`      | The ID of the machine.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `epoch`, `token`  | The grant that the executor acted with last. After a restart, the next heartbeat lists it. It counts as valid only after a heartbeat renews it, or after a new spec names it.           |
| `boot_generation` | The reboot generation of the last boot, so a restart never reboots a running machine again.                                                                                             |
| `pulled_move`     | The move whose disk the node pulled whole, so a restart before the report of the move pulls it no more. Absent for a machine that never moved here.                                     |
| `pending_move`    | The move whose disk the node waits for, or `unknown` for a moving machine whose spec names no move. Absent for a machine that never moved here.                                         |
| `acked_move`      | The move whose proof of the pull the control role accepted. Until it names the move of `pending_move`, the machine never boots on the node. Absent for a machine that never moved here. |

The executor writes the file at each new grant and each boot, through a temporary file, a rename, and a sync of the dir. At its start, it removes each temporary file `.tmp-*` that a crash left. It removes the file once the control role accepted the report `deleted`. A stale answer to that report ends the executor too: the driver deleted the machine already, and the control store dropped its row. A file that does not parse is logged as `cannot read the node-local state of a machine` at level error, and the other machines still load.

After a restart, the executor asks the driver for each machine of the state dir. It attaches to each microVM that runs, and logs `attached to the running microVM of the machine`. It acts only once the control role sent the spec again.

| Log message                                               | Level | Fields                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `attaching to the machines of this node`                  | info  | `machines` (a count), `driver`. The state dir names at least one machine. |
| `cannot save the node-local state of the machine`         | error | `err`                                                                     |
| `the control plane has the machine deleted already`       | info  | `reason`. The answer to the report `deleted` was stale.                   |
| `cannot remove the node-local state of a deleted machine` | error | `err`                                                                     |
| `cannot remove the log of a deleted machine`              | error | `err`                                                                     |
| `the executor of the deleted machine ends`                | info  |                                                                           |

## Metrics

| Metric                                    | Type      | Labels             | Description                               |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `hopbox_executor_actions_total`           | counter   | `action`, `result` | The actions of the executors of the node. |
| `hopbox_executor_action_duration_seconds` | histogram | `action`           | The duration of the actions.              |

| Label    | Values                                                                                                       |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `action` | `boot`, `wake`, `reboot`, `stop`, `delete`, `hibernate`, `link`, `report`, `config`, `start_command`, `pull` |
| `result` | `ok`, `failed`, or `canceled` for an action that ended with the loss of its lease                            |

The histogram has the buckets 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 30, 60, 120, and 300 seconds.

## Go API

`executor.New(Config)` returns a `Manager`. `Manager.Run(ctx)` reads the node-local state and runs the executors until `ctx` ends. The microVMs keep running after it returns.

| Field of `Config` | Default                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Driver`          | required                | The VMM driver.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Dir`             | required                | The state dir.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `NodeVersion`     | empty                   | The version of `hopboxd`, for the guest link.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `ActionTimeout`   | 5 min                   | The timeout of each action.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `StableRun`       | 5 min                   | The run time that starts the count of restarts again.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `Backoff`         | `domain.RestartBackoff` | The wait before restart number n.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Logger`          | `slog.Default()`        | The logger.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Metrics`         | none                    | The metrics of `executor.NewMetrics(registerer)`.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Logs`            | none                    | The logs of the start commands, an `executor.LogSink`: `Append(id, entry)` takes a line and must not block, and `Remove(id)` drops the log of a deleted machine. Nil drops the lines.                                                               |
| `Nameservers`     | none                    | A func that returns the resolvers of the machines of the node, such as `Nameservers` of a `netcfg.Network`. Nil gives a machine no resolver.                                                                                                        |
| `IPv6`            | none                    | A func that reports whether the node gives the machines IPv6, such as `IPv6` of a `netcfg.Network`. Then the guest of a machine with an address gets `address6` and `gateway6` ([Guest link](/reference/guest-link/)). Nil gives a machine no IPv6. |
| `Puller`          | none                    | Pulls the disk of a machine that moves to the node, such as a `transfer.Client` ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/)). Nil, or a driver that is no `vmm.Mover`, pulls none, and a moving machine waits.                                              |

The `Manager` is the `Machines` of the agent of the node, `node.Agent.Machines`. The agent calls these methods:

| Method                                   | When                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Reconcile(ReconcileMachine)`            | For each `ReconcileMachine` of the control role.           |
| `Leases()`, `Allocations()`, `Actions()` | For each heartbeat.                                        |
| `LeasesRenewed(sentAt, sent, renewed)`   | For each `HeartbeatAck`, with the leases of its heartbeat. |
| `ReportResult(MachineReportResult)`      | For each result of a report.                               |
| `Connected(send)`, `Disconnected()`      | At the start and the end of each channel.                  |

For the cold moves, the node role calls these methods ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#old-copies)):

| Method        | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Busy(id)`    | Reports whether the executor of the machine holds a valid lease, runs an action, or runs the microVM. A microVM that the executor attached to after a restart, before a spec arrived, counts too. The disk listener serves no disk of such a machine. |
| `Forget(ids)` | Removes the files of the machines that left the node, once their executor holds no valid lease and their microVM does not run. A machine that a later call names no more keeps its files.                                                             |
| `Removed()`   | Returns the machines whose files `Forget` removed, for the heartbeats.                                                                                                                                                                                |

# The executor protocol

> The executor protocol on the control channel: the machine leases and their renewals, ReconcileMachine, the current-state reports, and their results.

The executor protocol is the part of the control channel that runs the machines of a node ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/)). Each machine has one executor on its node. The executor is the only code that changes the microVM of the machine. A request only sets the target state in the control store. The control role then tells the executor what the machine must become, and the executor reports each step of the current state back.

The protocol has three parts:

1. The machine lease. The executor acts only with a live grant of the lease of its machine. The heartbeats of the node renew the leases.
2. `ReconcileMachine`. The control role sends the spec of a machine and the lease to act with.
3. `MachineReport`. The executor reports each step of the current state. The control role refuses a report of a grant that is not live.

The messages are in `proto/hopbox/cluster/v1/machine.proto`. The control side is in `internal/control/channel` (`executor.go`) and `internal/service` (`executor.go`). The node side is in `internal/node` (`agent.go`) and `internal/node/executor` ([the node executor](/reference/executor/)).

## The machine lease

Each machine has the lease `machine/<machine ID>` in the table `leases` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#leases)). The holder is the server ID of the node of the machine. One grant of the lease is one execution of the machine on its node. The epoch of the grant is the execution ID, and the epoch and the random token together are its fencing token. Every message of this protocol and every route record carries both.

| Value  | Default                                             | Description                                                                                                                      |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TTL    | 30 s (`domain.MachineLeaseTTL`, `lease.MachineTTL`) | The life of a grant after its grant or its last renewal.                                                                         |
| Margin | 3 s (`executor.LeaseMargin`)                        | The executor stops acting this long before the lease expires, so the clocks of the node and of the control store need not agree. |

### Grants

| When                                                         | Who                                                                    | What it writes                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CreateMachine` places a machine                             | the machine API ([Placement](/reference/placement/#the-machine-lease)) | the lease and the first row of `placements`                           |
| A heartbeat finds a machine of its node without a live lease | `RecordHeartbeat`                                                      | a new grant with a new epoch and token, and a new row of `placements` |

Three rules decide whether a heartbeat grants a lease again. All of them must hold:

* The heartbeat has `executor` set, so the node runs executors. A node without executors gets no new grant, so no grant stays alive for a node that cannot act.
* The machine is on the node, and its current state is not `deleted`.
* The lease of the machine expired, or has no row. A live grant that the node does not list waits for its expiry. So two executions never act at once.
* The machine is not held with the target `running` ([A machine whose env does not resolve](#a-machine-whose-env-does-not-resolve)). A held machine with another target gets its grant, so its stop or its delete goes on.

The same transaction moves the route record of the machine to the new grant ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#route_records)). After the commit, the control role sends `ReconcileMachine` with the new grant. The service logs `granted a machine lease again` at level info, with `machine` and `server`.

### Renewals

Each heartbeat lists in `leases` the grants that the executors of the node hold. `RecordHeartbeat` renews them in the same transaction as the facts of the heartbeat, with one statement (`lease.RenewAll`). For each grant, the machine must be on the node, and the grant must be its current one, with the same epoch and token. Then the grant is renewed. A renewal moves the expiry to 30 s after the time of the write. It never changes the epoch or the token.

The transaction takes its locks in this order ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#leases)):

1. The rows of the machines of the server, in the order of their IDs, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`.
2. The lease rows to renew, in the order of their names, `FOR UPDATE`.
3. The row of the server, `FOR UPDATE`.

`sequence` of `HeartbeatAck` names the heartbeat that the control role recorded last on the channel. `renewed` holds the grants of that heartbeat that the control role renewed. The node matches the answer to the heartbeat with the same `sequence`:

| Lease of that heartbeat | What the executor does                                                                       |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| in `renewed`            | It counts the lease as live until the send time of the heartbeat plus 30 s, less the margin. |
| not in `renewed`        | The lease is stale. The executor stops acting with it.                                       |

The control role records at most one heartbeat of a channel every 2.5 s ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#the-heartbeat)). A heartbeat that comes sooner gets the answer of the last recorded one, with its `sequence` and its `renewed`. The node takes each answer once, so a repeated answer changes nothing. A heartbeat that the control role fails to record gets no answer, and its leases are not renewed.

### Heartbeat fields

These fields of `Heartbeat` and `HeartbeatAck` carry the protocol. [The control channel](/reference/control-channel/#heartbeat) lists the others.

| Message        | Field              | Type                    | Description                                                                                                                                     | Limit        |
| -------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| `Heartbeat`    | `sequence`         | uint64                  | Numbers the heartbeats of one channel, from 1.                                                                                                  |              |
| `Heartbeat`    | `executor`         | bool                    | Tells that the server runs machine executors.                                                                                                   |              |
| `Heartbeat`    | `leases`           | repeated `MachineLease` | The grants that the executors hold.                                                                                                             | at most 4096 |
| `Heartbeat`    | `inbound_machines` | repeated string         | The machines of the node with inbound traffic since the last heartbeat ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#inbound-traffic-as-a-use)). | at most 4096 |
| `HeartbeatAck` | `sequence`         | uint64                  | The heartbeat that the control role recorded last.                                                                                              |              |
| `HeartbeatAck` | `renewed`          | repeated `MachineLease` | The grants of that heartbeat that the control role renewed.                                                                                     |              |

### MachineLease

| Field        | Type   | Description                                    |
| ------------ | ------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `machine_id` | string | The ID of the machine, a UUID.                 |
| `epoch`      | int64  | The number of the grant, and the execution ID. |
| `token`      | string | The random token of the grant, a UUID.         |

A lease whose `machine_id` or `token` is not a UUID ends the channel with `invalid_argument`.

## ReconcileMachine

`ReconcileMachine` (field 5 of `ChannelResponse`) tells the executor of a machine what the machine must become. The executor acts on the newest one. The control process that holds the channel of the node sends it in these cases:

| Case                                                                                                                                       | Machines                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| The first recorded heartbeat of a channel with `executor` set                                                                              | every machine of the server    |
| A change event `machine.created` or `machine.updated`, from any control process ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#change-events)) | the machine of the event       |
| A heartbeat that granted leases again                                                                                                      | the machines of the new grants |

Three rules decide which machines get a spec. The machine runs on the server. Its current state is not `deleted`. The server holds its lease live. A machine whose lease expired gets its spec after the heartbeat that grants its lease again. A machine whose current state is `deleted` gets no spec, because its executor is done.

The dispatcher of each control process (`Hub.Dispatch`) follows the change events of every machine. It reads the node of each machine, and sends the specs on the channels of this process. A read that fails is logged as `sending machine specs failed` at level warn, with `machines`, `err`, and `retry_in`. It runs again 1 s later, then after twice the wait each time, up to 1 min (`DispatchRetry`, `MaxDispatchRetry`). The dispatcher never waits for a slow node. If the send queue of a channel is full, the dispatcher skips the node and logs `the channel of a node is busy, so its next heartbeat gets every machine spec` at level info, with `server`. The next heartbeat of the node then sends every spec of the node. In the same way, a failed read of the specs after a heartbeat keeps the channel open: the service logs `sending machine specs failed`, and the next heartbeat tries again. The reports of the executors publish `machine.state_changed`, which changes no spec, so that kind sends nothing.

| Field                     | Type           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lease`                   | `MachineLease` | The grant that the executor acts with.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `lease_remaining`         | Duration       | The rest of the life of the grant at the send of the message. The control role counts it from the time before its read of the lease. The executor counts it from the arrival of the message, less the margin. The executor also ends the lease at most 30 s after its last heartbeat, less the margin. So a spec that waited in a slow channel cannot stretch it. |
| `spec`                    | `MachineSpec`  | What the machine must become.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `current_state`           | `MachineState` | The current state in the control store: the last report that the control role accepted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `current_boot_generation` | uint64         | The boot generation of that report.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `version`                 | int64          | The version of the machine row at the read. Two messages can arrive out of order, so the executor keeps the spec with the highest version of its grant.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

### MachineSpec

The spec holds the env vars and the secrets of the machine. No part of hopbox logs it, and the node never writes it to disk.

| Field               | Type                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `name`              | string                   | The name of the machine, and its host name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `target_state`      | `MachineState`           | The target state ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#machine-states)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `reboot_generation` | uint64                   | Grows with each reboot that a request asks for, and with each start of a failed machine. The executor boots the machine again until it booted this generation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `vcpus`             | uint32                   | The vCPUs of the size of the machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `memory_bytes`      | uint64                   | The RAM of the size, in bytes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `disk_bytes`        | uint64                   | The disk of the size, in bytes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `image`             | `MachineImage`           | The image that the disk starts from.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `env`               | repeated `MachineEnvVar` | The env vars and the open secrets of the machine, from `Service.ResolveEnv` ([the env var API](/reference/vars-api/#env-of-a-machine)). A machine without an org, or a private machine whose creator is gone, gets none.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `start_command`     | string                   | The start command. Empty means none ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#start-command)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `restart_policy`    | `RestartPolicy`          | `RESTART_POLICY_ALWAYS` or `RESTART_POLICY_NEVER`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `network`           | `MachineNetwork`         | The address setup of the machine ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#addresses)). Not set for a machine without an address, which then boots without network.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `authorized_keys`   | repeated string          | The public keys that sshd in the machine accepts for every Linux user: the client key of the SSH front door ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#keys)). Empty while the install has no keys of the front door, which needs a key-encryption key. The control role then logs `the machine specs go out without the key of the SSH front door` at level warn, with `component=service` and `err`. |
| `env_unresolved`    | bool                     | The env of the machine did not resolve. The spec then holds no env, and the executor pushes nothing to the guest with it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `move`              | `MachineMove`            | Set while the machine moves to this node: where the node pulls its disk ([Cold moves](#cold-moves)). Not set for any other machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `give_back_move_id` | string                   | Set while an instance admin asks this node to give the machine back to the source node of a failed move ([Give-back](#give-back)). Empty otherwise.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

### A machine whose env does not resolve

The env of a machine can fail to resolve for three causes. The keyring has no key-encryption key, the keyring does not open, or a secret does not open. A retry cannot help until something changes. So the control role does this:

* A machine with the target `running` gets no spec. It does not boot without its env.
* A machine with another target gets a spec with `env_unresolved` and no env. So its stop or its delete goes on.
* The other machines of the node get their specs.
* A machine with the target `running` that got no spec is held. The hub logs `the env of machines does not resolve, so they get no spec until it does` at level warn, with `server`, `machines`, and `err`. A held machine keeps the spec that its executor has, with the old env.
* The hub tries each held machine again at the recorded heartbeats of its node, at most once each 1 min. It also tries 1 min after the hold, then after twice the wait each time, up to 5 min (`HeldRetry`, `MaxHeldRetry`). Nothing else tells the control role that a key-encryption key came back or that a secret opens again.
* A try ends the hold once the env resolves, or once the target is not `running` any more. The hub then logs `held machines need their hold no more` at level info, with `server` and `machines`, and sends the spec. A spec with another target, such as the spec of a stop, ends the hold too.
* A heartbeat lists the held machines of its node in `Hold`. A held machine with the target `running` gets no new grant of its expired lease. So a grant that no spec carries never makes a row of `placements`. After the hold, the next heartbeat grants the lease again.
* Any other failure of the env is not a hold, for example a failed read of the control store. Then the whole read of the specs fails. The hub tries again as after any failed read ([ReconcileMachine](#reconcilemachine)). The dispatcher tries after 1 s, then after longer waits. A channel tries at its next heartbeat.
* The hub forgets the held machines of a node in two cases. The channel of the node to this process ends, or a timed try finds no channel. The next channel sends every spec again.

A held machine keeps its old env. The old env of a private machine holds the private values of its creator. So a share fails closed: `ShareMachine` resolves the env of the machine as a shared machine in its transaction. If that env does not resolve, the share fails with `failed_precondition`, and the machine stays private ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#sharemachine)). This check covers the moment of the share only. If the key goes away after the commit of the share, and before the hub resolves the new spec, the hub holds the machine with its old env, as above. `UnshareMachine` does not check the env. If the env of the machine as a private machine does not resolve, the hub holds the machine, and the machine keeps its old env. That env holds only the shared values and the all values of its org, which every member already uses in the shared machines.

The spec carries no link key of the guest link. The node makes a new link key for each boot of the machine, and for each attach after a restart of `hopboxd` ([Guest link](/reference/guest-link/#link-key)).

| `MachineImage` field | Type   | Description                                                                                  |
| -------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `digest`             | string | The digest of the artifact, `sha256:<hex>` ([Artifact format](/reference/artifact-format/)). |
| `url`                | string | Where the node downloads the image. Empty means that the node has it in its image cache.     |
| `kernel_sha256`      | string | The SHA-256, in hex, of the guest kernel.                                                    |
| `disk_sha256`        | string | The SHA-256, in hex, of the disk file.                                                       |
| `disk_size`          | uint64 | The size of the disk file, in bytes.                                                         |

| `MachineEnvVar` field | Type   | Description              |
| --------------------- | ------ | ------------------------ |
| `name`                | string | The name of the env var. |
| `value`               | string | The value.               |

| `MachineNetwork` field | Type            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `address`              | string          | The address of the machine with its prefix length, such as `10.240.0.5/32`. The node routes it to the tap device of the machine.                                                                                  |
| `gateway`              | string          | The on-link gateway of the default route: `169.254.0.1`.                                                                                                                                                          |
| `mtu`                  | uint32          | The MTU of the interface: `1420`.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `nameservers`          | repeated string | The DNS resolvers of the machine. The control role leaves it empty, and the executor then gives the guest the resolvers of its node ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#the-resolvers-of-the-machines)). |

Each value of `MachineState` is a state of [Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#machine-states) with the prefix `MACHINE_STATE_`, such as `MACHINE_STATE_RUNNING`. `MACHINE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED` is no state.

## Cold moves

A cold move takes a stopped machine to another node with its disk ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/)). The protocol carries it in these steps:

1. The move waits for the stop of the machine. Meanwhile, the spec of the machine on its node has the target `stopped`, apart from a target `deleted`. The executor stops the machine and reports `stopped`, as for any stop.
2. The leader hands the machine to the target node. In one transaction, it ends the grant of the source, grants the lease to the target, and writes a row of `placements`. It sets the current state `moving` and moves the machine and its address to the target node. No executor holds the lease at that time, so the control role writes this state itself.
3. The next heartbeat of the source finds its grant stale, and its executor stops acting. The spec goes to the target node with the current state `moving` and the field `move`.
4. The executor of the target writes the move in its node-local state, and pulls the disk with the action `pull` ([the node executor](/reference/executor/#actions)). It never boots the machine before the control role accepted the proof of the pull of that move. With the target `deleted`, it deletes what arrived instead. A pull that wrote bytes and ended early gets a report of the same state with `pull_received`, which holds off the pull deadline.
5. Once the disk is whole, the executor leaves `moving` through `stopped`, with the ID of the move in `pulled_move_id`. That report ends the move. If the target of the machine is `running`, the executor boots the machine after the control role accepted the report.
6. After 3 pulls in a row that fail for good, the executor reports `failed` from `moving`, and acts no more with its grant. The report gives the machine back to the source node. The control role ends the grant of the target in the transaction of the report, and writes the current state `stopped`.

The control role reads the move in the transaction of each report of the target node while the move pulls:

| Report of the target                                                | What the control role does in the transaction of the report                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Any state but `failed`, with the ID of the move in `pulled_move_id` | The move is done. The source node must remove its old copy. A report of the same state ends the move too.                                                                                                                 |
| The same state, without the proof                                   | Nothing ends. `pull_received` above 0 holds off the pull deadline.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `failed` from `moving`                                              | The move failed. The control role ends the lease of the target. It gives the machine and its address back to the source node with the current state and the target `stopped`. The target node must remove what it pulled. |
| Any other step                                                      | The same as `failed`, with the error `the target node left the state <state> with <new state>, without the whole disk of the move`.                                                                                       |

The control role gives the machine back only while it is in `moving` on the target. A control process of a release without moves can accept a step of the target out of `moving` during a pull. After that, a failed move leaves the machine on the target ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#a-step-that-an-older-control-process-accepted)).

A spec with the current state `moving` and without `move` makes the executor wait. A control process of a release without moves sends such a spec. The executor then logs `the executor cannot reach the target` with its reason. The node-local state of the executor keeps the move. While the disk of that move is not whole, a spec with another current state boots nothing either.

### Give-back

A failed move can leave a machine on its target while the source keeps a copy of its disk ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#give-back)). An instance admin can ask the target node to give the machine back. The spec of the machine then names the move in `give_back_move_id`. For each new version of the spec, the executor answers once, with a report of its current state, once no other report waits:

| Node                                                                                                                                          | Field of the report                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| It never proved the pull of the move, holds no disk file of the machine, and runs no microVM of it. A partial copy of a pull is no disk file. | `released_move_id`. The report has no `pulled_move_id`.      |
| It proved the pull, or holds the whole disk of the move, and its disk file is here                                                            | `kept_move_id`, with `pulled_move_id` while the disk is here |
| It holds a disk file without the proof of the move, it proved the pull and lost the disk file, or it cannot read the disk file                | `withheld_move_id`, with `withheld_reason`                   |
| A microVM of the machine runs                                                                                                                 | none                                                         |

A release gives the machine back to the source in the transaction of the report, and ends the grant of the target. So no later report of the target is accepted, and the executor never boots the machine. A node reports the feature `give-back` in its heartbeats ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#heartbeat)), and the control role asks only a node that reports it.

### MachineMove

| Field              | Type   | Description                                                                                        |
| ------------------ | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `move_id`          | string | The ID of the move, a UUID. A partial copy of another move starts again from zero.                 |
| `source_server_id` | string | The ID of the source node, a UUID. Its certificate must name it.                                   |
| `source_address`   | string | The disk listener of the source node: its mesh address and port `7444`, such as `10.239.0.2:7444`. |

## MachineReport

`MachineReport` (field 4 of `ChannelRequest`) is one step of the current state of a machine. The executor sends its reports one at a time: it sends the next one after the result of the one before. So the reports of a machine arrive in order. After a new channel opens, the executor sends its waiting report again. A report of the state that the control store holds already changes nothing, so a report that arrives twice is harmless.

| Field               | Type               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Limit                                                |
| ------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `lease`             | `MachineLease`     | The grant that the executor acts with.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |                                                      |
| `sequence`          | uint64             | Numbers the reports of one grant, from 1. The result names it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                      |
| `state`             | `MachineState`     | The new current state. `MACHINE_STATE_PENDING` and `MACHINE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED` are refused.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |                                                      |
| `boot_generation`   | uint64             | The reboot generation of the boot that the report is about: the boot that starts, runs, or failed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |                                                      |
| `stopped_by_itself` | bool               | Tells that the machine shut down from inside, with the restart policy `never`. Only a report of `stopped` can set it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |                                                      |
| `error`             | string             | Why the machine failed, for a report of `failed`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | at most 1024 bytes, valid UTF-8                      |
