# Go client

> The Go client of the public API: its options, idempotency keys, retries, typed errors, and credentials.

`internal/client` is the Go client of the public API `hopbox.v1`. The hopbox CLI uses it ([hopbox CLI](/reference/cli/)). It wraps the generated Connect clients of `gen/hopbox/v1/hopboxv1connect` with these rules: retries with backoff, idempotency keys on create calls, typed errors, and the bearer credential of the caller. The TypeScript SDK follows the same rules ([TypeScript SDK](/reference/ts-sdk/)). The package links no control code. The test `TestCLINeverLinksControlCode` of `tools/rolesplit` checks this for `internal/client`, `internal/cli`, and `cmd/hopbox`.

## Make a client

```go
c, err := client.New("https://example.com", client.Options{
  Credentials: client.BearerToken(os.Getenv("HOPBOX_API_KEY")),
})
if err != nil {
  return err
}
resp, err := c.Orgs.ListOrgs(ctx, connect.NewRequest(&hopboxv1.ListOrgsRequest{}))
if errors.Is(err, client.ErrPermissionDenied) {
  // The key cannot list orgs.
}
```

`New(rawURL, opts)` checks the URL with `ParseURL` and returns a `*Client`. A bad URL fails with an error that wraps `ErrBadURL`.

| `Options` field  | Type            | Default                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `HTTPClient`     | `*http.Client`  | `DefaultHTTPClient()`            | Sends the calls. The default speaks HTTP/2 over TLS, with HTTP/1.1 for a server without HTTP/2. To a loopback install without TLS, it speaks HTTP/2 with prior knowledge (h2c), as `hopboxd` does, because `Exec` needs a stream in both directions. A loopback server that speaks only HTTP/1.1 then fails the call. It follows no redirect, so the bearer token never goes to another host: a redirect fails the call. A client of your own must do the same. |
| `Credentials`    | `Credentials`   | nil                              | Gives the bearer token of each call. With nil, the calls carry no credential, as the device flow needs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `UserAgent`      | string          | `hopbox-go-client (<os>/<arch>)` | The `User-Agent` header of each call. The CLI sends `hopbox-cli/<version> (<os>/<arch>)`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `AttemptTimeout` | `time.Duration` | `DefaultAttemptTimeout`, 90 s    | The deadline of one try of a unary call. The server gives a call 30 s, and a lifecycle call of a machine 60 s.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `MaxRetryAfter`  | `time.Duration` | 0, no cap                        | The longest `Retry-After` that the client waits for. A longer one ends the call with its error, and `Error.RetryAfter` holds the wanted wait. With 0, the client waits as long as the server asks. The CLI sets 5 minutes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Logger`         | `*slog.Logger`  | no logs                          | Gets a debug record for each retry, and a record for each refresh of CLI tokens.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

`Client` has the field `BaseURL`, the URL of `ParseURL`. It has one generated client for each service of `hopbox.v1`: `Install`, `Auth`, `Accounts`, `Orgs`, `APIKeys`, `SSHKeys`, `Machines`, `Vars`, and `Audit`. Each call of each one goes through the steps below.

## Install URLs

`ParseURL(raw)` returns the base URL of an install, such as `https://example.com`.

* A bare domain gets `https://`.
* The host is in lower case, and a `/` at the end goes.
* `http://` works only for a loopback host: `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, or `::1`.
* A path, a query, a fragment, a user name, or a password fails with `ErrBadURL`.

The error of a refused URL hides its user info. It shows `xxxxx` in place of all text between `://` and the last `@`, such as `https://xxxxx@example.com`. A password with a `/` or a `?` in it stays hidden too. A URL without an `@` shows as it is.

## The steps of a call

Each unary call passes these steps in order:

1. **Typed errors.** The error of the call becomes an `*Error`. See [Errors](#errors).
2. **User agent.** The step sets `User-Agent`.
3. **Idempotency key.** See [Idempotency keys](#idempotency-keys).
4. **Retries.** See [Retries](#retries). The steps after this one run again on each try.
5. **Credential.** See [Credentials](#credentials).

A stream gets the steps 1, 2, and 5, without retries. If the credential fails, the first `Send` or `Receive` of the stream returns the error, and the stream sends no request.

## Idempotency keys

A method with the option `(hopbox.v1.idempotent)` needs an `Idempotency-Key` header ([the API server](/reference/api/#idempotency-keys)). Today these are `CreateMachine`, `CreateOrg`, `CreateAPIKey`, and `AddSSHKey`. The client puts a new UUIDv7 in the header of each such call that has no key yet. The step runs before the retries, so each try of one call sends the same key. The server then runs the call once. A key that the caller set stays.

## Retries

The client tries a unary call at most 3 times: the first try and `MaxRetries`, 2, retries.

| Code of the failed try | Retried                                                |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `unavailable`          | Only for a call that is safe to run again.             |
| `resource_exhausted`   | Only for a call that is safe to run again.             |
| `deadline_exceeded`    | Only for a call that is safe to run again.             |
| Any other code         | No. An auth error or a bad request never gets a retry. |

A call is safe to run again in these cases:

| Case                                     | How the client knows it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The call only reads.                     | Its method has the option `(hopbox.v1.read_only)`, or `idempotency_level` `NO_SIDE_EFFECTS` or `IDEMPOTENT` ([API definitions](/reference/api-definitions/#hopboxv1read_only)). Examples are `ListOrgs` and `GetMachine`.                                        |
| The call carries an idempotency key.     | Its method has the option `(hopbox.v1.idempotent)`, such as `CreateMachine` ([Idempotency keys](#idempotency-keys)).                                                                                                                                             |
| The try surely did not reach the server. | The try got no connection, because of a dial or TLS error, such as a refused connection. Or the answer of the try has the header `NotRunHeader`, `Hopbox-Not-Run`, with the value `1` ([the API server](/reference/api/#answers-of-calls-that-changed-nothing)). |

Each other call changes state and has no key, such as `CreateInvitation`. The client does not retry it after a lost answer, because the server can have run it. A second run can then act twice, for example with a second invitation. The client retries such a call only after a try that surely did not reach the server. The check holds for each try. A refusal with `Hopbox-Not-Run` on the first try, then a lost answer on the second try, ends the call with the error of the second try.

A try that ends without an answer can have run. A reset of an HTTP/2 stream, such as a server that drops the call, fails with `internal`, which never gets a retry. A try that waits for an answer until `AttemptTimeout` fails with `deadline_exceeded`. Only a call that is safe to run again then goes again.

`RefreshCLIToken` from a `TokenSource` is the one exception, as the owner decided on 2026-10-25. The refresh changes state and has no key. But the install takes a replaced refresh token once more within its `RefreshGrace` of 10 s ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#cli-tokens)). So after a lost answer, the client sends the refresh once more, if that retry starts within `RefreshReplayWindow`, 10 s, of the start of the first try. The wait before the retry counts. The same bound holds for every later try of the refresh after the lost answer, also a retry after a refusal with `Hopbox-Not-Run`, because each such try uses the one replay of the grace. The client gives up rather than start any of them later. Only `RefreshCLIToken` gets this retry, whatever the context of another call holds. The window starts before the install replaces the token, so a retry that reaches the install soon after its start falls within the grace. A retry that the network holds back past the grace counts as a reuse, and ends the CLI sign-in. A second lost answer fails the call. The other rules of the table still apply, so a refusal with `Hopbox-Not-Run` before the lost answer does not use up the one retry.

The client reads `Hopbox-Not-Run` from the HTTP answer, so it also sees the header on an answer that is not a Connect error, such as the `502` page of an edge server. For this, `New` wraps the transport of `Options.HTTPClient` in a copy of that client. The wrapper also gives each HTTP request a copy of the header of the call. So a try that the attempt timeout ended can still be in the transport while the next try sets its header. The wrapper looks at each HTTP request of a try, and only the last one counts. The credential step can send a call twice in one try: after `unauthenticated`, it sends the call again with a new token. So a refusal with `Hopbox-Not-Run` before a request that ran does not let the call go again.

The client knows that a try got no connection from two signs. A `ConnectDone` event of `net/http/httptrace` reports a failed dial, before any `GotConn` event. Or the error is one that only a dial or a TLS handshake returns: a dial `*net.OpError`, a `*net.DNSError`, a `tls.RecordHeaderError`, or a `*tls.CertificateVerificationError`. Any other error counts as a try that can have run. So a transport of your own that reports no such events never makes a lost answer look like a request that never left. The edge servers use the same check (`internal/notrun`).

The wait before a retry has full jitter: a random time from 0 up to 500 ms before the first retry, and up to 1 s before the second. If the error has a `Retry-After` header, the client waits that time instead. The header holds seconds, or an HTTP date. The client reads at most `MaxRetryAfterHeader`, 24 hours, from either form, so a date far ahead counts as 24 hours. A wait of `LongWait`, 10 s, or more logs `retrying a call` at level warn. A shorter one logs it at level debug. The client does not retry in these cases:

* `MaxRetryAfter` is set, and `Retry-After` is longer.
* The wait ends after the deadline of the context of the call.
* The context of the call ends.
* The credential step failed, also for a read call. An example is a refresh of CLI tokens that failed after its own retries. One more refresh with the same token would end the CLI sign-in.

Each try has its own deadline, `AttemptTimeout`. A try that runs out of time fails with `deadline_exceeded`, and the table above applies.

## Errors

Each error of a call is an `*Error`. Other errors, such as one of the credential, stay as they are.

| `Error` field | Type              | Description                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Code`        | `connect.Code`    | The code, such as `connect.CodeNotFound`.                                                                                                              |
| `Message`     | string            | The message of the server, without the code.                                                                                                           |
| `Procedure`   | string            | The call, such as `/hopbox.v1.OrgService/GetOrg`.                                                                                                      |
| `RequestID`   | string            | The `Hopbox-Request-Id` of the response ([the API server](/reference/api/#the-chain-of-a-call)). A call that did not reach the server has an empty ID. |
| `RetryAfter`  | `time.Duration`   | The `Retry-After` of the response, or 0.                                                                                                               |
| `Details`     | `[]proto.Message` | The typed details of the error, such as `*hopboxv1.MachineNameTaken`.                                                                                  |

`Error()` returns `<code>: <message>`, such as `not_found: not found: no org 01a1...`. `Unwrap` returns the `*connect.Error`, so `connect.CodeOf` works too.

`errors.Is(err, sentinel)` matches the code of an `*Error`. The codes are those of [the API server](/reference/api/#errors).

| Sentinel                | Code                  |
| ----------------------- | --------------------- |
| `ErrCanceled`           | `canceled`            |
| `ErrUnknown`            | `unknown`             |
| `ErrInvalidArgument`    | `invalid_argument`    |
| `ErrDeadlineExceeded`   | `deadline_exceeded`   |
| `ErrNotFound`           | `not_found`           |
| `ErrAlreadyExists`      | `already_exists`      |
| `ErrPermissionDenied`   | `permission_denied`   |
| `ErrResourceExhausted`  | `resource_exhausted`  |
| `ErrFailedPrecondition` | `failed_precondition` |
| `ErrAborted`            | `aborted`             |
| `ErrUnimplemented`      | `unimplemented`       |
| `ErrInternal`           | `internal`            |
| `ErrUnavailable`        | `unavailable`         |
| `ErrUnauthenticated`    | `unauthenticated`     |

| Other error    | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ErrSignedOut` | The client has no live CLI sign-in: none in the store, the refresh token ended, the tokens belong to another install, or the install refused the refresh token. The way out is a new sign-in. |
| `ErrBadURL`    | `ParseURL` or `New` refused the URL.                                                                                                                                                          |

## Credentials

```go
type Credentials interface {
  Token(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
}


type Renewer interface {
  Credentials
  Rejected(token string) bool
}
```

The client puts the token of `Credentials` in the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` of each try. If the credential fails, the call fails with that error, and no request goes out.

Sometimes the server refuses the token with `unauthenticated`, and the credential is a `Renewer`. Then the client calls `Rejected` with the token. If `Rejected` returns true, the client gets a token again. If the new token differs, the client sends the call once more with it. If getting the token fails with `ErrSignedOut`, the call returns that error.

`BearerToken` is a token that never changes, such as an API key. An empty `BearerToken` fails with `ErrSignedOut`.

### CLI tokens

`TokenSource` is a `Renewer` for the tokens of a CLI sign-in ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#cli-tokens)). `NewTokenSource(rawURL, store, opts)` makes one. It refreshes with its own client of `opts`, without a credential, because `RefreshCLIToken` must not carry an expired access token.

```go
type TokenStore interface {
  Lock(ctx context.Context) (unlock func(), err error)
  Load() (CLITokens, error)
  Save(CLITokens) error
  ClearIf(refreshToken string) error
}
```

The store keeps the tokens where every process of the CLI finds them. `Lock` holds off the `Lock` of every other process. With no tokens in the store, `Load` returns an error that wraps `ErrSignedOut`. The CLI keeps them in `credentials.toml` ([hopbox CLI](/reference/cli/#files)).

`CLITokens` has the fields `URL`, `AccountID`, `SignInID`, `AccessToken`, `AccessExpireTime`, `RefreshToken`, and `RefreshExpireTime`. `URL` is the install that issued the tokens. `TokensFrom(url, tokens)` makes `CLITokens` from the `CLITokens` message of the API.

`Token` works in these steps:

1. If the token in memory lives for more than `RefreshBefore`, 1 minute, and the server did not refuse it, return it.
2. Take the lock of the store, and load the tokens.
3. If the tokens belong to another install, fail with `ErrSignedOut`.
4. If the stored access token lives for more than 1 minute, and the server did not refuse it, keep it and return it. Another process refreshed meanwhile.
5. If the refresh token ended, fail with `ErrSignedOut`.
6. Call `RefreshCLIToken` with the stored refresh token. After a lost answer, the call goes once more within `RefreshReplayWindow` ([Retries](#retries)). If that answer gets lost too, fail, and keep the store as it is. The call waits at most `RefreshMaxRetryAfter`, 30 s, for a `Retry-After`. A shorter `MaxRetryAfter` of the options wins. The refresh holds the lock of the store, and every other process of the CLI waits for that lock. If the server refuses it, call `ClearIf` with that refresh token, and fail with `ErrSignedOut`. If the store still holds that refresh token, `ClearIf` deletes the stored tokens. Else it keeps them.
7. Save the new tokens, and return the new access token. If the save fails, call `ClearIf` with the old refresh token, log `the refreshed CLI tokens could not be stored, so the next command must sign in again` at level warn, and still return the token.

The install replaces the refresh token before step 7 saves the new one. Two cases leave the old refresh token in the store: the save and the `ClearIf` both fail, or the process dies between steps 6 and 7. The next refresh sends it again, and the install ends the sign-in as a reuse. The steps make this unlikely, but they cannot rule it out.

`Rejected(token)` forgets the token in memory, so the next `Token` reads the store again. Only a store that holds the same refused token leads to a refresh.

A replaced refresh token ends the sign-in, so these steps never send one. The store must have a real lock. The grace of 10 s of the install covers only one second refresh with the same token. So three processes that refresh at once without a lock end the sign-in. The store of the CLI refuses a dir without file locks ([hopbox CLI](/reference/cli/#files)). Two processes without a lock both get tokens through the grace, and the next refresh drops the second chain. Its process then reads the store again at the next refusal.

## Tests

* `internal/client/client_test.go` checks the retries, the waits, `Retry-After`, the idempotency keys, the typed errors, and the credentials against a fake API. Its table of retries covers a read call, a call with a key, and `CreateInvitation`, after a lost answer, an error code, an answer with `Hopbox-Not-Run`, and a refused connection. Other tests cover a reset stream, a hung answer, a resend with a new token after a refusal, a transport without connection events, and TLS with HTTP/2. `TestARefreshReplaysOnceWithinTheWindow` checks the one retry of a refresh, with a clock of the test, before and after the window.
* `internal/client/tokens_test.go` checks `TokenSource` with a store in memory.
* `internal/client/server_test.go` runs against a real install of `internal/api/apitest`. Four processes with one store make one refresh. Two processes without a lock both refresh through the grace, and the sign-in goes on after the next refresh. This shows the most that the grace covers. A sign-in that the console ends clears the store. One lost answer of a refresh recovers with no reuse, and the sign-in goes on. Two lost answers fail the call and keep the store as it is.

# Guest kernel

> The source, config, fragment, builder, outputs, make targets, boot arguments, and security modules of the guest kernel.

The guest kernel boots every machine. It is the Amazon Linux 6.1 microVM kernel, with the Firecracker 6.1 config and a hopbox config fragment. The recipe lives in `kernel/`. Two builds of the same recipe give the same `vmlinux`, byte for byte. `make kernel` builds it in Docker (the build guide of the repo has the steps, and how to change the kernel).

## Files

| File                    | What it holds                                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kernel/kernel.env`     | The pins: the source, the base config, and the build stamp.                                          |
| `kernel/hopbox.config`  | The config fragment. It holds every option that hopbox needs.                                        |
| `kernel/Dockerfile`     | The builder image.                                                                                   |
| `kernel/build.sh`       | Runs the build in the builder image. `make kernel` calls it.                                         |
| `kernel/container.sh`   | The build steps inside the builder image.                                                            |
| `kernel/vmlinux.config` | The final `.config`. `make kernel` writes it. Do not edit it by hand.                                |
| `kernel/vmlinux.sha256` | The sha256 of the last `vmlinux` and of its config. `make kernel` writes it. Do not edit it by hand. |
| `tools/kconfigcheck`    | Checks that a final config keeps every option of the fragment.                                       |

## Source

| Item           | Value                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Kernel version | 6.1.188                                                                                                            |
| Repository     | `https://github.com/amazonlinux/linux`                                                                             |
| Tag            | `microvm-kernel-6.1.188-56.393.amzn2023` (tag object `a9ea02bac2b0d3906e5ca32dd91fd0d406eb4951`)                   |
| Commit         | `8785eb28815fdac7e6743bb6fad34ef67dc24b26`                                                                         |
| Tarball        | `https://codeload.github.com/amazonlinux/linux/tar.gz/8785eb28815fdac7e6743bb6fad34ef67dc24b26`, 224,970,436 bytes |
| Tarball sha256 | `11cd54507d034b43f41690045ab26d90c8143f38210e9633432bc8a7c3eded2a`                                                 |

The build fetches the tarball by the commit, not by the tag, so a moved tag cannot change the source. If the tarball has another sha256, the build stops. If `make kernelversion` of the source is not the version in `kernel.env`, the build also stops.

GitHub makes the tarball on request. If GitHub changes how it makes archives, the sha256 changes and the build stops. In that case, check the new tarball against a git checkout of the commit before you change the pin.

Firecracker builds its 6.1 test kernels from the `microvm-kernel-*` tags. The tag above is the newest 6.1 microVM tag on 2026-10-15. It is later than 6.1.167, so it has the VMClock generation counter.

| Item                | Value                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Firecracker version | v1.17.0                                                                                                                                 |

| URL                 | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/v1.17.0/resources/guest_configs/microvm-kernel-ci-x86_64-6.1.config` |

Firecracker’s CI also merges `ci.config` and `nvme.config` into this file. hopbox does not use them. The fragment carries the options of `ci.config` that hopbox needs: the i8042 keyboard controller and `/proc/config.gz`.

## Config fragment

`kernel/hopbox.config` lists every option that hopbox needs, also the options that the base config already sets. If a new base config drops one of them, the build fails. Each option is built in, because the guest has no kernel modules. If Kconfig picks `m` for any option, the build fails too.

| Group                  | Options                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Release name           | `LOCALVERSION="-hopbox1"`, `# LOCALVERSION_AUTO is not set`, `BUILD_SALT="6.1.188-hopbox1"`                                                                                                                                                 | `uname -r` prints `6.1.188-hopbox1`, so a hopbox build differs from a stock kernel. The salt goes into the build ID of `vmlinux`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Module support         | `MODULES`, `# MODULE_SIG is not set`, `MODPROBE_PATH=""`                                                                                                                                                                                    | `BPF_JIT` needs `MODULES` in 6.1. The build makes no modules, and the guest has no module tree. The kernel never starts a module loader, and the boot argument `sysctl.kernel.modules_disabled=1` turns module loading off before the first program runs ([Boot requirements](#boot-requirements)). Module signing stays off, because a signing key made at build time breaks the reproducible build. |
| No 32-bit system calls | `# IA32_EMULATION is not set`, `# X86_X32_ABI is not set`                                                                                                                                                                                   | Nothing in the default image is 32-bit. A 64-bit process can make i386 system calls through `int 0x80`. Seccomp filters, such as `RestrictAddressFamilies` of systemd, see them as calls of another architecture. Without 32-bit calls, no process can go around a filter that way. A 32-bit program does not run in the guest.                                                                       |
| Firecracker devices    | `VIRTIO_MMIO`, `VIRTIO_BLK`, `VIRTIO_NET`, `HW_RANDOM_VIRTIO`, `SERIAL_8250_CONSOLE`, `KVM_GUEST`, `PTP_1588_CLOCK_KVM`                                                                                                                     | The disks, the network, the entropy device, the serial console, and the clock of a microVM.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Guest link             | `VSOCKETS`, `VIRTIO_VSOCKETS`                                                                                                                                                                                                               | The guest agent talks to the node over vsock.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Copy detection         | `ACPI`, `PTP_1588_CLOCK`, `PTP_1588_CLOCK_VMCLOCK`, `VMGENID`                                                                                                                                                                               | VMClock and VMGenID tell the guest that it is a restored copy. | Config in the guest    | `IKCONFIG`, `IKCONFIG_PROC`                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `/proc/config.gz` holds the config, so tools in the guest can check it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| systemd                | `DEVTMPFS`, `FHANDLE`, `INOTIFY_USER`, `SIGNALFD`, `TIMERFD`, `EPOLL`, `AUTOFS_FS`, `TMPFS_POSIX_ACL`, `TMPFS_XATTR`                                                                                                                        | systemd in the default image.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Default image          | `PSI`, `DMIID`, `BINFMT_MISC`, `EXT4_FS`, `EXT4_FS_POSIX_ACL`, `EXT4_FS_SECURITY`, `FUSE_FS`, `TUN`                                                                                                                                         | systemd and the programs of the default image.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

| BPF compiler           | `BPF_JIT`, `BPF_JIT_ALWAYS_ON`                                                                                                                                                                                                              | BPF programs, for example the seccomp filters of systemd and Docker, run as native code. `BPF_JIT_ALWAYS_ON` removes the BPF interpreter, which speculative execution attacks use.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| cgroup v2 controllers  | `CGROUPS`, `MEMCG`, `BLK_CGROUP`, `BLK_DEV_THROTTLING`, `CGROUP_SCHED`, `FAIR_GROUP_SCHED`, `CFS_BANDWIDTH`, `CGROUP_PIDS`, `CPUSETS`                                                                                                       | The controllers `cpu`, `cpuset`, `io`, `memory`, and `pids` for systemd and Docker.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

| IPVS                   | `IP_VS`, `IP_VS_NFCT`, `IP_VS_PROTO_TCP`, `IP_VS_PROTO_UDP`, `IP_VS_RR`                                                                                                                                                                     | The service load balancer of Docker swarm mode.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Traffic control        | `NET_SCHED`, `NET_CLS_ACT`, `NET_SCH_FQ_CODEL`, `NET_SCH_INGRESS`, `NET_CLS_BPF`                                                                                                                                                            | systemd sets `fq_codel` as the default queue discipline. The ingress queue discipline and BPF classifiers carry `tc` programs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| vsock sockets in `ss`  | `VSOCKETS_DIAG`                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `ss --vsock` lists the guest link.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Encrypted overlay      | `XFRM_USER`, `INET_ESP`, `CRYPTO_GCM`, `CRYPTO_SEQIV`, `CRYPTO_GHASH`                                                                                                                                                                       | Encrypted overlay networks of Docker.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

These options are not in the kernel:

| Option              | Why not                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SECURITY_APPARMOR` | The base config has SELinux and no AppArmor. If the kernel has no AppArmor, Docker runs without an AppArmor profile.       |
| `NET_CLS_CGROUP`    | Only cgroup v1 uses it.                                                                                                    |
| `BTRFS_FS`          | Docker uses overlay storage.                                                                                               |
| `IP_SCTP`           | No part of hopbox uses SCTP.                                                                                               |
| `CRYPTO_FIPS`       | With `MODULES`, it needs `MODULE_SIG`, which stays off. The base config has it. hopbox does not boot guests with `fips=1`. |

The moby script `contrib/check-config.sh` (moby commit `c5c09961ba9aa3db0aacae52b6a54fd7aee3dee4`) reports every “Generally Necessary” option of Docker as enabled in `kernel/vmlinux.config`. Of the optional options, it reports only `SECURITY_APPARMOR`, `NET_CLS_CGROUP`, `IP_SCTP`, and the Docker btrfs and zfs storage drivers as missing.

## Boot requirements

The kernel boots under Firecracker v1.17.0 as an uncompressed ELF `vmlinux`. The VMM driver gives it these kernel command line arguments:

| Argument                                | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `console=ttyS0`                         | The serial console.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `reboot=k`                              | A reboot in the guest ends the Firecracker process. With it, `SendCtrlAltDel` stops the microVM cleanly.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `panic=1`                               | A kernel panic reboots, so the Firecracker process ends.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `i8042.noaux i8042.nomux i8042.dumbkbd` | Firecracker emulates only a keyboard on its i8042 controller. With these arguments, the driver does not probe for a mouse port or a multiplexer, and does not test the keyboard. This saves tens of milliseconds at boot ([Firecracker actions](https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/v1.17.0/docs/api_requests/actions.md)). |
| `sysctl.kernel.modules_disabled=1`      | The kernel turns module loading off at boot, before init runs. The default image sets the same value again with `systemd-sysctl`.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `memhp_default_state=online_movable`    | The kernel puts memory that virtio-mem plugs online at once, in the movable zone, so the memory can be unplugged again. The 6.1 kernel has no Kconfig option for this.                                                                                                                                                                          |

Firecracker adds `pci=off`, `root=/dev/vda rw` for the root disk, and the `virtio_mmio.device` arguments itself.

Do not pass `i8042.nopnp`, although the Firecracker docs list it with the three arguments above. Firecracker 1.17 describes the controller in its ACPI tables, as the device `PNP0303` with its interrupt. The driver finds the controller there. With `i8042.nopnp`, the driver uses the legacy interrupt 1, which a Firecracker guest with ACPI does not have. The probe then fails with `i8042: probe of i8042 failed with error -22`, and `SendCtrlAltDel` does nothing. Without the argument, the kernel logs `serio: i8042 KBD port at 0x60,0x64 irq 30`, and `SendCtrlAltDel` stops the default image in about one second. The boot test of the default image checks both ([Default image](/reference/default-image/#boot-test)).

## Security modules

The base config builds in SELinux, Landlock, and the capability module. `/sys/kernel/security/lsm` in the guest lists `capability,landlock,selinux`. SELinux stays inactive:

* The default image has no SELinux policy and no tool that loads one.
* Without a policy, SELinux denies nothing. `/sys/fs/selinux/enforce` reads `0`.
* The kernel command line needs no `selinux=0`.

Docker and systemd work as on a kernel without SELinux. The kernel has no AppArmor ([Config fragment](#config-fragment)).

## Builder image

`kernel/Dockerfile` builds the image `hopbox-kernel-builder:<first 12 hex digits of the sha256 of kernel/Dockerfile>` for `linux/amd64`. A change to the Dockerfile gives a new tag. The image has the label `hopbox-build=kernel-builder`. `kernel/build.sh` builds the image only when it is missing or has no such label. On each run, it tags the image again with the same name, which gives the image a new tag time on the classic image store of Docker. The cleanup of the CI runner keeps an image with a recent tag time. Then the script runs the image by its ID.

| Item           | Value                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Base image     | `debian:bookworm-slim@sha256:7c7b2c966bc9ee8cedfeef67e0e279108992c77681fa595db4a9d65c06ccc587`                                                                 |
| Package source | `snapshot.debian.org` at `20261005T000000Z`, for `bookworm`, `bookworm-updates`, and `bookworm-security`. This is the snapshot that the base image comes from. |
| Packages       | `bc`, `bison`, `ca-certificates`, `cpio`, `curl`, `flex`, `gcc`, `libc6-dev`, `libelf-dev`, `libssl-dev`, `make`, `perl`                                       |
| Compiler       | gcc 12.2.0 (`gcc-12 12.2.0-14+deb12u1`)                                                                                                                        |
| Binutils       | 2.40 (`binutils 2.40-2`)                                                                                                                                       |

The image digest and the snapshot fix every package version. apt checks the signatures of the snapshot, so the snapshot uses plain HTTP.

## Reproducible build

The build runs in a new container each time, from a fresh copy of the source in `/build/linux`. The build path ends up in the kernel image, so it is the same on every host. `container.sh` sets these values:

| Variable                 | Value                         | Effect                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`      | `1791339570`                  | 2026-10-07T02:19:30Z, the committer date of the source commit.                    |
| `KBUILD_BUILD_TIMESTAMP` | `Wed Oct 7 02:19:30 UTC 2026` | The build date in `uname -v`. `container.sh` derives it from `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`. |
| `KBUILD_BUILD_USER`      | `hopbox`                      | The user in `/proc/version`.                                                      |
| `KBUILD_BUILD_HOST`      | `hopbox`                      | The host in `/proc/version`.                                                      |
| `KBUILD_BUILD_VERSION`   | `1`                           | The build number `#1` in `uname -v`.                                              |
| `LC_ALL`, `TZ`           | `C`, `UTC`                    | Tools sort and print dates the same way on every host.                            |

The guest sees:

```text
$ uname -a
Linux localhost 6.1.188-hopbox1 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed Oct  7 02:19:30 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```

## Outputs

`make kernel` writes these files to `bin/kernel/`, or to `KERNEL_OUT`:

| File             | What it is                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vmlinux`        | The kernel, an uncompressed x86_64 ELF image of about 45 MB.                          |
| `vmlinux.sha256` | The sha256 of `vmlinux` and of `vmlinux.config`, in `sha256sum` format.               |
| `vmlinux.config` | The final `.config`.                                                                  |
| `toolchain.txt`  | The versions of gcc, binutils, and the build packages.                                |
| `dl/`            | The downloaded tarball and base config. Later builds reuse them after a sha256 check. |

It also copies `vmlinux.config` and `vmlinux.sha256` to `kernel/`, where git tracks them. `make bundle` puts `vmlinux` into the release bundle, and it refuses a `vmlinux` with another sha256 than the one in `kernel/vmlinux.sha256` ([Release bundle](/reference/release-bundle/)). The current values are:

| File             | sha256                                                             |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `vmlinux`        | `dfb03703bab6d4b590964f2d9473fdc82994ae94384cc5ed1c1b4a0430118a91` |
| `vmlinux.config` | `99f0171775432d9239ed83f453811e09a496ffd88301feec3b9eb8924faf9ebc` |

## Make targets

| Target                | What it does                                                                                                                                                        | Needs  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| `kernel`              | Runs `make kernel-config` first, so a dropped option fails before the compile. Then builds `vmlinux` and writes the outputs.                                        | Docker |
| `kernel-config`       | Writes only the final config, without a compile. Then runs `kconfigcheck`.                                                                                          | Docker |
| `check-kernel`        | Runs `make kernel`. If `kernel/vmlinux.config` or `kernel/vmlinux.sha256` then differs from git, it fails. This proves that the build is reproducible on your host. | Docker |
| `check-kernel-config` | Runs `make kernel-config`. If `kernel/vmlinux.config` then differs from git, it fails.                                                                              | Docker |

| Variable     | Default                             | Description                                                                                                                      |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KERNEL_OUT` | `bin/kernel`                        | The output folder.                                                                                                               |
| `JOBS`       | the number of CPUs in the container | The number of parallel compile jobs. Set it in the environment, for example `JOBS=4 make kernel`. It does not change the output. |

## Checks

* `kconfigcheck` reads the fragment and a final config. If the final config does not keep an option of the fragment, it fails and lists each such line. If a dependency is missing, Kconfig drops an option without an error, so this check is the only guard.
* If the final config has an option set to `m`, `container.sh` fails. With `MODULES`, Kconfig can pick `m`. The build makes no modules, so such an option is then missing from the guest.
* `make test` runs two tests in `tools/kconfigcheck`. One checks that `kernel/vmlinux.config` keeps the fragment. The other checks that `kernel/vmlinux.sha256` names the sha256 of `kernel/vmlinux.config`, so a config change without a new build fails.
* The CI job `kernel` runs `make check-kernel-config`. It catches a fragment or pin change without a new config. It keeps `bin/kernel/dl` in the Actions cache. The cache key is the hash of `kernel/kernel.env`. So a run downloads the source tarball only after a pin change. CI does not compile the kernel, because the compile takes many minutes. On two threads of the [tested server](/reference/preflight/#the-tested-server), it takes about 15 minutes. The workflow `image.yml` compiles the kernel on request.

# Guest link

> The transport, link key, handshake, versions, messages, exec, and file copy of the guest link, and its Go API on the node.

The guest link is the channel between a node and the guest agent `hopbox-guest` in one machine. Each link has a version and uses authentication. The link carries the configuration of the machine, the status of the guest, the output of the start command, exec, and file copy.

The definitions are in `proto/hopbox/guest/v1/link.proto`, package `hopbox.guest.v1`. The node side is the Go package `internal/node/guestlink`. The guest side is the Go package `internal/guest`. The package `internal/guest/protocol` holds the constants and the proofs that both sides share.

## Transport

| Item                               | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Socket                             | vsock, a socket type between a virtual machine and its host                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Direction                          | The guest agent dials the host. The node never dials the guest.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Host context ID                    | `2`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Port                               | `10240`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Host side                          | The unix socket `<uds>_10240`. `<uds>` is the path of the vsock device socket of the microVM. Firecracker gives each guest connection to port 10240 to this socket, and the node listens on it. `protocol.SocketPath(uds)` returns the path.                                                                                                                |
| Protocol                           | Connect over HTTP/2 without TLS, with prior knowledge (h2c). The guest agent is the HTTP/2 client. The node is the HTTP/2 server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Compression                        | none. The node never compresses its messages with gzip. So the receive buffer of a call holds at most 256 KiB of the input of an exec, not a compressed copy of many MiB. A call of the guest agent in gzip fails with `unimplemented` and the message `unknown compression "gzip"`.                                                                        |
| Keepalive                          | After 15 s without frames, each side sends an HTTP/2 PING. If the answer takes more than 5 s, the side drops the connection.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Largest data in one message        | 32 KiB                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Largest message to the node        | 96 KiB. The node reads no larger message, also before the handshake. It checks the length in the header of each message, ends the call with `resource_exhausted`, and does not read the body.                                                                                                                                                               |
| Largest message to the guest agent | 4 MiB. The node refuses a configuration that does not fit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Calls at once on one connection    | 64                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| HTTP/2 receive buffers             | 256 KiB for each call, 16 MiB for each connection, on both sides. All 64 calls fit in the buffer of the connection at once. So a call whose reader stalls holds only its own buffer, and the other calls on the connection go on.                                                                                                                           |
| Connections at once                | 8. Any process in the guest can connect, also a user without root. So a connection that carries no authenticated `Link` and no accepted attach within `HandshakeTimeout` (10 s) closes. When 8 connections are open, a new connection closes the oldest connection that did not prove the key. If all 8 proved the key, the node closes the new connection. |
| Idle connections                   | A connection without calls closes after 2 min. The `Link` call keeps the connection of the guest agent busy.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

Each microVM has its own vsock device socket, so the socket tells the node which machine connects. The guest agent opens a new link at once after a drop. A Firecracker snapshot resets every vsock connection, also in the running machine. After a failed attempt, the guest agent waits 100 ms, then twice as long after each further failure, up to 5 s. A link that ends within 1 s counts as a failed attempt, so a link that drops at once does not loop without a pause.

## Link key

Each boot of a machine has its own link key: 32 random bytes. The node puts the key in the metadata service of the microVM, and keeps the same key for the handshake. The key never goes on the kernel command line.

| Item                           | Value                                                              |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Metadata service               | Firecracker MMDS version 2, at `http://169.254.169.254` by default |
| Path                           | `/hopbox/guest_link_key`                                           |
| Value                          | the key as 64 lowercase hex characters, in a JSON string           |
| MMDS data that the node writes | `{"hopbox": {"guest_link_key": "<64 hex characters>"}}`            |

The guest agent reads the key before each handshake, because a clone gets a new key. MMDS version 2 needs a session token:

1. `PUT /latest/api/token` with the header `X-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 60`. The body of the answer is the token.
2. `GET /hopbox/guest_link_key` with the headers `X-metadata-token: <token>` and `Accept: application/json`.

The guest agent also accepts the key as plain text, without the JSON quotes.

Before the network of the machine has its address, the guest cannot reach the metadata service. So when the metadata service has an IPv4 link-local address, the guest agent first does these steps on its network interface:

1. It brings the interface up.
2. When the interface has no IPv4 address, it adds `169.254.0.2/32` with link scope.
3. It adds the route `169.254.169.254/32` on the interface, with link scope.

The network setup of the first configuration removes the address `169.254.0.2/32` again. The route stays.

## Handshake

Every link starts with a handshake on the `Link` call. The guest agent speaks first.

1. The guest agent sends `GuestHello`: the lowest and the highest version that it speaks, its build version, and a new nonce of 32 random bytes. It also sends the boot ID of the guest kernel and a random ID of its own run. A new boot ID means that the machine booted again. A new run ID with the same boot ID means that the agent restarted, which restarts the start command.
2. The node picks the highest version that both sides speak. When no version fits, the node ends the call with the code `failed_precondition`.
3. The node sends `NodeHello`: the version, a new nonce of 32 random bytes, its proof, and its build version.
4. The guest agent checks the version and the proof. When one of them is wrong, it ends the call and sends nothing more. So a process that poses as the node never gets the proof of the guest.
5. The guest agent sends `GuestAuth` with its proof.
6. The node checks the proof. When it is wrong, the node ends the call with the code `unauthenticated`.
7. The node sends the configuration in a `Config` message. The first message after the proof tells the guest agent that the node accepted it.

The node waits at most 10 s for the hello and the proof together. `HandshakeTimeout` in `guestlink.Options` sets this limit.

| Message      | Field               | Type   | Description                                                                           |
| ------------ | ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GuestHello` | `min_version`       | uint32 | The lowest guest link version that the guest agent speaks.                            |
| `GuestHello` | `max_version`       | uint32 | The highest guest link version that the guest agent speaks.                           |
| `GuestHello` | `agent_version`     | string | The build version of `hopbox-guest`, for example `v0.1.0`.                            |
| `GuestHello` | `nonce`             | bytes  | 32 random bytes, new for each link.                                                   |
| `GuestHello` | `boot_id`           | string | The boot ID of the guest kernel. It changes at each boot of the machine.              |
| `GuestHello` | `agent_instance_id` | string | A random ID of this run of the guest agent. Each restart of the agent gives a new ID. |
| `NodeHello`  | `version`           | uint32 | The version that the node picked.                                                     |
| `NodeHello`  | `nonce`             | bytes  | 32 random bytes, new for each link.                                                   |
| `NodeHello`  | `proof`             | bytes  | The node proof.                                                                       |
| `NodeHello`  | `node_version`      | string | The build version of `hopboxd`.                                                       |
| `GuestAuth`  | `proof`             | bytes  | The guest proof.                                                                      |

### Proofs

Each proof is HMAC-SHA256 with the link key over these bytes, in this order:

| Part          | Bytes                                                                               |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label         | `hopbox guest link` and one zero byte                                               |
| Role          | `node` for the node proof, `guest` for the guest proof, then one zero byte          |
| Offered range | the lowest and the highest version of `GuestHello`, each a 32-bit big-endian number |
| Version       | the version of `NodeHello`, a 32-bit big-endian number                              |
| Guest nonce   | the 32 bytes of `GuestHello`                                                        |
| Node nonce    | the 32 bytes of `NodeHello`                                                         |

Both nonces are new on each link, so an old proof never works again. The role differs between the two proofs, so a guest agent cannot send the proof of the node back. The proofs cover the offered range and the version, so nothing between the two sides can force a lower version.

## Versions

A guest link version is a whole number from 1. This build speaks versions 1 to 3. Version 2 adds `ExecControl` on `Link`. On version 1, the node sends the resizes and the signals of an exec on `Exec`. From version 2 on, it sends them as `ExecControl`. Version 3 adds the credit of `Exec` ([Credit of an exec](#credit-of-an-exec)). On a link of version 3, the guest agent acks the messages of the node on `Exec`, and the node sends them on credit. The negotiated version of the link decides, not the build of the guest agent or of `hopboxd`.

| Rule              | Detail                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Range             | Each side speaks a range of versions, both ends included.                                                                            |
| Choice            | The node picks the highest version in both ranges.                                                                                   |
| Old guest agent   | A node with a newer `hopboxd` keeps the old versions in its range, so it still talks to a guest agent from an older image.           |
| No common version | The node refuses the link with `failed_precondition`, and its state records the error. The guest agent tries again with its backoff. |
| New fields        | A new field in a message needs no new version. An older side ignores fields that it does not know.                                   |
| New version       | A change that an older side reads wrongly needs a new version, for example a new meaning of a field.                                 |

## Link messages

After the handshake, both sides keep the `Link` call open. Each `LinkRequest` and each `LinkResponse` holds one message in its `oneof` field `message`.

| Message           | Field of the oneof               | From  | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GuestHello`      | `LinkRequest.hello`              | guest | the first message of each link                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `GuestAuth`       | `LinkRequest.auth`               | guest | the second message, after a `NodeHello` with a valid proof                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `NodeHello`       | `LinkResponse.hello`             | node  | the answer to `GuestHello`                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Config`          | `LinkResponse.config`            | node  | after the handshake, and after each change                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `ConfigApplied`   | `LinkRequest.config_applied`     | guest | after each `Config`. It holds the generation, the errors, and the count of env values that the agent left out.                                                                                                                  |
| `Status`          | `LinkRequest.status`             | guest | after the handshake, and after each change of the start command                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `LogEntry`        | `LinkRequest.log`                | guest | for each line of output of the start command                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `Attach`          | `LinkResponse.attach`            | node  | to start an exec, an upload, or a download. It holds the attach ID `id`, and the operation `exec` (an `ExecStart`), `upload` (an `UploadStart`), or `download` (a `DownloadStart`).                                             |
| `RunStartCommand` | `LinkResponse.run_start_command` | node  | to run the start command again, for the restart policy “always”. It has no fields. If the start command runs, the guest agent does nothing. If there is no start command, it sends the status `START_COMMAND_STATE_NONE` again. |
| `CancelAttach`    | `LinkResponse.cancel_attach`     | node  | to stop an exec, an upload, or a download early. It holds the attach ID `id`.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ExecControl`     | `LinkResponse.exec_control`      | node  | from version 2 on, for a resize or a signal of the command of an exec. It holds the attach ID `id`, and `resize` (a `WindowSize`) or `signal` (a name). `seq` numbers the controls of each exec from 1.                         |

### Configuration

| Field              | Type                                           | What the guest agent does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `generation`       | uint64                                         | Returns it in `ConfigApplied`. The node sets it: 1 for the first configuration, then one more for each change.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `hostname`         | string                                         | Writes `/etc/hostname`, points `127.0.1.1` at the name in `/etc/hosts`, and sets the kernel host name. An empty value leaves all three as they are. The name must be DNS labels of letters, digits, and hyphens, at most 64 characters in all.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `network.address`  | string                                         | Makes this address with its prefix length, for example `10.240.0.5/32`, the only IPv4 address of the interface.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `network.gateway`  | string                                         | Adds the default route through this address, on-link, for example `169.254.0.1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `network.mtu`      | uint32                                         | Sets the MTU of the interface, for example `1420`. Zero leaves it as it is.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `network.address6` | string                                         | Makes this IPv6 address with its prefix length, for example `fd65:1c74:e769::af0:5/128`, the only global IPv6 address of the interface. It skips duplicate address detection, because the machine is alone on its link with the node. The link-local address stays. Empty leaves the IPv6 of the interface as it is. A node whose kernel has IPv6 sends it ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/#the-ipv6-addresses-of-the-machines)). A guest agent before this field ignores it. |
| `network.gateway6` | string                                         | Adds the IPv6 default route `::/0` through this address, for example `fe80::1`. The node sends it with `address6`. The guest agent refuses a gateway that is not link-local, and the error of the network names it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `nameservers`      | list of strings                                | Writes one `nameserver` line for each IP address to `/etc/resolv.conf`. The new file replaces a symlink at that path. An empty list leaves the file as it is. In phase 1, the node sends the upstream resolvers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `env`              | list of `EnvVar`, each with `name` and `value` | Writes `/etc/hopbox/env`. Exec and the start command also get these values. The control role builds the list from the env vars and secrets of the org ([the env var API](/reference/vars-api/#env-of-a-machine)). The guest agent leaves out a value whose name it refuses, and logs it ([hopbox-guest](/reference/hopbox-guest/#files)).                                                                                                                                                     |
| `authorized_keys`  | list of strings                                | Writes the keys, in `authorized_keys` format, to `/etc/hopbox/authorized_keys`. sshd reads this file for every Linux user, next to the `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` of the user. So the SSH front door can log in as any user, and only root can remove its key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `start_command`    | string                                         | Runs the command once per boot, after the first configuration that it applies without an error, and after systemd reached `multi-user.target`. [hopbox-guest](/reference/hopbox-guest/#start-command) gives every case.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

The guest agent applies each part, even after another part failed. `ConfigApplied.error` then holds the errors of all failed parts, one per line. `ConfigApplied.skipped_env` counts the env values that the agent left out, because their names break its rules.
