Such a value is no error, so the configuration still applies. An older agent sends 0. A configuration without `network` leaves the network as it is. Network setup needs Linux.

On a new link, the node sends the current configuration again, and the guest agent applies it again. A second apply of a part gives the same result as the first. A new link never starts the start command a second time.

[hopbox-guest](/reference/hopbox-guest/#files) lists the files that the guest agent writes.

### Status

| Field                                   | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `start_command.state`                   | `start_command` is a `StartCommandStatus`. Its `state` is a `StartCommandState`. `START_COMMAND_STATE_NONE`: no start command, or no configuration yet. `START_COMMAND_STATE_WAITING`: the command waits for the end of the boot. `START_COMMAND_STATE_RUNNING`: the command runs. `START_COMMAND_STATE_EXITED`: the command ended. `START_COMMAND_STATE_FAILED`: the command did not start. |
| `start_command.runs`                    | How many times the start command started in this boot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `start_command.exit_code`               | The exit code of the last run. A run that a signal ended has 128 plus the number of the signal.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `start_command.signal`                  | The name of the signal that ended the last run, for example `SIGKILL`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `start_command.started_at`, `exited_at` | The times of the last run.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `start_command.error`                   | Why the start command did not start. In the state `WAITING`, it holds a warning after 2 min of waiting for the boot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `ssh_host_keys`                         | Each public SSH host key of the guest, from `/etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key.pub`, as an `SshHostKey`: `public_key` in `authorized_keys` format, and `fingerprint`, the SHA-256 fingerprint, for example `SHA256:...`. The SSH front door checks the host key of the guest against this list.                                                                                                        |

The guest agent reports the exit of the start command and does not start it again on its own. The node applies the restart policy, and sends `RunStartCommand` for the policy “always”.

### Logs

Each `LogEntry` holds one line of output of the start command in `data`, without its newline. It also holds its `time`, and its `stream`, a `LogStream`: `LOG_STREAM_STDOUT` or `LOG_STREAM_STDERR`. A line longer than 16 KiB arrives in parts of 16 KiB.

While the link is down, the guest agent keeps the lines in memory: at most 10,000 lines and 4 MiB. When the buffer is full, it drops the oldest line. The next line that it sends has the number of dropped lines in `dropped`.

## Exec and file copy

The node starts an exec, an upload, or a download with an `Attach` message on `Link`. The message holds a new attach ID of 16 random bytes and the operation. The guest agent then opens the matching call, `Exec`, `Upload`, or `Download`, and sends the attach ID as its first message. The node accepts each attach ID once, and only for the matching call. An unknown attach ID ends the call with the code `not_found`. The attach ID travels only on the authenticated link, so it proves that the call comes from the guest agent.

The node waits at most 10 s for the guest agent to open the call. If the link drops before that, the call fails at once.

In these three calls, the guest agent is the client. So a request message goes from the guest to the node, and a response message goes from the node to the guest.

### Exec

`ExecStart` describes the command:

| Field  | Default             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------ | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `argv` | empty               | The program and its arguments. The guest agent looks the program up in the `PATH` of the command. An empty list runs the login shell of the user as a login shell, which `hopbox connect` uses. |
| `env`  | empty               | Env vars on top of the env of the machine.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `user` | the main user       | The Linux user. The guest agent sets the user ID, the group ID, and the groups of the user from `/etc/passwd` and `/etc/group`.                                                                 |
| `dir`  | the home directory  | The working directory. A relative path starts at the home directory. When the home directory does not exist, the default is `/`.                                                                |
| `tty`  | `false`             | Runs the command in a pseudo-terminal. All output then arrives as stdout. As with sshd, the terminal belongs to the user and the group `tty`, with mode 0620.                                   |
| `size` | 24 rows, 80 columns | The first size of the terminal, a `WindowSize` with `rows` and `cols`.                                                                                                                          |
| `term` | `xterm-256color`    | The `TERM` env var, with `tty` only.                                                                                                                                                            |

The guest agent builds the env of a command in four steps. A later value replaces an earlier one.

1. `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `PATH`, and `LANG`. `LANG` comes from `/etc/default/locale`, the file that a login on Ubuntu reads. Without a value there, it is `C.UTF-8`.
2. `TERM`, with a terminal only.
3. The env of the machine.
4. The `env` field of `ExecStart`. The default `PATH` is the one of Ubuntu: `/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/games:/usr/local/games:/snap/bin`.

| Message                        | From  | Content                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ExecRequest.attach_id`        | guest | the attach ID, always the first message                                                                                                                 |
| `ExecRequest.stdout`, `stderr` | guest | output                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ExecRequest.exit`             | guest | the end of the command, always the last message                                                                                                         |
| `ExecRequest.read`             | guest | from version 3 on, an ack: what the messages of the node cost that the guest agent took off the call since its last ack                                 |
| `ExecResponse.stdin`           | node  | input                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ExecResponse.stdin_eof`       | node  | the end of the input. Without a terminal, the guest agent closes the input of the command. With a terminal, it sends the end-of-file character, Ctrl-D. |
| `ExecResponse.resize`          | node  | a new size of the terminal                                                                                                                              |
| `ExecResponse.signal`          | node  | a signal for the process group of the command, by name, for example `SIGINT`. The guest agent ignores a name that it does not know.                     |
| `ExecResponse.control`         | node  | from version 2 on, the copy of an `ExecControl` that the node sent on `Link`                                                                            |

From version 2 on, the node sends `resize` and `signal` as `ExecControl` on `Link` instead. On `Exec`, they wait behind the input that the command did not read yet. On `Link`, they reach a command that reads no input at once. The node queues each `ExecControl` for `Link`, at most 64 for each link. A guest agent that reads `Link` slowly never blocks the node: once the queue is full, the node refuses the next resize or signal, and `Process.Resize` or `Process.Signal` returns an error. The client of the exec does not learn of the refusal. The node logs `a resize or a signal of an exec did not reach the guest agent` at level warn, with `component=access`, `machine`, `err`, and `missed`, at most once a minute for each exec. A guest agent of version 2 or later takes them on both paths. An `ExecControl` for an exec whose command did not start yet waits for the start, and the guest agent applies it then, in order. At most 16 wait for each exec, and the guest agent drops the next one.

`Link` and `Exec` are two calls. So the guest agent can read a control on `Link` after the input that came after it on `Exec`. A shell can then print the old size of the terminal. The node prevents this with a copy of each `ExecControl` that it queued. It sends the copies as `ExecResponse.control` at once, and always before the next `stdin` or `stdin_eof`. A resize right after a resize replaces the copy of the older one while that copy waits.

The guest agent keeps the highest `seq` that it applied for each exec. It ignores a control whose `seq` is not higher. So the first copy to arrive takes effect, and the other does nothing. A `seq` of 0 comes from an older node, and the guest agent always applies that control. The result: a resize or a signal takes effect before any input that the node sends after `Process.Resize` or `Process.Signal` returns. A guest agent from an older image ignores the copies and keeps the old order.

The copies wait only while the guest agent reads no messages of the exec. From version 3 on, they also wait for the credit of the call ([Credit of an exec](#credit-of-an-exec)). At most 64 copies wait for each exec. Once 64 wait, the node refuses the next resize or signal, and `Process.Resize` or `Process.Signal` returns an error. A resize right after a waiting resize replaces it, so the node still takes it. The node logs the refusal as a control that did not reach the guest agent.

#### Credit of an exec

The HTTP/2 server of Go queues the WINDOW_UPDATE of a call behind the DATA of the same call ([golang/go#82615](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/82615)). The node is the HTTP/2 server. While its input for a command waits for the window of the guest agent, the node sends no WINDOW_UPDATE on the call, although it reads all output. Then the guest agent can send no more than 256 KiB of output. A command that blocks on its output before it reads more input, such as `gzip` or `cat`, then stops for good. This happens when the input fills the queue of the guest agent (64 chunks, 2 MiB), the pipe of the command, and the window of the call.

From version 3 on, the node sends on credit:

* The node keeps at most 128 KiB in flight on the call (`protocol.ExecCredit`), half of the window of the guest agent. A message costs its size as `proto.Size` counts it, plus 32 (`protocol.ExecMessageCost`). One message costs at most 96 KiB, so it always fits next to the part that the guest agent did not ack yet. A send that needs more waits until an ack comes or the command ends.
* The guest agent counts the cost of each message that it takes off the call. Once the count reaches 32 KiB (`protocol.ExecAckAfter`), it sends the count in `ExecRequest.read`. It sends from its own goroutine, so a wait of the output never holds back the input. It sends no ack after the exit.
* The node clamps each ack to 128 KiB and never lets the count in flight go below 0. A guest agent that acks more than it took, or before it took it, can only make the node wait for HTTP/2 flow control on its own call, as before version 3. The calls of other machines never see its acks.
* `Process.Signal` refuses a name of more than 32 bytes (`protocol.MaxSignalName`), and each input message holds at most 32 KiB. So every message costs at least its bytes on the wire.
* The node takes the acks in its reader of the call, behind the output. So a consumer of the output that stops reading stops the input too, but no command can stop its own output.

On version 2 and before, the node sends without a bound, and such a command can still stop. `TestExecWritesBeforeItReads` checks a command that writes 1 MiB before it reads 8 MiB of input. `TestExecCopiesBothWays` checks 4 MiB through `cat` with and without the credit. `TestExecWritesBeforeItReadsThroughEveryHop` runs the same command through the control role, the control channel, and the guest link. It needs the credit of both hops ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#credit-of-a-data-stream)).

`ExecExit` reports the end:

| Case                                                                                                                                         | `code`                            | `signal`                        | `error`    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------- |
| The command exited                                                                                                                           | its exit code                     | empty                           | empty      |
| A signal ended the command                                                                                                                   | 128 plus the number of the signal | the name, for example `SIGTERM` | empty      |
| The program is not in the `PATH`                                                                                                             | `127`                             | empty                           | the reason |
| The command did not start for another reason, for example an unknown user, a missing working directory, or a file without execute permission | `126`                             | empty                           | the reason |

When the node ends the call before the exit, it also sends `CancelAttach` with the attach ID on `Link`. The guest agent then sends `SIGTERM` to the process group of the command. After 2 s, it sends `SIGKILL` to a command that still runs. This works also for a command that reads no input and writes no output. Each command leads its own process group, so the signals also reach its children. The guest agent sends no signal after it reaps the command, because the kernel can then give its group ID to another process. A background child can keep the output of a command open. So after the exit, the guest agent waits at most 2 s for the rest of the output.

### Upload

`UploadStart` describes one upload into the machine:

| Field     | Default       | Description                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path`    | required      | The target. A relative path starts at the home directory of the user.                                                                                                       |
| `archive` | `false`       | The data is a tar stream of the contents of a directory. If the directory at `path` is missing, the guest agent creates it. Otherwise the data is the contents of one file. |
| `mode`    | `0644`        | The permission bits of a file. An archive carries the bits of each entry.                                                                                                   |
| `user`    | the main user | The user that owns the new files and directories.                                                                                                                           |

The guest agent sends the attach ID in `UploadRequest.attach_id` first. The node sends the data in `UploadResponse.data` messages, then `UploadResponse.eof`. The guest agent answers with `UploadRequest.result`, an `UploadResult`. Its field `error` is empty after an upload that succeeded.

A file upload writes a temporary file in the target directory, then renames it to the target in one step. So a reader never sees a part of the file, and a failed upload leaves no file. An upload to the path of a directory fails.

An archive upload writes regular files, directories, symlinks, and hard links. It skips other entry types. Every entry stays inside the target directory, also through a symlink in the archive. An entry that leaves it fails the upload. The guest agent keeps only the permission bits of each entry, never set-user-ID or set-group-ID bits, and keeps the modification time of files.

### Download

`DownloadStart` describes one download from the machine:

| Field  | Default       | Description                                                           |
| ------ | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path` | required      | The source. A relative path starts at the home directory of the user. |
| `user` | the main user | The user whose home directory a relative path starts at.              |

The guest agent sends the attach ID in `DownloadRequest.attach_id` first. Then it sends `DownloadRequest.info`, a `DownloadInfo`, then the data in `DownloadRequest.data` messages, then ends its side of the call. The node answers with an empty `DownloadResponse`. `DownloadInfo` holds:

| Field     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `archive` | The source is a directory, and the data is a tar stream of its contents. Otherwise it is the contents of one file.                                                                                                  |
| `mode`    | The permission bits of the file or the directory.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `size`    | The size of a file in bytes. The guest agent sends no more than this, also for a file that grows. The node fails the download at the first byte over this size, or at an end before this size. Zero for an archive. |

An archive holds regular files, directories, and symlinks, with names relative to the directory. It skips devices, sockets, and pipes. When the guest agent fails, it sends `DownloadRequest.error` and nothing more. The node limits the size of a download, not the guest agent: see `MaxBytes` below.

### Rights

The guest agent runs as root, but a file copy runs with the file system rights of the user of the copy: its user ID, its group ID, and its groups. The agent sets them on one thread with `setfsuid`, `setfsgid`, and `setgroups`. So a copy cannot read or write a file that its user cannot read or write. This also holds for a path through a symlink that the user made, for example a link from the home directory to `/etc`. New files belong to the user. Exec runs as its user.

## Threat model

The link key keeps a process that poses as the node from getting the proof of the guest, or from pushing a configuration. It also keeps a process outside the machine from posing as the guest, because each microVM has its own vsock device socket. It does not keep a process inside the machine away from the key: every process in the guest can read the metadata service, and the main user has sudo. A process in the machine with the key can pose as the guest agent of its own machine only.

## Node API

The executor of each machine uses the Go package `internal/node/guestlink` ([the node executor](/reference/executor/)). One `Server` serves one boot of one machine.

| Function                                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Listen(path, options...)`                        | Listens on the unix socket `path`, and first removes a socket file that a stopped node left. The option `SocketMode(mode)` sets the permission bits of the socket file, and `SocketOwner(uid, gid)` sets its owner. Firecracker connects to the socket from its jail as the user of the jailer, so it needs write permission.                                         |
| `NewServer(Options)`                              | Returns a server for one link key and one first configuration.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `Server.Serve(listener)`                          | Accepts guest agent connections until `Close`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `Server.Close()`                                  | Stops the server and ends every call. It waits for the handlers of the server and for `OnState`, so nothing logs or calls `OnState` after it returns.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Server.Ready(ctx)`                               | Waits until the guest agent applied the current configuration on an authenticated link. If the configuration failed, it returns the error of the guest agent. The node uses it for the “running” state of a machine.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Server.State()`                                  | Returns `State`. It holds whether a link is up, the version, and the build version of the guest agent. It holds the boot ID and the run ID of the agent from the last hello. It also holds the current and the applied generation, the configuration error, and the count of skipped env values. Last, it holds the last status of the guest and the last link error. |
| `Server.UpdateConfig(ctx, config)`                | Makes `config` the configuration, pushes it, and waits until the guest agent applied it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Server.RunStartCommand(ctx)`                     | Asks the guest agent to run the start command again.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Server.Exec(ctx, ExecOptions)`                   | Starts a command. `Process.Wait` returns its `ExecExit`. `Process.Resize` sets the terminal size. `Process.Signal` sends a signal by name. Both use `ExecControl` from version 2 on. When `ctx` ends first, the guest agent stops the command with `SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL`.                                                                                         |
| `Server.Upload(ctx, UploadStart, reader)`         | Uploads the data of the reader.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `Server.Download(ctx, DownloadStart, options...)` | Returns a `Download`, which holds the `DownloadInfo` and reads the data. The option `MaxBytes(n)` caps the data, for example at 4 MB for a laptop. A file over the cap fails before any data, and an archive fails at the cap, both with `ErrTooLarge`.                                                                                                               |

| Option             | Default                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Key`              | required                   | The link key, 32 bytes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `Config`           | empty                      | The first configuration.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `NodeVersion`      | empty                      | The build version of `hopboxd` for `NodeHello`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Versions`         | the versions of this build | The versions that the node speaks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `OnState`          | none                       | Gets each new `State`, in order, on a goroutine of the server. It can call the methods of the server. It gets no state after `Close` returns. When `OnState` falls behind, a new state replaces a queued state with the same `Connected` value, so every connect and disconnect stays in the queue. |
| `OnLog`            | none                       | Gets each `LogEntry`, in order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `HandshakeTimeout` | 10 s                       | The longest wait for the hello, for the proof, and for the attach ID of each call.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `AttachTimeout`    | 10 s                       | The longest wait for the guest agent to open a call after an `Attach`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

An error that the guest agent reports for a file copy has the type `GuestError`. A call that needs the link while no guest agent is connected fails with `ErrNotConnected`.

# hopbox-guest

> The commands, flags, files, systemd unit, logs, and exit status of the guest agent hopbox-guest.

`hopbox-guest` is the guest agent of hopbox. It runs inside every machine. Images ship it. Users and operators do not install it.

The guest agent keeps the guest link to the node open ([Guest link](/reference/guest-link/)). It applies the configuration that the node pushes, runs the start command, and runs exec and file copy for the node.

## Usage

```sh
hopbox-guest [--log-level=LEVEL] <command> [flags]
```

When you run `hopbox-guest` without a command, it prints its help and an error, and exits with status 80.

## Global flags

A global flag goes before or after the command.

| Flag           | Type  | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------- | ----- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--log-level`  | level | `info`  | The lowest level of the log records that `hopbox-guest` writes. The values are `debug`, `info`, `warn`, and `error`. Case does not matter. A value can also carry an offset, for example `info+2`, as in Go’s `log/slog`. |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool  | `false` | Prints the help of `hopbox-guest`, or of the command that it follows, and exits.                                                                                                                                          |

## Logs

`hopbox-guest` writes its logs to standard error, in the same JSON format as `hopboxd` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#logs)). Under systemd, standard error goes to journald. The output of the start command does not go to these logs. It goes over the guest link to the log of the machine.

| Message                                                                              | Level | Fields                                      | When                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `prepare the SSH host keys`                                                          | error | `err`                                       | At the start, the agent did not write the sshd drop-in, make the host key, or read the host keys. The agent goes on with the steps that worked.                     |
| `created the SSH host key`                                                           | info  |                                             | The image had no ed25519 SSH host key, so the agent made one.                                                                                                       |
| `tell systemd that the agent is ready`                                               | warn  | `err`                                       | The ready notice to systemd failed.                                                                                                                                 |
| `guest agent started`                                                                | info  | `link`, `metadata_url`, `interface`, `user` | The agent starts its guest link.                                                                                                                                    |
| `guest link up`                                                                      | info  | `version`, `node_version`                   | The node accepted the handshake.                                                                                                                                    |
| `guest link down, reconnecting`                                                      | warn  | `err`                                       | A link that was up for at least 1 s dropped. The agent opens a new link at once.                                                                                    |
| `guest link failed`                                                                  | warn  | `err`, `retry_in`                           | A link did not come up, or dropped within 1 s. The agent waits `retry_in` before the next try. The wait starts at 100 ms and doubles after each failure, up to 5 s. |
| `ignored an older configuration`                                                     | warn  | `generation`, `applied`                     | The node pushed a configuration with a lower generation than the one that the agent applied.                                                                        |
| `configuration applied`                                                              | info  | `generation`                                | The agent applied a configuration.                                                                                                                                  |
| `configuration failed`                                                               | error | `generation`, `err`                         | The agent did not apply a configuration. It sends the error to the node.                                                                                            |
| `left an env var out of the machine`                                                 | warn  | `err`                                       | An env var of the configuration breaks the rules of [Files](#files).                                                                                                |
| `ignored a guest link message that this agent does not know`                         | warn  |                                             | The node sent a message of a newer protocol.                                                                                                                        |
| `ignored an attach with a bad ID`                                                    | warn  | `size`                                      | An `Attach` message has an ID that is not 16 bytes long.                                                                                                            |
| `ignored an attach that this agent does not know`                                    | warn  |                                             | An `Attach` message names an operation of a newer protocol.                                                                                                         |
| `exec: attach failed`                                                                | warn  | `err`                                       | The agent did not send the attach ID on a new `Exec` call.                                                                                                          |
| `exec: send the exit`                                                                | warn  | `err`                                       | The agent did not send the exit of a command to the node.                                                                                                           |
| `upload: attach failed`                                                              | warn  | `err`                                       | The agent did not send the attach ID on a new `Upload` call.                                                                                                        |
| `upload: the node ended the call`                                                    | warn  | `path`, `err`                               | The node ended an upload before its end.                                                                                                                            |
| `upload failed`                                                                      | warn  | `path`, `err`                               | The agent did not write an upload. It sends the error to the node.                                                                                                  |
| `upload: send the result`                                                            | warn  | `err`                                       | The agent did not send the result of an upload to the node.                                                                                                         |
| `download: attach failed`                                                            | warn  | `err`                                       | The agent did not send the attach ID on a new `Download` call.                                                                                                      |
| `download failed`                                                                    | warn  | `path`, `err`                               | The agent did not read or send a download.                                                                                                                          |
| `the boot of the guest did not finish within <duration>, so the start command waits` | warn  |                                             | The boot did not reach `multi-user.target` within 2 min. The status of the start command holds the same text.                                                       |
| `wait for the end of the boot`                                                       | warn  | `err`                                       | The check of `multi-user.target` failed. Unless the agent stops, the start command then starts.                                                                     |
| `start command started`                                                              | info  | `pid`, `run`                                | The start command started. `run` counts the runs of this boot.                                                                                                      |
| `start command failed to start`                                                      | error | `err`                                       | The agent did not start the start command, for example for an unknown main user. The status of the start command is `FAILED`.                                       |
| `start command wait`                                                                 | warn  | `err`                                       | The wait for the end of the start command failed with an error other than its exit status.                                                                          |
| `start command exited`                                                               | info  | `code`, `signal`                            | The start command ended.                                                                                                                                            |

## Commands

| Command   | Description                                                                           |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `run`     | Runs the guest agent until it gets `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`.                             |
| `version` | Prints the version of `hopbox-guest`. See [the version command](/reference/version/). |

### run

```sh
hopbox-guest run [--link=ADDR] [--metadata-url=URL] [--interface=NAME] [--user=NAME]
```

| Flag             | Type    | Default                  | Description                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--link`         | address | `vsock://2:10240`        | The address of the node. `vsock://CID:PORT` dials vsock. `unix:///path` dials a unix socket, for tests and local runs.                                               |
| `--metadata-url` | URL     | `http://169.254.169.254` | The base URL of the metadata service that holds the link key. If the host of the URL is an IPv4 link-local address, the agent first routes it on `--interface`.      |
| `--interface`    | name    | `eth0`                   | The network interface that the network configuration sets up. The agent also reaches the metadata service through it.                                                |
| `--user`         | name    | `user`                   | The main Linux user. The start command runs as this user. If the node names no user, exec and file copy use this user. The group of this user can read the env file. |

The command does these steps:

1. It writes the sshd drop-in. If the image has no ed25519 SSH host key, it creates one. Each machine then has its own host key.
2. Under systemd, it tells systemd that it is ready. sshd starts after this step, so sshd always has a host key and the drop-in.
3. It reads the link key from the metadata service, dials the node, and does the handshake.
4. It applies each configuration that the node pushes, and starts the start command as [Start command](#start-command) says.
5. After a drop of the link, it reads the key again and opens a new link at once.

On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`, it kills the start command and exits with status 0.

The agent must run as root. Root can set the host name and the network, write the files below, and switch users for exec. Outside Linux, the host name and the network setup fail with an error, and the rest works.

Example, on a local unix socket with a local metadata service:

```sh
hopbox-guest run --link=unix:///tmp/box1.sock_10240 --metadata-url=http://127.0.0.1:8169
```

## Files

The agent writes these files in the guest. Each write replaces the file in one rename, so a reader never sees a part of a file.

| Path                                 | Mode | Owner                        | Content                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------ | ---- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `/etc/hostname`                      | 0644 | root                         | The host name, from the configuration.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `/etc/hosts`                         | 0644 | root                         | The agent points the line of `127.0.1.1` at the host name, as Debian and Ubuntu do. It keeps every other line.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `/etc/resolv.conf`                   | 0644 | root                         | One `nameserver` line for each resolver of the configuration. The file replaces a symlink at this path, for example the link of systemd-resolved.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `/etc/hopbox/env`                    | 0640 | root, group of the main user | The env vars and secrets of the machine, one `export NAME='value'` line each, in POSIX shell syntax. Only root and the group of the main user can read it, because it holds secrets. The agent checks each name with the rules of `domain.ValidateEnvVarName` ([the env var API](/reference/vars-api/#names-and-values)), and each value for a NUL byte. A value that fails stays out of the file, and out of the env of exec and the start command. The agent logs a warning for it, and writes the other values. |
| `/etc/profile.d/hopbox.sh`           | 0644 | root                         | A script. If the user can read `/etc/hopbox/env`, the script reads it. Every login shell runs the script, so the env vars and secrets reach every login shell. It holds no values.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `/etc/hopbox/authorized_keys`        | 0644 | root                         | The keys of the configuration, for example the key of the SSH front door. Only root can change it, so no user can remove the key of the front door.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/hopbox.conf` | 0644 | root                         | `AuthorizedKeysFile .ssh/authorized_keys .ssh/authorized_keys2 /etc/hopbox/authorized_keys`. The first two are the default of Ubuntu. sshd then reads the keys of the configuration for every Linux user, next to the keys of each user. Ubuntu reads this folder at the top of `sshd_config`, and sshd keeps the first value of a setting, so this value wins. At each start, the agent restores this content.                                                                                                    |
| `/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key`      | 0600 | root                         | The SSH host key. If the image has no such key, the agent writes it. Otherwise it keeps the key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub`  | 0644 | root                         | The public part of that key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

The agent reads `/etc/passwd` and `/etc/group` for the user ID, the groups, the home directory, and the login shell of each user. It reports every `/etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key.pub` key to the node.

Example of `/etc/hopbox/env`:

```sh
# Written by hopbox-guest from the env vars and secrets of the machine.
# hopbox-guest rewrites this file at each configuration.
export DATABASE_URL='postgres://db1/app'
export GREETING='it'\''s here'
```

## Kernel changes

The agent makes these changes through netlink. They need Linux.

| Change                                                                                                                                                      | When                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The kernel host name.                                                                                                                                       | The configuration has a host name.                                                                      |
| The interface comes up and gets its MTU. The configured address becomes its only IPv4 address. The default route goes through the gateway, on-link.         | The configuration has a network.                                                                        |
| The configured IPv6 address becomes the only global IPv6 address of the interface. The IPv6 default route goes through the IPv6 gateway, such as `fe80::1`. | The network has `address6` ([Guest link](/reference/guest-link/)).                                      |
| The interface comes up and gets a route to the metadata service. If it has no IPv4 address, it gets `169.254.0.2/32`.                                       | The metadata service has an IPv4 link-local address. The change comes before each read of the link key. |

## Start command

The start command runs with `/bin/sh -c` as the main user, in the home directory of that user. If the home directory does not exist, it runs in `/`. Its env holds two groups of values. A value of the second group replaces a value of the first.

1. The login basics: `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `PATH`, and `LANG`. `LANG` comes from `/etc/default/locale`, with the default `C.UTF-8`.
2. The env vars and secrets of the machine.

Two conditions must hold before the start command starts:

* The agent applied its first configuration without an error, so the env file is in place.
* systemd reports `multi-user.target` as active, so the services of the image, such as Docker, run. Until then, the state of the start command is `WAITING`. Without systemd, the agent does not wait. After 2 min of waiting, the agent logs a warning once and puts it in the `error` field of the status.

The agent sends each line of its output to the node, and reports its exit. The agent starts the start command in these cases only:

| Case                                              | What happens                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The first configuration of a boot                 | The start command starts, after the wait above.                                                    |
| A new configuration, or a new link                | Nothing. The start command keeps its state.                                                        |
| `RunStartCommand` from the node                   | The start command starts again, unless it runs. The node sends it for the restart policy “always”. |
| A restart of the agent, for example after a crash | systemd stops the start command with the agent. The new agent starts it again, as for a new boot.  |

When the agent stops, it kills the start command and its children.

## systemd unit

The default image installs the unit `images/default/rootfs/usr/lib/systemd/system/hopbox-guest.service` at `/usr/lib/systemd/system/hopbox-guest.service`, with the binary at `/usr/local/bin/hopbox-guest`. It enables the unit. [Default image](/reference/default-image/) lists the other files of the image.

| Setting                                              | Value                                                                                                                               | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Type`                                               | `notify`                                                                                                                            | The agent sends `READY=1` after the SSH host key exists.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `ExecStart`                                          | `/usr/local/bin/hopbox-guest run`                                                                                                   | The default flags fit a Firecracker machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Restart`                                            | `always`, after 1 s                                                                                                                 | The node cannot reach the machine without the agent.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `KillMode`                                           | `control-group`                                                                                                                     | A restart of the agent stops the start command and exec. The new agent runs the start command again.                                                                                                                                             |
| `DefaultDependencies`                                | `no`                                                                                                                                | The agent sets up the network itself, so it starts before `network-pre.target`.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Order                                                | after `local-fs.target` and `systemd-sysctl.service`. Before `network-pre.target`, `ssh.service`, `sshd.service`, and `ssh.socket`. | The values of `/etc/sysctl.d`, such as `kernel.modules_disabled`, hold before the agent runs a command. sshd starts with a host key.                                                                                                             |
| `WantedBy`                                           | `multi-user.target`                                                                                                                 | The agent runs in every normal boot.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `RestrictAddressFamilies`, `SystemCallArchitectures` | empty, from the drop-in `hopbox-guest.service.d/60-hopbox-allow-vsock.conf`                                                         | The image removes `AF_VSOCK` from every other service. The agent dials the node over vsock, so its drop-in undoes that ([Default image](/reference/default-image/#no-vsock-for-services)). The commands that the agent starts keep this freedom. |

## Exit status

| Status | Meaning                                                                                     |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0      | The command succeeded, or `run` stopped on a signal.                                        |
| 1      | The command failed, for example on a bad `--link` address.                                  |
| 80     | The command line is not valid, for example an unknown command or flag, or a bad flag value. |

# hopboxd

> The commands, flags, logs, and exit status of hopboxd, with the start and stop order of hopboxd run, the leader jobs, install, upgrade and its rollback, enroll, preflight, and the admin commands for tokens, servers, admin API keys, orgs, machines, and images.

`hopboxd` is the server binary of hopbox. It runs on every server of an install.

## Usage

```sh
hopboxd [--log-level=LEVEL] <command> [flags]
```

When you run `hopboxd` without a command, it prints its help and an error, and exits with status 80.

## Global flags

A global flag goes before or after the command.

| Flag           | Type  | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------- | ----- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--log-level`  | level | `info`  | The lowest level of the log records that `hopboxd` writes. The values are `debug`, `info`, `warn`, and `error`. Case does not matter. A value can also carry an offset, for example `info+2`, as in Go’s `log/slog`. |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool  | `false` | Prints the help of `hopboxd`, or of the command that it follows, and exits.                                                                                                                                          |

Example:

```sh
hopboxd --log-level=debug version
```

## Commands

| Command                               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `run`                                 | Runs the roles of this server until it gets `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`. See [run](#run).                                                                                                                                           |
| `install`                             | Installs the release of this `hopboxd` on this server, or brings the install up to date. See [install](#install).                                                                                                             |
| `upgrade`                             | Upgrades this server to the release of a bundle file, or rolls back to the previous release. See [upgrade](#upgrade).                                                                                                         |
| `enroll`                              | Makes this server a part of an install with an enrollment token. See [enroll](#enroll).                                                                                                                                       |
| `preflight`                           | Checks that this server can run machines. See [preflight](#preflight).                                                                                                                                                        |
| `admin kek rotate`                    | Adds a new key-encryption key through the admin socket, for an install with one control server. See [admin](#admin).                                                                                                          |
| `admin kek stage`                     | Adds a staged key-encryption key, which seals nothing yet.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `admin kek promote`                   | Makes a staged key-encryption key the current one on every control server.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `admin kek list`                      | Lists the key-encryption keys and the sealed values of each.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `admin kek rewrap`                    | Moves every sealed value to the current key-encryption key.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `admin config get`                    | Prints the settings of the install through the admin socket.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `admin config set`                    | Changes settings of the install through the admin socket.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `admin config smtp get`               | Prints the SMTP config, without its password.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `admin config smtp set`               | Replaces the SMTP config.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `admin config smtp clear`             | Removes the SMTP config.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `admin config oauth get`              | Prints the GitHub and Google clients for sign-in, without their secrets, with the redirect URIs. `admin config oauth` alone does the same.                                                                                    |
| `admin config oauth set`              | Sets the client of one sign-in provider.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `admin config oauth clear`            | Removes the client of one sign-in provider.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `admin certificate get`               | Prints the certificate of the install, without its key, and the state of the ACME job.                                                                                                                                        |
| `admin login-link`                    | Prints a one-time sign-in link for the first instance admin.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `admin instance-admin list`           | Lists the instance admins.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `admin instance-admin grant`          | Makes an account an instance admin.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `admin instance-admin revoke`         | Takes the instance admin role from an account.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `admin account sign-in-method list`   | Lists the sign-in methods of an account.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `admin account sign-in-method remove` | Removes a sign-in method of an account, to recover its sign-in.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `admin enrollment-token create`       | Makes an enrollment token for a new server through the admin socket.                                                                                                                                                          |
| `admin server list`                   | Lists the enrolled servers through the admin socket.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `admin server get`                    | Prints one server through the admin socket.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `admin server cordon`                 | Stops new machines from landing on a server, through the admin socket.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `admin server uncordon`               | Lets new machines land on a cordoned server again, through the admin socket.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `admin server set-labels`             | Replaces the labels of a server, through the admin socket.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `admin server drain`                  | Moves every machine of a server to other nodes, then decommissions the server, through the admin socket.                                                                                                                      |
| `admin server remove-role`            | Starts the removal of the roles edge, dns, node, or more than one from a running server, through the admin socket.                                                                                                            |
| `admin server cancel-remove-role`     | Ends the pending removal of roles from a server that cannot finish, through the admin socket.                                                                                                                                 |
| `admin server cancel-drain`           | Ends the drain of a server, which turns cordoned or ready as it was before the drain, through the admin socket.                                                                                                               |
| `admin server decommission`           | Takes a server out of the install for good, through the admin socket.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `admin control list`                  | Lists the control processes of the install, live or not, through the admin socket.                                                                                                                                            |
| `admin pool create`                   | Adds a pool of servers.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `admin pool get`                      | Prints one pool.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `admin pool list`                     | Lists the pools.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `admin pool delete`                   | Deletes a pool without servers and without live sizes.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `admin size create`                   | Adds a size of machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `admin size get`                      | Prints one size.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `admin size list`                     | Lists the sizes.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `admin size retire`                   | Stops new machines of a size.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `admin org list`                      | Lists every org of the install, with metadata only.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `admin org suspend`                   | Suspends an org.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `admin org unsuspend`                 | Ends the suspension of an org.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `admin org set-limits`                | Replaces the usage limits of one org.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `admin org default-limits get`        | Prints the default usage limits of every org.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `admin org default-limits set`        | Changes the default usage limits of every org.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `admin machine list`                  | Lists the machines of every org, or of one org, with metadata only.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `admin machine stop`                  | Stops any machine, also in a suspended org, and waits for it.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `admin machine delete`                | Deletes any machine, also in a suspended org, and waits for it.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `admin machine move`                  | Moves any machine cold to another node. It returns at once. With `--cancel`, it ends the move of the machine that runs. With `--give-back` too, it asks the target node to give back a machine that a failed move left there. |
| `admin machine moves`                 | Lists the cold moves of one machine, or of every machine, newest first.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `admin image register`                | Adds an image from its `artifact.json`.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `admin image list`                    | Lists the images of the install.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
