| `admin admin-key create`              | Makes an admin API key and prints it once.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `admin admin-key register`            | Makes an admin API key from the SHA-256 of a key that you made.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `admin admin-key list`                | Lists the admin API keys.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `admin admin-key revoke`              | Deletes an admin API key.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `admin mail list`                     | Lists the mail files that the file mail transport wrote on this server.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `admin mail show`                     | Prints one mail file, with its link whole.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `admin maintenance on`                | Turns maintenance mode of the install on, and waits until the writes, the control channels, and the leader jobs that ran have ended in every live control process.                                                            |
| `admin maintenance off`               | Turns maintenance mode of the install off.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `admin db export`                     | Copies the control store of this server from the bundled Postgres to an empty external Postgres, in maintenance mode, and prints the config lines for it.                                                                     |
| `version`                             | Prints the version of `hopboxd`. See [the version command](/reference/version/).                                                                                                                                              |
| `stop-guest`                          | Shuts down the guest of a machine unit. systemd runs it as the `ExecStop` of the unit. The help does not list it. See [stop-guest](#stop-guest).                                                                              |

## run

```sh
hopboxd run [--config=PATH]
```

`run` reads the bootstrap config, starts the roles that the config lists, and runs until it gets `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`. Then it stops the roles and exits with status 0. [The bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/) lists the keys of the bootstrap config.

| Flag       | Type | Default                    | Description                |
| ---------- | ---- | -------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `--config` | path | `/etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml` | The bootstrap config file. |

First, `run` starts the metrics listener and the host firewall. Then it starts the units of the control role, the DNS role, the edge role, and the node role, in this order. Then it starts the unit of the control channel. A role that the config does not list has no units. Each unit starts after the unit before it is ready.

| Order | Unit                | What it does | ----- | ------------------- | It installs the table again after a flush, and after a change of its sets or of the uplink of an edge server. Its stop keeps the table, so the firewall holds while `hopboxd` is down. With `postgres.url`, it starts no Postgres. It reads the CA file and the password file of the external Postgres, and the next units connect to it over TLS ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#external-postgres)). | 3     | `store`             | Opens the connection pool of the control store and runs the migrations ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#schema-migrations)). Then it checks the key files. It first applies a promote of a key-encryption key that happened while this process was down, and then opens the install CA of the control store with the key files of this server. It makes the CA when none exists. If the key files cannot open it, the start fails with `control: the key files in <dir> do not open the install CA of the control store: <error>. Copy the key files of a running control server there`. A keyring without any key passes this check ([Sealing](/reference/sealing/#several-control-servers)). Then it imports the bootstrap admin API key from the file that `hopboxd install` can leave ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#the-bootstrap-admin-api-key)). Then it registers the default image of the release ([The default image of the release](#the-default-image-of-the-release)). Until its stop, it reads the schema of the store every 10 s. If a newer `hopboxd` applied a migration that does not run with this one, if the store lost its schema, or if 12 reads in a row fail, it stops `hopboxd`. 12 reads take about 2 minutes, which outlasts the failover of a managed PostgreSQL ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#two-releases-on-one-store)). The limit is safe only because of the fence below: a process that cannot reach the store fences itself within 15 s, long before the schema watch stops it, so it never writes while the other control processes no longer count it. The migration runner writes the first row of this control process in the table `control_processes` while it still holds the migration lock, right after the migrations and with the same check of the schema, so no newer `hopboxd` applies a migration that does not allow this one before the first row exists ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#schema-migrations)). At the end of the unit, it writes the full row and keeps it up to date until its stop ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#control_processes)). The row holds a new random ID for each start, the ID of the enrolled server of the same `hopboxd` or none, the host name, the URL of the internal listener, the release, the schema version, the key files and the staged key files that it can open, the key with which it seals, and the maintenance and drained flags. While its key dir has a staged file, or while it misses the promoted key, each renewal first applies the promote of the install ([Sealing](/reference/sealing/#several-control-servers)), as does each change event `keyring.kek_promoted`. The unit renews the row on a fixed ticker every 5 s. Each try takes at most 2 s, so a slow store never moves the next renewal. It also renews at once after a turn of maintenance mode, after the internal listener starts, at a change event of a promote of a KEK, and once at the end of a drain, when no call, control channel, or leader job of the process runs any more in maintenance mode. A row renewed in the last 20 s is live. Each renewal reads the schema of the store in the same transaction, and fails when the store no longer runs with this `hopboxd`, so a renewal that works means both ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#two-releases-on-one-store)). A renewal that fails this way fences the process and stops `hopboxd` at once. When no renewal worked for 15 s (the 20 s of the live window less a margin of 5 s, counted from the start of the last renewal that worked), the process fences itself before its row stops being live. While it is fenced, every listener of the API refuses every call, reads too, with `unavailable`, the header `Hopbox-Not-Run: 1`, the header `Retry-After: 30`, and the message `this control server lost the control store for a while, so it takes no call until it reaches the store again. Retry later, or through another control server`. Only gRPC health and reflection pass. The plain HTTP routes that maintenance mode refuses, such as the starts of the GitHub and Google sign-in, answer 503 with that message. No control channel and no leader job runs. A leader that stays fenced for 15 s gives up its lease, and a fenced process does not try for the leader lock ([Leader jobs](#leader-jobs)). The fence lifts at the next renewal that works. `admin control list` shows the rows. | 5 s          |
| 4     | `events`            | Reads the change events of the control store from the head ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#subscribe)). It feeds them to the watches and the lifecycle waits of the machine API in this process ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#change-events)). So they see each change, also one of another control process or of a node. If the reader stops by itself, `hopboxd` stops. | 10    | `edge`              | The edge role ([the edge role](/reference/edge/)). At its start, it opens the HTTPS listener at `edge.https_listen` and the HTTP listener at `edge.http_listen`. At its stop, it closes the listeners, gives the open requests 2 s, and then ends the rest, also the streams and the WebSockets. | 11    | `machines`          | The node role. It first sets up the node network: it replaces the nftables table `inet hopbox_node` with one that holds the tap devices of the machines that run, and turns on IPv4 and IPv6 forwarding ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#at-the-start-and-at-the-stop-of-hopboxd)). Until its stop, it watches the table, and installs it again after a flush. It adds the guest kernel of `vmm.kernel` to the kernel cache. It starts the executors of the machines with the Firecracker driver ([the node executor](/reference/executor/), [the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/)). It also starts the store of the machine logs ([Machine logs](/reference/machine-logs/)). Once the server has a mesh address, it serves the disks of the cold moves on port 7444 of that address ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#the-disk-listener)). At its start, the executors attach to the microVMs that run. At its stop, the executors end their actions at once. Every microVM keeps running, because it runs in a systemd unit of its own. The unit of each machine runs [stop-guest](#stop-guest) at its stop, and is ordered before `hopboxd.service`.
