| 12    | `channel`           | Keeps the control channel of this server to one of the live control servers that the control role sent, kept in `<data_dir>/server/control-urls`, or to one of `channel.control_urls`, over mutual TLS. After a lost or refused channel, it dials the next URL ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#the-agent)). If the control role runs in the same `hopboxd`, the channel still goes over TLS ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/)). It hands the zones that the control role sends to the `dns` unit. It hands the certificate, the routes, and the access changes to the `edge` unit. It hands the specs of the machines to the executors of the `machines` unit, and the machine streams to its handlers. It also keeps the mesh device `hbm0` ([the mesh](/reference/mesh/)). It checks the device at its start, before the first heartbeat, and then every 2 s. It hands the device the mesh that the control role sends. At its start, it removes what the IPv6 block of a release before N29 left on the server, and tries again every 2 s until nothing is left ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/#what-the-ipv6-block-left)). It also keeps the egress tunnels `hbe*`, with a check at its start and then every 2 s ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/#checks-a-restart-and-a-reboot)). It hands them each mesh. On an edge server, it also checks the uplink at its start and then every 2 s. An edge server says `egress_exit` in each heartbeat only while its tunnel is ready and its uplink works ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/#the-uplink-of-an-egress-edge)). On an edge server with `edge.public_ipv4`, `edge.floating_addresses`, or `edge.public_ipv6`, it keeps the floating addresses on the uplink and the peer address as the source of the default route, with a check at its start, after each change of an address or a route, and every 2 s ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#the-check-of-the-uplink)). Its start returns after these first checks. Before the enrollment of the server, it waits for the identity in `<data_dir>/server`. So `run` can start before [enroll](#enroll).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | 5 s          |

Unit 1 runs for every role. Units 2 to 8 belong to the control role and unit 9 to the DNS role. Unit 10 belongs to the edge role and unit 11 to the node role. Unit 12 runs on a server that enrolls: one with a role other than `control`. Unit 13, `systemd notify`, runs for every role:

| Order | Unit             | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Stop timeout |
| ----- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| 13    | `systemd notify` | Sends `READY=1` to the socket of `NOTIFY_SOCKET` at its start, and `STOPPING=1` at its stop ([sd_notify(3)](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/sd_notify.html)). Without `NOTIFY_SOCKET`, it does nothing. It starts last. So the unit `hopboxd.service` of `Type=notify` becomes active only after every other unit is ready ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#hopboxdservice)). If it cannot send, the start fails. | 1 s          |

On a server with only the node role, `run` starts the metrics listener and the `host firewall` unit. Then it starts the `machines` unit, the `channel` unit, and the `systemd notify` unit. On a server with only the DNS role, it starts the `dns` unit in place of the `machines` unit. On a server with the edge role, it starts the `edge` unit before the `channel` unit. So what the channel gets for these roles always has a server.

`run` stops the units in the reverse order. First it stops `systemd notify`, then `channel`, `machines`, `edge`, and `dns`. Then it stops the units of the control role, from the admin socket to Postgres, then the host firewall, and last the metrics listener. So no unit stops before a unit that needs it. A server can have the control role and a role that enrolls. Then the control role sees the channel of its own server close before its listeners stop. Each stop has the timeout in the table:

* The `channel` unit closes the control channel and waits for its loop and its checks to end. It keeps the device `hbm0` and the egress tunnels. So their traffic goes on while `hopboxd` is down.
* The `machines` unit ends the actions of the executors, closes the guest links, and closes the files of the machine logs. It stops no microVM, and keeps the node network.
* The `edge` unit closes its listeners and gives the open requests 2 s. Then it cancels the rest: the streams, the WebSockets, and the long calls. At the timeout, it closes every connection ([the edge role](/reference/edge/)).
* The `dns` unit closes its sockets and waits for the queries in flight.
* The `api`, `internal listener`, and `admin socket` units stop taking new connections and wait for the running unary calls. They end every open stream at once, because a stream has no natural end. They cancel the stream and end every read of its request body. So a stream that waits for the client, such as a reflection stream, ends too. A unary call that still reads its request body gets 2 s more. So a stalled upload cannot hold the stop. At the timeout, they close the rest ([the API server](/reference/api/#when-a-listener-stops)).
* The `leader election` unit ends the term of the leader and releases the leader lease.
* The `events` unit stops its reader of change events and closes its connection.
* The `store` unit stops the renewals of the row of this control process, and marks the row stopped, so no check waits for this process. The row stays until the sweep. Then it stops the schema watch and closes its connections.
* The `host firewall` unit ends its watch of the table, and keeps the table.
* The `postgres` unit asks for a fast shutdown. After 20 s, it asks for an immediate shutdown, and 5 s later it kills Postgres. With an external Postgres, it does nothing.

Only the units of the roles of the server run, so the sum of their timeouts depends on the roles. The unit `hopboxd.service` gives `hopboxd` 105 s to stop (`TimeoutStopSec=105s`, [Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#hopboxdservice)).

| Roles                            | Sum of the stop timeouts |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `control`                        | 83.1 s                   |
| `control`, `dns`                 | 89.1 s                   |
| `control`, `edge`                | 93.1 s                   |
| `control`, `dns`, `edge`         | 94.1 s                   |
| `control`, `node`                | 98.1 s                   |
| `control`, `node`, `dns`         | 99.1 s                   |
| `control`, `node`, `edge`        | 103.1 s                  |
| `control`, `node`, `dns`, `edge` | 104.1 s                  |
| `dns`                            | 12.1 s                   |
| `edge`                           | 16.1 s                   |
| `dns`, `edge`                    | 17.1 s                   |
| `node`                           | 21.1 s                   |
| `node`, `dns`                    | 22.1 s                   |
| `node`, `edge`                   | 26.1 s                   |
| `node`, `dns`, `edge`            | 27.1 s                   |

Each sum is under the 105 s of `hopboxd.service`.

If the install has no key-encryption key yet, the internal listener starts all the same. It then has no certificate, and logs `the internal listener has no certificate yet`. Until root makes the first key with [admin kek rotate](#admin-kek-rotate), it fails each TLS handshake ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/)).

If `run` gets `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM` while a unit starts, it stops the units that started, in the reverse order, and exits with status 0.

If a unit fails to start, `run` stops the units that started, in the reverse order, and exits with status 1. If a unit fails while it runs, for example when the API listener stops, `run` stops every unit and exits with status 1. A supervisor such as systemd then restarts `hopboxd`. A crash of Postgres alone does not stop `hopboxd`, because the supervisor of Postgres restarts it ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#start-restart-and-stop)).

### Leader jobs

The leader of the control role runs these jobs. In maintenance mode, the leader pauses every job, and keeps its lease ([the API server](/reference/api/#maintenance-mode)). It logs `maintenance mode paused the leader jobs` at level info, with `component=leader`. A fence of the process also pauses every job ([Run](#run)). If the fence lasts longer than one lease TTL (15 s), the leader gives up its lease, so another control process can lead. It logs `this process stays fenced, so it gives up the leader lease to a process that can run the leader jobs`. While it is fenced, the process does not try for the leader lock. When maintenance mode ends, the jobs start again as at the start of a term, with the sweep first and 20 s without a check of silent servers. The sweep runs once at the start of each term of the leader, and then every 10 minutes. The check of silent servers runs every 5 s. The auto-delete of idle machines and the return of SSH host keys run every minute. The check of silent servers skips the first 20 s of each term. In that time, the servers can dial again after a stop of the control role, before the leader marks any of them.

| Job                                   | Every    | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sweep of idempotency keys             | 10 min   | Deletes the expired idempotency keys ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#sweep-the-expired-keys)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Sweep of sign-ins                     | 10 min   | Deletes the ended sessions, and the magic links, login links, and OAuth flows that are older than 24 hours ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#sweep)). Deletes the expired CLI tokens, the ended CLI sign-ins, and the device sign-ins and failed device approvals that are older than 24 hours. Deletes the API keys and admin API keys that expired more than 30 days ago ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#sweep)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Sweep of control processes            | 10 min   | Deletes the rows of the control processes that were not renewed for 24 hours. They ended without their stop ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#control_processes)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Sweep of the fleet                    | 10 min   | Deletes the enrollment tokens that expired more than 1 day ago, and the server certificates that expired more than 1 day ago. It keeps the newest certificate of each server ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#enrollment_tokens)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Check of silent servers               | 5 s      | Marks `unresponsive` each `ready`, `cordoned`, `draining`, or `shutting_down` server whose last heartbeat is 20 s old or older: 4 missed heartbeats. The write checks the leader lease, so a leader that lost its lease writes nothing. Each server that it marks gets an audit entry `server.mark_unresponsive` with the actor `system` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#servers)). The next heartbeat of the server makes it `ready` again, or `cordoned`, or `draining` when the server has a drain ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Step of the drains                    | 5 s      | Takes the drain of each `draining` or `shutting_down` server one step on: it starts the cold moves off the server, at most 2 at once, names the machines that cannot move, and runs the empty checks ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#drain-of-a-node)). The first empty check turns the server `shutting_down`, with the audit entry `server.mark_shutting_down`. A check that finds it not empty turns it `draining` again, with `server.mark_draining`. The third empty check in a row, one minute after the second, decommissions the server, with the audit entry `server.decommission`. Both entries have the actor `system`. Every write checks the leader lease.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Step of the removals of the node role | 5 s      | Takes each pending removal of the role `node` one step on, after the step of the drains. It keeps the server cordoned, and starts the cold moves off the server, at most 2 at once. It names the machines that cannot move ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#removal-of-the-node-role)). It runs no empty check and no decommission. Every write checks the leader lease.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Sweep of invitations                  | 10 min   | Deletes the invitations to orgs that ended more than 24 hours ago, by a use, a revoke, or the expiry. It also deletes the records of their rate limits that are older than 24 hours ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#invitations)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Sweep of machines                     | 10 min   | Frees the machine names and the SSH ports whose reservation of 7 days ended ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#name-reservation)). Drops the row of each machine that its executor deleted, 7 days after its delete request. Then deletes the machine lease of each machine whose row is gone ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#machines)). Last, it frees the subnet of a decommissioned node once no machine address of it is held ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#node_subnets)). Each of these five steps runs in a transaction of its own that checks the leader lease. So a leader that lost its lease frees nothing more.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Prune of change events                | 10 min   | Deletes the change events that are older than 24 hours. Every reader of the events starts from the head, so an older event serves nobody ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#events)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Certificate of the install            | when due | Gets the wildcard certificate of the install from the ACME CA, and renews it after two thirds of its lifetime. It starts at the start of each term, and plans again after each change of an input of the ACME job ([the certificate of the install](/reference/acme/#the-acme-job)). Every write checks the leader lease.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Auto-delete of idle machines          | 1 min    | Deletes each machine whose last recorded use is older than its auto-delete timeout plus 1 minute. A use is recorded at most once a minute ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#auto-delete)). It takes at most 100 machines per run, the oldest last use first. The next run takes the rest. It skips the machines of a suspended org. Each machine goes in a transaction of its own, which checks the leader lease, so a leader that lost its lease deletes nothing. The delete reserves the name and the SSH port, as `DeleteMachine` does. Each delete gets an audit entry `machine.delete` with the actor `system` and the detail `reason` (`auto-delete`), and the log record `deleted an idle machine`. A machine whose delete fails gets the log record `deleting an idle machine failed`, and the job goes on with the next one. Only a lost leader lease stops the run. |
| Return of SSH host keys               | 1 min    | Gives each SSH host key that a route record claims, and that no record lists, to the oldest record that claims it. A report that lets a key go gives it at once, but it skips a record that another transaction locks, and a `hopboxd` of v0.1.0 gives no key. It takes at most 100 keys per run, and each key goes in a transaction of its own. The write needs no leader lease, because a report makes the same write. Each key gets the log record `a machine got an SSH host key that no other machine holds` at level info, with `machine` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#route_host_keys)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

### Example

```sh
sudo hopboxd run --config /etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml
```

[Run the control role on a laptop](/guide/run-hopboxd/) runs the control role on a laptop. [Enroll the node role on one server](/guide/enroll-node/) enrolls the node role of a server with the control role of the same server. [Serve the domain of an install with the DNS role](/guide/dns-role/) runs the DNS role.

## enroll

```sh
hopboxd enroll --token=TOKEN [--config=PATH] [--json]
```

`enroll` makes this server a part of an install ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/)). It takes these steps:

1. It reads the bootstrap config. The config must list a role that enrolls: every role but `control`. Today that is `node`, `dns`, `edge`, or more than one.
2. It checks the form of the token.
3. If the config lists `node`, it runs the [preflight check](/reference/preflight/) and prints each result to standard error. A failed check of severity `fail` stops the enrollment, before any call. A failed check of severity `warn` only prints.
4. It reads the hardware of the server: the CPU model, the CPU threads, the RAM, and the whole disks ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#hardware-of-a-pool)).
5. It makes its own ECDSA P-256 key and a certificate request, and saves them with the token and the roles in `<data_dir>/server/pending.pem` before the call. If that file holds a pending enrollment for the same token and roles, it sends that request again instead, so a server that lost the answer gets its certificate ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#retry-after-a-lost-answer)). The private key never leaves the server.
6. It dials the first URL of `channel.control_urls`. The TLS handshake checks that the control listener has a certificate of the CA whose hash the token holds, before the token leaves the server. Only if a dial fails does it go on to the next URL, in the order of the list. A call that reached a control server can have used the token, so the next URL never gets it.
7. It calls `EnrollmentService.Enroll` with the token, the request, the host name, the roles, and the hardware. The roles are the roles of the config without `control`.
8. It checks the answer, writes the identity to `<data_dir>/server`, and removes `pending.pem`.

The whole command has 60 s. A running `hopboxd run` with a role other than `control` finds the new identity within 2 s and opens the control channel.

| Flag       | Type   | Default                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------- | ------ | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--token`  | string | none, required             | The enrollment token, `hbxe_<id>_<secret>_<cahash>`, from [admin enrollment-token create](#admin-enrollment-token-create). The environment variable `HOPBOX_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN` gives it too, so the token stays out of the process list. The flag wins over the variable. |
| `--config` | path   | `/etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml` | The bootstrap config file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--json`   | bool   | `false`                    | Prints one JSON object with the identity of the server instead of its ID.                                                                                                                                                                                                |

On success, `enroll` prints the server ID to standard output, and the line `hopboxd: enrolled as the server <id>. hopboxd run connects it to the control plane.` to standard error. With `--json`, it prints one object with these keys:

| Key                       | Description                                                               |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `server_id`               | The ID of the new server.                                                 |
| `roles`                   | The roles in its certificate, for example `["node"]` or `["node","dns"]`. |
| `ca_hash`                 | The SHA-256, in hex, of the certificate of the install CA.                |
| `certificate_expire_time` | The end of the server certificate, 30 days after the enrollment, in UTC.  |
| `dir`                     | The dir of the identity, `<data_dir>/server`.                             |

Example:

```text
$ sudo HOPBOX_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN="$TOKEN" hopboxd enroll
preflight kvm  ok
preflight cgroup2  ok
preflight tun  ok
preflight nftables  ok
preflight reflink  ok
preflight kernel  ok
hopboxd: enrolled as the server 01a14404-ce7b-72d9-b18e-5006c3e462db. hopboxd run connects it to the control plane.
01a14404-ce7b-72d9-b18e-5006c3e462db
```

A server that is enrolled already, and whose config lists a role beyond those of its identity, adds the new roles in place ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#add-roles-to-an-enrolled-server)). The token must allow each new role. A server whose config leaves out a role of its identity ends the removal of that role instead ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#remove-roles-from-an-enrolled-server)). The token must allow each role that stays. The server keeps its ID. `enroll` then prints `hopboxd: the server <id> has the roles <roles> now. Restart hopboxd to use them: systemctl restart hopboxd`. `hopboxd install` restarts it on its own. On the installed server, `enroll` takes the lock of the install, and writes the marker `/opt/hopbox/.restart-pending` before the call to the control role. It keeps the marker once the identity on disk changed. If an install, an upgrade, or another `enroll` holds the lock, `enroll` stops before the call with `another hopboxd install, upgrade, or enroll runs on this server. Wait for it to end`. So if you forget the restart, or `enroll` stops after the save, the next `hopboxd install` restarts `hopboxd`. A restart by hand leaves the marker, so that install restarts `hopboxd` once more. The installed server is the one whose config `/etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml` names the same `data_dir` as `--config`.

| Error                                                                                                                                                                      | Cause                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `the config <path> lists no role that enrolls. Add "node", "dns", "edge", or more than one to roles`                                                                       | The config lists only `control`.                                                                                                                                      |
| `the token does not have the form hbxe_<id>_<secret>_<cahash>. Make one with hopboxd admin enrollment-token create`                                                        | The token is not an enrollment token.                                                                                                                                 |
| `the preflight check failed, so this server cannot run machines:` and one line for each failed check                                                                       | A check of severity `fail` failed ([the preflight check](/reference/preflight/)). On a Mac, every check fails, as it must.                                            |
| `this server is enrolled already as the server <id> with the roles <roles>. To enroll it again, remove <dir> first`                                                        | `<data_dir>/server` holds an identity with the roles of the config.                                                                                                   |
| `enroll at <url>: invalid_argument: invalid argument: the roles drop <roles>, and the server <id> has no removal of them. Start one with hopboxd admin server remove-role` | The config lists fewer roles than the identity, and no removal of the missing roles is pending ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#removeserverroles)).            |
| `pki: the peer is not the control plane of this install: ...` inside `enroll at <url>: ...`                                                                                | The control listener has no certificate of the CA that the token names. The token never left the server.                                                              |
| `enroll at <url>: unauthenticated: the enrollment token is not valid...`                                                                                                   | The control role refused the token: it is unknown, it expired, it was used, or it was made for another CA ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/)). |
| `enroll at <url>: unavailable: ...`                                                                                                                                        | No control listener answers at this URL of `channel.control_urls`, or its TLS handshake failed, for example before the install has a key-encryption key.              |
| several lines `enroll at <url>: ...`, one for each URL                                                                                                                     | Every dial failed. The error joins the failures, in the order of the list.                                                                                            |

## preflight

```sh
hopboxd preflight [--config=PATH] [--json]
```

`preflight` runs the [preflight check](/reference/preflight/) of this server: KVM, cgroup v2, tun, nftables, reflinks on the data dir, and the tested OS and kernel. It reads the bootstrap config only for `data_dir`. It runs every check, also after a failure, and prints one line for each:

```text
preflight <name>  ok
preflight <name>  <severity>  <message>
```

`<severity>` is `fail` or `warn`. If a check of severity `fail` failed, the command exits with status 1 and the error `the preflight check failed, so this server cannot run machines`. A failed `warn` check alone exits with status 0.

| Flag       | Type | Default                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------- | ---- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--config` | path | `/etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml` | The bootstrap config file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--json`   | bool | `false`                    | Prints one JSON object with `passed` and `checks`. `passed` is false after a failed check of severity `fail`. `checks` is a list of objects with `name`, `severity`, `passed`, and `message`. The `message` of a check that passed is empty. |

Example on a Mac:

```text
$ hopboxd preflight --config /tmp/hb/hopboxd.toml
preflight kvm  fail  hopbox runs machines only on Linux with KVM, and this host runs darwin
...
hopboxd: error: the preflight check failed, so this server cannot run machines
```

## install

```sh
sudo ./hopboxd install --roles=ROLE,... [--domain=DOMAIN] [--bootstrap-admin-key-hash=HEX]
  [--enroll-token=TOKEN] [--control-url=URL] [--label=KEY=VALUE ...] [--dns-listen=HOST:PORT ...]
  [--edge-public-ipv4=ADDRESS] [--edge-floating-address=ADDRESS,...] [--edge-no-floating] [--peer-address=ADDRESS] [--internal-listen=ADDRESS:PORT] [--json]
```

`install` installs the release of the `hopboxd` that runs it. That release is the dir of the binary, with its `manifest.json` ([Release bundle](/reference/release-bundle/)). For a first install, run the `hopboxd` of an unpacked bundle. After that, `sudo hopboxd install` runs the current release. `install` must run as root on Linux. The Terraform provider runs it on each new server. [Install hopbox on a Debian 13 server by hand](/guide/install-debian/) runs it by hand.

An install is idempotent: a second run with the same flags changes nothing and does not restart `hopboxd`. A run from a new release is the last step of an [upgrade](#upgrade). [Server layout](/reference/server-layout/) lists every path, user, unit, and setting that it makes.

It takes these steps, in order:

1. It checks the flags. On an enrolled server whose `--roles` adds or drops an enrolling role, it checks the change of the roles ([Remove roles](#remove-roles)). It takes the lock `/opt/hopbox/.lock`, or the lock that an upgrade passes to it. If another install or upgrade holds the lock, the install stops. It checks the release dir against its manifest.
2. If the bootstrap config `/etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml` exists, it reads the file with the owner and mode checks of `hopboxd run` ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#file)). Then it applies the flags. The table `dns` goes with the role `dns`, and the table `edge` with the role `edge`, when the file listed the role and `--roles` does not. With `--internal-listen` on a server with a role that enrolls, the URL of the new listener takes the place of each loopback URL of `channel.control_urls` ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/#move-the-first-server-to-its-peer-address)).
3. With the control role and no Postgres cluster yet, the install makes the control store of this server, so it needs `--domain`. With `postgres.url`, the install connects to the external Postgres instead. If its database has no table `schema_migrations`, the install counts as the first one, and it needs `--domain`. An external Postgres that the install cannot reach, for example because of a wrong CA, stops the install here ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#external-postgres)).
4. With the node role, it checks that `data_dir` is on XFS with reflinks. The DNS role needs no XFS.
5. It checks that `/usr/local/bin/hopboxd` is a symlink or does not exist.
6. It makes the users: `hopbox-pg` for the control role without `postgres.url`, and `hopbox-jail` with the IDs of the jailer for the node role. It refuses IDs of the jailer that another entry of `/etc/subuid`, `/etc/subgid`, `/etc/passwd`, or `/etc/group` uses ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#users-and-ids)).
7. It makes the dirs of the roles: `<data_dir>/server` for a role that enrolls, and the dirs of the machines for the node role. It refuses a dir that is a symlink or that another user owns, and it sets the mode of each dir ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#paths)).
8. With the node role, it runs the [preflight check](/reference/preflight/) and prints each result to standard error. A failed check of severity `fail` stops the install.
9. If `/opt/hopbox/releases/<version>` does not exist, it copies the release there, and checks that the copy has the manifest of the source.
10. With the control role, it checks that the Postgres of the release has the major version of the cluster in `PG_VERSION` ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#upgrades)). With `postgres.url`, it skips that check. It also makes the schema check of [upgrade](#upgrade) with the migrations that this `hopboxd` knows, on the external Postgres when the config names one. So a `hopboxd install` of an older release dir, run by hand, cannot switch into a schema that does not run with it.
11. With the node role, it puts the default image of the release into the image cache. It removes the disk of the image from the release dir. If the cache has a dir of that image without `artifact.json`, it adds the file of the release. A node that downloads the disk of an image leaves such a dir ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/#the-image-cache)).
12. With the control role, it does three things. If the keyring has no key, it makes the first key-encryption key. On the install of step 3, it writes the hash of `--bootstrap-admin-key-hash` to a file. A later run ignores the flag and logs a warning. If no cluster exists and the config has no `postgres.url`, it runs `initdb`.
13. With the node role, it reserves the SSH ports 10000 to 30000.
14. On an enrolled server whose `--roles` adds or drops an enrolling role, it writes the marker `/opt/hopbox/.restart-pending`. Then it calls `Enroll` with the token and saves the new identity ([Remove roles](#remove-roles)). Without `--enroll-token`, it takes the token of a pending enrollment for the same enrolling roles ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#retry-after-a-lost-answer)). So a run that stops right after the save still restarts `hopboxd` at the next run. If the call fails, the install stops. It removes the marker first, but only when the identity on disk did not change and the marker was not there before this run. A call can fail after it saved the new identity, for example at the sync of the server dir. Then the marker stays, and the next run restarts `hopboxd` with the new identity. Only a change of the roles, and an install of a server that has no identity yet, read `<data_dir>/server/pending.pem`. So a damaged file stops no other install, such as an upgrade of an enrolled server. An install that reads a damaged file stops with `node: <path> must hold one PRIVATE KEY block and one CERTIFICATE REQUEST block with the token, the roles, and the end. Remove it to enroll with a new key`.
15. If the release, the config, a unit, or the roles are about to change, it writes the marker `/opt/hopbox/.restart-pending`. If the bootstrap config changed, it then writes the file.
16. It points `/opt/hopbox/previous` to the release that ran before, and then `/opt/hopbox/current` to the release. In this order, a crash between the two renames never loses the release of a rollback. It points `/usr/local/bin/hopboxd` to `/opt/hopbox/current/hopboxd`.
17. It writes each unit that changed. If a unit changed, or the marker was there before this run, it runs `systemctl daemon-reload`. Then it runs `systemctl enable hopboxd.service`.
18. If the release, the config, a unit, or the roles changed, or the marker was there before this run, it runs `systemctl restart hopboxd.service`. Otherwise it runs `systemctl start hopboxd.service`. If `hopboxd` runs, that start does nothing. Both wait until `hopboxd` is ready. After a good start, it removes the marker.
19. It removes the releases other than the current and the previous one.
20. With the control role, it reads the domain of the install through the admin socket. If `--domain` names another domain, it sets it. Without `--domain`, an install without a domain fails.
21. If the server has a role other than control and no identity yet, it enrolls with the enrollment token, as [enroll](#enroll) does. If the config names an enrolling role beyond the identity, it adds the role with the token and restarts `hopboxd`. It writes the marker `/opt/hopbox/.restart-pending` before that call, and removes it after the restart. So a run that stops after the save restarts `hopboxd` at the next run, as in step 14. Without `--enroll-token`, both take the token of a pending enrollment for the enrolling roles of the config ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#retry-after-a-lost-answer)).
22. With `--peer-address`, it reads the server of the identity through the admin socket. If the server has another peer address or none, it sets the address with `SetServerPeerAddress` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setserverpeeraddress)).

Steps 1 to 13 make every check that can refuse. They change nothing that a running `hopboxd` reads: the identity, the config, the current release, and the units stay the same until step 14. So a refused install leaves the running `hopboxd` as it was. If a run stops after the marker of step 14 or step 15 and before the restart, the marker stays. The next run then restarts `hopboxd`, also without another change. The install never removes data.

| Flag                         | Type                              | Default                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--roles`                    | list of strings, joined by commas | none, required           | The roles of this server: one or more of `control`, `node`, `dns`, and `edge`. The order does not matter. The config lists them in the order `control`, `node`, `dns`, `edge`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--domain`                   | string                            | none                     | The domain of the install, such as `example.com`. It must follow the rules in [Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#install-domain). It needs the control role. The install that makes the Postgres cluster needs it. A later run without it keeps the domain.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--bootstrap-admin-key-hash` | string                            | none                     | The SHA-256 of the first admin API key of the install, as 64 lowercase hex digits. It needs the control role. Only the install that makes the Postgres cluster writes it, to `<data_dir>/bootstrap-admin-key.sha256` ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#the-bootstrap-admin-api-key)). A later run ignores it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--enroll-token`             | string                            | none                     | An enrollment token, `hbxe_<id>_<secret>_<cahash>`. After the start, a server with a role other than `control` enrolls with it, unless it is enrolled. If `--roles` adds an enrolling role to an enrolled server, the install adds that role with the token. That step comes before the install writes the config ([Remove roles](#remove-roles) has the steps). Without a token, such an install takes the token of a pending enrollment for the same roles, after a lost answer ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#retry-after-a-lost-answer)). Without either, it fails before any change. If the config does not load before the install, the install adds the role after it writes the config. It then restarts hopboxd, so the control channel uses the new certificate. That install fails without a token. The error starts with `the config names the roles <roles>, but the server <id> enrolled with <roles>`. Give it in the environment variable `HOPBOX_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN` instead, so the token stays out of the process list. The flag wins over the variable. |
| `--control-url`              | URL, repeatable                   | the value of the config  | The URL of the internal listener of a control server. Repeat the flag for each control server, or join the URLs with commas. With one URL, the install writes the old key `channel.control_url`, unless the config has `channel.control_urls` already. So a rollback to a `hopboxd` from before `control_urls`, which refuses that key, still reads the file. With more than one URL, it writes `channel.control_urls` and deletes `channel.control_url` ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). With a token, the enrollment tries the URLs in order, as [enroll](#enroll) does. It needs a role that enrolls: `node`, `dns`, `edge`, or more than one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--label`                    | `KEY=VALUE`                       | the labels of the config | A label of the server, for `channel.labels`. Repeat the flag for each label. With one, it replaces every label of the config. It needs a role that enrolls: `node`, `dns`, `edge`, or more than one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--dns-listen`               | `HOST:PORT`                       | the value of the config  | An address of the DNS role, for `dns.listen`, such as `203.0.113.5:53`. Repeat the flag for each address. With one, it replaces the list of the config. The rules of `dns.listen` apply ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). It needs the role `dns`. A change of the list restarts `hopboxd`, as a change of any key of the config does. The Terraform provider runs it after a change of the floating addresses of a server with the DNS role ([hopbox Terraform provider](/reference/terraform-provider/#edge-servers-and-floating-addresses)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `--edge-public-ipv4`         | `ADDRESS`                         | the value of the config  | The floating IPv4 address of this edge server, for `edge.public_ipv4`, such as `203.0.113.101`. The egress of the machines leaves from it ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/#the-source-addresses)). The rules of `edge.public_ipv4` apply ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). It needs the role `edge`. A change of the key restarts `hopboxd`, and the same value changes nothing. The Terraform provider runs it after a change of the floating addresses of an edge server ([hopbox Terraform provider](/reference/terraform-provider/#edge-servers-and-floating-addresses)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--edge-floating-address`    | `ADDRESS`                         | the value of the config  | A floating IPv4 address of this edge server, for `edge.floating_addresses`, such as `203.0.113.102`. Repeat the flag for each address. With one, it replaces the list of the config. The rules of `edge.floating_addresses` apply ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). It needs the role `edge`. A change of the key restarts `hopboxd`. The Terraform provider gives it every floating address of an edge server ([hopbox Terraform provider](/reference/terraform-provider/#edge-servers-and-floating-addresses)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--edge-no-floating`         |                                   | false                    | Removes `edge.public_ipv4` and `edge.floating_addresses` from the config, for an edge server that holds no floating IPv4 address any more. It takes neither `--edge-public-ipv4` nor `--edge-floating-address`. A change of the config restarts `hopboxd`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `--internal-listen`          | `ADDRESS:PORT`                    | the value of the config  | The address of the internal listener, for `control.internal_listen`: the peer address of this server and port 7443, such as `203.0.113.12:7443` ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/#move-the-first-server-to-its-peer-address)). The address must be a peer address that an interface of the host holds, and it must equal `--peer-address` when both flags come. Without `--peer-address`, on a server whose roles enrolled, the install reads the peer address of the server through the admin socket, before any change, and the address must equal it. The other servers allow the stored peer address, and the control URLs name the listener, so the two must be one address. On a server with a role that enrolls, the URL `https://<ADDRESS:PORT>` takes the place of each loopback URL of `channel.control_urls`, or of the default `https://127.0.0.1:7443`, so the roles of the server dial the listener at its new address. It needs the control role. A change restarts `hopboxd`, and the same value changes nothing. The machines keep running.                   |
| `--peer-address`             | `ADDRESS`                         | none                     | The peer address of this server: one public unicast IPv4 address on its uplink, such as `203.0.113.12` ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#peer-addresses)). It is for the first server, whose roles enroll with a token from its own control role. After the enrollment, the install sets the address through the admin socket, and writes the audit entry `server.set_peer_address`. The same address again changes nothing. It needs the control role and a role that enrolls. A server without the control role gets its peer address from its enrollment token. The install does not keep the address in the config.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--json`                     | bool                              | `false`                  | Prints one JSON object instead of the version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

### Remove roles

`hopboxd install --roles <every role that stays>` with `--enroll-token` ends the removal of roles from an enrolled server ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#remove-roles-from-an-enrolled-server)). An add of a role that a removal took runs the same steps with every role, the old ones and the new ones ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#add-roles-to-an-enrolled-server)). `RemoveServerRoles` starts the removal, and the token names the server and the enrolling roles that stay ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#removeserverroles)). On a control server, `--roles` keeps `control`, such as `--roles control,node`. First the install makes each check that can refuse, such as the lock, the release, and the preflight check of the node role. Then it calls `Enroll` with the token and the enrolling roles that stay, and saves the new identity. It calls the control role at `--control-url`, or at `channel.control_urls` of the config. Then the install writes the config without the roles, and restarts `hopboxd` with the new identity. A refusal of a check or of the control role changes nothing on the server: the identity, the config, and the roles stay. If a later step of the install fails, the install still restarts `hopboxd`, because the registry refuses the old certificate at once. The log of that restart is `the install failed after the change of the roles, so hopboxd restarts with the new identity`, with `component=install` and the field `err`. If the call of the control role fails and the install cannot remove the marker `/opt/hopbox/.restart-pending` of step 14, it logs `the restart marker stays, so the next install restarts hopboxd` at level warn, with the field `err`. If the answer of the control role gets lost, the server keeps its old identity, which the registry refuses. Run the same install again within the lifetime of the token, without `--enroll-token` or with the same token. The server sends the request of `<data_dir>/server/pending.pem` again, and gets the same certificate ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#retry-after-a-lost-answer)). A new token replaces `pending.pem` with a new key, so the key of the used token is gone. After the end of the token, run the same install with a new token that names the server and allows every enrolling role of the registry. The server then resyncs with the key of its old identity ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#resync-after-the-end-of-the-token)). Without a token, and without a pending enrollment for the roles, the install refuses before any change:

* `--roles drops the roles <roles> of the server <id>. Start their removal with hopboxd admin server remove-role, and once it is ready, give a token for the server and the roles that stay with --enroll-token`, without a token
* `--roles names no role that enrolls, but the server <id> has the roles <roles>, and its certificate needs one. A drain takes a whole server out: hopboxd admin server drain <id>`
* `--roles adds roles to the server <id> and drops <roles>. Change the roles one change at a time`
* `--roles adds the roles <roles> to the server <id>, which enrolled with <roles>. Give an enrollment token for the server and the new roles with --enroll-token`, without a token

At its start, `hopboxd run` removes the data of each role that neither the config nor the identity names. For the DNS role, that is the dir `<data_dir>/dns` with the zones ([the DNS role](/reference/dns/#zones-on-the-disk)). For the node role, that is the table `inet hopbox_node` and the tap devices `hbt*` ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#subnet-of-a-server-without-the-node-role)). The edge role keeps the certificate of the install, its key, and the SSH host key of the install only in memory. So the restart drops them ([the edge role](/reference/edge/)). The host firewall opens only the ports of the roles of the config. So the ports of a role that went close at the restart ([the host firewall](/reference/host-firewall/)). The log records, with `component=roles`:

| Message                                                                          | Level | Fields            |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----------------- |
| `removed the data of a role that this server no longer has`                      | info  | `role`, `removed` |
| `cannot remove the zones of the DNS role that this server no longer has`         | warn  | `path`, `err`     |
| `cannot remove the node network of the node role that this server no longer has` | warn  | `removed`, `err`  |
| `cannot read the identity of this server, so it keeps the data of every role`    | warn  | `err`             |

A failure keeps `hopboxd` running, and the next start tries again.

### The config file of an install

The install keeps every key of an existing config that its flags do not set. When it changes the file, it drops the comments of the file, and it writes this header:

```toml
# The bootstrap config of hopboxd. hopboxd install keeps the keys that its
# flags do not set. docs/reference/hopboxd-config.md lists every key.
roles = ["control", "node"]
```

On success, `install` prints the version of the release to standard output. It prints a line such as `hopboxd: installed v0.1.0, and hopboxd runs. Changed: release, config.` to standard error. With `--json`, it prints one object with these keys:

| Key         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `version`   | The version of the release that runs now.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `previous`  | The version that ran before this install, or `""` on a first install. On a second run, it is the same as `version`.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `changes`   | What the install changed, as a list of words. The words of files are `release files`, `config`, `keys`, and `bootstrap admin key`. The other words are `users`, `postgres`, `ports`, `release`, `units`, `roles`, and `peer address`. An install that changed nothing gives `[]`. |
| `restarted` | Whether the install restarted `hopboxd`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `server_id` | The ID of the server, after an enrollment, or `""` before one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

Example of a first install of a server with the control role and the node role:

```text
$ tar -xzf hopbox-v0.1.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz
$ sudo ./hopbox-v0.1.0/hopboxd install --roles control,node --domain example.com
preflight kvm  ok
preflight cgroup2  ok
preflight tun  ok
preflight nftables  ok
preflight reflink  ok
preflight kernel  ok
hopboxd: installed v0.1.0, and hopboxd runs. Changed: users, release files, keys, postgres, ports, config, release, units.
v0.1.0
```

The log records go to standard error between these lines, as JSON ([Logs](#logs)).

| Error                                                                                                                                                              | Cause                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hopboxd install runs only on a Linux server, and this host runs <os>`                                                                                             | The host is not Linux.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `hopboxd install must run as root. Run it with sudo`                                                                                                               | The user is not root.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--roles: unknown role "<role>". ...` or `--roles: list at least one role, such as control,node`                                                                   | A bad `--roles`.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--domain is required on the first install of the control role on a server`                                                                                        | The control role has no Postgres cluster yet, and `--domain` is missing.                                                                                                    |
| `the install has no domain. Run the install again with --domain`                                                                                                   | The control store has no domain, and `--domain` is missing. `hopboxd` runs.                                                                                                 |
| `<dir> belongs to uid <n>, but root writes and runs what it holds, so it must belong to uid 0. ...`                                                                | A dir of the install, such as `/opt/hopbox/releases`, belongs to another user.                                                                                              |
| `<dir> is a symlink, but the install uses only real dirs, ...`                                                                                                     | A dir of the install, such as `/var/lib/hopbox`, is a symlink.                                                                                                              |

| `--peer-address sets the peer address of the enrolled server, but this server is not enrolled. ## upgrade

```sh
sudo hopboxd upgrade --bundle=FILE --sha256=HEX [--json]
sudo hopboxd upgrade --rollback [--json]
```

`upgrade` moves this server to the release of a bundle file. `upgrade --rollback` moves it back to the previous release. It must run as root on Linux, on a server with an install. If the `bundle` of a server changes, the Terraform provider runs it.

With `--bundle`, it takes these steps:

1. It reads the bootstrap config and `/opt/hopbox/current`, so it fails on a server without an install.
2. It takes the lock `/opt/hopbox/.lock`. It holds the lock until the install of step 6 ends. It passes the lock to that install as the file descriptor 3, which the environment variable `HOPBOX_INSTALL_LOCK_FD` names. So no other run can prune the new release in between.
3. It checks the sha256 of the bundle file against `--sha256`. The manifest proves only that the bundle is whole. The sha256 from a trusted place, such as the `.sha256` file of the build, proves that it is the bundle that you built.
4. It unpacks the bundle to a temp dir `/opt/hopbox/releases/.incoming-<random>`, and checks the release against its manifest and its owner ([Release bundle](/reference/release-bundle/#checks-of-a-release)). It renames the temp dir to `/opt/hopbox/releases/<version>`. If that dir exists with the same manifest, it keeps it. If it exists with another manifest, the upgrade stops.
5. With the control role, it reads the newest schema migration of the control store and the oldest schema version that runs with it. It compares that version with `schema_version` of the new release ([Release bundle](/reference/release-bundle/#manifest)). If the `schema_version` of the release is lower than that oldest schema version, the upgrade stops ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#two-releases-on-one-store)). It reads through the socket of the running Postgres. If no Postgres answers, it starts the Postgres of the current release for the read, and stops it again. If that Postgres does not start, it uses the Postgres of the new release. After the guard of the install, both have the same major version. Each read has 30 s, and each start has the 60 s of pgsup on top.
6. It runs `/opt/hopbox/releases/<version>/hopboxd install --roles=<roles>`, with the roles of the config. The [install](#install) of the new release does the rest: the Postgres guard, the image cache, the switch of `current` and `previous`, the units, and the restart.

With `--rollback`, it takes the same lock and checks the release of `/opt/hopbox/previous` and its owner. It makes the schema check of step 5, and runs the `hopboxd install --roles=<roles>` of that release. The install then points `current` to the previous release, and `previous` to the release that ran.

The old `hopboxd` only unpacks and checks. The new release runs its own install. So each release brings the steps that it needs. The CLI of `install` is the contract between two releases. Until the install of step 6 switches the release, the running `hopboxd` keeps running, and nothing that it reads changes.

The microVMs of the machines run in their own units in `hopbox-machines.slice`, not in `hopboxd.service`. So they keep running through the restart of an upgrade or a rollback ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#hopbox-machinesslice)).

| Flag         | Type   | Default                        | Description                                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | ------ | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--bundle`   | path   | none                           | The bundle file, such as `hopbox-v0.2.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz`.                                                                 |
