| `postgres.url: "<url>" needs sslmode=verify-full, so hopboxd checks the certificate of the server and its host name`                                                                                                          | `sslmode` is missing, appears twice, or has another value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `postgres.ca_file: postgres.url needs it`                                                                                                                                                                                     | `postgres.url` is set, and `postgres.ca_file` is not. The same error exists for `postgres.password_file`.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `postgres.ca_file and postgres.password_file need postgres.url`                                                                                                                                                               | A file is set without `postgres.url`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `postgres.ca_file: <path> holds no PEM certificate`                                                                                                                                                                           | At the start of `hopboxd run`, the file holds no certificate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `postgres.ca_file: config: ...` or `postgres.password_file: config: ...`                                                                                                                                                      | At the start of `hopboxd run`, the file is missing, or fails a check of the file of the bootstrap config, such as `belongs to uid <n>`.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `postgres.password_file: config: <path> has mode <mode>, which lets group or others read it, and it holds a secret. Give it mode 0400`                                                                                        | As root, group or others can read the password file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `postgres.password_file: <path> must hold the password on one line`                                                                                                                                                           | The file is empty, or holds more than one line.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `control.api_listen: "<value>" is not host:port: ...`                                                                                                                                                                         | The address has no port, or does not parse.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `control.api_listen: "<value>" is not a loopback IP address. ...`                                                                                                                                                             | The host is not a loopback IP address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `control.internal_listen: "<value>" is not host:port: ...`                                                                                                                                                                    | The address has no port, or does not parse.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `control.internal_listen: "<value>" has no port`                                                                                                                                                                              | The address ends with `:`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `control.internal_listen: "<value>" is not an IP address and a port, such as 127.0.0.1:7443`                                                                                                                                  | The host is a name, such as `localhost`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `control.internal_listen: "<value>" is also control.api_listen. Give each listener its own address`                                                                                                                           | Both listeners have the same address, with a port other than `0`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `acme.name_servers: "<value>" is not an IP address and a port, such as 127.0.0.1:7443`                                                                                                                                        | A name server is a host name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `acme.name_servers: "<value>" is not host:port: ...`                                                                                                                                                                          | A name server has no port, or does not parse.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `acme.name_servers: <n> addresses, more than 16`                                                                                                                                                                              | The list is too long.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `acme.ca_file: "<value>" is not an absolute path`                                                                                                                                                                             | The path is relative.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `control.release_image: "<value>" is not an absolute path`                                                                                                                                                                    | The path is relative.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `acme.ca_file: ...`                                                                                                                                                                                                           | At the start of `hopboxd run`, the file does not open, or holds no PEM certificate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `[node] is the old name of [channel]. Keep only [channel]`                                                                                                                                                                    | The file has both `[node]` and `[channel]`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `network.nameservers: "<value>" is not an IPv4 address that a machine can reach, such as 9.9.9.9`                                                                                                                             | A resolver is not IPv4, or is a loopback, unspecified, link-local, multicast, or machine address.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `network.nameservers: <address> appears twice`                                                                                                                                                                                | A resolver is in the list twice.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `network.nameservers: <n> resolvers, more than 3`                                                                                                                                                                             | The list is too long.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `channel.control_url is the old key of channel.control_urls. Keep only channel.control_urls`                                                                                                                                  | The file has both keys.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `channel.control_urls: "<value>" is not a URL: ...`                                                                                                                                                                           | A value does not parse as a URL.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `channel.control_urls: "<value>" is not an https URL of a host, such as https://127.0.0.1:7443`                                                                                                                               | The scheme is not `https`, the host is missing, or the URL has user info, a path, a query, or a fragment.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `channel.control_urls: <n> URLs, more than 8`                                                                                                                                                                                 | The list is too long.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `channel.control_urls: "<value>" appears twice`                                                                                                                                                                               | A URL is in the list twice.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `channel.labels: invalid label: ...`                                                                                                                                                                                          | A label breaks a rule of `channel.labels`. The rest of the message names the label and the rule.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `dns.listen: list 1 to 16 addresses, such as ":53"`                                                                                                                                                                           | `dns.listen` is empty, or has more than 16 addresses.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `dns.listen: "<value>" is not host:port: ...`                                                                                                                                                                                 | The address has no `:`, or does not parse.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `dns.listen: "<value>" has no port number`                                                                                                                                                                                    | The port is empty, is not a number, or is larger than 65535.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `dns.listen: "<value>" is not an IP address and a port, such as 203.0.113.10:53, or a port alone, such as :53`                                                                                                                | The host is a name, such as `localhost`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `dns.listen: "<value>" appears twice`                                                                                                                                                                                         | An address is in the list twice.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `edge.https_listen: "<value>" is not host:port: ...`                                                                                                                                                                          | The address has no `:`, or does not parse. The same errors exist for `edge.http_listen`.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `edge.https_listen: "<value>" has no port number`                                                                                                                                                                             | The port is empty, is not a number, or is larger than 65535.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `edge.https_listen: "<value>" is not an IP address and a port, such as 203.0.113.10:443, or a port alone, such as :443`                                                                                                       | The host is a name, such as `localhost`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `edge.http_listen: "<value>" is also edge.https_listen. Give each listener its own address`                                                                                                                                   | Both listeners of the edge role have the same address, with a port other than `0`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `edge.ssh_listen: "<value>" is in the SSH ports 10000 to 30000, which the redirect sends to it. Pick a port outside them, such as :2222`                                                                                      | The port of the SSH listener is an SSH port of a machine. The errors of `edge.https_listen` also exist for `edge.ssh_listen`.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `edge.ssh_listen: "<value>" listens on one address, but the redirect of the SSH ports sends each connection to the address of the interface that took it. Give a port alone, such as :2222, or set edge.ssh_redirect = false` | `edge.ssh_redirect` is true, and the host of `edge.ssh_listen` is one address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `edge.ssh_listen: "0.0.0.0:<port>" takes only IPv4, so the IPv6 clients that the redirect of the SSH ports sends to it get no answer. Give a port alone, such as :2222, or set edge.ssh_redirect = false`                     | `edge.ssh_redirect` is true, and the host of `edge.ssh_listen` is `0.0.0.0`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `edge.ssh_listen: "<value>" is also an HTTP listener. Give each listener its own address`                                                                                                                                     | The SSH listener has the address of `edge.https_listen` or `edge.http_listen`, with a port other than `0`.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `edge.public_ipv6: "<value>" is not an IPv6 address without a prefix length or a zone, such as 2001:db8::11`                                                                                                                  | The value does not parse as an IPv6 address. It is an IPv4 address, an IPv4 address in IPv6 form, or has a prefix length or a zone. A value with a prefix length and `edge.public_ipv6_gateway` gives a warning instead ([The IPv6 block of an older release](#the-ipv6-block-of-an-older-release)). |
| `edge.public_ipv6: <address> is not a public IPv6 address`                                                                                                                                                                    | The address is not a global unicast address, or is a unique local address of `fc00::/7`. A link-local address is not a global unicast address.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `edge.public_ipv6: only a server with the role edge holds a floating address`                                                                                                                                                 | A server without the role `edge` sets the key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `edge.public_ipv4: "<value>" is not an IPv4 address`                                                                                                                                                                          | The value does not parse as an IPv4 address, such as `203.0.113.101/32` or an IPv6 address.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `edge.public_ipv4: <address> is not a public IPv4 address`                                                                                                                                                                    | The address is not a global unicast address, or is in a private range or the machine range.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `edge.public_ipv4: only a server with the role edge holds a floating address`                                                                                                                                                 | A server without the role `edge` sets the key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `edge.floating_addresses: "<value>" is not an IPv4 address`                                                                                                                                                                   | An entry does not parse as an IPv4 address, such as `203.0.113.102/32` or an IPv6 address.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `edge.floating_addresses: <address> is not a public IPv4 address`                                                                                                                                                             | An entry is not a global unicast address, or is in a private range, the vRack range, or the machine range.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `edge.floating_addresses: <address> appears twice`                                                                                                                                                                            | The list holds an address two times.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `edge.floating_addresses: <n> addresses, more than 64`                                                                                                                                                                        | The list is too long.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `edge.floating_addresses: only a server with the role edge holds a floating address`                                                                                                                                          | A server without the role `edge` sets the key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `metrics.listen: "<value>" is not a loopback IP address. ...`                                                                                                                                                                 | The host of the metrics listener is not a loopback IP address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `metrics.listen: "<value>" is not host:port: ...`                                                                                                                                                                             | The address has no port, or does not parse.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

# The host firewall

> The host firewall of every server, the nftables table inet hopbox_host. It covers the zones and ports, the jump hosts, and the ways in that it keeps. It also covers the egress chains of an edge server, the uplink and the NAT66 of the IPv6 egress, the repair, metrics, logs, and tests.

The network redesign of 2026-10-27 changes this page. hopbox leaves the vRack and the OVHcloud API, and the servers talk over their public addresses (Q90). This page describes the code after milestone N31, which removes the vRack zone.

The host firewall is the nftables table `inet hopbox_host` of every server of an install. It makes the edge servers the bastion of the install (rules 2 and 5). Only an edge server takes traffic from the whole internet. On its public address, a control server or a node takes only the traffic of the install, from the peer addresses of the servers ([Sets](#sets)). A peer address is the public IPv4 address at which the other servers reach a server ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/)). On the mesh, each server takes only the ports of its roles. Operators reach a server that is not an edge server by SSH only through an edge server as a jump host. On an edge server, the table also forwards and translates the egress of the machines ([The egress of the machines](#the-egress-of-the-machines)).

The firewall is in `internal/hostfw`. `hopboxd run` starts it on every server, right after the metrics listener and before the units of the roles ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run)). The provider block of the Terraform provider names the jump host in `ssh_jump_host` ([hopbox Terraform provider](/reference/terraform-provider/#jump-host)).

In the examples, the edge servers have the peer addresses `203.0.113.21` and `203.0.113.22`.

## Zones

The table sorts each new connection by the interface that takes it. A zone is the set of interfaces that share one list of open ports.

| Zone        | Interfaces                                                                                                                                                                                          | Sources that a port takes                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Loopback    | `lo`                                                                                                                                                                                                | Every source. The table takes every packet of loopback.                                                                                                                                  |
| Mesh        | `hbm0`                                                                                                                                                                                              | The mesh range `10.239.0.0/16`.                                                                                                                                                          |
| Tap devices | The tap devices of the machines on a node, `hbt*`                                                                                                                                                   | The table takes them, and leaves them to the table `inet hopbox_node` ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#the-table-inet-hopbox_node)), which owns all traffic of the machines. |
| Public      | Each other interface, such as the uplink or a private network of the provider. The egress tunnels `hbe*` are in it too, so a machine reaches the public ports of an edge server through its tunnel. | Every source for the ports of the roles `edge` and `dns`. Each port of the traffic of the install takes only its set ([Sets](#sets)).                                                    |

A machine behind an egress tunnel reaches the public ports of its edge server at the floating addresses, as the internet does. It reaches no port at a peer address of the install. Its own edge server is no exception ([The egress of the machines](#the-egress-of-the-machines)). Each zone ends with a drop, so a port that no role opens takes nothing. The replies of the connections of the server pass in every zone, and so do the ICMP messages of [ICMP and DHCPv6](#icmp-and-dhcpv6).

## Ports

Each role opens its ports. A server with more than one role opens the ports of each role.

| Role                                            | Zone   | Port                                                                                     | Source                                                                                                                | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A server without the role `edge`                | Public | TCP 22                                                                                   | The set `jump_hosts`. While the server never knew an edge server, every source ([Never a lockout](#never-a-lockout)). | The SSH of the operators and of the provider through an edge server ([The jump hosts](#the-jump-hosts)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| A server that enrolls: `node`, `dns`, or `edge` | Public | UDP 51820                                                                                | The set `peers`                                                                                                       | The WireGuard packets of the mesh, which runs on the peer addresses ([the mesh](/reference/mesh/#values)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `edge`, on a server that enrolls                | public | UDP 51821                                                                                | The set `peers`                                                                                                       | The egress tunnel `hbe0`, which takes the egress of the nodes ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/#the-tunnel-of-an-edge-server)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `node` without `edge`, on a server that enrolls | public | UDP 51821 to 51836                                                                       | The set `peers`                                                                                                       | The egress tunnels `hbe0` to `hbe15` of the node ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/#the-tunnels-of-a-node)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `control`                                       | Public | TCP 7443, the port of `control.internal_listen`                                          | The sets `peers` and `registered`                                                                                     | The internal listener on the peer address of the control server: the enrollment, the control channels, and the API and the console that the edge servers forward ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `node`                                          | Mesh   | TCP 7444                                                                                 | The mesh range                                                                                                        | The disk listener of the cold moves ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#the-disk-listener)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `edge`                                          | Public | TCP 22                                                                                   | Every source                                                                                                          | The `sshd` of the operators. The edge server is the jump host.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `edge`                                          | Public | TCP 80 and 443                                                                           | Every source                                                                                                          | The HTTP and HTTPS listeners ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#listeners)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `edge`                                          | Public | TCP 2222, the port of `edge.ssh_listen`, only for connections that a redirect sent there | Every source                                                                                                          | The SSH ports of the machines, TCP 10000 to 30000. The table `inet hopbox_edge` sends them to `edge.ssh_listen` ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/)), so the input hook sees port 2222. When conntrack records the redirect (`ct status dnat`), the rule takes the connection there. Any redirect or destination NAT to that port passes, also one that an operator with `edge.ssh_redirect = false` writes. A connection straight to port 2222 takes nothing. |
| `dns`                                           | Public | TCP and UDP 53                                                                           | Every source                                                                                                          | The DNS role ([the DNS role](/reference/dns/)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

The edge servers of an install run the DNS role. Port 53 follows the role `dns`, not the role `edge`, as the owner decided on 2026-10-27 (plan question Q74). So a server with the DNS role alone, as in [Serve the domain of an install with the DNS role](/guide/dns-role/), opens port 53 and no edge port. An edge server without the DNS role keeps port 53 closed. The table opens the same ports whatever the listen addresses of the config say, as the owner decided on 2026-10-27 (plan question Q80). A listener on another port, such as `edge.https_listen = ":8443"`, takes no connection from outside the server. So at its start, `hopboxd` logs `the host firewall opens no public port for this listener, so it takes no connection from outside the server` at level warn, for each such listener of `edge.https_listen`, `edge.http_listen`, and `dns.listen`. A listener on loopback gets no warning.

The other listeners of `hopboxd` take nothing from outside the server: the API listener on `127.0.0.1:7080`, the metrics listener on `127.0.0.1:9464`, and the listener of the SSH front door on port 2222.

The ports follow the roles of the bootstrap config at the start of `hopboxd`. So when a removal takes a role from a running server, the restart at its end closes the ports of that role: 80, 443, and the SSH ports of the machines for `edge`, 53 for `dns`, and 7444 for `node` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#removeserverroles)). Port 22 of a server that is no longer an edge takes only the set `jump_hosts`, which the server knew as an edge already. The other servers get the new edge set and the new `jump_hosts` within one heartbeat ([the mesh](/reference/mesh/)).

## Sets

The table holds up to four sets of IPv4 addresses. A port of the traffic of the install takes only the addresses of its set.

| Set           | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Ports that take it                                                                                                          |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `peers`       | The peer addresses of the servers of the install that are not decommissioned ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#servers)). A server without a peer address is not in it. It also holds the address of the internal listener of each live control process on a peer address ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#control_processes)). A server with the control role alone has no row in `servers`, so this address lets the control servers reach the internal listeners of each other. This is a build default of N28, not an owner decision.                                                             | Public UDP 51820, the UDP ports of the egress tunnels, and TCP 7443 of a control server.                                    |
| `jump_hosts`  | The peer addresses of the edge servers among them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Public TCP 22 of a server without the role `edge`.                                                                          |
| `registered`  | The peer addresses of the enrollment tokens that are not used and not expired ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/)). Only a server with the control role has this set.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Public TCP 7443 of a control server.                                                                                        |
| `known_peers` | Every peer address that the install knows, and each address of `peers`. These are the peer addresses of the servers that are not decommissioned, and the address of the internal listener of each row of `control_processes`, live or not. An address leaves only with the decommission of its server or with the sweep of its row, 24 hours after the last renewal, never with a missed heartbeat. Only a server with the egress of the machines, an edge server, has this set. A control role of an older release sends no known peers, and the set then holds `peers` alone. This is a build default of N28, not an owner decision. | None. The egress of the machines reaches none of its addresses ([The egress of the machines](#the-egress-of-the-machines)). |

A registered address reaches the internal listener only while its token works. So a new server enrolls from its peer address, and its later control channel comes from the same address, which `peers` then holds. `hopboxd` binds the control channel to the peer address once the server has its sets ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#the-source-of-the-own-connections)). A peer address stays in `peers` until its server is decommissioned. Providers reuse addresses, so a stranger can get the address of a decommissioned server.

The sets come from two places:

| Server                            | Where the sets come from                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A server with the control role    | The control role reads `peers`, `jump_hosts`, `known_peers`, and `registered` from the store every second ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#servers)). So a new enrollment token reaches `registered` within 2 s, and the Terraform provider waits for that before it enrolls a server. The control role hands the sets to the firewall only after a change.                                                     |
| A server without the control role | Each mesh that the control role sends holds `peers`, `jump_hosts`, and `known_peers` in its field `firewall` ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#mesh-pushes)). A change reaches the server within one heartbeat, 5 s. The agent hands the sets to the firewall before the mesh device takes the mesh. A mesh of a control role of an older release has no `firewall`, and the server keeps the sets that it has. |

Each server keeps its last `peers`, `jump_hosts`, and known peers in the file `<data_dir>/hostfw/peers` ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#paths)), and writes it after each change, through a temp file and a rename. The start of `hopboxd` loads the file before the control channel comes back. So a restart without a control server keeps the mesh port and the way in through the jump hosts. Without the file, the start takes the sets of the table before it. It never takes `registered` from the file or the table: the control role reads it within a second, and each registration ends with its token.

The file has one address on each line, after its kind. The kinds are `peer`, `jump_host`, and `known_peer`. Two more lines stand alone, without an address. The line `knew_edge` records that the server knew an edge server ([Never a lockout](#never-a-lockout)). The line `known_peers_whole` records that the known peers came from the control role ([The egress of the machines](#the-egress-of-the-machines)). A line that starts with `#` is a comment:

```text
# The last peers, jump hosts, and known peers of the host firewall of this server. hopboxd writes this file.
knew_edge
known_peers_whole
peer 203.0.113.21
peer 203.0.113.22
peer 203.0.113.31
jump_host 203.0.113.21
jump_host 203.0.113.22
known_peer 203.0.113.11
known_peer 203.0.113.21
known_peer 203.0.113.22
known_peer 203.0.113.31
```

Each check compares the elements of each set with the sets of the firewall. So a flush of a set alone comes back within 2 s, and so does a delete of an element. Each new set from the control role or from a mesh checks the table again, also the same sets.

## The jump hosts

Port 22 of the public interface of a server without the role `edge` takes the peer addresses of the edge servers alone, the set `jump_hosts`. An edge server reaches a peer address straight over the internet. So the SSH of an operator through an edge server comes from the peer address of the edge server. That SSH leaves from the source that the kernel picks, so the default route of the edge server must carry its peer address as the source. `hopboxd` sets that source again when the route loses it ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#the-check-of-the-uplink)). The Terraform provider dials the peer address of a server through the jump host too.

An edge list that turns empty keeps the last `jump_hosts`, as the owner decided on 2026-10-27 (plan question Q93). So the last edge server that leaves stays a jump host of each server, and `hopboxd` logs `the install has no edge server now, so port 22 of the public interface keeps the last jump hosts` at level warn. A new edge server replaces the list. The kept address has the risk of reuse of the peers ([Sets](#sets)): a stranger who gets the address of the last edge server that left reaches port 22 of each server, but still needs an SSH key.

## Never a lockout

A change of the table never closes the way of an operator into a server in a way that this section does not name. The owner decided the ways of SSH on 2026-10-27 (plan question Q93, which replaces Q75):

* A server that never knew an edge server keeps port 22 open on its public interface, to every source. No jump host reaches it. This covers a new server before its first control channel, and a first server without the edge role, such as ks. A server knew an edge server once its set `jump_hosts` had an address. While port 22 of its public interface takes every source, `hopboxd` logs `this server never knew an edge server, so no jump host reaches it, and its public interface keeps port 22 open` at level warn, at each install of the table. An edge server opens port 22 to every source anyway.
* A server that knew an edge server keeps port 22 of its public interface closed to every address outside `jump_hosts`, also while that set is empty. This holds after a restart, through the file `<data_dir>/hostfw/peers`, and after the last edge server left ([The jump hosts](#the-jump-hosts)). The way back after a lockout is the rescue mode or the console of the provider. A computer that the operator owns has no such provider tools, so its way back is its own console.
* A server that had a vRack address under a release before N31 counts as a server that knew an edge server. So port 22 of its public interface stays closed, also before it knew an edge server. The owner decided this on 2026-10-27 (plan question Q75, and question Q10 of the review of N16). Such a release kept the file `<data_dir>/hostfw/vrack-interface`. At its start, `hopboxd` writes the line `knew_edge` to the file `peers`, and then removes the file `vrack-interface`. If the write fails, the file stays, and the next start tries again.
* One netlink batch replaces the whole table. If the kernel refuses the batch, the table before it stays as it was.
* The table outlives `hopboxd`. A stop, a crash, or an upgrade of `hopboxd` keeps the table, so SSH through the jump host goes on.
* A destroy of the Terraform provider stops `hopboxd`, and then removes the table. Its public address then takes SSH again ([The Terraform provider](#the-terraform-provider)).

To let a server that left its install for good take SSH from every source again, run these commands on it:

```sh
sudo rm /var/lib/hopbox/hostfw/peers
sudo nft delete table inet hopbox_host
sudo systemctl restart hopboxd
```

While the server is still in an install, the next sets of the control role close port 22 again.

A release from before the host firewall keeps the table of a later release, and never changes its jump hosts. So the Terraform provider removes the table after it moves a server to such a release ([hopbox Terraform provider](/reference/terraform-provider/#roles-of-a-running-server)). The owner decided it on 2026-10-27 (plan question Q79). It reads the release from `hopboxd version --json`: from N16 on, the field `features` names `host-firewall` ([the version command](/reference/version/#json-output)). After a move by hand, run `sudo nft delete table inet hopbox_host` on the server through the jump host.

If a server stays closed, the rescue mode of its provider boots it into another system, which runs no table.

## The Terraform provider

The provider reaches a server without the role `edge` through the jump host of `ssh_jump_host`, which dials the peer address of the server ([hopbox Terraform provider](/reference/terraform-provider/#jump-host)). If the provider block has no `ssh_jump_host`, a create or an update of such a server fails before any step. The owner decided two more rules of the provider on 2026-10-27:

* An import takes the peer address of the server alone, such as `203.0.113.21`. The import of a server without the role `edge` dials that address through the jump host. The install must know a server with that peer address, or the import fails (plan question Q96, [hopbox Terraform provider](/reference/terraform-provider/#import)).
* A destroy removes the table once `hopboxd` stopped. It also removes the files `peers` and `vrack-interface` of `<data_dir>/hostfw`. A server of this release has no file `vrack-interface`, but a test server of a build before N31 can keep one. So a later `hopboxd` on the server never starts with the jump hosts of the old install. So its public address takes SSH again (plan question Q77, [hopbox Terraform provider](/reference/terraform-provider/#delete)). A server without `nft` gets the package `nftables` first. The login, the stop of `hopboxd`, or the removal of the table can fail. On a server without the role `edge`, the table then keeps port 22 closed to every address but the edge servers. The jump host still reaches the server. So the destroy fails with an error that names the commands to run, and keeps the resource. The next destroy goes on.

## The egress of the machines

An edge server that enrolls takes the egress of the machines of the nodes from its egress tunnel `hbe0` ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/)). Its table then has six more chains:

| Chain           | Hook and priority                      | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `egress_mark`   | prerouting, mangle                     | Puts the conntrack mark bit `0x20000000` on each new connection from a tunnel. Puts the packet mark `0x68620100` on each reply of such a connection. The rule of that mark routes the reply back into the tunnel, and not over the mesh ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/#the-tunnel-of-an-edge-server)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `egress_output` | output, mangle, of the type `route`    | Puts the same mark on each reply of the server itself. A machine reaches a public port of its own edge server, and the reply goes back through the tunnel (plan question Q52).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `forward`       | forward, filter                        | Sends each packet from a tunnel to the chain `egress`. Lets the replies into a tunnel, and drops each other packet into a tunnel. On a server with the node role, it takes the local exit too. It drops each packet from a tap device that conntrack marks invalid, and each packet from a tap device to an address of the set `known_peers`. It refuses each IPv6 packet from a tap device to `2000::/3` that leaves through another interface than the uplink. Drops the forwarded traffic of the other interfaces, as [The forward guard](#the-forward-guard) says. |
| `egress`        | none, the chain `forward` jumps to it  | Drops each packet that conntrack marks invalid. Drops each destination in the set `known_peers`. Drops the private ranges of the node table, which hold the mesh range. Drops each IPv6 destination outside `2000::/3`. Accepts IPv4 to the public zone. Accepts IPv6 from `fd65:1c74:e769::/48` only to the uplink, and only while the uplink has a global IPv6 address. Refuses the rest: TCP with a reset, and other packets with ICMP administratively prohibited.                                                                                                 |
| `egress_nat`    | postrouting, srcnat, of the type `nat` | Translates the source of the egress. IPv4 from a tunnel to the public zone gets `edge.public_ipv4`, or the masquerade without that key. IPv6 of every machine to the uplink gets the global IPv6 address of the uplink (NAT66). This holds for the tunnel and for the local exit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `egress_guard`  | postrouting, `srcnat + 10`             | Drops each packet with a source in `10.240.0.0/12` or `fd65:1c74:e769::/48` that leaves through an interface other than `lo`, `hbm0`, a tunnel, or a tap device. It comes after the source NAT, so it sees the translated source.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

The table of the node network translates the IPv4 egress of the machines of a node with the edge role. So the rule of IPv4 in `egress_nat` takes the egress of a tunnel alone ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#the-table-inet-hopbox_node)). The rule of IPv6 takes the machines of the tunnel and of the local exit alike.

The egress of a machine reaches no peer address of the install, through a tunnel or through the local exit. An edge server without `edge.public_ipv4` translates the IPv4 egress to the address of its uplink, which is its peer address. Without the drop, a machine reaches the ports that the other servers open to the set `peers`, such as the internal listener of a control server. The drop holds also when the edge server is a control server. It also holds for a server with the control role alone that stopped: such a server has no row in `servers`, so it leaves `peers` 20 s after its stop, but its own table keeps its sets and still takes this edge. It stays in `known_peers` until the sweep of its row. This is a known limit: a control server that stays down for more than 24 hours leaves `known_peers`. At its return, its start writes its row again, and the edges drop its address again within seconds.

The drop needs the whole set `known_peers`. The start of `hopboxd` knows the whole set when the file `<data_dir>/hostfw/peers` has the line `known_peers_whole` and no line that the start skips. The firewall writes that line once the sets come from the control role or from a mesh. So an empty set counts as whole too, such as on a server without a peer address. The table before the start never counts, because a start with a closed egress installs a partial set too. Until then, the chain `egress` drops each packet, and the chain `input` drops each packet from a tunnel. On a server with the node role, the chain `forward` also drops each packet from a tap device to the public zone. So no machine reaches a public address before the first sets of the control role or of a mesh, and no machine reaches a peer that the set lacks. This covers these starts:

* A start with a file of a later release that has a line that this `hopboxd` skips.
* A start with a file that it cannot read.
* A start with a file of a release before N28, without the line `known_peers_whole`.
* A start after a reboot, without the file.
* A start without the file that adopts the table before it.
* A second start before the first sets, after a start with a closed egress. The first start writes the file again without `known_peers_whole`.

At such a start, `hopboxd` logs `the host firewall does not know every peer address of the install yet, so the egress of the machines reaches no public address until the first sets of the control plane` at level warn. The first sets open the egress again. This is a build default of N28, not an owner decision.

A connection of a machine to the peer address of its own edge server never passes the forward hook. The input hook takes it, with the address of the machine as its source. The chain `input` drops each packet from a tunnel to an address of the set `known_peers`, before the jump to the zones. So a machine behind the tunnel reaches no port at the peer address of its edge server. It still reaches the public ports at the floating addresses, as the internet does. On the local exit, the node table drops a connection of a machine to its own server ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#what-a-machine-can-reach)). Peer addresses are IPv4 only (plan question Q91), so these drops have no rule of IPv6.

NAT never runs for a packet that conntrack cannot place, such as a TCP segment with SYN and FIN, or one without flags. Without a rule, such a packet leaves the uplink with the address of the machine. Two rules stop it. The chains `egress` and `forward` drop each such packet from a tunnel or a tap device, before any accept. The chain `egress_guard` drops each packet that still has the source of a machine on the way out. Each rule holds alone.

### The uplink and the NAT66

The IPv4 egress leaves through the public zone. The IPv6 egress leaves only through the uplink. The uplink is the device of the IPv6 default route of the main table, with the lowest metric. Without `edge.public_ipv4`, `hopboxd` logs `this edge server has no edge.public_ipv4, so the egress of the machines leaves from the address of its output interface` at level warn, at each start.

The NAT66 gives the IPv6 egress one global IPv6 address of the uplink. The firewall picks it in this order:

1. If the uplink holds the preferred source (`src`) of the IPv6 default route, that address.
2. Else the lowest permanent address, such as a static address of the network config of the host.
3. Else the lowest other address, such as an address of a router advertisement.

The pick skips an address in duplicate address detection, an address that failed it, a deprecated address, and a temporary address. It also skips unique local addresses, link-local addresses, and the floating address of `edge.public_ipv6` ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). The AAAA records name that floating address, and the egress never leaves from it.

With a multipath IPv6 default route, the uplink is the device of its first next hop. The kernel can send a flow to another next hop, and the table refuses the IPv6 egress there. So such a flow gets a reset or ICMPv6 administratively prohibited. Give an edge server one IPv6 default route.

Each check of the table reads the uplink again, every 2 s ([The table must stay](#the-table-must-stay)). A new uplink or a new address installs the table again. A failed read keeps the uplink of the last check.

Without an IPv6 default route, or without a global IPv6 address on the uplink, the edge server has no NAT66. The chain `egress` then refuses the IPv6 egress of the tunnel. The chain `forward` refuses the IPv6 egress of the local exit to `2000::/3`. TCP gets a reset, and other packets get ICMPv6 administratively prohibited (plan question Q85). `hopboxd` logs a warning at the start and at each change ([Logs](#logs)).

To see the uplink and the address of the NAT66 on an edge server, run these commands:

```sh
ip -6 route show default
sudo nft list chain inet hopbox_host egress_nat
```

### The forward guard

At the start of an edge server that enrolls, the host firewall reads `net.ipv4.ip_forward`. When it is `0`, the firewall turns it on for the egress, after the install of the table. Then the chain `forward` drops each forwarded IPv4 packet that touches neither a tunnel nor a tap device:

```text
    meta nfproto ipv4 iifname != "hbe*" oifname != "hbe*" drop
```

On a server with the node role, the rule also names the tap devices: `iifname != "hbt*" oifname != "hbt*"`. The file `<data_dir>/hostfw/forward-guard` records that `hopboxd` turned forwarding on ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#paths)). Each later start finds forwarding on, reads the file, and keeps the guard. Something else can turn forwarding on before the first start of `hopboxd`, such as Docker. The table then has no guard for IPv4, and the forwarding of that host stays as it was. To remove the guard, remove the file and restart `hopboxd`:

```sh
sudo rm /var/lib/hopbox/hostfw/forward-guard
sudo systemctl restart hopboxd
```

IPv6 forwarding is one switch for the whole host. The firewall turns it on at each start of an edge server that enrolls, also after the install of the table ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/#ipv6-forwarding)). So the chain `forward` always drops each forwarded IPv6 packet that touches neither a tunnel nor a tap device.

## ICMP and DHCPv6

Each interface takes these packets, also without a connection, as the owner decided on 2026-10-27 (plan question Q78 rule 2):

| Packets                                                                                                                                                   | Why                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ICMP echo request, and ICMPv6 echo request                                                                                                                | The monitoring of OVHcloud pings each server. A server that does not answer can get an intervention.              |
| ICMP destination unreachable, time exceeded, and parameter problem. ICMPv6 destination unreachable, packet too big, time exceeded, and parameter problem. | Path MTU discovery and the errors of the routes.                                                                  |
| ICMPv6 router advertisement, neighbor solicitation, neighbor advertisement, and multicast listener query                                                  | IPv6 on the link stops without them.                                                                              |
| UDP to port 546 from a link-local address                                                                                                                 | The answers of a DHCPv6 server. The request goes to a multicast address, so the answer does not count as a reply. |

## The table

On a server with the control role and the node role, the table looks like this. The set `jump_hosts` holds the edge servers:

```text
table inet hopbox_host {
  set jump_hosts {
    type ipv4_addr
  }


  set peers {
    type ipv4_addr
  }


  set registered {
    type ipv4_addr
  }


  chain input {
    type filter hook input priority filter; policy accept;
    iifname "lo" accept
    ct state established,related accept
    iifname "hbt*" accept
    meta l4proto icmp icmp type echo-request accept
    meta l4proto icmp icmp type destination-unreachable accept
    meta l4proto icmp icmp type time-exceeded accept
    meta l4proto icmp icmp type parameter-problem accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type echo-request accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type destination-unreachable accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type packet-too-big accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type time-exceeded accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type parameter-problem accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type mld-listener-query accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type nd-router-advert accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type nd-neighbor-solicit accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type nd-neighbor-advert accept
    meta nfproto ipv6 ip6 saddr fe80::/10 meta l4proto udp th dport 546 accept
    iifname "hbm0" jump mesh
    jump public
  }


  chain mesh {
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip saddr 10.239.0.0/16 meta l4proto tcp th dport 7444 accept
    drop
  }


  chain public {
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip saddr @jump_hosts meta l4proto tcp th dport 22 accept
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip saddr @peers meta l4proto udp th dport 51820 accept
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip saddr @peers meta l4proto tcp th dport 7443 accept
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip saddr @registered meta l4proto tcp th dport 7443 accept
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip saddr @peers meta l4proto udp th dport 51821-51836 accept
    drop
  }
}
```

While the server never knew an edge server, the first rule of the chain `public` is `meta l4proto tcp th dport 22 accept`. A server without the control role has no set `registered`.

Take an edge server with the DNS role, `edge.public_ipv6 = "2001:db8:1::99"`, and `edge.public_ipv4 = "203.0.113.101"`. Its uplink is `eno1`, with the global IPv6 address `2001:db8:1::11`. On it, these chains differ, and the table has no set `registered`. The edge server enrolls, and `hopboxd` turned IPv4 forwarding on, so the table has the chains of the egress too:

```text
  chain input {
    type filter hook input priority filter; policy accept;
    iifname "lo" accept
    ct state established,related accept
    meta l4proto icmp icmp type echo-request accept
    meta l4proto icmp icmp type destination-unreachable accept
    meta l4proto icmp icmp type time-exceeded accept
    meta l4proto icmp icmp type parameter-problem accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type echo-request accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type destination-unreachable accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type packet-too-big accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type time-exceeded accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type parameter-problem accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type mld-listener-query accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type nd-router-advert accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type nd-neighbor-solicit accept
    meta l4proto ipv6-icmp icmpv6 type nd-neighbor-advert accept
    meta nfproto ipv6 ip6 saddr fe80::/10 meta l4proto udp th dport 546 accept
    iifname "hbe*" meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr @known_peers drop
    iifname "hbm0" jump mesh
    jump public
  }


  chain mesh {
    drop
  }


  chain public {
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip saddr @peers meta l4proto udp th dport 51820 accept
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip saddr @peers meta l4proto udp th dport 51821 accept
    meta l4proto tcp th dport 22 accept
    meta l4proto tcp th dport 80 accept
    meta l4proto tcp th dport 443 accept
    meta l4proto tcp th dport 2222 ct status dnat accept
    meta l4proto tcp th dport 53 accept
    meta l4proto udp th dport 53 accept
    drop
  }


  chain egress_mark {
    type filter hook prerouting priority mangle; policy accept;
    iifname "hbe*" ct state new ct mark set ct mark | 0x20000000
    ct direction reply ct mark & 0x20000000 == 0x20000000 meta mark set 0x68620100
  }


  chain egress_output {
    type route hook output priority mangle; policy accept;
    ct direction reply ct mark & 0x20000000 == 0x20000000 meta mark set 0x68620100
  }


  chain forward {
    type filter hook forward priority filter; policy accept;
    iifname "hbe*" jump egress
    oifname "hbe*" ct state established,related accept
    oifname "hbe*" drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 iifname != "hbe*" oifname != "hbe*" drop
    meta nfproto ipv6 iifname != "hbe*" oifname != "hbe*" drop
  }


  chain egress {
    ct state invalid drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr @known_peers drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr 0.0.0.0/8 drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr 10.0.0.0/8 drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr 100.64.0.0/10 drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr 127.0.0.0/8 drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr 169.254.0.0/16 drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr 172.16.0.0/12 drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr 192.0.0.0/24 drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr 192.168.0.0/16 drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr 198.18.0.0/15 drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr 224.0.0.0/3 drop
    meta nfproto ipv6 ip6 daddr != 2000::/3 drop
    meta nfproto ipv4 oifname != "lo" oifname != "hbm0" oifname != "hbe*" accept
    meta nfproto ipv6 ip6 saddr fd65:1c74:e769::/48 oifname "eno1" accept
    meta l4proto tcp reject with tcp reset
    reject with icmpx admin-prohibited
  }


  chain egress_nat {
    type nat hook postrouting priority srcnat; policy accept;
    iifname "hbe*" meta nfproto ipv4 ip saddr 10.240.0.0/12 oifname != "lo" oifname != "hbm0" oifname != "hbe*" snat ip to 203.0.113.101
    meta nfproto ipv6 ip6 saddr fd65:1c74:e769::/48 oifname "eno1" snat ip6 to 2001:db8:1::11
  }


  chain egress_guard {
    type filter hook postrouting priority srcnat + 10; policy accept;
    meta nfproto ipv4 ip saddr 10.240.0.0/12 oifname != "lo" oifname != "hbm0" oifname != "hbe*" drop
    meta nfproto ipv6 ip6 saddr fd65:1c74:e769::/48 oifname != "lo" oifname != "hbm0" oifname != "hbe*" drop
  }
```
