The floating address `2001:db8:1::99` is in no rule. Without `edge.public_ipv4`, the rule of IPv4 in `egress_nat` ends with `masquerade`. An edge server can have no IPv6 default route, or no global IPv6 address on the uplink. Then the chain `egress` has no rule of IPv6 to the uplink, and `egress_nat` has no rule of IPv6 ([The uplink and the NAT66](#the-uplink-and-the-nat66)).

On a server with the node role, more rules name the tap devices `hbt*`. These are the rules of the guard, of `egress_guard`, and of the public zone in `egress` and `egress_nat`. The chain `forward` also gets these rules of the local exit:

```text
    iifname "hbt*" ct state invalid drop
    iifname "hbt*" meta nfproto ipv4 ip daddr @known_peers drop
    iifname "hbt*" meta nfproto ipv6 ip6 daddr 2000::/3 oifname != "eno1" meta l4proto tcp reject with tcp reset
    iifname "hbt*" meta nfproto ipv6 ip6 daddr 2000::/3 oifname != "eno1" reject with icmpx admin-prohibited
```

Without the NAT66, the two rules of IPv6 have no `oifname`, so they refuse each IPv6 packet of a tap device to `2000::/3`.

Until the start knows the whole set `known_peers`, the chain `egress` holds one `drop`. The rule of the tunnel in the chain `input` is `iifname "hbe*" drop`, without the set. On a local exit, the chain `forward` keeps the drop of the invalid packets, and then drops each packet from a tap device to the public zone, in place of the rules of the peers and of IPv6.

`internal/hostfw/testdata` holds both tables, and a test compares them with the rules of the code. `nft list table inet hopbox_host` prints the same rules in its own words.

### The other tables

A server can have three tables of `hopboxd`. Each table sees each packet of its hooks. An accept of one table does not stop the next table, and a drop of any table drops the packet.

| Table              | Server         | Its part                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `inet hopbox_host` | Every server   | What reaches the server.                                                                                                       |
| `inet hopbox_node` | A node         | What the machines reach, and what reaches a machine ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#the-table-inet-hopbox_node)). |
| `inet hopbox_edge` | An edge server | The redirect of the SSH ports to the SSH front door ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/)).                        |

On a server that is not an edge server, the table `inet hopbox_host` filters only the input hook. So it does not touch the traffic that a node forwards between the mesh, its machines, and its egress tunnels. On an edge server that enrolls, it also has the chains of [The egress of the machines](#the-egress-of-the-machines).

## At the start and at the stop of hopboxd

The unit `host firewall` of `hopboxd run` takes these steps at its start:

1. It reads the sets of the table that an earlier `hopboxd` installed. Without such a table, the sets start empty.
2. It reads `<data_dir>/hostfw/peers`, which gives `peers`, `jump_hosts`, and `known_peers` ([Sets](#sets)). On an edge server, the egress stays closed until the start knows the whole set `known_peers`. Only a file with `known_peers_whole` and no skipped line gives the whole set, never the table of step 1 ([The egress of the machines](#the-egress-of-the-machines)). Without the file, it keeps those of step 1. A file or a line of it that the start cannot read never stops the start, because after a reboot no table is left. The start logs the error, skips each such line, and counts the server as one that knew an edge server, so port 22 of the public interface stays closed. Without a readable file, it keeps the sets of step 1. The next sets write the file again.
3. It reads the file `<data_dir>/hostfw/vrack-interface` of a release before N31. If the file exists, the server counts as one that knew an edge server. Once the file `peers` keeps the line `knew_edge`, the start removes the file `vrack-interface` ([Never a lockout](#never-a-lockout)).
4. On an edge server that enrolls, it reads `net.ipv4.ip_forward` and the file of [the forward guard](#the-forward-guard). It finds the uplink and the address of the NAT66 ([The uplink and the NAT66](#the-uplink-and-the-nat66)).
5. It replaces the table with the rules of the roles and the sets, in one netlink batch. No packet sees a table that is half made. If the batch fails, the start of `hopboxd` fails, and the table before it stays.
6. On an edge server that enrolls, it turns on the IPv4 forwarding that step 4 found off. Then it turns on IPv6 forwarding ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/#ipv6-forwarding)).
7. It starts to watch the table.

The stop of `hopboxd` ends the watch, and keeps the table.

### The table must stay

Do not flush the nftables ruleset of a server: no `nft flush ruleset`, and no restart of `nftables.service` of Debian, whose start flushes the ruleset.

The unit watches nftables. After each change in nftables, and every 2 s in case the watch fails, it checks the table: its sets, its chains, the expressions of each rule, and the elements of each set. So a flush, a delete of a part, and a replace of a rule each show. When a part differs, it installs the whole table again. It logs this error at most once a minute, with the count of repairs in the field `repairs`:

```text
the nftables table inet hopbox_host lost a part outside hopboxd, so the host firewall installs it again. Do not flush the nftables ruleset of a server
```

The bound of the repair is 2 s, the time between two checks. In the test fleet, the table was back 22 to 48 ms after a flush. A change in nftables within 2 s of a repair waits for the next check. So two writers of the table take turns every 2 s, not at the speed of the events. Two `hopboxd` processes or another tool can be such writers. In the gap, the server has no host firewall. A connection that opened in the gap stays open after the repair, because the table takes the packets of each connection that conntrack knows. While `hopboxd` does not run, nothing repairs the table, and the next start installs it.

On an edge server, each check also finds the uplink of the NAT66 again. A check installs the table again after a new uplink or uplink address, and after new sets.

## Check the firewall

On a server, list the table, the jump hosts, and the peers:

```sh
sudo nft list table inet hopbox_host
sudo nft list set inet hopbox_host jump_hosts
sudo nft list set inet hopbox_host peers
sudo cat /var/lib/hopbox/hostfw/peers
```

In these commands, the node has the peer address `203.0.113.31`, and the edge server has the floating address `203.0.113.101`. From a host on the internet that is not a server of the install, probe the public address of the node. A connection must time out, also on port 22:

```sh
nc -vz -w 3 203.0.113.31 22
```

Log in to the node through the edge server as the jump host, at the peer address of the node:

```sh
ssh -J debian@203.0.113.101 debian@203.0.113.31
```

## Metrics

| Metric                               | Type    | Labels | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | ------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hopbox_host_firewall_repairs_total` | counter | none   | The installs of the table after it lost a part outside `hopboxd`. On a healthy server, it stays flat. It can grow every 2 s while nothing else writes nftables. Then the kernel reads a rule back in another form than the one that `hopboxd` wrote. |
| `hopbox_host_firewall_up`            | gauge   | none   | 1 when the last check found the table whole or installed it. 0 when its install failed.                                                                                                                                                              |

A host without nftables, such as a Mac, serves neither metric.

## Logs

The firewall logs with `component=hostfw`. A check logs a state only after a change of the state, so a check every 2 s does not repeat a line.

| Message                                                                                                                                                                                              | Level | Fields                                       | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `the host firewall installed its table`                                                                                                                                                              | info  | `table`, `jump_hosts`, `peers`, `registered` | An install at the start, or after a change of a set or of the uplink. `peers` and `registered` are the counts of the addresses of these sets. A repair logs the next row instead.                                                  |
| `the nftables table inet hopbox_host lost a part outside hopboxd, so the host firewall installs it again. Do not flush the nftables ruleset of a server`                                             | error | `err`, `repairs`                             | A check found the table broken, at most once a minute ([The table must stay](#the-table-must-stay)).                                                                                                                               |
| `this server had a vRack address, so port 22 of its public interface takes the jump hosts alone. The file of the last sets keeps that, so the host firewall removed the file of the vRack interface` | info  | `file`, `peers_file`                         | The start removed `<data_dir>/hostfw/vrack-interface` of a release before N31 ([Never a lockout](#never-a-lockout)).                                                                                                               |
| `cannot read the file of the vRack interface of an older release, so the host firewall keeps port 22 of the public interface closed`                                                                 | error | `err`, `file`                                | The start cannot read `<data_dir>/hostfw/vrack-interface`. The file stays.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `cannot remove the file of the vRack interface of an older release. The next start tries again`                                                                                                      | error | `err`, `file`                                | The remove of `<data_dir>/hostfw/vrack-interface` failed. Port 22 stays closed, because the file `peers` keeps `knew_edge`.                                                                                                        |
| `cannot keep the sets of the host firewall on its disk, so a restart takes them from the table, and a restart after a loss of the table opens port 22 of the public interface`                       | error | `err`, `dir`                                 | The write of `<data_dir>/hostfw/peers` failed. The next set of the control role tries again. It logs once until a write works.                                                                                                     |
| `cannot read the last sets of the host firewall, so it takes the sets of the table, and keeps port 22 of the public interface closed`                                                                | error | `err`, `file`                                | The start cannot read `<data_dir>/hostfw/peers`. It goes on with the sets of the table before it ([At the start and at the stop of hopboxd](#at-the-start-and-at-the-stop-of-hopboxd)).                                            |
| `the file of the last sets of the host firewall has a line that this hopboxd cannot read, so it skips the line, and keeps port 22 of the public interface closed`                                    | error | `file`, `line`, `text`                       | A line of `<data_dir>/hostfw/peers` is not `peer <address>`, `jump_host <address>`, or `knew_edge`, or its address is no peer address, such as a line of a later release after a rollback. The start goes on with the other lines. |
| `the install has no edge server now, so port 22 of the public interface keeps the last jump hosts`                                                                                                   | warn  | `jump_hosts`                                 | The last edge server left the install ([The jump hosts](#the-jump-hosts)). It logs once until an edge server comes back.                                                                                                           |
| `cannot install the host firewall. The next check tries again`                                                                                                                                       | error | `err`, `retry_in`                            | An install after the start failed. The table before it stays.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `this server never knew an edge server, so no jump host reaches it, and its public interface keeps port 22 open`                                                                                     | warn  |                                              | An install on a server without the edge role that never knew an edge server ([Never a lockout](#never-a-lockout)).                                                                                                                 |
| `cannot read the sets of the table before this start, so the host firewall takes the sets of its file alone`                                                                                         | warn  | `err`                                        | The start did not read the sets of the table before it. `peers` and `jump_hosts` still come from `<data_dir>/hostfw/peers`.                                                                                                        |

| `the IPv6 egress of the machines leaves from the uplink address of this edge server`                                                                                                                 | info  | `device`, `address`                          | The start of an edge server, or a new uplink or uplink address. `device` is the uplink, and `address` the source of the NAT66 ([The uplink and the NAT66](#the-uplink-and-the-nat66)).                                             |

It logs once until the error changes.                                                                                           |
| `the host firewall does not know every peer address of the install yet, so the egress of the machines reaches no public address until the first sets of the control plane`                           | warn  | `file`                                       | The start of an edge server that does not know the whole set `known_peers`. The next read tries again`                                                                                                    | warn  | `err`, `retry_in`                            | A read of the sets from the store failed, on a server with the control role. The control role logs it with `component=control`, once until a read works.                                                                           |

## Errors

| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hostfw: install the nftables table inet hopbox_host: ... hopboxd needs CAP_NET_ADMIN and the kernel needs nf_tables`                                                                           | The start cannot make the table. `hopboxd` stops, and systemd starts it again.                                                                                                                                 |
| `hostfw: read the IPv4 forwarding of the host: ...`, `hostfw: read the IPv6 forwarding of the host: ...`, `hostfw: record the forward guard: ...`, or `hostfw: record the IPv6 forwarding: ...` | The start of an edge server cannot read `net.ipv4.ip_forward` or `net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding`, or cannot write `<data_dir>/hostfw/forward-guard` or `<data_dir>/hostfw/forward-guard-ipv6`. `hopboxd` stops. |
| `hostfw: turn on IPv4 forwarding: ...` or `hostfw: turn on IPv6 forwarding: ...`                                                                                                                | The start of an edge server cannot write the sysctl. The table is in place. `hopboxd` stops.                                                                                                                   |

# Host kernel

> The build, the kernel configuration, and the install of the tested host kernel, with the scripts in build/hostkernel/.

This page covers the host kernel of hopbox servers: its build from kernel.org sources, its config, and its install. The host kernel is the Linux kernel of the server that runs Firecracker. The tested kernel is `6.18.57-hopbox1` on Debian 13. Firecracker supports the host kernel 6.18 but not 6.12, the kernel of Debian 13, so hopbox builds 6.18 from kernel.org sources.

## Files

| File                                      | What it holds                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `build/hostkernel/build.sh`               | The build script. It downloads the source, checks it, and builds Debian packages.                                                               |
| `build/hostkernel/install.sh`             | The install script. It installs the kernel package and makes it the GRUB default.                                                               |
| `build/hostkernel/config-6.18.57-hopbox1` | The final kernel config. It is the same file as `/boot/config-6.18.57-hopbox1` on the [tested server](/reference/preflight/#the-tested-server). |

## Pinned values

Each script pins its versions and checksums in variables at its top. To move to a new kernel release, change these values, `config-<release>`, and this page in one change.

| Variable            | Script       | Value                                                              | Meaning                                                                        |
| ------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `KERNEL_VERSION`    | `build.sh`   | `6.18.57`                                                          | The kernel.org release. It was the longterm 6.18 release on 2026-10-15.        |
| `KERNEL_SHA256`     | `build.sh`   | `5bd9acdc82ec5efc3790ae840e5aaa40dfde7efff261cf6dde902dc570acf98c` | The sha256 of `linux-6.18.57.tar.xz`.                                          |
| `LOCAL_VERSION`     | `build.sh`   | `-hopbox1`                                                         | The suffix of the kernel release. `uname -r` prints `6.18.57-hopbox1`.         |
| `GREGKH_FPR`        | `build.sh`   | `647F28654894E3BD457199BE38DBBDC86092693E`                         | The key of Greg Kroah-Hartman. It signs the tarball.                           |
| `AUTOSIGNER_FPR`    | `build.sh`   | `B8868C80BA62A1FFFAF5FDA9632D3A06589DA6B1`                         | The key of the kernel.org checksum autosigner. It signs `sha256sums.asc`.      |
| `DEBIAN_PACKAGE`    | `build.sh`   | `linux-image-6.18.15+deb13-amd64`                                  | The Debian package that holds the base config. It comes from trixie-backports. |
| `DEBIAN_DEB_SHA256` | `build.sh`   | `d38a7af6260782a47cd615ad717347a528b45f076245b4deabb3f1ecf8459186` | The sha256 of the Debian package file.                                         |
| `KERNEL_RELEASE`    | `install.sh` | `6.18.57-hopbox1`                                                  | The kernel release that the script installs.                                   |
| `PACKAGE_VERSION`   | `install.sh` | `6.18.57-1`                                                        | The version of the Debian package that `build.sh` writes.                      |

## Environment variables of build.sh

| Variable             | Default                 | Meaning                                                                                              |
| -------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WORK_DIR`           | `$PWD/hostkernel-build` | The folder for the downloads, the source tree, and the packages. It needs about 40 GB of free space. |
| `JOBS`               | the output of `nproc`   | The number of parallel `make` jobs.                                                                  |
| `ALLOW_CONFIG_DRIFT` | `0`                     | With `1`, the build goes on after `make olddefconfig` changes the config.                            |

## Requirements

* An amd64 host with Debian 13.
* A normal user for `build.sh`. The build needs no root.
* The build packages in the `BUILD_DEPS` list of `build.sh`. If one is missing, `build.sh` prints the `apt-get install` command and stops.
* Root for `install.sh`.
* UEFI Secure Boot off. The kernel has no Secure Boot signature.

These are the build packages:

```sh
sudo apt-get install bc bison build-essential cpio debhelper dwarves flex gawk gnupg \
  kmod libdw-dev libelf-dev libncurses-dev libssl-dev python3 rsync xz-utils zstd
```

## Build

```sh
build/hostkernel/build.sh
```

The script takes these steps:

1. It downloads `linux-6.18.57.tar.xz`, `linux-6.18.57.tar.sign`, and `sha256sums.asc` from `cdn.kernel.org`.
2. It checks the tarball against `KERNEL_SHA256`, and it checks that `sha256sums.asc` lists the same sha256.
3. It gets the kernel.org keys over WKD into a temporary GnuPG home. The autosigner key must sign `sha256sums.asc`, and the key of Greg Kroah-Hartman must sign the tarball.
4. It unpacks the source into `$WORK_DIR/linux-6.18.57`.
5. It copies `config-6.18.57-hopbox1` to `.config` and runs `make olddefconfig`. If the config changes, the script prints the change with `scripts/diffconfig` and stops.
6. It runs `make bindeb-pkg` and writes `SHA256SUMS.debs`.

The build writes these files into `$WORK_DIR`:

| File                                                  | What it holds                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `linux-image-6.18.57-hopbox1_6.18.57-1_amd64.deb`     | The kernel and its modules. `install.sh` installs only this package.          |
| `linux-image-6.18.57-hopbox1-dbg_6.18.57-1_amd64.deb` | The debug symbols, about 1 GB. The config keeps `DEBUG_INFO`, as Debian does. |
| `linux-headers-6.18.57-hopbox1_6.18.57-1_amd64.deb`   | The headers for modules outside the kernel tree. hopbox does not use them.    |
| `linux-libc-dev_6.18.57-1_amd64.deb`                  | The kernel headers for user programs. hopbox does not use them.               |
| `SHA256SUMS.debs`                                     | The sha256 of each package.                                                   |

On the tested server, the build took 48 minutes with 12 jobs, Debian gcc 14.2.0-19, and pahole 1.30.

## Config

The config starts from the Debian 6.18.15 config. `build.sh config` makes `config-6.18.57-hopbox1` again from that base:

1. It downloads the Debian package with `apt-get download` and checks it against `DEBIAN_DEB_SHA256`. If the archive no longer has the package, put the file in `$WORK_DIR/dl/` by hand. The script then uses that file.
2. It copies `/boot/config-6.18.15+deb13-amd64` from the package to `.config` and runs `make olddefconfig`.
3. It applies the changes below with `scripts/config` and runs `make olddefconfig` again.
4. It writes the result to `build/hostkernel/config-6.18.57-hopbox1` and prints the difference to the Debian config.

These changes are on purpose:

| Option                                                            | Debian 6.18.15  | 6.18.57-hopbox1 | Reason                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `LOCALVERSION`                                                    | `""`            | `"-hopbox1"`    | The release name shows a hopbox build. `LOCALVERSION_AUTO` stays off.                                                   |
| `MODULE_SIG`                                                      | `y`             | `n`             | hopbox does not sign modules. Unsigned modules on a kernel with `MODULE_SIG=y` mark the kernel as tainted at each load. |
| `MODULE_SIG_ALL`                                                  | `y`             | not set         | It depends on `MODULE_SIG`.                                                                                             |
| `SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM`                                           | `y`             | `n`             | It selects `MODULE_SIG`. `MODULE_SIG` cannot go off while this option is on.                                            |
| `SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM_EARLY`                                     | `y`             | `n`             | It depends on `SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM`.                                                                                  |
| `MODULE_SIG_KEY`, `SYSTEM_TRUSTED_KEYS`, `SYSTEM_REVOCATION_KEYS` | not in the file | `""`            | The build makes no signing key and embeds no key. Kconfig then drops `MODULE_SIG_KEY` and `SYSTEM_REVOCATION_KEYS`.     |

Kconfig also drops the options that depend on the options above, such as `CRYPTO_FIPS`, the other `MODULE_SIG_*` options, and `LOCK_DOWN_KERNEL_FORCE_*`.

`make olddefconfig` on the build host makes these changes:

* Rust is off, because the tested server has no `rustc` and no `bindgen`. The Rust drivers and `ANDROID_BINDER_IPC` drop out.
* The options that exist only in the Debian kernel patches drop out, such as `LOCK_DOWN_IN_EFI_SECURE_BOOT` and `SECURITY_PERF_EVENTS_RESTRICT`.
* The options that are new in 6.18.16 to 6.18.57 take their defaults, such as `CXL_RAS=y` and `UNWIND_USER=y`.
* `ACPI_PLATFORM_PROFILE` changes from `m` to `y`.

A different toolchain on the build host can change the config. For example, a host with `rustc` turns Rust on. Then `build.sh` stops at step 5 of the build.

The config has these features that hopbox needs:

| Feature                                                                       | Options                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| KVM                                                                           | `CONFIG_KVM=m`, `CONFIG_KVM_INTEL=m`, `CONFIG_KVM_X86=m`                                                                       |
| vsock to the guest                                                            | `CONFIG_VHOST_VSOCK=m`, `CONFIG_VHOST=m`, `CONFIG_VSOCKETS=m`                                                                  |
| tap devices                                                                   | `CONFIG_TUN=m`                                                                                                                 |
| cgroup v2                                                                     | `CONFIG_CGROUPS=y`, `CONFIG_MEMCG=y`, `CONFIG_BLK_CGROUP=y`, `CONFIG_CGROUP_PIDS=y`, `CONFIG_CPUSETS=y`, `CONFIG_CGROUP_BPF=y` |
| nftables                                                                      | `CONFIG_NF_TABLES=m`, `CONFIG_NF_TABLES_INET=y`, `CONFIG_NFT_NAT=m`, `CONFIG_NFT_MASQ=m`                                       |
| The egress of the machines ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/)) | `CONFIG_NFT_HASH=m`, `CONFIG_NFT_REJECT=m`, `CONFIG_NFT_REJECT_INET=m`                                                         |
| XFS with reflink                                                              | `CONFIG_XFS_FS=m`. Reflink has no option in 6.18. `xfs.ko` always has it.                                                      |
| btrfs                                                                         | `CONFIG_BTRFS_FS=m`                                                                                                            |
| WireGuard                                                                     | `CONFIG_WIREGUARD=m`                                                                                                           |

## Install

```sh
sudo build/hostkernel/install.sh /path/to/hostkernel-build
```

The argument is the `WORK_DIR` of the build. Its default is `$PWD/hostkernel-build`. The script takes these steps:

1. It checks that it runs as root on Debian 13 amd64.
2. It checks the image package against `SHA256SUMS.debs`.
3. It installs the image package with `dpkg -i`. The package makes `/boot/initrd.img-6.18.57-hopbox1` and runs `update-grub`.
4. It writes `/etc/default/grub.d/20_hopbox_kernel.cfg` and runs `update-grub` again.
5. It checks that `/boot/grub/grub.cfg` has the entry of the new kernel. If the entry is missing, the script removes the file of step 4, runs `update-grub`, and stops with an error.

The script does not reboot. Reboot by hand.

The file of step 4 pins the GRUB default by the ID of the menu entry. GRUB names each entry after the UUID of the root file system:

```sh
GRUB_DEFAULT="gnulinux-advanced-<root-uuid>>gnulinux-6.18.57-hopbox1-advanced-<root-uuid>"
```

A Debian kernel upgrade through `linux-image-amd64` does not change this default. The script does not edit `/etc/default/grub`.

After the reboot, these commands show a good host:

```sh
uname -r                      # 6.18.57-hopbox1
cat /proc/sys/kernel/tainted  # 0
ls /dev/kvm /dev/vhost-vsock
```

On the tested server, SSH answered 187 to 319 seconds after the reboot command.

## Fallback

The Debian kernels stay installed. They are in the “Advanced options” menu of GRUB.

To boot a Debian kernel once, run `sudo grub-reboot '<entry ID>'` and reboot. On the tested server, the GRUB environment block is on mdraid, and GRUB cannot clear `next_entry` at boot. `grub-reboot` prints a warning about this. After the reboot, clear it by hand:

```sh
sudo grub-editenv /boot/grub/grubenv unset next_entry
```

To go back to the Debian default for good, remove the pin and update GRUB:

```sh
sudo rm /etc/default/grub.d/20_hopbox_kernel.cfg
sudo update-grub
```

# The internal listener

> The TLS internal listener of the control role, its certificate, its client certificates, and the server caller.

The internal listener is the TLS listener of the control role for the servers of the install. New servers enroll on it ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/)), and enrolled servers keep their control channel on it ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/)). The edge servers call `EdgeService` on it, and send it the requests of the clients of the API and the console ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#forwarded-requests)). The code is in `internal/control` and `internal/api`.

## Listener

| Item               | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Address            | `control.internal_listen` of the bootstrap config, by default `127.0.0.1:7443` ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Address rules      | An IP address and a port. A host name, even `localhost`, is refused. Any IP address works, also one that is not loopback. Port `0` picks a free port.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Transport          | TLS 1.3 only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| HTTP versions      | HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1, picked with ALPN                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| HTTP/2 frames      | At most 64 KiB for each frame that a peer sends. A client of HTTP/2 holds a buffer of that size for each request body that it streams. So the edge holds 64 KiB for each request that it forwards, not 512 KiB.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Protocols          | Connect, gRPC, and gRPC-Web, with the binary protobuf and JSON codecs. `ControlService` takes no gzip: a request in gzip fails with `unimplemented` and the message `unknown compression "gzip"`, and no response uses gzip ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#limits-and-windows-of-the-data-streams)). The other services of the listener take gzip and answer in it. |
| Services           | `hopbox.cluster.v1.EnrollmentService`, `hopbox.cluster.v1.ControlService`, `hopbox.cluster.v1.ControlPeerService`, `hopbox.cluster.v1.EdgeService`, gRPC reflection, and gRPC health. A forwarded request reaches the public API instead. See [Forwarded requests](#forwarded-requests).                                                                                                |
| Server certificate | the control certificate of the install CA, with the URI SAN `hopbox://control` ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#control-certificate))                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Client certificate | asked for in every handshake. A client can send none. A certificate that it sends must chain to the install CA and allow client auth, or the handshake fails. A server certificate and the control certificate of another control process both pass ([Callers](#callers)).                                                                                                              |
| Unit               | `internal listener`, after `api` and before `admin socket` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Stop timeout       | 5 s. A stop ends every open stream at once, so every control channel ends ([the API server](/reference/api/#when-a-listener-stops)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Metrics            | the label `listener="internal"` for the cluster API, and `listener="edge"` for the forwarded requests ([Metrics](/reference/metrics/#metrics-of-the-api))                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

On an install with one server, the listener stays on `127.0.0.1`, and the `channel` unit of the same server dials it on loopback. With more servers, it listens on the peer address of the control server, such as `203.0.113.11:7443`, so the other servers can reach it. The host firewall takes its port on the public interface only from the peer addresses of the servers, the internal listeners of the live control processes, and the registered addresses of the enrollment tokens that work ([the host firewall](/reference/host-firewall/#sets)). Each other server then lists the listener of one or more control servers in `channel.control_urls` ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). The control role sends each server the listeners on the peer addresses of the live control processes, and the server dials them first ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#control-urls)). A listener on loopback or on a private address is not in that list.

Each control process records the URL of its listener in its row of `control_processes` (`internal_url`, [Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#control_processes)), as `https://` and the address of the listener. The other control processes forward data streams to that URL ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#streams-through-another-control-process)). A listener on every address, such as `0.0.0.0:7443`, names no address, so its row has no URL, and no data stream reaches its channels from another control process. With several control servers, set `control.internal_listen` to the peer address of the server and port 7443. `hopboxd install --internal-listen` sets it ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#install)).

## Move the first server to its peer address

The first server of an install has every role, and its listener stays on loopback while it is the only server. Before a second server enrolls, the listener moves to the peer address of the first server. The Terraform provider runs this step at an update of the first server ([hopbox Terraform provider](/reference/terraform-provider/#the-internal-listener)). To run it by hand, take these steps on the first server.

1. Make sure that the server has its peer address. The line `peer_address` of `sudo hopboxd admin server get <id>` names it. If it is empty, set it with `sudo hopboxd admin server set-peer-address <id> <address>` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-server-set-peer-address)). The install refuses a listener on another address than the stored peer address.

2. Run the install with the peer address and port 7443:

   ```sh
   sudo hopboxd install --roles control,node,dns,edge --internal-listen 203.0.113.11:7443
   ```

The install writes `control.internal_listen = "203.0.113.11:7443"`. It writes `https://203.0.113.11:7443` in the place of each loopback URL of `channel.control_urls`, or of the default `https://127.0.0.1:7443`. Then it restarts `hopboxd`, and the roles of the server dial the listener at the new URL. No loopback URL stays: the listener has one address. The machines keep running through the restart.

After the restart, these things hold:

* The control role publishes `https://203.0.113.11:7443`, so each server keeps that URL in `<data_dir>/server/control-urls` ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#control-urls)).
* The roles of the first server dial the listener from the peer address, not from loopback. The enrollment takes a call from the address of the control server itself as a call from loopback, so a token without a peer address still adds a role to the first server ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#peer-addresses)).
* The host firewall takes port 7443 of the public interface from the set `peers` and the set `registered` alone. A connection of the server to its own address goes over loopback, so the firewall takes it.

Then make the token of the second server with its peer address, and enroll the server at `https://203.0.113.11:7443` ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#peer-addresses)).

The HTTP server has the timeouts and limits of the API listener ([the API server](/reference/api/#listener)): the header read timeout, the body read timeout of a unary call, the idle timeout, and the largest request message of 4 MiB.

In maintenance mode, the listener refuses every call of the cluster API with `unavailable`, and takes only health and reflection. No method of `hopbox.cluster.v1` has the option `(hopbox.v1.read_only)`. The forwarded requests of the edge servers get the refusals of the public API ([the API server](/reference/api/#maintenance-mode)).

## Before the first key-encryption key

The certificate of the listener comes from the install CA, and the CA needs a key-encryption key to seal its key ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#install-ca)). A fresh install has no such key. So the listener starts without a certificate, and logs this warning:

```json
{"time":"2026-10-16T09:00:00Z","level":"WARN","msg":"the internal listener has no certificate yet","err":"failed precondition: the keyring has no key-encryption key to seal or open the value. Run hopboxd admin kek rotate to make the first one"}
```

Until then, each TLS handshake fails, and the HTTP server logs `http: TLS handshake error from <peer>: the internal listener has no certificate: ...` with `component=http`. `hopboxd install` makes the first key-encryption key, so a server that it set up never logs this. On another server, run `sudo hopboxd admin kek rotate` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-kek-rotate)). The next handshake then makes the CA and the certificate, without a restart.

Any other failure to read the CA stops the start of the unit.

## Callers

The request gate of the listener has one resolver, the server-certificate resolver ([the API server](/reference/api/#request-gate)):

| Case                                                                                                                            | Caller                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The connection has no client certificate.                                                                                       | `anonymous`                                                                               |
| The certificate names `hopbox://control`, and so is the control certificate of another control process.                         | `control`, with no account and no credential ID                                           |
| The certificate passes the checks of [Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#client-certificates-on-each-call). | `server`, with the ID of the server                                                       |
| The certificate fails those checks, for example its serial is unknown or its server is decommissioned.                          | none. The call ends with `unauthenticated` and the message `the credential is not valid`. |

The TLS handshake already checked that the install CA signed a certificate that names `hopbox://control`. The `control` caller has no audit credential and no idempotency scope. The policy lets it do only `control.forward_stream`, besides the actions that every caller may do (`GetInstallInfo`, health, and reflection).

Every procedure of the listener needs a server certificate or a control certificate, except `EnrollmentService.Enroll`, whose enrollment token is its credential. An anonymous call of another procedure ends with `unauthenticated` and the message `this call needs a server certificate`. This rule runs after the gate and before the policy check. So it covers health and reflection too, which the policy allows for every caller on the other listeners.

| Procedure                                                                                            | Without a certificate | With a server certificate                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `EnrollmentService.Enroll`                                                                           | allowed               | allowed                                                                                                  |
| `ControlService.Channel`, `ControlService.AttachStream`                                              | `unauthenticated`     | allowed for the server itself ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#controlservice))        |
| `ControlPeerService.ForwardStream`                                                                   | `unauthenticated`     | `permission_denied`. Only the control certificate of another control process is allowed.                 |
| `EdgeService.ExchangeMachineCode`, `EdgeService.AuthorizeMachineRequest`, `EdgeService.AuthorizeSSH` | `unauthenticated`     | allowed for a server whose certificate carries the role `edge`. Another server gets `permission_denied`. |
| `grpc.health.v1.Health`, reflection                                                                  | `unauthenticated`     | allowed                                                                                                  |

## ControlPeerService

`hopbox.cluster.v1.ControlPeerService` lets a control process forward a data stream to the control process that holds the channel of a server ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#streams-through-another-control-process)). It takes no gzip, as `ControlService` does not. Each call needs the control certificate of another control process, which is also a client certificate: the control certificate has the extended key usage client auth ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#control-certificate)).

| Procedure                                             | Policy action            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/hopbox.cluster.v1.ControlPeerService/ForwardStream` | `control.forward_stream` | Opens a data stream of a kind to a server whose channel this process holds, and carries its bytes both ways. The first request names the server and the kind. The first response has no bytes and tells that the server attached the stream. |

The messages and the errors are in [the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#controlpeerservice).

## EdgeService

`hopbox.cluster.v1.EdgeService` serves the sign-in of private machine URLs ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#private-machine-urls)) and of the SSH front door ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/)) to the edge servers. Each call needs the certificate of a server with the edge role.

| Procedure                                                | Policy action                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/hopbox.cluster.v1.EdgeService/ExchangeMachineCode`     | `server.exchange_machine_url_code` | Trades the one-time code of a private machine URL for the token of the cookie `__Host-hopbox_machine` of that URL. The code works once, within 60 s, and only for its machine. The new token replaces any older token of the same console session and machine.                                                                                                  |
| `/hopbox.cluster.v1.EdgeService/AuthorizeSSH`            | `server.authorize_ssh`             | Checks that the account of an SSH key can open a shell, as a Linux user, in the machine of an SSH port now. Each answer that allows also records a use of the machine, and each allowed sign-in writes the audit entry `machine.ssh`. The request, the response, and the rules are in [the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#edgeserviceauthorizessh). |
| `/hopbox.cluster.v1.EdgeService/AuthorizeMachineRequest` | `server.authorize_machine_url`     | Checks that the account of a token can open the private URL of the machine now. Each answer that allows also records a use of the console session, as a call of the console does ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/)).                                                                                                                |

| Message                           | Field        | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------- | ------------ | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ExchangeMachineCodeRequest`      | `machine`    | string                     | The name of the machine of the host of the request, such as `box1` for `box1.example.com`.                                                                                                                            |
| `ExchangeMachineCodeRequest`      | `code`       | string                     | The code of the query of the request.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `ExchangeMachineCodeResponse`     | `token`      | string                     | The value of the cookie `__Host-hopbox_machine`, valid only for that machine.                                                                                                                                         |
| `AuthorizeMachineRequestRequest`  | `machine`    | string                     | The name of the machine of the host of the request.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `AuthorizeMachineRequestRequest`  | `token`      | string                     | The value of the cookie `__Host-hopbox_machine`.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `AuthorizeMachineRequestResponse` | `machine_id` | string                     | The ID of the machine, a UUID.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `AuthorizeMachineRequestResponse` | `account_id` | string                     | The account of the token, a UUID.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `AuthorizeMachineRequestResponse` | `valid_for`  | `google.protobuf.Duration` | How long the edge can keep the answer: at most 1 minute, and never past the end of the console session. A change event of the access ends it sooner ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#edge-pushes)). |

`AuthorizeMachineRequest` checks four rules. Each must hold:

* The token names a row of `machine_url_sessions`, and the console session of that row lives: its absolute end and its idle end are ahead ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#machine_url_sessions), [Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/)).
* The machine of the request holds its name, its target is not `deleted`, and it is the machine of the token.
* The account uses the machine, under the policy action `machine.open_url`: it is the creator of a private machine, or a member of the org of a shared one ([the API server](/reference/api/#callers-and-policy)). An org admin does not open the private machine of another member.
* An instance admin did not suspend the org of the machine.

| Code                  | Message                                                                                  | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unauthenticated`     | `the sign-in of the machine URL is not valid: ...`                                       | The code or the token is malformed, unknown, used, expired, replaced, or for another machine, or its console session ended. The machine can also be gone. The edge starts the sign-in again. |
| `permission_denied`   | `permission denied: ...`                                                                 | The account has no access to the machine now. Another server than an edge server gets it too.                                                                                                |
| `failed_precondition` | `failed precondition: org suspended: an instance admin suspended the org of the machine` | The org of the machine is suspended.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `invalid_argument`    | `invalid argument: ...`                                                                  | The machine name is not a valid name ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/)).                                                                                                             |

## Forwarded requests

The edge servers forward the requests of the domain of the install to this listener, over the mutual TLS of their server certificates ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#forwarded-requests)). Each forwarded request carries the header `Hopbox-Client-Addr` with the address of the client, `IP:port`. The edge sets the header on each request, over any value that the client sent.

The listener splits the requests by this header:

* A request without the header reaches the cluster API, as in [Callers](#callers).
* A request with the header reaches the public API and the admin API, as on the API listener ([the API server](/reference/api/)). The plain HTTP routes under `/auth/` and the WebSocket of exec are there too. So a forwarded request never reaches the cluster API with the certificate of the edge server.

Before it serves a forwarded request, the listener checks the certificate of its connection. The certificate must pass the checks of [Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#client-certificates-on-each-call). It must also carry the role `edge`, under the policy action `server.forward_requests`. The listener keeps a passed check for 5 s, by the serial of the certificate. So each request does not cost a read of the control store. It keeps at most 1024 checks. So a decommission or a retired certificate stops the forwards within 5 s. Then the address of the header becomes the peer of the request, and the header goes. The request gate, the rate limits, and the logs see the address of the client. The credentials of the request, such as the session cookie or an API key, prove its caller. The certificate of the edge server proves no caller. Only this check trusts a client address: no listener reads `X-Forwarded-For`.

| Status | Body                                                                | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 403    | `only a server with the edge role forwards the requests of clients` | The connection has no TLS client certificate, or the certificate is refused, or its server has no edge role. The listener logs `forwarded request refused` at level warn, with `peer` and `err`. |
| 503    | `the server failed to check the credential. Retry later`            | The check of the certificate failed, for example on a failure of the control store. The listener logs `forwarded request check failed` at level error, with `peer` and `err`.                    |
| 400    | `the header Hopbox-Client-Addr must hold one IP:port`               | The header has more than one value, or a value that is not an IP address and a port.                                                                                                             |

The forwarded requests get the label `listener="edge"` in the metrics of the API. Each forwarded call also gets the access log record `api call` ([the API server](/reference/api/#logs)).

## Examples

Root on an enrolled server can call the listener with the identity of the server. `identity.pem` holds both the certificate and the key, and `ca.pem` holds the install CA ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#identity-files)). The control certificate names the IP address of the listener, so the usual host check of curl and grpcurl passes for that address.

A health check with curl and the Connect protocol:

```sh
cd /var/lib/hopbox/server
sudo curl -s --cacert ca.pem --cert identity.pem --key identity.pem \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' \
  https://127.0.0.1:7443/grpc.health.v1.Health/Check
```

```json
{"status":"SERVING"}
```

The same call without the certificate:

```sh
sudo curl -s --cacert /var/lib/hopbox/server/ca.pem \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' \
  https://127.0.0.1:7443/grpc.health.v1.Health/Check
```

```json
{"code":"unauthenticated","message":"this call needs a server certificate"}
```

The services of the listener, with grpcurl:

```sh
cd /var/lib/hopbox/server
sudo grpcurl -cacert ca.pem -cert identity.pem -key identity.pem 127.0.0.1:7443 list
```

```text
hopbox.cluster.v1.ControlService
hopbox.cluster.v1.EdgeService
hopbox.cluster.v1.EnrollmentService
```

Reflection lists only the services of the cluster API, as on the other listeners.

A control server that is not enrolled has no identity files. Use `ca.pem` of an enrolled server, or `--insecure` with curl only to see the error of a call without a certificate.

# The machine API

> The machine calls of the public API, MachineService: who can do what, the messages, the lifecycle calls, the access calls, sharing, settings, the suspension, the audit entries, and the change events.

The service `hopbox.v1.MachineService` of the public API creates, reads, and changes the machines of an org. [Placement](/reference/placement/) covers how a create picks the node of a machine. [The admin API](/reference/admin-api/#machineservice) covers the calls of instance admins on machines, and [the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#imageservice) the images that new machines start from. [The API server](/reference/api/) covers the parts that every call shares: the request gate, the policy check, the idempotency keys, and the error codes. The generated reference is [Public API](/api/public/). The code is in `internal/service` (`machines.go`, `machine_lifecycle.go`, `machine_admin.go`, `machine_events.go`) and `internal/api` (`handlers_machine.go`). The access calls are in `machine_access.go` and `handlers_machine_access.go`.

| Calls                                                                            | What they do                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `CreateMachine`                                                                  | Makes a machine and places it on a node.                                                                                                                                 |
| `GetMachine`, `ListMachines`, `WatchMachines`                                    | Read the machines that the caller sees, once or as a stream of changes.                                                                                                  |
| `ListMachineSizes`                                                               | Reads the sizes that a machine can have.                                                                                                                                 |
| `StartMachine`, `StopMachine`, `RebootMachine`, `RenameMachine`, `DeleteMachine` | Set the target state of a machine, then wait for it ([Lifecycle calls](#lifecycle-calls)).                                                                               |
| `ShareMachine`, `UnshareMachine`                                                 | Open a private machine to the whole org, or make it private again.                                                                                                       |
| `UpdateMachine`                                                                  | Changes the restart policy, the start command, or the auto-delete timeout.                                                                                               |
| `SetMachineURLPort`, `SetMachineURLVisibility`                                   | Change the port that the URL of a machine reaches, and who can open the URL.                                                                                             |
| `Exec`, `Upload`, `Download`, `StreamMachineLogs`                                | Run a command in a machine, copy files in and out, and read its log ([Access calls](#access-calls)). The WebSocket `/api/ws/exec` carries the same exec for the console. |

The examples on this page use the shell function `browser` of [the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/), with the session cookie of the caller. [Create and manage machines](/guide/machines/) runs the whole flow on a server.

## What runs the machines

The machine API sets the target state of a machine and waits for it. The executor of the machine on its node moves the machine there, and reports each step back ([the node executor](/reference/executor/), [the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/)). The waits of the lifecycle calls end once the machine got there ([Lifecycle calls](#lifecycle-calls)).

On a server with the node role, `hopboxd run` runs the executors with the Firecracker driver ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/)). A new machine reaches `running` once its guest agent applied the configuration of the machine. The first boot of an image on a node also unpacks the image. For the default image on the [tested server](/reference/preflight/#the-tested-server), the whole create takes about 25 s.

Each machine gets an IPv4 address of the subnet of its node at its create ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#addresses)). Its URL and the SSH front door reach it at this address ([the edge role](/reference/edge/), [the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/)). When the subnet of the node has no free address, the create fails with `no capacity`. Exec, file copy, and the log run over the guest link, without the network ([the node executor](/reference/executor/#exec-file-copy-and-logs)). Env vars and secrets reach a machine through its spec ([the env var API](/reference/vars-api/)).

## The org of a request

`CreateMachine`, `ListMachines`, and `WatchMachines` act in one org. They have the field `org_id`, an optional string. Leave it out to act in the default org of the caller: the org of an API key, or else the personal org of the account. A caller without either acts in no org, and the policy refuses it.

The service layer reads the role of the caller in the org before the policy check. A caller that is not a member has no role. So an org that does not exist gets the same `permission_denied` as an org of others. An `org_id` that is not a UUID gets `invalid_argument`.

## Naming a machine

A call on one machine names it in the oneof field `machine`: either `id`, the UUID of the machine, or `name`, its name. Machine names are unique in the whole install ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#machine-names)), so a name alone finds the machine.

| Case                         | Code               | Message                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Neither field is set         | `invalid_argument` | `invalid argument: the request names no machine`                                           |
| `id` is not a UUID           | `invalid_argument` | `invalid argument: the machine ID "<id>" is not a UUID`                                    |
| `name` breaks the name rules | `invalid_argument` | `invalid argument: invalid name: ...`, or `invalid argument: reserved machine name: "ns1"` |
| No machine has the ID        | `not_found`        | `not found: no machine has the ID <id>`                                                    |
| No machine has the name      | `not_found`        | `not found: no machine has the name "<name>"`                                              |

A machine that is being deleted keeps its name in its row until its executor deleted it. Meanwhile, a new machine of the same org can take the name back. A name then names two machines for a while. The lookup by name returns the one that holds the name live, else the newest. A lookup by name never finds a machine whose current state is `deleted`. A lookup by ID still finds it, until the leader drops its row ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#leader-jobs)).

## Who can do what

The creator of a machine is the account that made it, or the org key that made it. A machine starts private to its creator. Its creator can share it with the whole org.

| Call                                                                                                 | The creator | A member, on a shared machine | A member, on a private machine of another | An org admin or owner, on a private machine of another |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GetMachine`, and the machine in `ListMachines` and `WatchMachines`                                  | yes         | yes                           | no, `not_found`                           | yes                                                    |
| `StopMachine`, `DeleteMachine`                                                                       | yes         | yes                           | no, `not_found`                           | yes                                                    |
| `StartMachine`, `RebootMachine`, `RenameMachine`, `UpdateMachine`                                    | yes         | yes                           | no, `not_found`                           | no, `permission_denied`                                |
| `ShareMachine`, `UnshareMachine`, `SetMachineURLPort`, `SetMachineURLVisibility`                     | yes         | no, `permission_denied`       | no, `not_found`                           | no, `permission_denied`                                |
| `Exec`, `Upload`, `Download`, `StreamMachineLogs`, and the WebSocket of exec (action `machine.exec`) | yes         | yes                           | no, `not_found`                           | no, `permission_denied`                                |

These rules hold for each caller that acts in the org of the machine:

* A `session` or a `cli_token` acts in each org where its account has a role.
* A `member_key` acts only in its own org, as its account, while the account has a role there.
* An `org_key` acts only in its own org. It has the rights of a member, without private machines. It is never an org admin. A machine that an org key makes is shared from the start, and its creator is that key.
* An instance admin has only the rights of its own roles here. It acts on the machines of others through the admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#machineservice)).

A caller that cannot read a machine gets `not_found`, with the same message as for a machine that does not exist. So the call tells nothing about the private machines of others.

`RenameMachine`, `UpdateMachine`, `SetMachineURLPort`, and `SetMachineURLVisibility` check their fields before they look up the machine. So a bad value gets `invalid_argument`, also for a machine that does not exist, or that the caller cannot read. The check reads only the request, so it tells nothing about the machine. One check of `RenameMachine` comes after the lookup: a new name that looks like a credential ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#machine-names)). So a rename of a machine to its own name never fails on it. An anonymous caller still gets `unauthenticated` first. A caller that can read the machine, but not do the action, gets `permission_denied` with the message `permission denied: a caller of kind <kind> may not do <action>`.

The API listener resolves session cookies, CLI tokens, and API keys ([the API server](/reference/api/#request-gate)). A CLI token acts as its account. A member key acts as its account, in the org of the key only. An org key acts as a member of its org without private machines.

## Messages

### Machine

| Field                 | Type                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| `skipped_env_vars`    | int32                       | The count of env vars and secrets that the guest agent of the running machine left out, because their names break its rules ([the env var API](/reference/vars-api/#names-and-values)). 0 is the normal case.                                                                     |

| `version`             | int64                       | The version of the machine. It starts at 1 and grows by 1 with each change of the machine. A request makes such a change. A report of its executor makes one too. So does a new count of skipped env values. So does a change of an env var or a secret that reaches the machine. |
| `create_time`         | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The creation time of the machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `update_time`         | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the last change that a request made.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

In the JSON codec, a field with its default value is left out, for example `shared` false or an empty `start_command`.

### MachineSize

| Field          | Type   | Description                                  |
| -------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `name`         | string | The name of the size, for example `default`. |
| `vcpus`        | int32  | The count of vCPUs.                          |
| `memory_bytes` | int64  | The RAM, in bytes.                           |
| `disk_bytes`   | int64  | The size of the sparse disk, in bytes.       |

A fresh install has one size, `default`: 2 vCPUs, 8 GiB of RAM, and a sparse disk of 100 GB ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#sizes)). An instance admin can add other sizes ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#sizeservice)).

### MachineState

| Value                       | State                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `MACHINE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED` | Never in a response.                                                           |
| `MACHINE_STATE_PENDING`     | `pending`: the machine exists, but no node acted on it yet.                    |
| `MACHINE_STATE_STARTING`    | `starting`: the microVM boots.                                                 |
| `MACHINE_STATE_RUNNING`     | `running`: the microVM runs.                                                   |
| `MACHINE_STATE_STANDBY`     | `standby`: the microVM is paused, and its memory stays in the RAM of the node. |
| `MACHINE_STATE_HIBERNATED`  | `hibernated`: the memory is in a file on disk, and the microVM does not run.   |
| `MACHINE_STATE_STOPPED`     | `stopped`: the microVM does not run. The disk stays.                           |
| `MACHINE_STATE_FAILED`      | `failed`: an action failed. The saved state of the machine stays.              |
| `MACHINE_STATE_DELETED`     | `deleted`: the machine and its saved state are gone.                           |
| `MACHINE_STATE_MOVING`      | `moving`: a drain moves the machine to another node.                           |

### RestartPolicy

| Value                        | Policy                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
