# Sign-in with GitHub and Google

> The sign-in with GitHub and Google: its config, redirect URIs, browser endpoints, checks, cookies, errors, limits, logs, and audit entries.

A person can sign in to an install with GitHub or Google. The operator registers an OAuth app at each provider and gives hopbox the client ID and the client secret. hopbox cannot register these apps itself, because each app has redirect URIs on the domain of one install. This page gives the config, the browser endpoints, and the checks of a sign-in. It also gives the link of an identity to a signed-in account, the cookies, the errors, the rate limits, the logs, and the audit entries. [Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/) covers the session that a sign-in starts. [Sign in with GitHub and Google](/guide/github-google-sign-in/) sets up both providers step by step. The code is in `internal/auth/oauth`, `internal/service/oauth.go`, and `internal/api/oauth.go`.

## Providers

| Provider | Name in commands | Protocol                                                                                  | Scopes                 | Subject                              | Email                                                                         |
| -------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| GitHub   | `github`         | OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, a GitHub OAuth app                                                   | `user:email`           | the numeric user ID from `GET /user` | the primary email from `GET /user/emails`, which GitHub verified              |
| Google   | `google`         | OpenID Connect with PKCE and a nonce, a Google OAuth client of the type “Web application” | `openid email profile` | the `sub` claim of the ID token      | the `email` claim of the ID token. The claim `email_verified` must be `true`. |

hopbox takes only an email of ASCII characters from a provider. The provider verified the exact address, and a case mapping of other letters can lead to another address. For example, a case mapping makes `ceo@icorp.com` out of `ceo@İcorp.com`. An email with a character that is not ASCII thus never signs in.

The subject names the person at the provider and never changes. A later sign-in finds the account by the subject, also after the person changes the email at the provider. hopbox trusts only an email that the provider verified. At GitHub, only the primary email counts. A secondary email can be an old address that the person no longer holds, so it never links to an account.

hopbox keeps no token of a provider. The token of GitHub serves only the two reads of the sign-in. The ID token of Google serves only its checks.

## Config

The client of each provider lives in the table `install_config` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#install_config)). An instance admin sets it through the admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#getoauthconfig)) or with `hopboxd admin config oauth` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-config-oauth-get)).

| Field         | Type   | Default                       | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ------ | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Client ID     | string | empty, so the provider is off | 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters, without spaces.                                                                                                                                 |
| Client secret | string | none                          | 1 to 512 printable ASCII characters, without spaces. A client ID needs a secret. The secret stays only with the client ID that it came with. A new client ID needs the secret again. |

The control store keeps the secret sealed with the current key-encryption key ([Sealing](/reference/sealing/#places)). The place is the install secret `oauth.github.client_secret` or `oauth.google.client_secret`. `RewrapSealedValues` covers both secrets, and `ListKEKs` counts them. The API never returns a secret, only `client_secret_set`.

A provider with a client is on, on an install with a domain. Then `GetInstallInfo` lists `SIGN_IN_METHOD_GITHUB` or `SIGN_IN_METHOD_GOOGLE` ([the API server](/reference/api/#getinstallinfo)). A clear of the client turns the provider off. The sign-in methods of that provider stay on their accounts. After a new set of the client, they work again.

## Redirect URIs

The redirect URI of a provider is the URI to which the provider sends the browser back. Register exactly this URI at the provider:

| Provider | Redirect URI                            |
| -------- | --------------------------------------- |
| GitHub   | `https://<domain>/auth/github/callback` |
| Google   | `https://<domain>/auth/google/callback` |

For an install with the domain `example.com`, the URIs are `https://example.com/auth/github/callback` and `https://example.com/auth/google/callback`. `hopboxd admin config oauth` prints them. Each sign-in sends this exact URI to the provider twice: in the authorization URL and in the token request. The provider refuses a code for another URI only with exact matching. Google always matches exactly. A GitHub OAuth app with one callback URL can match by wildcard: it then also takes a URI on a subdomain or in a subdirectory of the callback URL. A machine URL is a subdomain of the install that serves the content of a user. So the operator must turn off wildcard matching for the callback URL of the GitHub app ([Sign in with GitHub and Google](/guide/github-google-sign-in/#register-the-github-oauth-app)). A change of the domain changes the URIs, and the operator must register the new URIs at each provider.

## Endpoints

Each provider has two endpoints on the API listener. The edge servers forward them, with the rest of the domain of the install ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#forwarded-requests)). They are plain HTTP `GET` requests, not Connect calls, because the browser goes to them through links and redirects. Another method gets `405 Method Not Allowed`.

| Endpoint                        | Query parameters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Answer                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /auth/{provider}/start`    | `return_to`: optional, the path on the install to open after the sign-in. The default is `/`. `link`: optional, `1` for a link of the identity to the account of the session ([Link to a signed-in account](#link-to-a-signed-in-account)). Another value of `link`, or two of them, gets `400`. | `303 See Other` to the authorization URL of the provider, with the state cookie             |
| `GET /auth/{provider}/callback` | `code`, `state`, and `error`, which the provider sets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `303 See Other` to the return path, with the session cookie. A link sets no session cookie. |

`{provider}` is `github` or `google`. Another name gets `404 Not Found`.

Each answer has `Cache-Control: no-store`. The callback also has `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, because its URL holds the code.

### Start

A start makes a flow: a new state, a PKCE code verifier, and a nonce. The state is 32 random bytes in base64url, 43 characters. The browser gets the state in the URL of the provider and in the state cookie. The verifier never leaves the server before the token request. The URL of the provider has the client ID, the redirect URI, the scopes, and the state. It also has the PKCE challenge with the method `S256`, and for Google the nonce.

The control store keeps the flow in the table `oauth_flows` for 10 minutes ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#oauth_flows)). It keeps only the SHA-256 of the state.

Only a page of the install, or the person, can start a sign-in. The start refuses a request whose header `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `cross-site` or `same-site`. A browser sets this header on its own, and a page cannot change it. So a page of another site cannot start a sign-in in the browser of a visitor. A machine URL such as `https://box1.example.com` is `same-site`, so a page that a machine serves cannot start one either. A request without the header passes, and so does a typed URL or a bookmark, which has the value `none`.

### Return path

The return path must be a plain path on the install, so a link to the start can never send the browser to another site. A return path must have all of these properties:

* It starts with exactly one `/`.
* It has no scheme and no host. `https://evil.example/` and `//evil.example` fail.
* It has no backslash, no space, and no control character.
* It has no `.` or `..` segment, also in the encoded form `%2e%2e`.
* It has at most 512 characters.

A query and a fragment can follow the path, for example `/device?code=ABCD-EFGH`. The flow keeps the return path, and the callback sends the browser to it as it is, without a decode. A client that builds the start link, such as the console ([Console](/reference/console/#sign-in)), must pass the path as it is too. It must never decode `return_to` before it sends the browser there, because a decode can turn a safe path such as `/%2F%2Fevil.example` into `//evil.example`. Thus a change of the URL between the start and the callback has no effect on it.

### Callback

The callback ends a sign-in in these steps. Any failed step ends the sign-in with an error page.

1. The callback limit of the client IP address must allow the request ([Rate limits](#rate-limits)).
2. The response clears the state cookie, whatever the result.
3. The `state` parameter must have the form of a token and must equal the state cookie of the browser. The compare takes the same time for any value.
4. One statement marks the flow used. It must exist, have the same provider, be unused, and be within its 10 minutes. So a flow works once, also with two callbacks at the same time.
5. If the provider sent `error`, the sign-in ends. The flow stays used.
6. The server trades the code for a token at the provider, with the client secret, the redirect URI, and the PKCE verifier.
7. For GitHub, the server reads `GET /user` and `GET /user/emails`. For Google, it checks the ID token ([Checks of the ID token of Google](#checks-of-the-id-token-of-google)).
8. The provider must prove a verified email. The server then signs the person in, as [Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#what-a-sign-in-does) gives. A flow of a link adds the identity to the account instead ([Link to a signed-in account](#link-to-a-signed-in-account)).
9. The response sets the session cookie and sends the browser to the return path. After a link, it only sends the browser to the return path.

The callback is the one request that sets the session cookie without the `Origin` check of [Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#calls-with-the-cookie). The provider sends the browser back from its own site, so the request has no `Origin` of the install. Step 3 replaces the check. Another site can start a flow in its own browser and send the callback URL to a victim. But the browser of the victim does not have the state cookie of that flow, so the callback fails. A machine subdomain cannot set the cookie either, because of the `__Host-` prefix.

The calls to the provider run outside of any database transaction, with a limit of 20 s for the whole exchange.

If the browser has a live session, the new session replaces it, as for any sign-in.

### Link to a signed-in account

A person who is signed in links a GitHub user or a Google account to the account ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#link-a-new-sign-in-method)). Once the account has an identity of a provider, this is the only way to add another one. The browser opens the start with `link=1`, and the console sends it there from `/account`:

```text
https://example.com/auth/google/start?link=1&return_to=%2Faccount
```

The start reads the session cookie of the browser. It checks the session in this order:

| Session                                                                                                                           | Answer                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No live session                                                                                                                   | `303 See Other` to `/signin?return_to=<path>`. After the sign-in, the console opens the return path, where the person starts the link again. |
| A session whose sign-in is more than 10 minutes old ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#recent-sign-in)) | `303 See Other` to `/signin?again=1&return_to=<path>`.                                                                                       |
| A session with a recent sign-in                                                                                                   | The start of a sign-in, as above. The flow also records the session in `oauth_flows.link_session_id`.                                        |

A return path of `/` leaves out `return_to`. A return path that breaks a rule gets the error page instead of the redirect. The limits of starts count a link as a start.

The callback of a link must come with the session cookie of the same session. Another session, or a browser without a session, gets `400` at step 4, and the flow is used. The exchange with the provider runs as for a sign-in. The callback then adds the identity to the account, with the checks of [Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#link-a-new-sign-in-method). It sets no session cookie, and the session of the browser stays. The callback sends the browser to the return path, for example `/account`.

### Checks of the ID token of Google

The server reads the discovery document of the issuer `https://accounts.google.com` once per process and keeps it. A failed read is not kept, so the next sign-in reads it again. The ID token must pass these checks:

| Check                                                                       | Error                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| The token response holds an `id_token`.                                     | the provider failed              |
| The signature matches a key of the `jwks_uri` of Google.                    | the provider refused the sign-in |
| The issuer is the issuer of Google.                                         | the provider refused the sign-in |
| The audience holds the client ID of the install.                            | the provider refused the sign-in |
| The token is not expired.                                                   | the provider refused the sign-in |
| The `nonce` claim equals the nonce of the flow.                             | the provider refused the sign-in |
| The `sub` claim is not empty.                                               | the provider refused the sign-in |
| The `email` claim is not empty, and `email_verified` is `true` or `"true"`. | no verified email                |

## Cookies

The start sets the state cookie, and the callback clears it:

```text
Set-Cookie: __Host-hopbox_oauth_github=<state>; Path=/; Expires=<end>; Max-Age=600; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
```

| Attribute               | Value                                                        | Reason                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Name                    | `__Host-hopbox_oauth_github` or `__Host-hopbox_oauth_google` | The `__Host-` prefix keeps the cookie on the host of the install. A machine subdomain cannot set it or read it.                                              |
| `Max-Age`               | 600, the 10 minutes of the flow                              | An old cookie cannot match a new flow.                                                                                                                       |
| `HttpOnly` and `Secure` | set                                                          | Scripts cannot read the state, and the browser sends it only over HTTPS.                                                                                     |
| `SameSite`              | `Lax`                                                        | The provider sends the browser back with a top-level `GET` from its own site. A browser sends a `Lax` cookie with such a request, but not a `Strict` cookie. |

One browser has one state cookie per provider. A second start with the same provider replaces the cookie, so the first flow then fails at its callback with `400`.

The callback sets the session cookie of [Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#the-session-cookie).

## Errors

Each error answers with a plain text page, `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'`. A browser thus never runs markup from a URL parameter. The page has this form:

```text
The sign-in failed: <message>


Request ID: <request ID>
```

| Status                      | When                                                                                                                                                                                              | Message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400 Bad Request`           | The state is missing, malformed, not the state of the browser, unknown, used, or expired. The callback has no code.                                                                               | `the sign-in is not valid: it did not start in this browser, it was used, or it expired. Start the sign-in again`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `400 Bad Request`           | Two tabs of one browser started the same provider. The second start replaced the state cookie of the first, so the first callback fails.                                                          | the same message as above                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `400 Bad Request`           | The return path breaks a rule.                                                                                                                                                                    | `invalid argument: the return path must be a path on the install, such as /orgs: ...`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `403 Forbidden`             | The start came from another site.                                                                                                                                                                 | `start the sign-in from a page of this install, or open its link yourself`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `403 Forbidden`             | The provider sent `error`. For example, the person clicked Cancel at the provider.                                                                                                                | `the provider did not approve the sign-in: GitHub answered access_denied. Start the sign-in again`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `403 Forbidden`             | The provider refused the code, the token, or the ID token.                                                                                                                                        | `the provider did not approve the sign-in: GitHub refused the sign-in code. Start the sign-in again. If this repeats, the operator must check the GitHub client`                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `403 Forbidden`             | The email of the provider has a character that is not ASCII.                                                                                                                                      | `the provider has not verified an email of this account: hopbox cannot use the email that GitHub gave: invalid email: ... holds a character that is not ASCII`                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `403 Forbidden`             | The provider proved no verified email.                                                                                                                                                            | `the provider has not verified an email of this account: verify an email at GitHub, make it the primary email there, and sign in again`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `400 Bad Request`           | The parameter `link` of the start is not `1`, or comes twice.                                                                                                                                     | `invalid argument: the parameter link must be 1`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `409 Conflict`              | The account of the verified email has an identity of a provider, so a new method joins it only through a link ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#what-a-sign-in-does)). | `the sign-in conflicts with a sign-in method of the account: the account of dana@example.org signs in with GitHub or Google, so a new sign-in method joins it only through a link. Sign in with a method of the account, then link Google on the account page. If you lost every method of the account, the operator removes the lost one with hopboxd admin account sign-in-method remove` |
| `409 Conflict`              | A link: the identity signs in to another account.                                                                                                                                                 | `the sign-in conflicts with a sign-in method of the account: this Google identity signs in to another account. Remove it from that account first`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `409 Conflict`              | A link: the account has another identity of the same provider.                                                                                                                                    | `the sign-in conflicts with a sign-in method of the account: the account already signs in with another GitHub identity. Remove that method first, then link the new one`                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `403 Forbidden`             | A link: the session ended between the start and the callback.                                                                                                                                     | `this call needs a credential: the session that started the link ended. Sign in again, then link the method again`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `409 Conflict`              | A link: the account has this identity already.                                                                                                                                                    | `already exists: the account already signs in with this GitHub identity`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `404 Not Found`             | The provider name is unknown.                                                                                                                                                                     | `no sign-in provider "gitlab". Use github or google`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `404 Not Found`             | The install has no client for the provider, or no domain.                                                                                                                                         | `failed precondition: this install has no GitHub client, so it offers no sign-in with GitHub`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `429 Too Many Requests`     | A rate limit refused the request.                                                                                                                                                                 | the message of the limit, see below                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `502 Bad Gateway`           | The provider did not answer, or answered with an error of its own.                                                                                                                                | `unavailable: GitHub did not answer. Start the sign-in again later`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `500 Internal Server Error` | Any other failure, such as a control store that does not answer.                                                                                                                                  | `internal error. The server log has the details under the request ID`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

The messages say Google instead of GitHub for a sign-in with Google. A value of `error` from the URL that is not 1 to 64 letters, digits, `_`, `.`, or `-` shows as `unknown`.

## Recover a lost identity

A person can lose the GitHub user or the Google account that the account signs in with. A sign-in with a new GitHub user and a verified email of the account then gets `409`. The account has an identity of a provider, so the email links no new method ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#what-a-sign-in-does)). The rule stops the new owner of a lapsed domain, who can prove an old address of the account. The person recovers in one of two ways.

With another sign-in method of the account, such as its email link or Google:

1. Sign in with that method.
2. On `/account`, remove the old GitHub method. The API call is `RemoveSignInMethod` ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/#removesigninmethod)).
3. On `/account`, select “Link GitHub”, and approve the new GitHub user at GitHub ([Link to a signed-in account](#link-to-a-signed-in-account)).

Without another method, for example on an install without SMTP, an instance admin removes the lost method on a control server:

```sh
sudo hopboxd admin account sign-in-method list --email dana@example.org
sudo hopboxd admin account sign-in-method remove --account-id <account> --method-id <method> --allow-last
```

The account then has no method, and so no identity of a provider. A sign-in that proves a verified email of the account links to it again. No other account holds an email link of that email, because a link refuses the verified email of another account ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#link-a-new-sign-in-method)) ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-account-sign-in-method-remove)). The person signs in with a magic link to that email, or with the new GitHub user. Then the person links the other methods from `/account`.

The operator must first make sure that the person holds the email. Otherwise the removal hands the account to the holder of the address. The audit log of the personal org records the removal, with the actor.

The message of the `409` names both ways.

## Rate limits

| Limit                                                        | Value                                                                                                             | Where it counts                                                                         | Message                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Starts from one client: one IPv4 address, or one IPv6 /64    | 30 per hour, for both providers together                                                                          | the rows of `oauth_flows` in the control store, so it holds across every control server | `too many requests: this client started the most sign-ins of an hour. Wait, then retry`                                           |
| Starts of the whole install                                  | 5000 per hour (`service.OAuthStartsPerHour`), for both providers together, for every client, also a loopback peer | the rows of `oauth_flows` in the control store                                          | `too many requests: the install started the most sign-ins with GitHub and Google of an hour. Wait, or sign in with an email link` |
| Callbacks from one client: one IPv4 address, or one IPv6 /64 | 60 per hour                                                                                                       | the memory of each `hopboxd` process                                                    | `too many requests: this client sent the most sign-in callbacks of an hour. Wait, then retry`                                     |

Each callback that reaches a provider needs a start, so the limit of starts also bounds the calls to the providers. The limit of callbacks keeps a flood of bad callbacks away from the control store. It tracks at most 100,000 clients per process. When it holds that many, it first drops the clients whose hour ended. If it is still full, it lets each new client pass without a count, and keeps the counts of the clients that it holds. So a flood of new addresses cannot reset the count of a client. It cannot lock every new client out for an hour either. Each callback still needs a start, and the limits of starts hold.

The limit of the install bounds the rows of `oauth_flows`. It holds also against many clients at once. Its cost: such a flood can block the sign-ins with GitHub and Google of everyone for up to an hour. The email links still work then. When the install reaches the limit, the service logs `the install reached its limit of OAuth sign-ins of an hour` at level warn, with `limit` and `request_id`.

As for magic links, the limits of a client skip a loopback peer, such as `127.0.0.1` or `::1` ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#rate-limits)). A loopback peer is a process or an SSH tunnel on the same server, which stands for every client. Behind the edge, the peer is the address of the client that the edge forwards. Only a server with the edge role can name it ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/#forwarded-requests)). Each start takes a transaction lock (`LockKeyOAuthFlows`, [the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#advisory-lock-keys)), so starts at the same time cannot pass a limit together.

## Logs

Each record has `component=api` or `component=service`, and never holds a state, a code, a verifier, a nonce, a token, or a secret.

| Record                                                       | Level         | Fields                                                     | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `oauth sign-in started`                                      | info          | `provider`, `link`, `request_id`                           | A start sent the browser to the provider. `link` is `true` for a link to a signed-in account.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `oauth sign-in start refused`                                | info          | `provider`, `sec_fetch_site`, `request_id`                 | A start came from another site.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `oauth sign-in start failed`                                 | warn          | `provider`, `err`, `request_id`                            | The discovery document of Google did not load.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `oauth sign-in`                                              | info          | `provider`, `account`, `new_account`, `request_id`         | A callback signed a person in.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `oauth link`                                                 | info          | `provider`, `account`, `request_id`                        | A callback linked an identity to the account of the session.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `oauth sign-in refused`                                      | info          | `provider`, `request_id`, `reason`, and `err` for an email | A callback failed a check of the state, had no code, or had no verified email. The callback of a link came without its session: `the link did not come back with the session that started it`.                                                                      |
| `oauth sign-in refused`                                      | warn          | `provider`, `request_id`, `reason`, `subject`              | The account of the email has an identity of a provider: `the account needs a link for a new sign-in method`. Or a link found the identity on another account, or another identity of the provider on the account: `the identity or the account holds another link`. |
| `oauth sign-in denied by the provider`                       | info          | `provider`, `request_id`, `error`                          | The callback had the `error` parameter.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `oauth sign-in refused by the provider`                      | warn          | `provider`, `request_id`, `err`                            | The provider refused the code or the token. A repeat can mean a wrong client secret or redirect URI.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `oauth sign-in failed`                                       | warn or error | `provider`, `err`, `request_id`                            | The provider did not answer (warn), or another failure (error).                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `the install reached its limit of OAuth sign-ins of an hour` | warn          | `limit`, `request_id`                                      | A start found 5000 starts in the last hour.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## Audit entries

A sign-in writes the entries of [the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/#audit-entries) in its transaction. For GitHub and Google, `auth.sign_in` has the `method` `github` or `google`, and these details:

| Detail        | Value                                                                           |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `email`       | the verified email, in lower case                                               |
| `new_account` | `true` for a first sign-in                                                      |
| `oauth_flow`  | the UUID of the flow                                                            |
| `subject`     | the subject at the provider                                                     |
| `login`       | the GitHub login. Google has no login, so a sign-in with Google has no `login`. |

A first sign-in also writes `account.create`, and a link by a verified email writes `account.link_sign_in_method` with the `kind` `github` or `google`. A link to a signed-in account writes only `account.link_sign_in_method`, with the session as the actor. Its details are `kind`, `email`, `session`, `oauth_flow`, `subject`, and for GitHub `login`. Each `account.link_sign_in_method` of an instance admin also has `instance_admin` set to `true`, and tells the instance admins ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#notices-to-instance-admins)). A start, a refused callback, and a failed callback write no entry, because no account acts. The log records above cover them.

The calls of the config write the entries of [the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#getoauthconfig): `oauth_config.get`, `oauth_config.set`, and `oauth_config.clear`.

## Sweep

The leader deletes the flows that are older than 24 hours, every 10 minutes, with the sign-in links ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#sweep)). A flow stays after its use or expiry for the limit of starts.

# The org API

> The org calls of the public API, OrgService: orgs, roles, members, invitations, usage limits, the suspension, and their audit entries.

The service `hopbox.v1.OrgService` of the public API manages the orgs of the caller, their members, their invitations, and reads their usage and limits. [The admin API](/reference/admin-api/#orgservice) covers the calls of instance admins on orgs: the list of every org, the suspension, and the limits. [The API server](/reference/api/) covers the parts that every call shares: the request gate, the policy check, the idempotency keys, and the error codes. The generated reference is [Public API](/api/public/). The code is in `internal/service` (`orgs.go`, `invitations.go`) and `internal/api`.

| Calls                                                                         | What they do                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CreateOrg`, `GetOrg`, `ListOrgs`, `UpdateOrg`, `DeleteOrg`                   | Make, read, rename, and delete orgs.                    |
| `GetOrgUsage`                                                                 | Reads what an org uses, and its limits.                 |
| `ListOrgMembers`, `SetOrgMemberRole`, `RemoveOrgMember`, `LeaveOrg`           | Read and change the members of an org.                  |
| `CreateInvitation`, `ListInvitations`, `RevokeInvitation`, `AcceptInvitation` | Invite a person by email, and join with the invitation. |

Each call acts as the account of a `session` or `cli_token` caller. A `member_key` acts as its account too, but only in the org of the key, and it never creates, joins, or leaves an org. An `org_key` has the rights of a member in its own org, without personal resources: it reads the org, its usage, and its members ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#api-keys)). An instance admin sees the orgs of others only through the admin API. Here, a session of an instance admin has only the rights of its own roles.

The examples on this page use the shell function `browser` of [the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/), with the session cookie of the caller. [Work in a team org](/guide/orgs/) runs the whole flow on a laptop.

## The org of a request

A request that acts in one org has the field `org_id`, an optional string. Leave it out to act in the personal org of the caller ([the API server](/reference/api/#callers-and-policy)). `ListOrgs`, `CreateOrg`, and `AcceptInvitation` have no `org_id`.

The service layer reads the role of the caller in the org before the policy check. A caller that is not a member has no role. So an org that does not exist gets the same `permission_denied` as an org of others. An `org_id` that is not a UUID gets `invalid_argument`.

## Roles

The enum `OrgRole` names the role of an account in an org ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#org-roles)). Each role has every right of the roles before it.

| Value                  | Role                                                            | Default                                      |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `ORG_ROLE_UNSPECIFIED` | Never in a response. In a request, the field takes its default. |                                              |
| `ORG_ROLE_MEMBER`      | `member`                                                        | the role of an invitation without a role     |
| `ORG_ROLE_ADMIN`       | `admin`                                                         |                                              |
| `ORG_ROLE_OWNER`       | `owner`                                                         | the role of the account that creates the org |

A value that is not in the enum gets `invalid_argument` with the message `invalid argument: the org role <n> is not known`.

### What each role can do

| Call                                                  | `member` | `admin` | `owner` |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- | ------- |
| `GetOrg`, `GetOrgUsage`, `ListOrgMembers`, `LeaveOrg` | yes      | yes     | yes     |
| `ListInvitations`, `RevokeInvitation`                 | no       | yes     | yes     |
| `CreateInvitation` with the role `member`             | no       | yes     | yes     |
| `CreateInvitation` with the role `admin` or `owner`   | no       | no      | yes     |
| `RemoveOrgMember` of a `member`                       | no       | yes     | yes     |
| `RemoveOrgMember` of an `admin` or an `owner`         | no       | no      | yes     |
| `SetOrgMemberRole`, `UpdateOrg`, `DeleteOrg`          | no       | no      | yes     |

Only an owner makes other owners and admins. So an admin invites and removes members only. A caller without the right gets `permission_denied`, with the message `permission denied: a caller of kind session may not do <action>`.

### Every org keeps an owner

An org always has at least one owner. If a change takes the last owner from the org, it fails with `failed_precondition`. These changes can do so: `SetOrgMemberRole` of the last owner to another role, `RemoveOrgMember` of the last owner, `LeaveOrg` by the last owner, and `DeleteAccount` of the last owner ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/#deleteaccount)).

Each such change first locks the row of the org in `orgs`. Then it reads the role of the caller again, checks the policy again, and counts the owners in a new statement ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#orgs)). So two owners that each step down, leave, or remove the other at the same time leave one owner. The second change sees the first one, and fails with `failed_precondition` or `permission_denied`. The delete of an account locks every org of the account in the same way. So a promotion of the account to owner during its delete waits for the delete, and then fails with `not_found`.

## Messages

### Org

| Field            | Type                        | Description                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`             | string                      | The UUID of the org.                                                                                                                                   |
| `name`           | string                      | The name of the org ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#org-names)). A personal org starts with the name `Personal`, and its owner can rename it. |
| `personal`       | bool                        | `true` for the personal org of an account.                                                                                                             |
| `role`           | `OrgRole`                   | The role of the caller in the org.                                                                                                                     |
| `suspended`      | bool                        | `true` while an instance admin suspends the org ([Suspension](#suspension)).                                                                           |
| `suspend_time`   | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The start of the suspension. Unset for an org that is not suspended.                                                                                   |
| `suspend_reason` | string                      | The reason that the instance admin gave, or empty.                                                                                                     |
| `version`        | int64                       | The version of the org. It starts at 1 and grows by 1 with each change, such as a rename, a suspension, or new limits.                                 |
| `create_time`    | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The creation time of the org.                                                                                                                          |

### OrgMember

| Field          | Type                        | Description                                                                                           |
| -------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `account_id`   | string                      | The UUID of the account.                                                                              |
| `display_name` | string                      | The display name of the account.                                                                      |
| `emails`       | repeated `AccountEmail`     | The emails of the account ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/#accountemail)). |
| `role`         | `OrgRole`                   | The role of the account in the org.                                                                   |
| `join_time`    | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the join.                                                                                 |

### OrgLimits and OrgUsage

`OrgLimits` holds the usage limits of an org, and `OrgUsage` holds what the org uses ([Usage limits](#usage-limits)). Both have the same fields.

| Field          | Type  | Description                                  |
| -------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `machines`     | int32 | The machines.                                |
| `vcpus`        | int32 | The vCPUs of all machines together.          |
| `memory_bytes` | int64 | The RAM of all machines together, in bytes.  |
| `disk_bytes`   | int64 | The disk of all machines together, in bytes. |

### Invitation

| Field                | Type                        | Description                                                                                  |
| -------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                 | string                      | The UUID of the invitation.                                                                  |
| `org_id`             | string                      | The UUID of the org.                                                                         |
| `email`              | string                      | The email that the invitation is for, in lower case.                                         |
| `role`               | `OrgRole`                   | The role that the invitation gives.                                                          |
| `inviter_account_id` | string                      | The UUID of the account that made the invitation, or empty after the delete of that account. |
| `create_time`        | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the invitation.                                                                  |
| `expire_time`        | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The end of the invitation, 7 days after `create_time`.                                       |

## Orgs

### CreateOrg

Makes an org with the caller as its owner.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.OrgService/CreateOrg`                                                                                                                       |
| Policy action     | `org.create`: `session` and `cli_token`                                                                                                                 |
| Idempotent option | yes. A call must have an `Idempotency-Key` header ([the API server](/reference/api/#idempotency-keys)). A retry with the same key returns the same org. |
| Audit entry       | action `org.create`, org the new org, target kind `org`, details `name`                                                                                 |

The request `CreateOrgRequest` has the field `name`, a string ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#org-names)). The response `CreateOrgResponse` has the field `org`, an `Org`.

An account owns at most 10 orgs besides its personal org. Every new org brings its own usage limits, so this cap keeps one account from many limits. An instance admin changes the cap with `SetDefaultOrgLimits` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setdefaultorglimits)). The cap counts each org in which the account is an owner. The call takes the row lock of the account, so two creates at the same time cannot pass the cap together.

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                                | Code                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| A bad name, for example `invalid argument: invalid org name: it must not start or end with a space`                                                                                                  | `invalid_argument`   |
| The account owns the most orgs: `usage limit exceeded: the account owns 10 orgs besides its personal org, the most that the install allows. Delete one, or ask an instance admin to raise the limit` | `resource_exhausted` |

```sh
browser -H 'Idempotency-Key: 6f1c2f0e-team' -d '{"name":"Team"}' $API/hopbox.v1.OrgService/CreateOrg
```

```json
{"org":{"id":"01a14565-a2df-75a1-9401-ed28dfa37fc4","name":"Team","role":"ORG_ROLE_OWNER","version":"1","createTime":"2026-10-16T15:47:31.166821Z"}}
```

| Audit entry       | none                                                                                                    |

The request `GetOrgRequest` has the field `org_id`. The response `GetOrgResponse` has the field `org`.

### ListOrgs

Lists the orgs of the caller: the personal org first, then the others, oldest first.

### UpdateOrg

Changes the name of an org, and returns the org after the change.

| Item              | Value                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.OrgService/UpdateOrg`                                             |
| Policy action     | `org.update`: a `session`, `cli_token`, or `member_key` with the role `owner` |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                            |
| Audit entry       | action `org.update`, target kind `org`, details `name` and `old_name`         |

| Field              | Type            | Description                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------ | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `org_id`           | optional string | The org.                                                                                                                              |
| `name`             | optional string | The new name. Leave it out to keep the name.                                                                                          |
| `expected_version` | optional int64  | The `version` of the org that the caller read. If the org has another version now, the call fails with `aborted` and changes nothing. |

A request that sets no field gets `invalid_argument` with the message `invalid argument: the update sets no field`. The response `UpdateOrgResponse` has the field `org`.

### DeleteOrg

Deletes an org, its memberships, its invitations, and every resource in it. The request must hold the name of the org in `confirm`.

| Item              | Value                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.OrgService/DeleteOrg`                                             |
| Policy action     | `org.delete`: a `session`, `cli_token`, or `member_key` with the role `owner` |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                            |
| Audit entry       | action `org.delete`, org the deleted org, target kind `org`, details `name`   |

| Field     | Type            | Description                   |
| --------- | --------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `org_id`  | optional string | The org.                      |
| `confirm` | string          | The name of the org, exactly. |

The response `DeleteOrgResponse` has no fields. The audit log keeps the entries of the deleted org, and instance admins read them.

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                       | Code                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `confirm` is not the name: `invalid argument: confirm the delete with the name of the org, "Team"`                                                                                          | `invalid_argument`    |
| The personal org: `failed precondition: a personal org goes only with its account. Delete the account instead`                                                                              | `failed_precondition` |
| A suspended org: `failed precondition: org suspended: an instance admin suspended the org, and nothing deletes its data until the suspension ends. Ask for the end of the suspension first` | `failed_precondition` |

A suspension keeps the org and its resources, for example as the evidence of abuse. So the owners delete the org only after an instance admin ends the suspension.

```sh
browser -d '{"orgId":"01a14565-a2df-75a1-9401-ed28dfa37fc4","confirm":"Team"}' $API/hopbox.v1.OrgService/DeleteOrg
```

Returns what an org uses, and its limits ([Usage limits](#usage-limits)).

| Item              | Value                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| Policy action     | `org.get_usage`: a `session`, `cli_token`, or `member_key` with a role in the org, or an `org_key` of the org |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                            |
| Audit entry       | none                                                                                                          |

The request `GetOrgUsageRequest` has the field `org_id`. The response `GetOrgUsageResponse` has the fields `usage`, an `OrgUsage`, and `limits`, an `OrgLimits`.

```sh
browser -d '{"orgId":"01a14565-a2df-75a1-9401-ed28dfa37fc4"}' $API/hopbox.v1.OrgService/GetOrgUsage
```

```json
{"usage":{},"limits":{"machines":3,"vcpus":6,"memoryBytes":"25769803776","diskBytes":"300000000000"}}
```

In the JSON codec, a field with its default value is left out, so a usage of 0 is `{}`.

## Members

### ListOrgMembers

Lists the members of an org, in the order that they joined.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.OrgService/ListOrgMembers`                                                                          |
| Policy action     | `org.member_list`: a `session`, `cli_token`, or `member_key` with a role in the org, or an `org_key` of the org |

| Audit entry       | none                                                                                                            |

The request `ListOrgMembersRequest` has the field `org_id`. The response `ListOrgMembersResponse` has the field `members`, a repeated `OrgMember`. For the other members, `emails` holds only their verified emails, because nobody proved an unverified email. For the caller, it holds every email.

### SetOrgMemberRole

Changes the role of a member. A change to the role that the member has already changes nothing and succeeds.

| Item              | Value                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.OrgService/SetOrgMemberRole`                                               |
| Policy action     | `org.member_set_role`: a `session`, `cli_token`, or `member_key` with the role `owner` |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                     |
| Audit entry       | action `org.member_set_role`, target kind `account`, details `role` and `old_role`     |

| Field        | Type            | Description             |
| ------------ | --------------- | ----------------------- |
| `org_id`     | optional string | The org.                |
| `account_id` | string          | The UUID of the member. |
| `role`       | `OrgRole`       | The new role.           |

The response `SetOrgMemberRoleResponse` has no fields.

| Error                                                                                                                                                            | Code                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `account_id` is not a UUID, or `role` is `ORG_ROLE_UNSPECIFIED` or not known: `invalid argument: unknown org role: "". The role must be member, admin, or owner` | `invalid_argument`    |
| The account is not a member: `not found: the account <id> is not a member of the org`                                                                            | `not_found`           |
| The last owner: `failed precondition: the account is the only owner of the org, and every org keeps at least one owner. Make another member an owner first`      | `failed_precondition` |

The call checks `account_id` and `role` before it reads the org. So a bad value gets `invalid_argument`, also in an org that does not exist, or of which the caller is not a member. The check reads only the request, so it tells nothing about the org. An anonymous caller still gets `unauthenticated` first.

### RemoveOrgMember

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                    |

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                             | Code                  |

| A suspended org, with the message of `DeleteOrg`                                                                                                                                                  | `failed_precondition` |
| The last owner                                                                                                                                                                                    | `failed_precondition` |

### LeaveOrg

Takes the account of the caller out of an org, with what it made in the org and did not share.

| Item              | Value                                                          |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.OrgService/LeaveOrg`                               |

| Error                                                                                                                                                                          | Code                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| The personal org: `failed precondition: an account cannot leave its personal org`                                                                                              | `failed_precondition` |
| The last owner: `failed precondition: the account is the only owner of the org, and every org keeps at least one owner. Make another member an owner first, or delete the org` | `failed_precondition` |
| A suspended org, with the message of `DeleteOrg`                                                                                                                               | `failed_precondition` |

### What a member leaves behind

A leave, a removal, and the delete of an account take the account out of the org. They also delete what the account made in the org and did not share. The delete of an org deletes every resource of the org. The service layer does this through the Go interface `service.OrgResource`, in the transaction of the change:

| Method                        | Called by                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MemberLeaving(org, account)` | `LeaveOrg`, `RemoveOrgMember`, and `DeleteAccount`, once for each org other than the personal org |
| `OrgDeleting(org)`            | `DeleteOrg`, and `DeleteAccount` for the personal org                                             |
| `OrgSuspending(org)`          | `SuspendOrg` of the admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#suspendorg))                 |

Each call holds the row lock of the org while the method runs. A leave, a removal, and an account delete also hold the lock of the account, which they take first. The lock order is the account row, then the org row, then the rows of the resource, such as machines ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#orgs)). A change of a resource outside these calls takes the locks in the same order.

The env vars and secrets are built into the service layer, and it runs their methods first. `MemberLeaving` deletes the private values of the account in the org, with a `var.delete` entry for each ([the env var API](/reference/vars-api/#what-a-member-leaves-behind)). The other values of the org stay. The delete of an org deletes its values through the foreign key. Each other kind of resource in an org adds its implementation to `Service.OrgResources`. The control role adds the machines ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/)). A method that fails rolls the whole change back, and the call fails with `internal`.

The machines do this in each method. Each method locks the machine rows in the order of their IDs, and skips a machine whose target is `deleted` already.

| Method                        | What it does to the machines                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Audit entry of each machine that changes                                     |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MemberLeaving(org, account)` | Sets the target `deleted` on each machine that the account made in the org and did not share. A shared machine stays in the org.                                                                                                                    | `machine.delete`, with the detail `reason` (`member left`)                   |
| `OrgDeleting(org)`            | Sets the target `deleted` on every machine of the org.                                                                                                                                                                                              | `machine.delete`, with the detail `reason` (`org deleted`)                   |
| `OrgSuspending(org)`          | Sets the target `stopped` on every machine of the org, except a machine whose target is `hibernated`. A hibernated machine stays hibernated, because only a delete drops its memory file ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#org-suspension)). | `machine.stop`, with the details `old_target` and `reason` (`org suspended`) |

A delete reserves the name and the SSH port of the machine for 7 days, as `DeleteMachine` does ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#deletemachine)). The actor of each entry is the caller of the change, and each change publishes the event `machine.updated` ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#change-events)). A delete of an org sets `org_id` of its machines to null once their target is `deleted`. The machines then wait for their executor ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#machines)).

## Invitations

An org owner or an org admin invites a person by email, and the person accepts after the sign-in. An invitation is for one email and gives one role.

| Rule                  | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Link                  | `https://<domain>/invite#token=<token>`. The token is 32 random bytes in base64url, as for a sign-in link ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#tokens)). It is in the fragment, so a browser never sends it to a server. The console page `/invite` reads it and calls `AcceptInvitation`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Storage               | The control store keeps only the SHA-256 of the token ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#org_invitations)). The audit log never holds the token.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Lifetime              | 7 days                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Use                   | once                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
