| Open invitations      | one for each email in an org. A new invitation for the email revokes the open one, so its link stops working.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Rate limits           | An org makes at most 20 invitations in an hour. An inviting account makes at most 20 in an hour, in all its orgs together. An email gets at most 5 in an hour, from every org together. The control store counts them in `org_invitation_sends`, a table without foreign keys ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#org_invitation_sends)). So the limits hold across every control server, and the delete of an org or an account resets no limit. Each new invitation takes a transaction lock (`LockKeyInvitations`, [the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#advisory-lock-keys)), so invitations at the same time cannot pass a limit together. |
| Email                 | With an SMTP config, the server sends the link to the email ([SMTP config](/reference/smtp/)). Without one, only the inviter gets the link. With the file mail transport, the server writes the email to a file on the server, and the inviter passes the link on ([Mail](/reference/mail/#invitations)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Who accepts           | A `session` whose account holds the email of the invitation as a verified email. The email of a login link stays unverified, so it does not count ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#what-a-sign-in-does)). A link of the email from a session of the account verifies it ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#link-a-new-sign-in-method)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Orgs                  | A personal org belongs to one account, so it takes no invitations. A suspended org sends none and takes no new members.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Rights of the inviter | An invitation never gives more than its inviter can give now. A leave, a removal, or an account delete of the inviter revokes each open invitation of the inviter in the org. A role change of the inviter revokes each one with a role that the new role cannot give.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

The leader deletes an invitation 24 hours after its end: its use, its revoke, or its expiry ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#leader-jobs)).

### CreateInvitation

Invites an email to join an org with a role, and returns the link. With an SMTP config, it also sends the link to the email.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.OrgService/CreateInvitation`                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Policy action     | `org.invitation_create`: a `session`, `cli_token`, or `member_key` with the role `admin` for the role `member`, or with the role `owner` for any role                                                            |
| Idempotent option | no. The response holds the link, which must never stay in the table of idempotency keys. A retry revokes the invitation of the first try and makes a new one.                                                    |
| Audit entries     | action `org.invitation_create`, target kind `invitation`, details `email` and `role`. A replaced invitation gets the action `org.invitation_revoke` with the details `email`, `role`, and `reason` (`replaced`). |

| Field    | Type            | Default                                  | Description                                                                                           |
| -------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `org_id` | optional string | the personal org, which the call refuses | The org.                                                                                              |
| `email`  | string          | none, required                           | The email of the person, such as `bob@example.org` ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#emails)). |
| `role`   | `OrgRole`       | `ORG_ROLE_MEMBER`                        | The role that the invitation gives.                                                                   |

The response `CreateInvitationResponse` has these fields:

| Field        | Type         | Description                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------ | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invitation` | `Invitation` | The new invitation.                                                                                                                                         |
| `url`        | string       | The link. It is a secret until its use or its end.                                                                                                          |
| `email_sent` | bool         | `true` after a sent email. It is `false` without an SMTP config, after a failed email, and with the file mail transport, because that email reaches nobody. |

The server sends the email after the invitation commits, and waits at most 20 s for the SMTP server. A failed email does not fail the call, because the inviter has the link. The server then logs `the invitation email failed` at level error, with `component=service`, `invitation`, and `err`.

The email has this form:

```text
From: hopbox <no-reply@example.org>
To: bob@example.org
Subject: Join Team on example.com


You are invited to join the org "Team" on example.com as admin.


Open this link, and sign in with the email bob@example.org to accept:


https://example.com/invite#token=<token>


The link works once, until Fri, 23 Oct 2026 15:47:31 UTC. If you did not expect it, you can ignore this email.
```

| Error                                                                                                                                                  | Code                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| The email breaks a rule, or the role is not known                                                                                                      | `invalid_argument`    |
| The install has no domain: `failed precondition: the install has no domain, and the invitation link needs one`                                         | `failed_precondition` |
| The personal org: `failed precondition: a personal org belongs to one account, so it takes no invitations`                                             | `failed_precondition` |
| A suspended org: `failed precondition: org suspended: an instance admin suspended the org, so it sends no invitations`                                 | `failed_precondition` |
| An account with the email as a verified email is a member already                                                                                      | `failed_precondition` |
| The org made 20 invitations in the last hour: `too many requests: this org made the most invitations of an hour. Wait, then retry`                     | `resource_exhausted`  |
| The caller made 20 invitations in the last hour, in any orgs: `too many requests: this account made the most invitations of an hour. Wait, then retry` | `resource_exhausted`  |
| The email got 5 invitations in the last hour, from any orgs: `too many requests: this email got the most invitations of an hour. Wait, then retry`     | `resource_exhausted`  |
| The SMTP password does not open, for example after the loss of its key-encryption key                                                                  | `internal`            |

```sh
browser -d '{"orgId":"01a14565-a2df-75a1-9401-ed28dfa37fc4","email":"bob@example.org","role":"ORG_ROLE_ADMIN"}' \
  $API/hopbox.v1.OrgService/CreateInvitation
```

```json
{"invitation":{"id":"01a14565-a316-74dd-968e-fac72d706827","orgId":"01a14565-a2df-75a1-9401-ed28dfa37fc4","email":"bob@example.org","role":"ORG_ROLE_ADMIN","inviterAccountId":"01a14565-8448-774f-9317-ea6348e9a930","createTime":"2026-10-16T15:47:31.221754Z","expireTime":"2026-10-23T15:47:31.221754Z"},"url":"https://example.com/invite#token=vH_2434xeosR22NllAU0tHE8LoqC08ZYHX1JhHZK4UA","emailSent":true}
```

### ListInvitations

Lists the open invitations of an org, oldest first. An open invitation is not used, not revoked, and not expired.

| Item              | Value                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.OrgService/ListInvitations`                                                           |
| Policy action     | `org.invitation_list`: a `session`, `cli_token`, or `member_key` with the role `admin` or `owner` |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                |
| Audit entry       | none                                                                                              |

The request `ListInvitationsRequest` has the field `org_id`. The response `ListInvitationsResponse` has the field `invitations`, a repeated `Invitation`. It never holds a link.

### RevokeInvitation

Ends an open invitation, so its link stops working.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.OrgService/RevokeInvitation`                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Policy action     | `org.invitation_revoke`: a `session`, `cli_token`, or `member_key` with the role `admin` or `owner`. An admin also revokes an invitation that gives the role `owner`, because a revoke gives nobody a right. |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Audit entry       | action `org.invitation_revoke`, target kind `invitation`, details `email` and `role`                                                                                                                         |

The request `RevokeInvitationRequest` has the fields `org_id` and `id`, the UUID of the invitation. The response `RevokeInvitationResponse` has no fields. An invitation that the org does not have open gets `not_found` with the message `not found: the org has no open invitation <id>`.

### AcceptInvitation

Joins the org of an invitation with its role. The account of the caller must hold the email of the invitation as a verified email.

| Item              | Value                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.OrgService/AcceptInvitation`                                                          |
| Policy action     | `org.invitation_accept`: `session` and `cli_token`                                                |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                |
| Audit entry       | action `org.invitation_accept`, org the org, target kind `invitation`, details `email` and `role` |

The request `AcceptInvitationRequest` has the field `token`: the value after `#token=` in the link. The response `AcceptInvitationResponse` has the field `org`, the `Org` with the new role of the caller.

The call locks the row of the org, then the row of the invitation, in the order that `CreateInvitation` takes them. So two accepts of one link at the same time make one membership. A refused try that is not a used, revoked, or expired link leaves the invitation open, so the right person can still accept it.

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Code                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| The token is unknown, used, revoked, or expired: `not found: the invitation is not valid: it is unknown, used, revoked, or expired. Ask for a new one`                                                                      | `not_found`           |
| The account has no verified email of the invitation: `failed precondition: the invitation is for bob@example.org, and the account has no verified email bob@example.org. Sign in with that email, then open the link again` | `failed_precondition` |
| The account is a member already: `failed precondition: the account is a member of the org already, as <role>`                                                                                                               | `failed_precondition` |
| A suspended org: `failed precondition: org suspended: an instance admin suspended the org, so it takes no new members`                                                                                                      | `failed_precondition` |

The server logs a refused token as `invitation refused` at level info, with `component=service`, and never the token.

```sh
browser -d '{"token":"vH_2434xeosR22NllAU0tHE8LoqC08ZYHX1JhHZK4UA"}' $API/hopbox.v1.OrgService/AcceptInvitation
```

```json
{"org":{"id":"01a14565-a2df-75a1-9401-ed28dfa37fc4","name":"Team","role":"ORG_ROLE_ADMIN","version":"1","createTime":"2026-10-16T15:47:31.166821Z"}}
```

## Usage limits

Each org has usage limits on machines, vCPUs, RAM, and disk. The install has default limits for every org. An instance admin can change the defaults, and set limits for one org that replace the defaults ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setorglimits)).

| Limit    | Default                     |
| -------- | --------------------------- |
| Machines | 3                           |
| vCPUs    | 6                           |
| RAM      | 24 GiB (25769803776 bytes)  |
| Disk     | 300 GB (300000000000 bytes) |

The defaults fit three machines of the default size ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#sizes)). A limit of 0 allows nothing. [Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#usage-limits) gives the rules of the check.

| Usage             | The machines that count                                   |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Machines and disk | every machine that is not deleted                         |
| vCPUs and RAM     | the machines whose target state is `running` or `standby` |

So a stopped machine keeps its disk and its place in the machine count, but frees its vCPUs and its RAM. A machine whose target is `deleted` counts no more, also while its executor still deletes it. `CreateMachine` and `StartMachine` check the limits ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#usage-and-limits)). A start adds only the vCPUs and the RAM of a machine that does not count already, so a start never counts a machine twice. A new limit below the usage stops nothing: the org then creates and starts no more machines until its usage fits.

## Suspension

An instance admin can suspend an org, for example to handle abuse. The calls are on the admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#suspendorg)). The members of the org see the suspension in `GetOrg`. Its owners and admins see its audit entry in the audit log of the org.

| Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Since                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Reads still work.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | now                                         |
| The org sends no invitations. `CreateInvitation` fails with `failed_precondition`.                                                                                                                                                                                | now                                         |
| The org takes no new members. `AcceptInvitation` fails with `failed_precondition`.                                                                                                                                                                                | now                                         |
| Owners can still change roles and rename the org.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | now                                         |
| Nothing deletes the data of the org, for example the evidence of abuse. `DeleteOrg`, `LeaveOrg`, and `RemoveOrgMember` in the org fail with `failed_precondition`. So does `DeleteAccount` of a member of the org, or of the account of a suspended personal org. | now                                         |
| The env vars and secrets of the org do not change. `SetVar` and `DeleteVar` fail with `failed_precondition` ([the env var API](/reference/vars-api/#suspension)).                                                                                                 | now                                         |
| The members cannot delete a machine of the org. `DeleteMachine` fails with `failed_precondition` ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#org-suspension)).                                                                                                       | now                                         |
| The machines of the org stop. A hibernated machine stays hibernated ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#org-suspension)).                                                                                                                                    | now, through `OrgSuspending`                |
| The org cannot create, start, or reboot a machine. `CreateMachine`, `StartMachine`, and `RebootMachine` fail with `failed_precondition` ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#suspension)).                                                                  | now                                         |
| The org cannot resume, wake, fork, or restore a machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                          | with the calls of these actions, in phase 3 |
| The auto-delete of the leader skips the machines of the org.                                                                                                                                                                                                      | now                                         |
| Instance admins can still stop and delete any machine of the org ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#machineservice)).                                                                                                                                         | now                                         |
| Exec and file copy are blocked ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#suspension)).                                                                                                                                                                           | now                                         |
| The machine URLs are blocked. The edge answers `403`, and `GET /auth/machine` gives no code ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#private-machine-urls)).                                                                                                             | now                                         |
| SSH is blocked. The SSH front door refuses every key, and ends the open SSH connections of the org ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#checks-of-an-open-connection)).                                                                               | now                                         |

The end of the suspension starts no machine. The users of the org start them again.

## Audit entries

The org calls write these entries in the transaction of the change. Their org is the org of the change, so its owners and admins read them with `ListAuditEntries` ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/#listauditentries)). The actor is the caller.

| Action                  | Call                                                                                                                                                   | Target         | Details                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `org.create`            | `CreateOrg`                                                                                                                                            | the org        | `name`                                                                                                            |
| `org.update`            | `UpdateOrg`                                                                                                                                            | the org        | `name`, `old_name`                                                                                                |
| `org.delete`            | `DeleteOrg`                                                                                                                                            | the org        | `name`                                                                                                            |
| `org.member_set_role`   | `SetOrgMemberRole`                                                                                                                                     | the account    | `role`, `old_role`                                                                                                |
| `org.member_remove`     | `RemoveOrgMember`, and `DeleteAccount` for each org of the account                                                                                     | the account    | `role`, `reason` (`removed` or `account deleted`)                                                                 |
| `org.leave`             | `LeaveOrg`                                                                                                                                             | the account    | `role`                                                                                                            |
| `org.invitation_create` | `CreateInvitation`                                                                                                                                     | the invitation | `email`, `role`                                                                                                   |
| `org.invitation_revoke` | `RevokeInvitation`, `CreateInvitation` for the invitation that it replaces, and a leave, a removal, an account delete, or a role change of the inviter | the invitation | `email`, `role`, and for a revoke by another call `reason`: `replaced`, `inviter left`, or `inviter role changed` |
| `org.invitation_accept` | `AcceptInvitation`                                                                                                                                     | the invitation | `email`, `role`                                                                                                   |

The admin calls on orgs add `org.suspend`, `org.unsuspend`, and `org.set_limits` to the audit log of the org ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#orgservice)). The machine calls write their own entries in the audit log of the org ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#audit-entries)).

# Placement

> How a create picks the node of a machine: the hard filters, the usage of a node, the score, the retries, the no-capacity error, the room check of a start, and the placement metric.

Placement picks the node of a new machine. `CreateMachine` runs it in its transaction ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#createmachine)). The start of a stopped machine uses the same rules of room on the node of the machine. A cold move picks its target node with the same filters ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#start-of-a-move)). The Go package `internal/placement` holds the rules, without I/O. The service layer reads the nodes and makes the placement (`internal/service/machines.go`).

## The steps of a placement

1. It reads every server that is not decommissioned, with what the machines of each one use ([What a node uses](#what-a-node-uses)). A decommissioned server is never a candidate, and the message of [When no node has room](#when-no-node-has-room) does not count it.
2. It runs the [hard filters](#hard-filters) on each server. A server that fails a filter is out, and the first filter that it fails is its reason.
3. It shuffles the servers that pass, and takes up to 3 of them: the candidates.
4. It scores each candidate ([Score](#score)). The lowest score wins.
5. It tries the winner. The try locks the row of the server in `servers` with `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, and reads its state, its labels, and its usage again. Then it runs the filters again. A server that fails a filter now refuses the placement, for example a server that has no room any more, or whose labels changed.
6. After a refusal, it waits, reads the servers again, and goes back to step 2 without the servers that refused. It tries at most 3 servers in all.

The try runs in a savepoint of the transaction of the create. A server that refuses rolls back its savepoint, so its lock goes at once, and its heartbeats and other placements need not wait. The server that takes the machine stays locked until the create commits. The heartbeat of that server waits for the commit too.

| Rule                       | Value                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Candidates                 | 3 random servers that pass the filters (`placement.Candidates`)                                                |
| Tries                      | 3 servers at most (`placement.Tries`)                                                                          |
| Wait before the second try | 20 ms (`placement.DefaultBackoff`)                                                                             |
| Wait before the third try  | 40 ms: each wait is twice the wait before it                                                                   |
| Jitter                     | Each wait is a random time from half of its value to the whole value, so the tries of many creates spread out. |
| vCPU overcommit            | 2 vCPUs for each CPU thread of a server (`placement.CPUOvercommit`)                                            |
| RAM overcommit             | none                                                                                                           |

## Hard filters

A server must pass every filter, in this order:

| Order | Filter              | The server passes when                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Reason of a server that fails |
| ----- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| 1     | Role                | Its roles hold `node`.                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `not_node`                    |
| 2     | State               | Its state is `ready`. A `cordoned` or `unresponsive` server fails ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#servers)).                                                                                         | `not_ready`                   |
| 3     | Health              | Its last heartbeat had the status `ok`. A server whose last heartbeat had the status `degraded` fails: a check of severity `fail` failed, such as a missing `/dev/kvm` ([the preflight check](/reference/preflight/)). | `degraded`                    |
| 4     | Pool                | The request names no pool, or the pool of the server.                                                                                                                                                                  | `pool`                        |
| 5     | Labels              | The server has each label of the request, with the same value.                                                                                                                                                         | `labels`                      |
| 6     | Compatibility class | The request names no class, or the class of the server.                                                                                                                                                                | `class`                       |
| 7     | Version             | Its `hopboxd` is at least the oldest version that the request allows. The version must be a valid semver version.                                                                                                      | `version`                     |
| 8     | Cold move           | Only for the target of a cold move: its heartbeats say that it pulls disks with its current `hopboxd`, and it is in the mesh ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#two-releases)). A create skips this filter.            | `move`                        |
| 9     | vCPUs               | The vCPUs that it uses, plus the vCPUs of the size, are at most 2 times its CPU threads.                                                                                                                               | `cpu`                         |
| 10    | RAM                 | The RAM that it uses, plus the RAM of the size, is at most its RAM.                                                                                                                                                    | `ram`                         |

A create takes the pool and the labels of its size for filters 4 and 5. So does a cold move, with the size of the machine. The size `default` names no pool and no label, so its machines pass both filters on every server. A move with memory state names a compatibility class. A cold move carries no memory, so it names none, and filter 6 passes every server. The target of a cold move is never the node of the machine.

The oldest version that a create allows is `version.MinNodeVersion`. Today it is `v0.0.0-0.unknown`, which sorts below every build ([the version command](/reference/version/#version-format)). So every node with a valid version passes. Only a release whose executor protocol needs it raises it, to the oldest release that follows the new protocol ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#two-releases)). In a rolling upgrade, the nodes of the release before then take no new machine until they upgrade.

Disk is not a filter in phase 1. The disk of a machine is sparse, so its size says little about the space that it takes on the node.

## What a node uses

A machine uses its vCPUs and its RAM on its node in these cases:

* Its target is `running` or `standby` (`HoldsCompute`, [Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#usage-limits)).
* Its current state is `starting`, `running`, `standby`, or `moving`, because its microVM can still run on the way to another target.

A stopped, hibernated, or failed machine whose target is `stopped` or `hibernated` uses nothing. A machine whose target is `deleted` uses its vCPUs and RAM until its microVM stops.

A placement that runs in another transaction counts too. The try of step 5 locks the server row and reads the usage again in a new statement. A second placement on the same server waits for that lock. When it gets the lock, the first create committed, and the new statement sees its machine. So two creates at the same time never pass the room check of one server together.

## Score

The score of a candidate is how full it is after it takes the machine:

```text
score = 0.7 × (used RAM + RAM of the size) / RAM of the server
      + 0.3 × (used vCPUs + vCPUs of the size) / (2 × CPU threads)
```

RAM counts most, because it has no overcommit. The lowest score wins. For example, take the size `default` (2 vCPUs, 8 GiB) and two servers with 12 threads and 128 GiB each. A server that uses 4 vCPUs and 16 GiB scores 0.7 × 24/128 + 0.3 × 6/24 = 0.21. An empty server scores 0.7 × 8/128 + 0.3 × 2/24 = 0.069, and wins.

## When no node has room

A placement fails in two cases: no server passes the filters, or 3 servers refused it. The create then fails with `unavailable`, and leaves nothing behind ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#createmachine)). A retry can succeed once a node has room, and the SDKs retry `unavailable`.

The message names the size and the reason of each server:

```text
no capacity: no node has room for a machine of size <size> (<n> vCPUs, <RAM> of RAM): <reasons>
```

`<RAM>` is in GiB for a whole number of GiB, else in MiB. `<reasons>` counts the servers by the first filter that each one failed, in the order of the filters, joined by `, `. A server that refused the placement counts as `refused the placement`. After 3 refusals, the counts come from the last read of the servers.

| Reason      | One server                                            | More servers                                              |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `not_node`  | `1 node has no node role`                             | `<n> nodes have no node role`                             |
| `not_ready` | `1 node is cordoned, unresponsive, or decommissioned` | `<n> nodes are cordoned, unresponsive, or decommissioned` |
| `degraded`  | `1 node failed a check in its last heartbeat`         | `<n> nodes failed a check in their last heartbeat`        |
| `pool`      | `1 node is in another pool`                           | `<n> nodes are in another pool`                           |
| `labels`    | `1 node lacks a label`                                | `<n> nodes lack a label`                                  |
| `class`     | `1 node is in another compatibility class`            | `<n> nodes are in another compatibility class`            |
| `version`   | `1 node runs a hopboxd that is too old`               | `<n> nodes run a hopboxd that is too old`                 |
| `move`      | `1 node pulls no disk of a cold move`                 | `<n> nodes pull no disk of a cold move`                   |
| `cpu`       | `1 node has too few free vCPUs`                       | `<n> nodes have too few free vCPUs`                       |
| `ram`       | `1 node has too little free RAM`                      | `<n> nodes have too little free RAM`                      |
| `refused`   | `1 node refused the placement`                        | `<n> nodes refused the placement`                         |

Examples:

```text
no capacity: no node has room for a machine of size default (2 vCPUs, 8 GiB of RAM): 1 node is cordoned, unresponsive, or decommissioned, 2 nodes have too little free RAM
```

An install without a server that is not decommissioned gets this message:

```text
no capacity: no node has room for a machine of size default (2 vCPUs, 8 GiB of RAM). The install has no node yet
```

The error wraps `placement.ErrNoCapacity`. The API maps it to `unavailable` ([the API server](/reference/api/#errors)). The Go type `placement.NoCapacityError` holds the size, the count of servers, and the count of each reason.

## Start of a stopped machine

The disk of a machine lives on its node, so a start never moves the machine. Only a cold move takes a machine and its disk to another node ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/)), and the next start checks the room on the new node. The start of a machine whose target is `stopped` checks the room on its own node with the same rules: the vCPUs with an overcommit of 2, and the RAM without overcommit ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#startmachine)). It locks the server row with `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, and counts every other machine of the node as in [What a node uses](#what-a-node-uses). It checks no other filter: a cordoned or unresponsive node keeps its machines. For a machine on a decommissioned node, a start skips the check.

| Case                | Code          | Message                                                                                                          |
| ------------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Too few free vCPUs  | `unavailable` | `no capacity: the node of the machine has too few free vCPUs to start it. Stop another machine, or retry later`  |
| Too little free RAM | `unavailable` | `no capacity: the node of the machine has too little free RAM to start it. Stop another machine, or retry later` |

## The machine lease

The placement grants the machine lease `machine/<machine ID>` to the chosen node, in the transaction of the create, with a TTL of 30 s ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#leases)). The holder is the server ID of the node. The row of `placements` keeps the epoch and the token of the grant, and the count of tries. The control role then sends the spec of the machine to the node with this grant. The executor of the machine acts with it ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/)). The heartbeats of the node renew the lease. The executor protocol keeps this contract ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#leases)):

* The lease row always holds the epoch and the token of the current grant.
* Each new grant of the lease writes a new row of `placements` with its epoch and token, in the same transaction. An example is a new grant after an expiry.
* A heartbeat that renews or grants the leases of its machines locks the machine rows first, then the server row, as a placement does.

A machine stays on its node. A new grant after an expiry goes to the same node, and only after the node sends a heartbeat again. An unresponsive node keeps its machines, and no other node starts them.

## Logs

A create that finds no node with room writes this record with `component=service`:

| Message                          | Level | Fields                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no node has room for a machine` | warn  | `org`, `err` (the message of [When no node has room](#when-no-node-has-room)), `request_id` |

## Metrics

| Metric                    | Type    | Labels             | Description                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hopbox_placements_total` | counter | `result`, `reason` | The placements of creates ([Metrics](/reference/metrics/#metrics-of-placement)). |

| Label    | Values                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `result` | `placed` for a create that committed, `no_capacity` for a create that found no node with room or no free SSH port                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `reason` | Empty for `placed`. For `no_capacity`, the reason that skipped the most servers: `not_node`, `not_ready`, `degraded`, `pool`, `labels`, `class`, `version`, `cpu`, `ram`, or `refused`. A tie goes to the reason of the earlier filter. `none` for an install without a server, and `ssh_ports` for a full range of SSH ports. |

A create with an idempotency key runs in the transaction of its key, so it counts as `placed` only after that transaction commits.

A create that fails before its placement, or for another cause after it, does not count. A start of a stopped machine does not count either.

```text
hopbox_placements_total{reason="",result="placed"} 4
hopbox_placements_total{reason="ram",result="no_capacity"} 1
```

# The bundled Postgres

> The bundled Postgres: its build, tools/pgdist, paths, OS users, roles, logs, errors, and the schema migrations.

`hopboxd` brings its own Postgres 18 and runs it as a supervised child process. This page lists the build of that Postgres, with the OpenSSL that it links to, and the tool that builds it. It also lists the paths, OS users, database roles, server parameters, logs, and errors of Postgres. The last part covers the schema migrations of the control store.

The package `internal/pgsup` supervises Postgres, and the package `internal/store` runs the migrations. `hopboxd run` starts both for the control role, with the paths on this page ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run)). The keys `data_dir`, `run_dir`, `postgres.install`, and `postgres.user` of the bootstrap config set the paths and the OS user ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). With `postgres.url`, the control role uses an external Postgres in place of the bundled one ([External Postgres](#external-postgres)).

## Version

| Item                         | Value                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Postgres version             | 18.6                                                                                      |
| Source                       | `https://ftp.postgresql.org/pub/source/v18.6/postgresql-18.6.tar.bz2`                     |
| sha256 of the source         | `555610c24d53e4316da5b7d3fc25c279d96856d5e0e23ee308c328c5fa881d9f`                        |
| OpenSSL version              | 3.5.9, a long-term support release                                                        |
| OpenSSL source               | `https://github.com/openssl/openssl/releases/download/openssl-3.5.9/openssl-3.5.9.tar.gz` |
| sha256 of the OpenSSL source | `603f5602e2eef00d77fbd429d34dcd5822bb301757a1bc9cdb24c670f1eb859a`                        |

The file `build/postgres/source.env` pins each version, URL, and hash. `tools/pgdist` refuses a download with another hash. A fix of OpenSSL reaches the servers as a change of `source.env` in a new release of `hopboxd`.

## Build recipe

The folder `build/postgres` holds the recipe:

| File         | What it does                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `source.env` | Pins the source tarballs, one `key=value` per line: `version`, `url`, and `sha256` for Postgres, and `openssl_version`, `openssl_url`, and `openssl_sha256` for OpenSSL. |
| `build.sh`   | `build.sh <postgres tarball> <openssl tarball> <empty output dir>`. Builds OpenSSL, then Postgres, and checks the result.                                                |
| `Dockerfile` | Runs `build.sh` for Linux in Debian 12 (`debian:bookworm-slim`, pinned by digest).                                                                                       |

`build.sh` first builds the libraries of OpenSSL. `pg_dump` and `pg_restore` need them to reach an external Postgres over TLS, for `hopboxd admin db export` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-db-export)). It runs the `Configure` of OpenSSL with these flags:

| Flag                          | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--prefix=/hopbox-ssl-prefix` | A path that no server has, and that only root can make. On macOS, the prefix is a temp dir of the build, because macOS loads a library by its install name, and the Postgres build runs programs that link to OpenSSL.                                                                                                          |
| `--openssldir=/etc/ssl`       | The config dir of OpenSSL on Debian. A client that asks for the roots of the system, such as `sslrootcert=system`, finds them on a server. `hopboxd admin db export` runs `pg_dump` and `pg_restore` with `OPENSSL_CONF=/dev/null`, so they read no `openssl.cnf` of the host ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-db-export)). |
| `--libdir=lib`                | The libraries go to `lib/`, never `lib64/`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `shared`                      | `libssl` and `libcrypto` are shared libraries, so each program of the install links to one copy.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `no-tests`                    | The build makes no test programs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

It builds only the libraries (`make build_libs`) and installs them with their headers into a stage dir. Then it runs the `configure` of Postgres with these flags:

| Flag                                     | Reason                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--disable-rpath`                        | `build.sh` sets relative library paths after the build.                                                                                                                          |
| `--without-icu`                          | The install must not need ICU. The cluster uses the builtin collation provider.                                                                                                  |
| `--without-readline`                     | The install must not need readline.                                                                                                                                              |
| `--without-zlib`                         | The install must not need zlib. `pg_dump` and `pg_basebackup` cannot compress.                                                                                                   |
| `--with-ssl=openssl`                     | `libpq` speaks TLS, so `pg_dump` and `pg_restore` can use `sslmode=verify-full`. The server of the bundled Postgres keeps `ssl` off, because it listens only on its unix socket. |
| `--with-includes` and `--with-libraries` | They name the headers and the libraries of the OpenSSL stage dir, not those of the system.                                                                                       |

ICU, readline, and zlib are the only libraries that `configure` turns on by default. Every other optional library is off. During the build of Postgres, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` names the OpenSSL stage dir, because the build runs programs that it links, such as `zic`.

After `make install-strip`, `build.sh` deletes `include/`, `lib/postgresql/pgxs/`, `lib/pkgconfig/`, and the static libraries. It copies the versioned files of `libssl` and `libcrypto` into `lib/`, without their symlinks and headers, and strips them. It then makes the install relocatable:

* On Linux, `patchelf` sets the run path of each file that links to `libpq`, `libecpg`, `libpgtypes`, `libssl`, or `libcrypto`. The run path is `$ORIGIN/../lib` in `bin/`, `$ORIGIN/..` in `lib/postgresql/`, and `$ORIGIN` in `lib/`.
* On macOS, `install_name_tool` changes the install name of each library of Postgres and OpenSSL to `@rpath/<name>`, and adds the run path `@loader_path/../lib`, `@loader_path/..`, or `@loader_path/.`. `codesign` then signs each changed file again.

`build.sh` checks each file. A link to a library outside the install, other than the C library, fails the build. An absolute library path also fails the build. At the end, it runs `--version` on `postgres`, `initdb`, `pg_ctl`, `psql`, `pg_dump`, `pg_restore`, and `pg_upgrade` from the output dir. That dir is not the configured prefix, so the runs prove that the install is relocatable. Last, it runs `psql` with `sslmode=require`. A `libpq` without TLS refuses that mode before it connects, and the build fails with `build.sh: libpq has no TLS support`.

### Targets

| Target         | Builder           | Runs on                                                      | Used by                |
| -------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- |
| `linux/amd64`  | Docker, Debian 12 | glibc 2.36 and later, for example Debian 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 | the release bundle, CI |
| `darwin/arm64` | native            | macOS on Apple Silicon                                       | tests on a Mac         |

The Linux build uses Debian 12 because a binary built against an older glibc runs on newer ones.

### The install

An install is one folder:

```text
bin/      postgres, initdb, pg_ctl, psql, pg_dump, pg_restore, pg_upgrade, and the other client programs
lib/      libpq, libecpg, libpgtypes, libssl, libcrypto, and lib/postgresql/ with the server modules
share/    share/postgresql/ with the catalog files, time zones, and extensions
```

It links only to its own libraries and to the C library of the system: `libc`, `libm`, and the dynamic loader on Linux, and `libSystem` on macOS. The OpenSSL libraries are `lib/libssl.so.3` and `lib/libcrypto.so.3` on Linux, and `lib/libssl.3.dylib` and `lib/libcrypto.3.dylib` on macOS.

## pgdist

`tools/pgdist` builds the install from the recipe, caches it, and prints its path on stdout. Progress logs go to stderr.

```sh
go run ./tools/pgdist [flags]
```

| Flag       | Type      | Default                                                                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-target`  | `os/arch` | the host, for example `darwin/arm64`                                    | The platform of the build: `darwin/arm64` or `linux/amd64`.                                                                                                                                       |
| `-builder` | string    | `docker` for a `linux` target, `native` for `darwin`                    | `native` runs `build.sh` on the host. It builds only the host target. `docker` runs the `Dockerfile` with `docker build --platform <target> --output type=local`. It builds only `linux` targets. |
| `-cache`   | dir       | `$HOPBOX_PGDIST_CACHE`, else `hopbox/pgdist` in the user cache dir      | Where builds and source tarballs live.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `-recipe`  | dir       | `build/postgres` in the first parent dir of the current dir that has it | The recipe folder.                                                                                                                                                                                |

| Environment variable  | Description                           |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `HOPBOX_PGDIST_CACHE` | The cache dir. `-cache` overrides it. |

The user cache dir is `~/Library/Caches` on macOS, and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `~/.cache` on Linux.

The cache holds:

| Path                                             | Contents                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<cache>/postgres-<version>-<os>-<arch>-<hash>/` | One install. `<hash>` is the first 12 hex digits of a sha256 over every file of the recipe folder. Thus each change to the recipe makes a new build. |
| `<cache>/postgres-<...>.lock`                    | A lock file. Parallel runs of pgdist wait for each other.                                                                                            |
| `<cache>/postgres-<...>.tmp/`                    | A build in progress. After a good build, pgdist renames it to the install dir.                                                                       |
| `<cache>/src/postgresql-<version>.tar.bz2`       | The source tarball of Postgres. If its hash does not match, pgdist downloads it again.                                                               |
| `<cache>/src/openssl-<version>.tar.gz`           | The source tarball of OpenSSL, with the same check.                                                                                                  |

Two runs of pgdist can share one cache, such as two CI jobs on one runner. A run writes each download to a temp file in `src/` and renames it into place, so a second run never reads half a file. The lock file makes the second run wait for the build of the first, and then reuse it.

If the install dir exists, pgdist prints its path and builds nothing. On each run, pgdist sets the modes of the install to `u=rwX,go=rX`: `0755` for dirs and programs, `0644` for other files. The OS user `hopbox-pg` must read and run them, whatever modes the build or the Docker export left. It exits with status 1 and an error log on any failure.

What each builder needs:

| Builder           | Needs                                                                                                   |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `native` on macOS | the Xcode command line tools (clang, make, bison, flex, perl, `strip`, `install_name_tool`, `codesign`) |
| `native` on Linux | gcc, make, bison, flex, perl, patchelf, readelf, strip                                                  |
| `docker`          | Docker with BuildKit                                                                                    |

Example:

```sh
$ go run ./tools/pgdist
/Users/me/Library/Caches/hopbox/pgdist/postgres-18.6-darwin-arm64-82e44458122c
```

## Paths on a server

| Path                           | Owner       | Mode   | Contents                                                                    |
| ------------------------------ | ----------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/var/lib/hopbox/pg`           | `hopbox-pg` | `0700` | The Postgres state dir. If it does not exist, pgsup creates it.             |
| `/var/lib/hopbox/pg/data`      | `hopbox-pg` | `0700` | The cluster, which is the data dir of Postgres.                             |
| `/var/lib/hopbox/pg/data.init` | `hopbox-pg` | `0700` | A cluster that `initdb` is creating. It exists only during the first start. |
| `/run/hopbox/pg`               | `hopbox-pg` | `0700` | The socket dir. It holds `.s.PGSQL.5432` and its lock file.                 |

pgsup creates a missing parent dir, such as `/var/lib/hopbox` or `/run/hopbox`, with mode `0755`. A parent dir that exists must let `hopbox-pg` enter it. pgsup sets the mode `0700` on the state dir and the socket dir on each start. `hopbox-pg` must also be able to read the Postgres install. The path of the socket file must be at most 103 bytes, the limit of unix sockets on macOS.

## OS users and database roles

| Name        | Kind          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `hopbox-pg` | OS user       | Postgres refuses to run as root. So when `hopboxd` runs as root, Postgres runs as this user. The user must exist before the first start. When `hopboxd` is not root, Postgres runs as the user of `hopboxd`. |
| `hopbox`    | database role | The bootstrap superuser of the cluster. `hopboxd` connects with this role.                                                                                                                                   |
| `hopbox`    | database      | The control store database. On each start, pgsup makes sure that it exists.                                                                                                                                  |

Postgres accepts connections only on the unix socket, and only with peer authentication. Peer authentication takes the OS user of the client from the kernel. The two files that pgsup writes after `initdb` set this up:

pg_hba.conf

```text
local all all peer map=hopbox


# pg_ident.conf: maps the OS user of hopboxd to the role hopbox
hopbox root hopbox
```

When `hopboxd` is not root, the second line names the user of `hopboxd` in place of `root`. pgsup writes both files on each start, so a change of the user of `hopboxd` takes effect at the next start. pgsup syncs them to disk, because an empty `pg_hba.conf` after a power loss locks `hopboxd` out.

As root, pgsup works in dirs that `hopbox-pg` owns, and `hopbox-pg` can plant symlinks there. So pgsup does each file operation in the state dir through a handle on that dir that never leaves it. It reads only regular files of at most 4 KiB. It writes a file under a new temp name with `O_EXCL`, changes the owner through the open file, and renames it into place. It never opens an existing path for writing, and never follows a symlink with `chown` or `chmod`.

## initdb flags

pgsup runs `initdb` as the Postgres OS user, with the environment `LC_ALL=C` and `TZ=UTC`:

| Flag                                                       | Reason                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--pgdata=<dir>/data.init`                                 | pgsup renames the dir to `data` only after `initdb` succeeds, so a crash never leaves a partial cluster in `data`. |
| `--username=hopbox`                                        | The bootstrap superuser.                                                                                           |
| `--encoding=UTF8`                                          |                                                                                                                    |
| `--locale=C`                                               | No dependency on the locales of the OS.                                                                            |
| `--locale-provider=builtin` and `--builtin-locale=C.UTF-8` | A collation that stays the same across OS and ICU updates.                                                         |
| `--auth-local=peer` and `--auth-host=reject`               | pgsup replaces `pg_hba.conf` right after, but no other method is ever on.                                          |
| `--no-instructions`                                        |                                                                                                                    |

Postgres 18 turns on data checksums by default.

## Server parameters

pgsup starts `bin/postgres -D <dir>/data` with these parameters as `-c name=value`. A caller can pass extra parameters, but not these, and not `config_file`, `data_directory`, `hba_file`, `ident_file`, or `unix_socket_group`. Start refuses such a parameter, because it can undo the socket-only and peer-only setup. Postgres reads parameter names without regard to case, so the check does the same: `Hba_File` is refused too.

| Parameter                 | Value          | Reason                                   |
| ------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `listen_addresses`        | empty          | No TCP listener.                         |
| `unix_socket_directories` | the socket dir |                                          |
| `unix_socket_permissions` | `0700`         |                                          |
| `port`                    | `5432`         | Names the socket file `.s.PGSQL.5432`.   |
| `log_destination`         | `stderr`       | pgsup turns each line into a log record. |
| `logging_collector`       | `off`          |                                          |
| `log_line_prefix`         | `[%p]`         | pgsup reads the process ID from it.      |
| `timezone`                | `UTC`          |                                          |
| `log_timezone`            | `UTC`          |                                          |

Postgres runs in its own process group, with the environment `LC_ALL=C` and `TZ=UTC`. It does not inherit the environment of `hopboxd`.

## Start, restart, and stop

On start, pgsup does these steps in order:

1. It runs `postgres --version` as the Postgres OS user, with the clean environment of the server, and reads the major version of the binaries. This run also proves that `hopbox-pg` can run the install.

2. It refuses a state dir, data dir, or socket dir that is a symlink.

3. It reads `data/PG_VERSION`. If the file holds another major version, pgsup refuses to start and changes nothing on disk. If the file is missing and `data` is not empty, pgsup also refuses.

4. If `data/postmaster.pid` names a running postmaster, pgsup refuses to start. A Postgres can outlive a `hopboxd` that was killed, because it runs in its own process group. The parent death signal on Linux and the watchdog on macOS make that rare (see below), but not impossible: a postmaster that does not stop in time still holds the data dir. A PID file can also outlive its server, for example after a power loss. So pgsup ignores the file in three cases:

   * No process has the PID.
   * The start time in the file is before the boot of the host.
   * On Linux, the process with the PID is not `postgres`.

5. It creates the state dir and the socket dir. As root, it gives them to `hopbox-pg`.

6. If `data` is missing or empty, it creates the cluster. It deletes any `data.init` from an earlier crash and runs `initdb`. Then it writes `pg_hba.conf` and `pg_ident.conf`, and renames `data.init` to `data`. For a cluster that exists, it writes the two files again.

7. It starts the postmaster and connects every 50 ms until a connection succeeds and `postmaster.pid` names the new process. The first start fails after 60 s. An exit of the postmaster also fails it at once.

8. If the database `hopbox` does not exist, it creates it.

After the first start, pgsup restarts Postgres each time it exits without a stop request. It waits 1 s before the first restart, and doubles the wait after each failed attempt, up to 30 s. A server that ran for more than 1 minute before it exited restarts after 1 s again.

On stop, pgsup sends `SIGINT`, the fast shutdown, which rolls back open transactions and writes a checkpoint. After 30 s, it sends `SIGQUIT`, the immediate shutdown. After 5 s more, it sends `SIGKILL` to the process group of Postgres, because a killed postmaster cannot stop its backends. If the caller stops the wait early, pgsup sends `SIGQUIT` and returns the error of the caller. A second stop call then waits until Postgres exits.

On Linux, the postmaster has a parent death signal: when `hopboxd` dies, for example by `SIGKILL`, the kernel sends the postmaster `SIGINT`, the fast shutdown. So Postgres does not wait for the timeout of the stop of `hopboxd.service` before systemd kills it. The kernel sends this signal at the end of the thread that started the postmaster. So pgsup starts each postmaster from a goroutine that holds its own thread until the postmaster exits. Other systems, such as macOS, have no parent death signal. There, pgsup starts a watchdog process for each postmaster: a `/bin/sh` that waits on a pipe. Only `hopboxd` holds the write end of the pipe. When `hopboxd` dies, the kernel closes that end, and the watchdog sends the postmaster `SIGINT`. The watchdog runs in its own process group, so a Ctrl-C in the terminal does not stop it first. When the postmaster exits, its PID can go to another process. So pgsup kills the watchdog first, and then closes the pipe. If the watchdog cannot start, pgsup logs the warning `postgres will outlive a crash of hopboxd` and runs Postgres without it.

The test `TestPostgresStopsWhenHopboxdDies` kills a supervisor process with `SIGKILL`, and checks that its postmaster exits within 10 s. It runs on Linux and on macOS. `make test-linux` with `PG_LINUX` also runs it as root, where Postgres runs as `hopbox-pg`, and CI does so in the job `test-linux`.

## Upgrades

A release bundle carries the Postgres of its release ([Release bundle](/reference/release-bundle/)). An upgrade of `hopboxd` that keeps the major version, for example from 18.6 to 18.7, swaps the binaries with the release: `postgres.install` names `/opt/hopbox/current/postgres`, and the next start of Postgres runs the new binaries on the same cluster.

An upgrade must never start a cluster with binaries of another major version. `hopboxd install` is the last step of each upgrade. Before it switches the release, it runs the check of step 3 of [Start, restart, and stop](#start-restart-and-stop) ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#install)). The Go call is `pgsup.CheckVersion`:

* It runs `postgres --version` of the new release as the Postgres OS user, as a start does.
* It reads `PG_VERSION` of the cluster. A dir without a cluster passes.
* It returns the error of a start with `PG_VERSION` of another major version, and it changes nothing on disk.
* It only reads, so it works while the old `hopboxd` runs Postgres.

The install then stops before it changes the config, the current release, or the units, and the running `hopboxd` keeps running. A move to a new major version needs `pg_upgrade`, which `hopboxd admin db upgrade` runs. That command comes with the first change of the major version.

The first install of a control server runs `initdb` through pgsup: it starts Postgres once, which makes the cluster and the database `hopbox`, and stops it ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#install)). So a broken Postgres stops the install, not the first start of the service.

A control server on an external Postgres skips the checks of this section. The operator upgrades that Postgres ([External Postgres](#external-postgres)).

## Logs

pgsup writes slog records with `component=pgsup`.

| Message                         | Level | Fields                                                                                |
| ------------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `creating postgres cluster`     | info  | `data_dir`                                                                            |
| `initdb`                        | debug | `line`, one record per output line of `initdb`                                        |
| `postgres started`              | info  | `pid`, `data_dir`                                                                     |
| `postgres ready`                | info  | `pid`, `socket_dir`                                                                   |
| `created database`              | info  | `database`                                                                            |
| `postgres exited`               | error | `pid`, `err`, `uptime`                                                                |
| `restarting postgres`           | info  | `delay`                                                                               |
| `postgres restart failed`       | error | `err`                                                                                 |
| `postgres did not become ready` | warn  | `pid`, `err`                                                                          |
| `stopping postgres`             | info  | `pid`, `mode`: `fast`, `immediate`, or `kill`                                         |
| `postgres log lost`             | warn  | `err`. A log line was longer than 1 MiB. pgsup drops the rest of the log of that run. |
| `postgres stopped`              | info  | `pid`, `duration`                                                                     |

Each line that Postgres writes becomes one record. The message is the text of the line, and the fields are `pid`, `severity`, and `source=postgres`. The level follows the severity:

| Postgres severity         | slog level |
| ------------------------- | ---------- |
| `PANIC`, `FATAL`, `ERROR` | error      |
| `WARNING`                 | warn       |
| `DEBUG1` to `DEBUG5`      | debug      |
| every other severity      | info       |

Some lines have no prefix, for example the second line of a long statement. Each of them becomes a record with the message `postgres` and the field `line`.

## Errors

| Error                                                                                                                         | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `postgres data dir <dir> holds a Postgres <N> cluster, but the bundled binaries are Postgres <M>, so pgsup will not start it` | `PG_VERSION` names another major version. A major upgrade needs `pg_upgrade`, which `hopboxd` does not run yet. An install or an upgrade gives the same error from `pgsup.CheckVersion` ([Upgrades](#upgrades)). |
| `postgres data dir is not empty and has no PG_VERSION file, so pgsup will not use it: <dir>`                                  | `data` holds files that are not a cluster.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `pgsup: look up the postgres OS user "hopbox-pg": ...`                                                                        | `hopboxd` runs as root, and the user `hopbox-pg` does not exist.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `pgsup: socket dir <dir> makes a socket path of <n> bytes, more than the 103 that unix sockets allow`                         | The socket dir path is too long.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `pgsup: hopboxd cannot run <install>/bin/postgres --version: ...`                                                             | The install has no working `postgres` binary.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `pgsup: the postgres OS user hopbox-pg cannot run <install>/bin/postgres --version: ...`                                      | As root: `hopbox-pg` cannot enter a dir of the install path, or cannot read or run a file of it.                                                                                                                 |
