| `pgsup: <dir> is a symlink, so pgsup will not use it`                                                                         | The state dir, the data dir, or the socket dir is a symlink.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `pgsup: <dir>/PG_VERSION does not hold a version number`                                                                      | `PG_VERSION` holds something other than digits.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `pgsup: read PG_VERSION: ...` or `pgsup: read postmaster.pid: ...`                                                            | The file is a symlink that leaves the state dir, or it is not a regular file.                                                                                                                                    |
| `pgsup: initdb: ...`                                                                                                          | `initdb` failed. The error ends with the last lines of its output.                                                                                                                                               |
| `start postgres: postgres exited before it was ready: ...`                                                                    | The postmaster exited during the first start. The Postgres log records give the reason.                                                                                                                          |
| `start postgres: postgres not ready: context deadline exceeded ...`                                                           | The first start took more than 60 s.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `postgres supervisor is stopped`                                                                                              | A call after `Stop`.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `a postgres server already runs on the data dir, so pgsup will not start another: pid <n> in <dir>/postmaster.pid`            | A live process holds the data dir. Stop it, or remove a stale `postmaster.pid` whose PID now belongs to another process.                                                                                         |
| `pgsup: the setting <name> is fixed and cannot be in Settings`                                                                | The caller passed a parameter from the [Server parameters](#server-parameters) list, or a protected one.                                                                                                         |
| `pgsup: stop postgres: context canceled`                                                                                      | The caller stopped the wait of a stop. Postgres got `SIGQUIT`.                                                                                                                                                   |

## External Postgres

Several control servers need one shared Postgres, and the bundled Postgres listens only on its unix socket. So the control role can use an external Postgres, such as managed PostgreSQL of OVHcloud or a Postgres with Patroni. `hopboxd admin db export` moves the store of a one-server install there ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-db-export)). The keys `postgres.url`, `postgres.ca_file`, and `postgres.password_file` of the bootstrap config name it ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). [Run the control store on an external Postgres](/guide/external-postgres/) sets one up.

With `postgres.url`, the control role changes in these ways:

* The unit `postgres` of `hopboxd run` starts no Postgres. It reads `postgres.ca_file` and `postgres.password_file`, and logs `using the external postgres` at level info, with `url`, the URL without its query, and `ca_file` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run)). A file that fails a check stops the start.
* The connection pool, the connection of the leader election, and the connection of the event subscriber connect over TCP with TLS and `sslmode=verify-full`. The client checks that the CA of `postgres.ca_file` signed the certificate of the server, and that the certificate names the host of `postgres.url`. The client sends the password only after that check. A failed check stops the unit `store`, and `hopboxd run` exits with status 1.
* No `<data_dir>/pg`, no `<run_dir>/pg`, and no OS user `hopbox-pg` exist. `hopboxd install` makes none of them, and runs no `initdb` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#install)).
* `hopboxd install` reads the schema version from the external Postgres. A database without the table `schema_migrations` counts as a new control store, so the install needs `--domain`.
* The upgrades of Postgres and its failover are the job of the operator. After a failover, the connections end. The pool connects again for the next call. The leader election loses its lock with its connection, and takes part again. The event subscriber connects again and reads the events that it missed.

The external Postgres must meet these rules:

| Rule                                                                                                                                                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Postgres 18 or later: the major version of the bundled Postgres, or a newer one.                                                                    | The migrations are tested on Postgres 18. `hopboxd admin db export` refuses an older target, because `pg_restore` of a newer dump into an older server can fail.                                                                                                                            |
| TLS with a certificate that names the host of `postgres.url`.                                                                                       | `sslmode=verify-full` checks both. The server can refuse connections without TLS.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| The user of `postgres.url` owns the database, or can create tables in its schema `public`. It needs no superuser.                                   | The migrations create tables, indexes, and sequences. They need no extension. Managed PostgreSQL gives no superuser.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Each connection is a session of its own: a direct connection, or a pooler in session mode. A pooler in transaction or statement mode does not work. | The leader election holds the session advisory lock `LockKeyLeader` on one connection, and the event subscriber runs `LISTEN` on one connection ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#leader-election)). A pooler in transaction mode would hand that session to other clients. |
| The user can set `application_name`, `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout`, and `idle_session_timeout` for its session.                             | Each connection sets them at its start ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#connections)). Every user can set them, unless the operator forbids it.                                                                                                                            |
| Room for the connections of each control process: the pool, with at most 4 connections or the CPU count of the server if that is larger, plus 2.    | pgx sizes the pool by default, and the leader election and the event subscriber hold one connection each.                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Errors of the unit `store` on an external Postgres include these:

| Error                                                                                                                           | Cause                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `store: ping: failed to connect to ...: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`       | The CA of `postgres.ca_file` did not sign the certificate of the server. |
| `store: ping: failed to connect to ...: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate is valid for <names>, not <host>`  | The certificate does not name the host of `postgres.url`.                |
| `store: ping: failed to connect to ...: server error: FATAL: password authentication failed for user "<user>" (SQLSTATE 28P01)` | The password of `postgres.password_file` is wrong.                       |
| `store: migration <NNNN_name>: ERROR: permission denied for schema public (SQLSTATE 42501)`                                     | The user cannot create tables in the database.                           |

## Schema migrations

The control store schema comes from numbered SQL files in `internal/store/migrations/`. The `hopboxd` binary embeds them.

* Each file is named `NNNN_name.sql`. The name has four digits, a `_`, then lowercase letters, digits, and `_`.
* The numbers start at `0001` and have no gaps. Any other file in the folder fails the load.
* A migration never changes after it ships. A schema change is a new file.
* A migration must not control its transaction. The runner refuses a file with a top-level `BEGIN`, `START`, `COMMIT`, `END`, `ROLLBACK`, or `ABORT` statement. The check skips comments, string literals, quoted names, dollar-quoted bodies, and `BEGIN ATOMIC` function bodies.
* A migration can have one line `-- oldest_schema_version: <n>`. See [Two releases on one store](#two-releases-on-one-store).

Migration `0001_schema_migrations.sql` creates the table that records the applied migrations, and migration `0043_oldest_schema_version.sql` adds its last column:

| Column                  | Type                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `number`                | `integer`, primary key | The number of the migration.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `name`                  | `text`                 | The name part of the file name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `sha256`                | `bytea`                | The sha256 of the file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `applied_at`            | `timestamptz`          | When the migration ran.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `oldest_schema_version` | `integer`, null        | The oldest schema version that runs with the migration, from the line `-- oldest_schema_version` of its file. It is from 1 to `number`. `NULL` means `number`: only a `hopboxd` that knows the migration runs with it. The rows of the migrations before `0043`, and of each migration without the line, hold `NULL`. |

The rows of this table never change after their insert, so the table has no row version column.

[Control store tables](/reference/control-store/) lists the tables of the later migrations.

The runner does these steps:

1. It takes the session advisory lock `LockKeyMigrations` on one connection. Other runners wait for it, so many processes can migrate at the same time.
2. If the table `schema_migrations` exists, it reads the table.
3. It stops with an error in two cases. The first case is a database whose newest migration does not run with this binary ([Two releases on one store](#two-releases-on-one-store)). The second case is an applied migration whose name or hash differs from the file of this binary.
4. If the table `control_processes` exists, it waits for the live control processes that the missing migrations do not run with ([Two releases on one store](#two-releases-on-one-store)).
5. It runs each missing migration in its own transaction, together with the insert of its row. A migration that fails leaves no trace. A database with migrations that this binary does not know, and that run with it, gets no migration.
6. The runner of the control role (`store.MigrateAndRecord`) then writes the first row of its process in `control_processes`, while it still holds the lock. The write reads `schema_migrations` again and fails with the error of the first case of step 3 when the store no longer runs with this `hopboxd`. So no newer `hopboxd` can apply a migration that does not allow this one between the migrations and the first row. The full row, with the keys, maintenance mode, and the server ID, follows at the end of the `store` unit ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run)). The other runners write no row.
7. It frees the lock. If the unlock fails, it closes the connection, which frees the lock too.

### Two releases on one store

An install can run two releases at the same time: release N and release N-1. For example, a rolling upgrade moves one server at a time, and a rollback moves one server back. So a `hopboxd` of N-1 can run on a store that a `hopboxd` of N migrated.

The schema version of a `hopboxd` is the number of the newest migration that it knows. A release bundle records it as `schema_version` ([Release bundle](/reference/release-bundle/#manifest)). Each migration records the oldest schema version that runs with it, in `oldest_schema_version`. A `hopboxd` runs on a store only when its schema version is at least the oldest schema version of the newest migration of the store.

A migration names this version in a line of its own:

```sql
-- oldest_schema_version: 43
ALTER TABLE machines ADD COLUMN note text NOT NULL DEFAULT '';
```

Here, a `hopboxd` that knows migration 43 or later runs on a store with this migration. Name the schema version of release N-1 only when the code of N-1 still works with the schema after the migration. For example, a new column with a default value works with N-1, and a dropped column that N-1 reads does not. A migration without the line runs only with a `hopboxd` that knows it, so a rollback across it stops. The guide Write a change in two releases shows how to split a change that N-1 cannot follow.

The load of the migrations checks the line:

* The value is a migration number from 1 to the number of the migration.
* A file has the line at most once.
* The value is never lower than the oldest schema version of the migration before it. A release that does not run with an earlier migration does not run with a later one either. So the newest migration of a store speaks for all of its migrations.

The rule holds at three points:

* The start of the control role. The runner of step 3 refuses the store, and `hopboxd run` exits.
* A running control role. The `store` unit reads the schema every 10 s (`control.SchemaCheckEvery`). When a newer `hopboxd` applies a migration that does not run with this one, the unit logs an error and stops `hopboxd` ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run)). systemd starts it again, and the start then refuses the store. The unit also stops `hopboxd` when the store has no `schema_migrations`, or when a read fails because a column or a table is gone (SQLSTATE `42703` or `42P01`). Then the role cannot tell whether it may still write. Other failed reads only log, but 12 failed reads in a row stop `hopboxd` too. A read that takes more than 5 s counts as failed, so a store that does not answer for about 2 minutes stops `hopboxd`. This outlasts the failover of a managed PostgreSQL, which promotes a replica after 60 s. A process that cannot reach the store does not wait for this limit: it fences itself within 15 s, as the paragraph after this list says. The limit of 12 reads is safe only because of this fence. A process that cannot reach the store takes no call and runs no job long before the watch stops it, so it never writes while the other processes no longer count it. Until the next read, the older control role can still write for up to 10 s on the new schema. The runner closes most of this window: it waits for older control processes before it applies a migration, as the paragraph after this list says. It does not see a control role of a release before migration `0045`, because that role records no row. So a migration that does not allow N-1 must also not break a write of N-1 in that window.
* An upgrade or a rollback. `hopboxd upgrade` refuses a release that does not run on the store, before it switches ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#upgrade)).

Since migration `0045`, each control process records itself in `control_processes` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#control_processes)). Before the runner applies the missing migrations, it looks at this table, if it exists. The runner takes the newest of the missing migrations and its `oldest_schema_version`. It waits while a control process that is not gone has a schema version below that number. A process that ended without its stop counts as gone only 35 s after its last renewal (`store.ControlProcessGone`: the live window of 20 s and the dead peer timeout of 15 s), because a COMMIT that it sent before its fence can still land until the store ends its session. A process that stopped cleanly counts as gone at once. The runner polls each second, for at most 40 s, 5 s more than that. A control process that stops, or whose row is gone, lets the runner go on.

The runner logs the wait once, with the last message of the log table below. If the wait ends with a live process still in the way, the runner fails with the error `store: a live control process runs a hopboxd that does not run with a new migration: ...` of the table below, and applies nothing. Upgrade or stop the control role of that server, then start again.

Each control process renews its row in one transaction (`store.RecordControlProcess`). If the row is gone, stopped, or has no more than 5 s left to live (`store.ControlProcessFenceMargin`), the write first takes `LockKeyMigrations` shared (`pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared`). So it waits for a runner that holds the lock, and a runner that checks the live rows never misses a process that comes back. The write then reads `schema_migrations`, and fails with the error `store: the database has a migration that does not run with this hopboxd: ...` of the table below when the store no longer runs with this `hopboxd`. Only then does it write the row. A renewal that fails this way fences the process and stops `hopboxd` at once, without the wait for the next read of the schema watch. So a renewal that works means that the row is live and that the store runs with this `hopboxd`.

A process that no renewal reached for 15 s (the live window less a margin of 5 s, counted from the start of the last renewal that worked) fences itself before its row stops being live. While it is fenced, the API refuses every call, runs no control channel, and runs no leader job ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run)). The fence lifts at the next renewal that works.

A control process of a release before migration `0045` records no row, so the runner cannot see it. The schema watch of that process still stops it within 10 s after the migration.

v0.1.0 and the builds before migration `0043` have an older rule: their control role refuses every store with a migration that it does not know. So no control role of v0.1.0 runs on the store of a later release. A rollback of a control server to v0.1.0 always stops, because migration `0043` has no line `-- oldest_schema_version`. The roles without the control role do not read the store. So the hopbox Terraform provider upgrades an install of v0.1.0 one server at a time too: the first server first, then the nodes ([hopbox Terraform provider](/reference/terraform-provider/#rolling-upgrade)). In that time, servers of v0.1.0 work with the control role of the later release. No test covers this pair, because the fleet tests start only from a release with the new rule. So watch the servers of v0.1.0 in the first upgrade of a real install.

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `store: the database has a migration that does not run with this hopboxd: the database is at migration <n>, which runs only with a hopboxd that knows migration <m> or later, and this hopboxd knows the migrations up to <k>`                                                                                                  | A newer `hopboxd` applied a migration that does not allow this one. Upgrade `hopboxd` to a release that knows migration `<m>`.                                                                                                       |
| `the control store changed: store: the database has a migration that does not run with this hopboxd: .... Upgrade hopboxd on this server`                                                                                                                                                                                       | The same, found by the `store` unit while `hopboxd` runs. `hopboxd` stops.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `the control store changed: schema_migrations is gone`, or `the control store changed: store: read schema_migrations: ERROR: ... (SQLSTATE 42703)` or `(SQLSTATE 42P01)`                                                                                                                                                        | The store of a running control role lost `schema_migrations`, or a column or a table that the read needs. The second form comes when the table goes away between the check that it exists and the read of its rows. `hopboxd` stops. |
| `the schema of the control store did not read 12 times in a row: ...`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | The `store` unit could not read the schema for 12 checks in a row, about 2 minutes. `hopboxd` stops.                                                                                                                                 |
| `store: a live control process runs a hopboxd that does not run with a new migration: migration <NNNN_name> runs only with a hopboxd that knows migration <m> or later, and the control process <id> on <host> runs hopboxd <rel>, which knows the migrations up to <n>. Upgrade or stop the control role of that server first` | The runner waited 30 s, and the live control process still runs a `hopboxd` that does not run with the new migration. The runner applied nothing.                                                                                    |
| `store: an applied migration changed, but migrations must only grow: <NNNN_name>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | An applied migration file changed or got a new name.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `store: migration <NNNN_name>: ...`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | The SQL of a migration failed.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `store: migration file "<file>" is not NNNN_name.sql`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | A file in the folder has a bad name.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `store: migration <file> has number <n>, want <m>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | A gap or a doubled number.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `store: migration <file> has a top-level <WORD>, but the runner runs each migration in its own transaction`                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | The file has a statement that ends or starts a transaction.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `store: migration <file>: its oldest_schema_version <n> is not a migration number from 1 to <m>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | The line names a number that is 0 or later than the migration.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `store: migration <file>: it has more than one line oldest_schema_version`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | The file has the line twice.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `store: migration <file>: its oldest_schema_version is <n>, but migration <NNNN> before it runs only with <m> or later. ...`                                                                                                                                                                                                    | The line names a lower version than the migration before it.                                                                                                                                                                         |

These are the log records of the runner and of the `store` unit. Their records have `component=store`.

| Message                                                                                                           | Level | Fields                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `applied migration`                                                                                               | info  | `number`, `name`                                                                                                                                    |
| `waited for the migration lock`                                                                                   | info  | `duration`, after a wait of more than 1 s                                                                                                           |
| `the database has migrations that this hopboxd does not know, and they run with it`                               | info  | `applied`, `known`, `oldest_schema_version`                                                                                                         |
| `a newer hopboxd applied a migration that does not run with this one, so it stops`                                | error | `applied`, `oldest_schema_version`, `known` from the schema watch. From a renewal of the row of the process, `component=control` and `err` instead. |
| `reading the schema of the control store failed`                                                                  | warn  | `err`, `failures`: the failed reads in a row. The unit reads again 10 s later, and stops `hopboxd` at 12.                                           |
| `the control store lost the schema that this hopboxd migrated, so it stops`                                       | error | `err`                                                                                                                                               |
| `a live control process runs a hopboxd that does not run with a new migration, so the runner waits for it to end` | warn  | `process`, `hostname`, `release`, `schema_version`, `migration`, `oldest_schema_version`. Once for each run of the runner.                          |

### Advisory lock keys

The file `internal/store/locks.go` holds every advisory lock key of hopbox. Each key has `hopbox` in ASCII in its top six bytes, then a 16-bit purpose number. A test checks the prefix and that no two keys are the same.

| Key                           | Value                | Holder                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `LockKeyMigrations`           | `0x686f70626f780001` | The migration runner. The write of a row of `control_processes` that is gone or has no more than 5 s left to live takes it too, as a shared transaction lock, so the runner and such a write wait for each other.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `LockKeyLeader`               | `0x686f70626f780002` | The leader of the control role, on its own connection ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#leader-election)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `LockKeySignIn`               | `0x686f70626f780010` | A sign-in that can create or link an account, as a transaction lock ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#what-a-sign-in-does)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `LockKeyMagicLinks`           | `0x686f70626f780011` | A request for a magic link, as a transaction lock, so the rate limits count every request ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#rate-limits)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `LockKeyInvitations`          | `0x686f70626f780012` | A new invitation to an org, as a transaction lock, so the rate limits per inviter and per email count every invitation ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#invitations)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `LockKeyDeviceAuthorizations` | `0x686f70626f780013` | A start of a device sign-in, as a transaction lock, so the limits of the device flow count every start ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#limits-of-the-device-flow)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `LockKeyDeviceApprovals`      | `0x686f70626f780014` | An approval of a device sign-in, as a transaction lock, so the limit of wrong codes counts every failure ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#limits-of-the-device-flow)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `LockKeyServerRegistry`       | `0x686f70626f780015` | A transaction lock of each change of the server registry: an enrollment, the retry and the resync of an enrollment, the add of roles, the start and the end of a removal of roles, `SetServerPeerAddress`, `DecommissionServer`, and each empty check of a drain, whose last check can decommission the node ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#resync-after-the-end-of-the-token), [Cold move](/reference/cold-move/)). Each one takes it before the row of the server, so none of them deadlocks with another. A decommission of the node on the host of the control role counts the other servers under it. So a server that enrolls at that time counts ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#decommissionserver)). |
| `LockKeyOAuthFlows`           | `0x686f70626f780016` | A transaction lock of each start of a sign-in with GitHub or Google that the rate limit counts. The limit thus counts every start ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/#rate-limits)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `LockKeyRetiredGuestHostKeys` | `0x686f70626f780017` | Retired, do not reuse. Up to v0.1.0, a report of `running` with SSH host keys took it as an exclusive transaction lock. A `hopboxd` of v0.1.0 can still take it during an upgrade. So in the release after v0.1.0, each report takes it as a shared transaction lock, and migration `0041_route_host_keys.sql` takes it exclusively for its fill. The table `route_host_keys` now keeps each key in one route record ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#route_host_keys)). The release after that drops the shared lock.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `LockKeyNodeSubnets`          | `0x686f70626f780018` | A transaction lock of each claim of a node subnet. So two nodes that get their first machine at once never pick the same subnet ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#node_subnets)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `LockKeyReleaseImages`        | `0x686f70626f780019` | A transaction lock of each register of the default image of a release at the start of the control role, around the check for an image of a newer release and the insert ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#the-default-image-of-the-release)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `LockKeyMeshAddresses`        | `0x686f70626f78001a` | A transaction lock of each claim of a mesh address. So two servers that join the mesh at once never pick the same address ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#mesh_members)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### Queries

sqlc generates Go code for the queries in `internal/store/queries/*.sql` into the package `internal/store/db`. Its schema input is the migrations folder, so the generated types always match the schema that the runner builds. The file `internal/store/sqlc.yaml` holds the config of sqlc.

sqlc maps column types to Go types with these rules:

| Postgres type    | Go type                                                              | Go type of a `NULL` column             |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `uuid`           | `uuid.UUID` from the Go standard library                             | `*uuid.UUID`                           |
| `timestamptz`    | `time.Time`                                                          | `*time.Time`                           |
| every other type | the default type of sqlc for pgx v5, for example `int64` or `string` | a pointer to it, for example `*string` |

IDs are UUIDv7. The Go code makes them with `uuid.NewV7`, not the database. `make generate` runs sqlc after buf. If `internal/store/db` differs from git, `make check-generate` fails.

## Tests

| Environment variable | Description                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `HOPBOX_PG_DIR`      | The Postgres install for tests. `make test` sets it to the output of `tools/pgdist`. If it is not set, tests run `go run ./tools/pgdist` themselves. |

The package `internal/store/storetest` starts one Postgres per test package, with `fsync`, `synchronous_commit`, and `full_page_writes` off. It creates the template database `hopbox_template` with every migration applied. Each test gets its own database, copied from the template with `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE`, and a cleanup drops it.

`pgsuptest.StartTLS` starts a Postgres of the bundled install that plays an external Postgres, as the user of the test. It runs `initdb` in a temp dir, and takes TCP connections on `127.0.0.1` only over TLS, with a password. Its certificate names `127.0.0.1`, so a client can use `sslmode=verify-full`. It owns a database through a user that is no superuser, as on managed PostgreSQL. It also writes the password file and a second CA that did not sign the certificate. A cleanup stops it. Postgres refuses root, so it skips a test that runs as root. `TestControlRoleExternalPostgres` runs the control role on it and checks that each connection uses TLS. `TestControlRoleExternalPostgresWrongCA` checks that the start fails with the second CA.

A test binary that panics, times out, or gets Ctrl-C or `SIGKILL` skips its cleanup and leaves its dirs behind. Its Postgres stops within seconds, by the parent death signal on Linux or the watchdog on macOS ([Start, restart, and stop](#start-restart-and-stop)). So at each start, `storetest.Main` removes old dirs of earlier runs: socket dirs `/tmp/hbpg-*` and data dirs `storetest-*` in the temp dir. A dir goes only on two conditions: it is older than 10 minutes, and its PID file names no live process. A Postgres that still runs keeps its dirs. A test package calls `storetest.Main` from `TestMain`, and `storetest.New` in each test (the build guide of the repo has an example).

# The preflight check

> The preflight checks of a server, their severities, their errors, the tested OS and kernel, and the tested server.

The preflight check tests that a server can run machines. `hopboxd install` runs it on a server with the node role, before it switches the release ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#install)). `hopboxd enroll` runs it on a server with the node role, before it contacts the control role ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#hopboxd-enroll)). On a server with the node role, the `channel` unit of `hopboxd run` runs it again at its first heartbeat. The heartbeats report the result ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#the-heartbeat)). A server with only the DNS role runs no machine. So its enrollment and its heartbeats skip the preflight check. `hopboxd preflight` runs it on demand. The code is in `internal/node/preflight`.

## Severities

| Severity | A failure means                                                                                                                 |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fail`   | The node cannot run a microVM. The check stops an enrollment, and the heartbeats report the status `degraded`.                  |
| `warn`   | hopbox runs, with a higher risk. An enrollment goes on, and the status stays `ok`. The problem still appears in the heartbeats. |

Every check runs, also after a failure, so one run lists every problem. Each check has at most 10 seconds.

## The tested host

hopbox tests one operating system and one host kernel ([Host kernel](/reference/host-kernel/)):

| Item             | Value                                                           |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Operating system | Debian 13: `ID=debian` and `VERSION_ID=13` in `/etc/os-release` |
| Kernel release   | `6.18.57-hopbox1`, as `uname -r` prints it                      |

### The tested server

The tested server is the server on which hopbox measures its times and runs its acceptance suite. It is an OVHcloud dedicated server:

| Item             | Value                                                      |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| CPU              | Intel Xeon E5-1650 v4, with 12 threads                     |
| Operating system | Debian 13                                                  |
| Host kernel      | `6.18.57-hopbox1` ([Host kernel](/reference/host-kernel/)) |

A page that gives a time or a result “on the tested server” gives a number of this server. Another server can give other numbers.

## Checks

The checks run in the order of this table.

| Check      | Severity | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `kvm`      | `fail`   | Opens `/dev/kvm` for reading and writing, and asks for the KVM API version with the ioctl `KVM_GET_API_VERSION`. The version must be 12.                                                                                                               |
| `cgroup2`  | `fail`   | Checks with `statfs` that `/sys/fs/cgroup` is a cgroup v2 file system, the unified hierarchy that the jailer needs.                                                                                                                                    |
| `tun`      | `fail`   | Opens `/dev/net/tun` for reading and writing.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `nftables` | `fail`   | Opens a netlink socket for nftables and lists the tables. This needs the kernel module `nf_tables` and the capability `CAP_NET_ADMIN`.                                                                                                                 |
| `reflink`  | `fail`   | Makes a missing `data_dir`. Then it writes a test file of 64 KiB in `data_dir` and clones it with the ioctl `FICLONE`. It removes both files after the test. The test files are `.preflight-reflink-<random>` and `.preflight-reflink-<random>.clone`. |
| `kernel`   | `warn`   | Compares the operating system and the kernel release with the tested host.                                                                                                                                                                             |

The checks need root, or rights that most users do not have, such as the group `kvm` and `CAP_NET_ADMIN`. Run them as root.

### Errors of the checks

| Check      | Error                                                                                                                                               | Cause                                                                                                             |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kvm`      | `/dev/kvm does not exist. Turn on virtualization (VT-x or AMD-V) in the firmware, and load the kvm_intel or kvm_amd module`                         | The CPU or the kernel gives no KVM.                                                                               |
| `kvm`      | `open /dev/kvm: <error>. hopboxd must run as root or in the group kvm`                                                                              | The user cannot open the device.                                                                                  |
| `kvm`      | `KVM_GET_API_VERSION on /dev/kvm: <error>`                                                                                                          | The ioctl failed.                                                                                                 |
| `kvm`      | `/dev/kvm has the KVM API version <n>, not 12`                                                                                                      | A KVM that hopbox does not know.                                                                                  |
| `cgroup2`  | `statfs /sys/fs/cgroup: <error>`                                                                                                                    | `/sys/fs/cgroup` does not exist.                                                                                  |
| `cgroup2`  | `/sys/fs/cgroup is not cgroup v2. The jailer needs the unified cgroup hierarchy: boot without systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=0`                   | The host runs cgroup v1 or a hybrid hierarchy.                                                                    |
| `tun`      | `/dev/net/tun does not exist. Load the tun module`                                                                                                  | The kernel has no tun device.                                                                                     |
| `tun`      | `open /dev/net/tun: <error>`                                                                                                                        | The user cannot open the device.                                                                                  |
| `nftables` | `open a netlink socket for nftables: <error>`                                                                                                       | The socket failed.                                                                                                |
| `nftables` | `list the nftables tables: <error>. The kernel needs nf_tables, and hopboxd needs CAP_NET_ADMIN`                                                    | The kernel has no `nf_tables`, or the user lacks the capability.                                                  |
| `reflink`  | `create the data dir: <error>`                                                                                                                      | `data_dir` is missing, and `hopboxd` cannot make it.                                                              |
| `reflink`  | `create a test file in <dir>: <error>`, `write a test file in <dir>: <error>`, or `sync a test file in <dir>: <error>`                              | `data_dir` is not writable, or the disk is full.                                                                  |
| `reflink`  | `FICLONE in <dir>: <error>. The data dir needs a file system with reflinks, such as XFS made with reflink=1`                                        | The file system of `data_dir` has no reflinks, for example ext4 or tmpfs.                                         |
| `kernel`   | `this host runs <name> with the kernel <release>, and hopbox tests only Debian 13 with the kernel 6.18.57-hopbox1. hopbox runs, with a higher risk` | Another operating system or kernel. `<name>` is `PRETTY_NAME` of `/etc/os-release`, or its `ID` and `VERSION_ID`. |
| `kernel`   | `read os-release: <error>` or `uname: <error>`                                                                                                      | `hopboxd` cannot read the host. It reads `/etc/os-release`. Without that file, it reads `/usr/lib/os-release`.    |

### Off Linux

hopbox runs machines only on Linux with KVM. On another operating system, such as macOS, every check of severity `fail` fails with `hopbox runs machines only on Linux with KVM, and this host runs <os>`. The `kernel` check reports the name of the operating system and its kernel release. So a real `hopboxd enroll` on a Mac fails, as it must.

## hopboxd preflight

```sh
hopboxd preflight [--config=PATH] [--json]
```

`preflight` runs every check on this server and prints the result. It changes nothing, except for the test files of the `reflink` check, which it removes, and a missing `data_dir`, which it makes.

| Flag       | Type | Default                    | Description                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------- | ---- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--config` | path | `/etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml` | The bootstrap config. `preflight` reads its `data_dir` for the `reflink` check ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). |
| `--json`   | bool | `false`                    | Prints one JSON object instead of the lines.                                                                                                         |

The text output has one line for each check. A line has the word `preflight`, a space, and the name of the check. Then come a tab and `ok`, or a tab, the severity, a tab, and the error:

```text
preflight <check>  ok
preflight <check>  <warn|fail>  <error>
```

The JSON object has these keys:

| Key                 | Type   | Description                                      |
| ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `passed`            | bool   | Whether every check of severity `fail` passed.   |
| `checks`            | array  | One object for each check, in order.             |
| `checks[].name`     | string | The name of the check, such as `kvm`.            |
| `checks[].severity` | string | `fail` or `warn`.                                |
| `checks[].passed`   | bool   | Whether the check passed.                        |
| `checks[].message`  | string | The error of a failed check, or an empty string. |

| Exit status | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0           | No check of severity `fail` failed. Warnings can still appear.                                                                                                                                           |
| 1           | A check of severity `fail` failed. `hopboxd` prints `hopboxd: error: the preflight check failed, so this server cannot run machines` to standard error. A config that does not load also gives status 1. |

Example on the tested server:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd preflight
preflight kvm  ok
preflight cgroup2  ok
preflight tun  ok
preflight nftables  ok
preflight reflink  ok
preflight kernel  ok
```

Example on a Mac:

```text
$ ./bin/darwin_arm64/hopboxd preflight --config /tmp/hb/hopboxd.toml
preflight kvm  fail  hopbox runs machines only on Linux with KVM, and this host runs darwin
preflight cgroup2  fail  hopbox runs machines only on Linux with KVM, and this host runs darwin
preflight tun  fail  hopbox runs machines only on Linux with KVM, and this host runs darwin
preflight nftables  fail  hopbox runs machines only on Linux with KVM, and this host runs darwin
preflight reflink  fail  hopbox runs machines only on Linux with KVM, and this host runs darwin
preflight kernel  warn  this host runs darwin with the kernel 27.0.0, and hopbox tests only Debian 13 with the kernel 6.18.57-hopbox1. hopbox runs, with a higher risk
hopboxd: error: the preflight check failed, so this server cannot run machines
```

## In hopboxd enroll

With the node role in the config, `hopboxd enroll` runs the checks. It prints the same lines to standard error. A failed check of severity `fail` stops it before it contacts the control role, with this error:

```text
hopboxd: error: the preflight check failed, so this server cannot run machines:
  kvm: /dev/kvm does not exist. Turn on virtualization (VT-x or AMD-V) in the firmware, and load the kvm_intel or kvm_amd module
```

The error has one indented line for each failed check of severity `fail`. Warnings do not stop the enrollment.

## In hopboxd install

With the node role in `--roles`, `hopboxd install` runs the checks after it makes the dirs of the data dir. It prints the same lines to standard error. A failed check of severity `fail` stops the install with the error of `hopboxd enroll`. The install then has not changed the config, the current release, or the units. Before the checks, the install also refuses a data dir that is not on XFS with reflinks ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#the-file-system-of-the-data-dir)).

## In the heartbeats

On a server with the node role, the `channel` unit runs the checks once, at the first heartbeat after `hopboxd run` starts. Each failed check, of either severity, becomes one problem line `<check>: <error>` in the heartbeats. A failed check of severity `fail` makes the status `degraded` ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#the-heartbeat)). `sudo hopboxd admin server get <id>` shows both ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-server-get)). A fix of the host shows after the next restart of `hopboxd`.

## Tests

| Test                                                                    | Where it runs                                        | What it checks                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `TestReport`, `TestChecksOrder`, `TestParseOSRelease`, `TestHostTested` | `make test`                                          | The report, the order of the checks, and the tested host, with injected checks.                                                                                  |
| `TestChecksFailOffLinux`                                                | `make test` on a Mac                                 | Every check of severity `fail` fails off Linux.                                                                                                                  |
| `TestLinuxChecks`                                                       | `make test-linux`, as root in a privileged container | `cgroup2`, `tun`, and `nftables` pass. On a host with `/dev/kvm`, such as the CI runner, `kvm` passes. On a host without it, `kvm` reports the missing device.   |
| `TestReflinkRefusesAFileSystemWithoutReflinks`                          | `make test-linux`                                    | The `reflink` check fails on a tmpfs and leaves no file.                                                                                                         |
| `TestReflinkPasses`                                                     | by hand, with `HOPBOX_TEST_REFLINK_DIR`              | The `reflink` check passes in the dir that the variable names, such as a dir on XFS with `reflink=1` on the tested server. Without the variable, the test skips. |

The tests of `hopboxd enroll` swap the checks, so they run on a Mac too.

# Release bundle

> The release bundle: its file, contents, manifest, the checks of a release, make bundle, tools/bundle, and the Firecracker pins.

A release bundle is one file with every file of one server release of hopbox. The same bundle plays every role. `hopboxd install` puts its release on a server, and `hopboxd upgrade` moves a server to it ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#install)). The Go package `internal/bundle` reads, writes, and checks bundles. `tools/bundle` builds them, and `make bundle` runs it.

## File

| Item     | Value                                                                                                                           |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name     | `hopbox-<version>-linux-amd64.tar.gz`, for example `hopbox-v0.1.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz`                                           |
| Format   | A tar file in the PAX format, compressed with gzip                                                                              |
| Top dir  | One dir, `hopbox-<version>/`. Every other entry is inside it.                                                                   |
| Checksum | `make bundle` writes `<name>.sha256` beside the bundle, in the format of `sha256sum`: the hex sha256, two spaces, and the name. |

`<version>` is the semver version of `hopboxd` in the bundle, from `tools/gitversion` ([the version command](/reference/version/)). A server keeps each release in `/opt/hopbox/releases/<version>` ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/)).

A bundle is about 600 MB. The compressed disk of the default image is about 560 MB of it.

## Contents

| Path in the bundle                                                     | Mode          | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `manifest.json`                                                        | 0644          | The [manifest](#manifest). It is the first entry after the top dir.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `hopboxd`                                                              | 0755          | `hopboxd` for `linux/amd64`, built with `CGO_ENABLED=0` by `make build`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `firecracker/firecracker`                                              | 0755          | Firecracker v1.17.0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `firecracker/jailer`                                                   | 0755          | The jailer v1.17.0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `firecracker/LICENSE`, `firecracker/NOTICE`, `firecracker/THIRD-PARTY` | 0644          | The license files of the Firecracker release. The Apache License 2.0 asks for them in each copy.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `postgres/`                                                            | 0755 and 0644 | The bundled Postgres 18.6 for `linux/amd64`: `bin/`, `lib/`, and `share/` ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#the-install)). `lib/` also holds the OpenSSL libraries `libssl.so.3` and `libcrypto.so.3`, which `pg_dump` and `pg_restore` need for TLS. It holds symlinks, such as `lib/libpq.so`. |
| `kernel/vmlinux`                                                       | 0644          | The guest kernel ([Guest kernel](/reference/guest-kernel/)). Its sha256 is the one in `kernel/vmlinux.sha256` of the checkout.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `image/artifact.json`                                                  | 0644          | The metadata of the default image ([Artifact format](/reference/artifact-format/#artifactjson)).                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `image/disk.raw.zst`                                                   | 0644          | The compressed disk of the default image, under the name that `artifact.json` gives it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `systemd/hopboxd.service`                                              | 0644          | The unit of `hopboxd` ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#systemd-units)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `systemd/hopbox-machines.slice`                                        | 0644          | The slice of the machines.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

Every dir has mode 0755. A bundle holds only dirs, regular files, and symlinks.

### The default image in the bundle

The bundle carries the default image, not only a reference to it. These reasons decide it:

* The image is built and tested with one guest kernel, and `artifact.json` names that kernel by its sha256. The bundle checks that the kernel and the image belong together, so they ship together.
* An install needs no download at run time, just as for Postgres. No hosting for releases and images exists yet.
* The image holds `hopbox-guest` of the same checkout, so its digest changes with each commit anyway.

The cost is size: an upgrade uploads the image again, about 560 MB. A server keeps one copy of each image. The install moves the image from the release into the image cache `/var/lib/hopbox/images/<digest>` and keeps no copy in the release dir ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#the-image-cache)).

## Manifest

`manifest.json` is a JSON object with these fields, in this order. Every field is required.

| Field                 | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `format_version`      | number | `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `version`             | string | The semver version of the release, such as `v0.1.0`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `os`                  | string | `linux`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `arch`                | string | `amd64`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `postgres_version`    | string | The version of the bundled Postgres, such as `18.6`, from `build/postgres/source.env`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `firecracker_version` | string | The Firecracker release, such as `v1.17.0`, from `build/bundle/firecracker.env`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `schema_version`      | number | The number of the last schema migration that `hopboxd` of the release knows, at least 1 ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#schema-migrations)). An upgrade or a rollback refuses a release whose `schema_version` is lower than the oldest schema version of the newest migration of the control store ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#upgrade), [the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#two-releases-on-one-store)). |
| `kernel_sha256`       | string | The sha256 of `kernel/vmlinux`, as 64 lowercase hex digits.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
