The control role logs the reason `the Linux user name looks like a credential, which the audit log never stores`.

### Who opens a machine

The control role finds the account of the key by its fingerprint ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#ssh-keys)), and the machine by the port. If all of these are true, the key opens the machine:

* The account uses the machine, as for an exec: it created the machine, or the machine is shared and the account is a member of its org. An org admin or an org owner cannot open a private machine of another member. The rule is the policy action `machine.ssh`, with the caller kind `ssh_key` ([the API server](/reference/api/#callers-and-policy)).
* An instance admin did not suspend the org of the machine.
* The machine holds the port, and its target is not `deleted`.

Each allowed check records a use of the machine for its auto-delete timeout ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#auto-delete)). Each allowed sign-in also writes an audit entry ([Audit](#audit)). SSH never creates, starts, or changes a machine.

## Connection to the machine

After the sign-in, the front door reads the route of the port ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#machine-urls)). Then it opens an SSH connection to port 22 of the address of the machine.

| Item     | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Address  | The address of the route record of the machine, port 22. An edge server without the node role reaches it only over the mesh ([The mesh](#the-mesh)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| User     | The user name of the client.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Key      | The client key of the install.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Host key | Only a host key that the guest agent of the machine reported. The executor sends the host keys of the guest with each report of running ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#machinereport)), and the route record keeps them. So the front door does not sign in to another honest guest at an old address. Every guest accepts the client key, so the host key is what tells two machines apart. A guest can show a host key that the route of another machine holds, such as after a copy of a disk. The guest that reports the key second then does not get that key in its route. If the guest has no other key, it loses SSH. An honest guest loses it too. When the first route lets the key go, because its guest changed its keys or its machine stopped, the second route gets the key in the same transaction. If another transaction locks the second route, or a `hopboxd` of v0.1.0 let the key go, a leader job gives the key within a minute ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#route_host_keys)). A hostile guest can show a stolen host key. The guard against it is the hold of a released address: no new machine gets the address of a deleted machine for 5 minutes, much longer than a machine lease ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#the-hold-of-a-released-address)). |
| Timeouts | 10 s for the TCP connection, and 10 s for the SSH handshake.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Retries  | A machine reports `running` once its guest agent applied its config. OpenSSH can start listening about a second later. So when the machine refuses the TCP connection, the front door dials again. It waits 100 ms first, then twice as long each time, up to 1 s. It stops at the end of the 10 s of the TCP connection. Another failure, such as no route to the address, ends the dial at once.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

When the front door cannot reach the machine, the client stays signed in, and each channel that it opens fails with a message. The connection closes after the first refused channel, or after 30 s. With `ssh`, the message reads `channel 0: open failed: connect failed: hopbox: the machine box1 cannot take SSH connections now: <reason>`.

| Reason                                                                                          | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `it is stopped. Start it with: hopbox machine start box1`                                       | The machine does not run, or its lease ended at the edge. The state in the message is the state of the machine.                                                                                                     |
| `it has no network address on its node. Use hopbox connect instead`                             | The route record has no address. Each report of running sets the address of the machine there ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#where-the-address-shows)), so only a machine without an address gets it. |
| `its guest agent has not reported the SSH host keys of the machine yet. Retry in a few seconds` | The route has no host key.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `the front door cannot reach the OpenSSH server of the machine`                                 | The TCP connection failed, or the machine refused it for 10 s. The front door logs `the front door cannot reach the OpenSSH server of a machine` at level info, with `machine`, `addr`, and `err`.                  |
| `the OpenSSH server of the machine refused the front door`                                      | The SSH handshake failed: another host key, or no sign-in with the client key.                                                                                                                                      |
| `the machine is gone`                                                                           | The routes name no machine at the port any more.                                                                                                                                                                    |

A machine in standby or hibernated does not wake at a connection before phase 3.

## The mesh

The front door reaches the OpenSSH server of a machine in the same way as the edge role reaches a machine URL ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#the-way-to-the-machines)):

* On an edge server with the node role, the routes of the host decide: the tap device of a machine of this server, or the mesh device `hbm0` for a machine of another node.
* On an edge server without the node role, each connection to a machine is bound to `hbm0`, and leaves from the mesh address of the edge server. An address outside the machine range `10.240.0.0/12` fails at once.

So the OpenSSH server of the machine sees the mesh address of the edge server as the client. The audit entry `machine.ssh` keeps the address of the real client ([Audit](#audit)).

When the edge server has no mesh device yet, each channel fails with the reason `the front door cannot reach the OpenSSH server of the machine`, and the log record of that reason has an `err` such as `This edge server reaches the machines only over the mesh, and has no mesh device hbm0 yet`.

## Channels and requests

The front door forwards each channel and each request that the table names, both ways, with its answer. It refuses the others. A refused channel fails with `the SSH front door of hopbox does not forward <type> channels`. A refused request that wants an answer gets a failure.

| From        | Channels                                                                                           | Requests                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The client  | `session` (shell, exec, scp, SFTP, rsync), `direct-tcpip` (`ssh -L`, `ssh -D`, VS Code Remote-SSH) | Global: `tcpip-forward` and `cancel-tcpip-forward` (`ssh -R`), `keepalive@openssh.com`, `no-more-sessions@openssh.com`. On a session: `pty-req`, `env`, `shell`, `exec`, `subsystem`, `window-change`, `signal`, `break`, `auth-agent-req@openssh.com` (`ssh -A`), `keepalive@openssh.com`. |
| The machine | `forwarded-tcpip` (`ssh -R`), `auth-agent@openssh.com` (`ssh -A`)                                  | Global: `keepalive@openssh.com`. On a session: `exit-status`, `exit-signal`, `eow@openssh.com`, `xon-xoff`, `keepalive@openssh.com`.                                                                                                                                                        |

So these stay off:

* X11 forwarding: the channel `x11` and the request `x11-req`.
* The forwarding of Unix sockets: the channels `direct-streamlocal@openssh.com` and `forwarded-streamlocal@openssh.com`, and `streamlocal-forward@openssh.com`.
* `hostkeys-00@openssh.com` of the OpenSSH server of the machine. The client knows only the host key of the install, so the host keys of a guest never reach its `known_hosts`.

The OpenSSH server of the machine applies its own `sshd_config` too, such as `AllowTcpForwarding` and `AcceptEnv`.

The front door sends the exit status of a session only after the last output of the session. It closes each end of a channel only after the answers to the requests of that end.

## Checks of an open connection

An open connection keeps its access only while the control role allows it. The front door calls `AuthorizeSSH` again:

* every `valid_for` of the last answer, 30 s today. The period is at least 5 s and at most 1 minute,
* at each access change that the control role pushes for the machine, or for every machine ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#private-machine-urls)). For a change of every machine, such as a sign-out, each connection waits a random time of up to 10 s first. So the connections of an edge server do not all call the control role at once.

An answer of `permission_denied`, `unauthenticated`, `failed_precondition`, `not_found`, or `invalid_argument`, or an answer for another machine, ends the connection. Any other error, such as a control role that does not answer, keeps the connection until the next check. Each allowed check also records a use of the machine for its auto-delete timeout. These checks set `recheck`, so they write no audit entry.

Each change of a machine pushes an access change, such as a share, an unshare, or a delete. So do a removed SSH key, a member that leaves an org or that an admin removes, a deleted account, and a suspended org ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#the-event-edgeaccess_changed)). A sign-out does too, but it does not end SSH connections, because an SSH key is not a sign-in.

New routes end an open connection at once in four cases. The port has no machine. Another machine holds the port. The org of the machine is suspended. The machine runs in another execution, with another lease.

## Limits

Each edge server counts its own limits. An install with more edge servers allows more in all.

Users behind one IPv4 address, or in one IPv6 /64, are one client, so they share its 30 tries a minute. A known key does not skip this bucket.

Other clients in a network can spend the bucket of that network with new keys. The new users of that /24 or /48 then wait for the bucket to fill again. The users that this edge server allowed in the last 15 minutes still sign in.

The bucket of every client is the last guard of the control role. Clients in many networks can still spend it, with new keys that open nothing. While it is spent, the users that this edge server allowed in the last 15 minutes still sign in. A user whose key is new to this edge server waits until the bucket fills again. That is the trade-off. A flood of new keys can keep new users out for a while. It never keeps out the users of the last 15 minutes, and it never floods the control role.

| Limit                                  | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Past it                                                         |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Open connections of the listener       | 16,384                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | The connection waits in the backlog of the kernel.              |
| Open connections of one client         | 64                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | The front door closes the connection at once.                   |
| Sign-in tries of one client            | 30 a minute. A try is a key that the client signed with. The bucket fills again over a minute.                                                                                                                                                                         | The try fails without a call to the control role.               |
| Sign-in tries of one network           | 300 a minute. A network is the /24 of an IPv4 address, or the /48 of an IPv6 address. So a client with many addresses of one network, such as the many /64 of one IPv6 /48, counts once. A key that this edge server allowed in the last 15 minutes skips this bucket. | The try fails without a call to the control role.               |
| Sign-in tries of every client together | 60,000 a minute, in one bucket. A key that this edge server allowed in the last 15 minutes skips this bucket.                                                                                                                                                          | The try fails without a call to the control role.               |
| Open connections of one SSH key        | 64, over every client                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The front door refuses the key before it asks the control role. |
| Sign-in tries of one connection        | 6                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | The connection ends.                                            |
| Handshake                              | 30 s                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | The connection ends.                                            |

## EdgeService.AuthorizeSSH

`hopbox.cluster.v1.EdgeService.AuthorizeSSH` serves the edge servers on the internal listener ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#edgeservice)). It needs the certificate of a server with the edge role. Another caller gets `permission_denied`. The front door calls it with a timeout of 10 s.

| Request field | Type   | Meaning                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ssh_port`    | uint32 | The port that the client dialed, 10000 to 30000.                                                                                                            |
| `public_key`  | bytes  | The public key of the client in the SSH wire format, at most 16 KiB.                                                                                        |
| `linux_user`  | string | The user name of the client.                                                                                                                                |
| `client_ip`   | string | The IP address of the client, such as `192.0.2.10`. An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address counts as its IPv4 address. A sign-in needs it. The audit entry records it. |
| `recheck`     | bool   | `true` for a check of an open connection, which writes no audit entry. `false` for a sign-in.                                                               |

| Response field | Type     | Meaning                                                   |
| -------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `machine_id`   | string   | The ID of the machine, a UUID.                            |
| `machine_name` | string   | The name of the machine, for the messages to the client.  |
| `account_id`   | string   | The account of the key, a UUID.                           |
| `valid_for`    | duration | How long the connection runs before the next check: 30 s. |

Every refusal is `permission_denied` with the same message: `permission denied: the SSH key opens no machine at this port for this user`. The control role logs the reason ([Logs](#logs)). Other errors, such as `unavailable`, mean that the control role did not check the key.

| Error                                   | Code               | Message                                                              |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A sign-in without `client_ip`           | `invalid_argument` | `invalid argument: a sign-in needs the IP address of the SSH client` |
| A `client_ip` that is not an IP address | `invalid_argument` | `invalid argument: the client IP is not an IP address`               |

An edge server of an older release sends no `client_ip`, so the control role refuses each of its sign-ins. Until milestone N09 of phase 2 adds two releases side by side, the edge servers and the control role must run the same release.

## Audit

Each sign-in that `AuthorizeSSH` allows writes one audit entry `machine.ssh` in the transaction of the check ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#audit_log)). The owner decided this on 2026-10-24.

| Field         | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Org           | The org of the machine. The org owners and the org admins read the entry with `ListAuditEntries` ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/#listauditentries)). An org member reads no entry of the org, as for every audit entry. Instance admins read every entry. |
| Actor         | The kind `ssh_key`, the account of the key, and the ID of the SSH key as the credential ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#ssh-keys)).                                                                                                     |
| Target        | The kind `machine`, and the machine ID.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `name`        | The name of the machine. The entry goes without it when the audit log refuses the name, as for a name from before a new credential pattern ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#machine-names)). The target ID still names the machine.                                           |
| `linux_user`  | The user name of the connection.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `fingerprint` | The SHA256 fingerprint of the key, such as `SHA256:FXuRc2JyZfKx3tXHxoblBpr+f1jfrmFaGfkF4S5o0Ho`.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `client_ip`   | The IP address of the client, as the edge server saw it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Each sign-in that the control role allows writes one entry. The checks of an open connection write none. A refusal writes none, and the control role logs it ([Logs](#logs)).

The entry records each sign-in that the control role allowed, also one that the edge server refuses after it. The edge server refuses the key in two cases: its routes name another machine at the port, or another sign-in of the key took its last slot in the meantime ([Sign-in](#sign-in)). The client then tries its next key, and a key that opens the machine writes a second entry. A key that holds 64 open connections before the call never reaches the control role, so it writes no entry. A machine that cannot take SSH now gets an entry too, because the client signed in ([Connection to the machine](#connection-to-the-machine)).

An entry of the API looks like this:

```json
{"id":"01a173a5-aa40-7cd0-82d6-384d41fcc7fe", "orgId":"01a173a5-aa01-7045-a1cb-415460b1ee81", "actor":{"kind":"ssh_key", "accountId":"01a173a5-aa08-7da5-a57a-88b0a1766cdc", "credentialId":"01a173a5-aa3b-7649-8377-8034b2728136"}, "action":"machine.ssh", "targetKind":"machine", "targetId":"01a173a5-aa2d-7824-a289-9a0fa1342bdb", "details":{"client_ip":"192.0.2.10", "fingerprint":"SHA256:FXuRc2JyZfKx3tXHxoblBpr+f1jfrmFaGfkF4S5o0Ho", "linux_user":"user", "name":"box1"}, "requestId":"01a173a5-aa3f-7d61-9b0e-36c1f2a7d4e5", "createTime":"2026-10-25T15:19:59.295802Z"}
```

The `requestId` is the ID of the call of `AuthorizeSSH` on the internal listener.

## Metrics

The edge role serves these metrics on the metrics listener of `hopboxd` ([Metrics](/reference/metrics/#metrics-of-the-edge-role)).

| Metric                              | Type    | Labels           | Meaning                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hopbox_edge_ssh_connections_total` | counter | `result`         | The TCP connections of the front door, by result. See the table of results below.                                                                         |
| `hopbox_edge_ssh_auth_total`        | counter | `result`         | The keys that clients signed with: `allowed`, `refused`, `limited`, or `error` (the control role did not answer).                                         |
| `hopbox_edge_ssh_unreachable_total` | counter | `reason`         | The signed-in connections that reached no OpenSSH server: `not_running`, `no_address`, `no_host_key`, `dial`, or `handshake`.                             |
| `hopbox_edge_ssh_channels_total`    | counter | `type`, `result` | The channels, by type, and by result: `forwarded`, `refused` (by the other side), or `prohibited` (by the front door). An unknown type counts as `other`. |
| `hopbox_edge_ssh_ended_total`       | counter | `reason`         | The open connections that the front door ended: `access_lost`, `route_changed`, or `shutdown`.                                                            |
| `hopbox_edge_ssh_open_connections`  | gauge   | none             | The signed-in connections that the front door holds now.                                                                                                  |

| `result` of `hopbox_edge_ssh_connections_total` | Meaning                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `forwarded`                                     | The connection reached its machine.                        |
| `unreachable`                                   | The client signed in, but the machine cannot take SSH now. |
| `refused`                                       | No key of the client opened the machine.                   |
| `limited`                                       | The client held 64 open connections.                       |
| `no_machine`                                    | The port is outside the SSH ports.                         |
| `no_keys`                                       | The keys of the front door have not arrived yet.           |
| `handshake_failed`                              | The SSH handshake did not finish.                          |

## Logs

The front door logs with `component=sshfd`.

| Message                                                                                                          | Level | When                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SSH front door listening`                                                                                       | info  | The listener is open, with `addr`.                                                                                                         |
| `the SSH ports reach the front door`                                                                             | info  | The redirect is in place, with `ports` and `listen_port`.                                                                                  |
| `this system has no nftables, so no SSH port reaches the front door. Only Linux runs the redirect`               | warn  | `edge.ssh_redirect` on a system without nftables, with `os`.                                                                               |
| `the nftables table inet hopbox_edge lost a part outside hopboxd, so the SSH front door installed it again. ...` | error | The check of the redirect found its table broken, and installed it again.                                                                  |
| `cannot repair the redirect of the SSH ports`                                                                    | error | `err`. The check of the redirect failed. It tries again 2 s later.                                                                         |
| `serving the SSH host key of the install`                                                                        | info  | The first keys, with the `fingerprint` of the host key.                                                                                    |
| `closed a connection that reached no SSH port`                                                                   | debug | A connection came to a port outside the SSH ports, with `client`, `port`, and `err`.                                                       |
| `closed an SSH connection: <error>`                                                                              | warn  | The keys of the front door have not arrived yet, with `client`. The error is `sshfd: the keys of the SSH front door have not arrived yet`. |
| `an SSH connection did not sign in`                                                                              | debug | The SSH handshake with the client failed, or no key of the client opened the machine, with `client`, `port`, and `err`.                    |
| `SSH connection forwarded`                                                                                       | info  | A connection reached its machine, with `client`, `machine`, `port`, `user`, and `fingerprint`.                                             |
| `SSH connection closed`                                                                                          | info  | A forwarded connection ended.                                                                                                              |
| `a signed-in SSH connection cannot reach its machine`                                                            | info  | With `reason` and `err` ([Connection to the machine](#connection-to-the-machine)).                                                         |
| `the front door cannot reach the OpenSSH server of a machine`                                                    | info  | The TCP connection to the machine failed, with `machine`, `addr`, and `err`. A client that leaves during the dial gets no record.          |
| `the SSH connection to a machine failed`                                                                         | warn  | The SSH handshake with the machine failed, with `addr`, `user`, and `err`.                                                                 |
| `cannot check an SSH key with the control role`                                                                  | warn  | `AuthorizeSSH` failed without an answer.                                                                                                   |
| `refused an SSH connection past the bound of open connections of its key`                                        | info  | With `fingerprint` and `max`.                                                                                                              |
| `ended an SSH connection that lost its access`                                                                   | info  | A check refused the access of an open connection.                                                                                          |
| `checking an SSH connection failed. The next check tries again`                                                  | warn  | A check got no answer.                                                                                                                     |
| `ended the SSH connections of machines whose route changed`                                                      | info  | New routes ended open connections, with `connections`.                                                                                     |
| `cannot remove the redirect of the SSH ports`                                                                    | warn  | The stop did not delete the table.                                                                                                         |

The control role logs each refusal of `AuthorizeSSH` as `refused an SSH connection` at info level. Its fields are `ssh_port`, `linux_user`, `client_ip`, `fingerprint`, and `reason`, such as `the account does not use the machine`. A refusal writes no audit entry, so this record is the only trace of it. It logs each access that it allows as `allowed an SSH connection` at debug level, with `ssh_port`, `linux_user`, `client_ip`, `fingerprint`, `machine`, and `account`. It logs `created the keys of the SSH front door` once, with `host_key`.

## Not in phase 1

* A machine in standby or hibernated wakes at the first packet to its SSH port (phase 3).

# hopbox Terraform provider

> The hopbox Terraform provider for any Debian 13 host over SSH, its provider block, the host that the operator sets up, the resources hopbox_server, hopbox_pool, and hopbox_size, their steps and errors, and the binary.

`terraform-provider-hopbox` is the hopbox Terraform provider. Terraform runs it as a plugin. It installs hopbox over SSH on hosts that run Debian 13, from any provider of servers, or computers that the operator owns. The operator orders each host and installs Debian 13 on it, and the provider takes it from there. It installs the tested host kernel and `hopboxd`, and enrolls the server. Then it manages the server through the admin API. An install can grow into a fleet: edge servers with floating addresses, more control servers, and nodes in pools. The provider reaches a server that is not an edge server through a jump host. The provider calls no API of a provider of servers (plan question Q90). The code is in `internal/tfprovider`. [Install hopbox on your servers with Terraform](/guide/install-with-terraform/) walks through a first install.

The provider has three resources, [`hopbox_server`](#resource-hopbox_server), [`hopbox_pool`](#resource-hopbox_pool), and [`hopbox_size`](#resource-hopbox_size), and no data sources.

## Provider address

| Item            | Value                                    |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Source address  | `registry.terraform.io/hopboxdev/hopbox` |
| Short source    | `hopboxdev/hopbox`                       |
| Local name      | `hopbox`                                 |
| Plugin protocol | 6                                        |

The provider is not in a registry yet. v0.2.0 is the first release with this provider. Until the hopbox team tags it, build the release files from a checkout. The release files hold a zip of the provider for macOS on Apple Silicon and for Linux on x86_64, such as `terraform-provider-hopbox_0.2.0_darwin_arm64.zip`, in the packed layout of a filesystem mirror. Put the zip in `~/.terraform.d/plugins/registry.terraform.io/hopboxdev/hopbox/`, and set `version = "0.2.0"` for the provider in `required_providers`. Terraform reads that dir as a local mirror only without a `provider_installation` block in its CLI configuration. With such a block, add a `filesystem_mirror` block for the dir ([Install hopbox on your servers with Terraform](/guide/install-with-terraform/#3-write-the-terraform-files)).

To use a local build from a checkout instead, give Terraform the dir of the binary in a `dev_overrides` block of a Terraform CLI configuration file (the build guide of the repo has an example).

## Provider block

```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    hopbox = {
      source = "hopboxdev/hopbox"
    }
  }
}


provider "hopbox" {
  ssh_private_key = file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519")
}
```

The provider block of a fleet, after its first server runs:

```hcl
provider "hopbox" {
  ssh_private_key = file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519")
  install_url     = "https://example.com"


  ssh_jump_host = {
    address  = "203.0.113.11"
    host_key = "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAI..."
  }
}
```

Every attribute is optional. An attribute that you leave out takes the value of its environment variable.

| Attribute         | Type              | Environment variable     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ssh_private_key` | string, sensitive | `HOPBOX_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` | The SSH private key of the operator, in the OpenSSH or PEM format. A key with a passphrase does not work. The operator puts its public key in the `authorized_keys` of the login user of each host before the create ([The host](#the-host)). The provider logs in with it for every step. A create, an update, a delete, and an import need it.                                                                            |
| `install_url`     | string            | `HOPBOX_INSTALL_URL`     | The URL of the install, such as `https://example.com`. The provider calls the admin API there with `admin_api_key`. It must be an `https` URL. Only a loopback address can use `http`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `admin_api_key`   | string, sensitive | `HOPBOX_ADMIN_API_KEY`   | An admin API key, `hbxadm_...` ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/)). The provider sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `control_url`     | string            | `HOPBOX_CONTROL_URL`     | The URL of the internal listener of the control role on its peer address, such as `https://203.0.113.10:7443`. A new server that is not the first one enrolls there, as `channel.control_urls` ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). It must be an `https` URL. Not with `control_urls`. Leave both out to take the control URLs from the install.                                          |
| `control_urls`    | list of strings   | none                     | The URLs of the internal listeners of the control servers, such as `["https://203.0.113.10:7443", "https://203.0.113.13:7443"]`. A new server that is not the first one enrolls at the first one that answers, and keeps its control channel to one of them. Each URL must be an `https` URL. Not with `control_url`: both fail with `Two control URL settings` and the detail `Set control_urls or control_url, not both.` |
| `ssh_jump_host`   | object            | none                     | An edge server as the jump host of the provider ([Jump host](#jump-host)). Every SSH step of a server that is not an edge server goes through it. The table below lists its attributes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

The object `ssh_jump_host` has these attributes:

| Attribute  | Type   | Default        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------- | ------ | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `address`  | string | none, required | The address of the jump host, as a host or `host:port`, such as `203.0.113.11`. The port defaults to 22.                                                                                       |
| `user`     | string | none           | The login user on the jump host, such as `debian`. Without it, the provider tries `root`, then `debian`.                                                                                       |
| `host_key` | string | none, required | The SSH host key of the jump host, in the `authorized_keys` format. Copy the `ssh_host_key` of the `hopbox_server` of the edge server. The provider never trusts a jump host on its first use. |

The servers that are not the first one need `install_url` and `admin_api_key`. A `hopbox_pool` and a `hopbox_size` need them too. The first server needs none of them: the provider reaches its admin API over SSH. The admin API is public behind the edge role, so `install_url` can be `https://<domain>` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#where-the-admin-api-is-served)).

A server that is not the first one enrolls at the control URLs of `control_urls` or `control_url`. Without them, the provider takes the URLs from the install: the `internal_url` of each live control process of `ListControlProcesses` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#listcontrolprocesses)). It keeps only a URL whose address is a peer address, where the other servers reach it ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#peer-addresses)). A listener on loopback serves only its own server. A first server from before peer addresses listens on loopback until its update moves the listener ([The internal listener](#the-internal-listener)). That update can run in the same apply, so the create of a new server waits up to 5 minutes for a listener on a peer address. Then it fails with `a server that is not the first one enrolls at the internal listener of a control server on its peer address, and the install lists none`.

## Resource hopbox_server

A `hopbox_server` is one server of an install, on a host that the operator set up ([The host](#the-host)). In the example, the paths name the release files in the folder of the configuration. A build from a checkout uses `bin/bundle/hopbox-v0.2.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz` and `hostkernel-build/linux-image-6.18.57-hopbox1_6.18.57-1_amd64.deb` instead.

```hcl
resource "hopbox_server" "first" {
  address      = "203.0.113.10"
  ssh_host_key = "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIFirst..."
  bootstrap    = true
  domain       = "example.com"
  labels       = { zone = "zone1" }


  bundle = {
    source = "hopbox-v0.2.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
    sha256 = "3f6a...c1d2"
  }
  host_kernel = {
    source = "linux-image-6.18.57-hopbox1_6.18.57-1_amd64.deb"
    sha256 = "9b1e...77aa"
  }


  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}


output "admin_api_key" {
  value     = hopbox_server.first.admin_api_key
  sensitive = true
}
```

Servers of a fleet, beside the first server. The edge server holds a floating address, the control server shares the control store, and the node joins the pool `big`:

```hcl
resource "hopbox_server" "edge2" {
  address            = "203.0.113.11"
  ssh_host_key       = "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIEdge2..."
  roles              = ["edge", "dns"]
  floating_addresses = ["198.51.100.6"]


  bundle      = local.bundle
  host_kernel = local.host_kernel


  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}


resource "hopbox_server" "cp2" {
  address      = "203.0.113.13"
  ssh_host_key = "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAICp2..."
  roles        = ["control", "node"]


  copy_control_from = {
    address  = hopbox_server.first.address
    host_key = hopbox_server.first.ssh_host_key
    user     = hopbox_server.first.ssh_user
  }


  bundle      = local.bundle
  host_kernel = local.host_kernel
}


resource "hopbox_server" "node1" {
  address      = "203.0.113.21"
  ssh_host_key = "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAINode1..."
  pool         = hopbox_pool.big.name


  bundle      = local.bundle
  host_kernel = local.host_kernel
}
```

`prevent_destroy` makes Terraform refuse each plan that destroys the first server, whose destroy ends the install. The provider also refuses a plan that replaces the first server ([Update](#update)).

### Arguments

| Attribute            | Type           | Default                                                                | Change                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `address`            | string         | none, required                                                         | replaces                                | The peer address of the server: one public IPv4 address on its uplink, with no NAT, such as `203.0.113.12` ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#peer-addresses)). The other servers reach the server there, and the provider logs in there, port 22. A private, loopback, link-local, shared, or multicast address fails with `Invalid address`, as does an address in the mesh range or the machine ranges. A change replaces the server. The plan refuses a change of the first server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `ssh_host_key`       | string         | none, required                                                         | refused                                 | The SSH host key of the server, in the `authorized_keys` format, such as `ssh-ed25519 AAAA...`. Copy it from the console of the provider of the server (plan question Q95). The provider pins it before its first login, and refuses any other key ([Host key trust](#host-key-trust)). A comment after the key changes nothing. A plan with another key fails with `The SSH host key of a server cannot change`, unless it replaces the server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `ssh_user`           | string         | `root`                                                                 | in place, changes nothing on the server | The login user of the provider: `root`, or a user with `sudo` without a password, such as `debian` on ks. When it is not `root`, each script runs with `sudo -n`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `bootstrap`          | bool           | `false`                                                                | replaces                                | True for the first server of a new install. It starts with the roles `control`, `node`, `dns`, and `edge`. It needs `domain`, and the provider makes the first admin API key for it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `domain`             | string         | none                                                                   | in place                                | The domain of the install, such as `example.com` ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#install-domain)). Only the first server takes it, and it needs it. A change runs `hopboxd admin config set --domain` on the server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `pool`               | string         | `default`                                                              | replaces                                | The pool that the server joins: `default`, or the name of a pool, such as `hopbox_pool.big.name` ([Resource hopbox_pool](#resource-hopbox_pool)). It must be a lowercase DNS label. The first server joins `default`. A server whose hardware differs from the first server of its pool fails to enroll ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#hardware-of-a-pool)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `labels`             | map of string  | `{}`                                                                   | in place                                | The labels of the server, such as `zone = "zone1"`. Placement filters use them. The rules of `channel.labels` apply ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). A server has at most 64 labels. A key has 1 to 63 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, and `-`, and starts with a letter. A value has at most 255 bytes. The provider sets them with `SetServerLabels`, so the install ignores the labels of the bootstrap config of the server ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setserverlabels)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `roles`              | list of string | `["control", "node", "dns", "edge"]` with `bootstrap`, else `["node"]` | updates in place                        | The roles of the server, in any order. The first server starts with every role, so leave it out at its create. Another server has one or more of `control`, `node`, `dns`, and `edge`, each once. `dns` needs `edge`, because the DNS role runs on the edge servers. `control` needs another role too, such as `["control", "node"]`, so that the server enrolls and the registry knows it ([Control servers](#control-servers)). A plan that drops `edge`, `dns`, or `node` from a running server removes the role in place, also on the first server. A plan that adds `node` back to a server whose node role a removal took adds it in place ([Roles of a running server](#roles-of-a-running-server)). The role `control` never goes. A refresh reads the roles that the server has: `control` from its bootstrap config or the state, and the others from the registry of the install.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `copy_control_from`  | object         | none                                                                   | in place, changes nothing               | The live control server whose keys and external Postgres a new control server copies before its install, with its pinned host key. A control server that is not the first one needs it, and no other server takes it. Only the create reads it. See [Control servers](#control-servers).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `floating_addresses` | set of string  | none                                                                   | in place                                | The floating IPv4 addresses of an edge server, such as `["198.51.100.6"]` (rule 4). Each one is one public IPv4 address that the operator routes to the server at its provider. Only a server with the role `edge` takes them, and the peer address of the server is none of them. A change puts the new addresses on the uplink of the server, and removes the old ones. See [Edge servers and floating addresses](#edge-servers-and-floating-addresses).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `public_ipv6`        | string         | none                                                                   | refused                                 | The floating IPv6 address of an edge server, without a prefix length, such as `2001:db8::12` ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#the-public-ipv6-address)). The operator routes it to the server at its provider. The network setup of the provider puts it on the uplink of the server as a `/128` ([The network setup of an edge server](#the-network-setup-of-an-edge-server)). The provider writes it to `edge.public_ipv6` of the bootstrap config. On a server with the DNS role, it adds port 53 of the address to `dns.listen` ([Create](#create)). The zone names it in its AAAA records. The IPv6 egress of the machines never leaves from it. Only a server with the role `edge` takes it. The rules of `edge.public_ipv6` apply ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). Give each edge server its own address: a second resource with the same address fails the plan with `two hopbox_server resources have the public IPv6 address <address>`. The plan refuses a change in place with `The public IPv6 address of a server cannot change`. A replacement with the same value takes the same address. See [Edge servers and floating addresses](#edge-servers-and-floating-addresses). |
| `bundle`             | object         | none, required                                                         | in place                                | The release bundle that the server runs ([Release bundle](/reference/release-bundle/)), with `source` and `sha256`. A change of `sha256` upgrades `hopboxd` on the server. A change of `source` alone changes nothing on the server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `bundle.source`      | string         | none, required                                                         |                                         | A local path, or an `https` URL that the server downloads with `curl`. The file name must be `hopbox-<version>-linux-amd64.tar.gz`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `bundle.sha256`      | string         | none, required                                                         |                                         | The sha256 of the bundle, in 64 lowercase hex digits, from the `.sha256` file of `make bundle`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `host_kernel`        | object         | none, required                                                         | in place                                | The Debian package of the tested host kernel, `linux-image-6.18.57-hopbox1_6.18.57-1_amd64.deb` from `build/hostkernel/build.sh` ([Host kernel](/reference/host-kernel/)), with `source` and `sha256` as for `bundle`. The provider installs it only on a server that does not run the tested kernel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

### Attributes the provider sets

| Attribute       | Type              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`            | string            | The peer address of the server, as `address`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `server_id`     | string            | The ID of the server in the install, a UUID.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `admin_api_key` | string, sensitive | Only on the first server: the first admin API key of the install, `hbxadm_` and 43 characters. The provider makes it and passes only its SHA-256 to the install ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#the-bootstrap-admin-api-key)). The state holds its only copy. The install registers it with the name `bootstrap` and a lifetime of 90 days.                     |
| `version`       | string            | The version of `hopboxd` on the server, such as `v0.1.0`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `internal_url`  | string            | On a control server, the URL of its internal listener on its peer address, such as `https://203.0.113.10:7443` ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/)). The other servers enroll there. A refresh reads it from the live control process of the server. Null on a server without the role `control`. See [The internal listener](#the-internal-listener). |

### The host

The operator orders each host at its provider and sets it up, before the create of its `hopbox_server` (plan questions Q95 and Q98):

* Debian 13 on `amd64`, with KVM.
* The peer address on its own uplink, with no NAT in front of it. An edge server also holds its floating addresses at the provider.
