| An instance admin cancels the drain ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#canceldrain)).                      | The delete fails with `the drain of the server <id> ended before its decommission, and the server is <state>. Run terraform destroy again`. The server stays in the install and in the Terraform state. The provider never cancels a drain itself. |
| The server is not decommissioned after 6 h.                                                                    | The delete fails with `the server <id> did not leave the install within 6h0m0s: ... The drain goes on in the install. Run terraform destroy again: it waits for the drain, then stops hopboxd on the server`.                                      |
| A read of the server fails with `unauthenticated` or `permission_denied`, such as for a revoked admin API key. | The delete fails at once with that error. No wait fixes it.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| The SSH connection to the first server breaks during the wait.                                                 | The delete logs in again and goes on waiting.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

After a failed delete, the server stays in the Terraform state, `hopboxd` keeps running on it, and the server stays `draining` and cordoned. The drain goes on in the install, and can decommission the server before the next destroy. So the resource records the drain in its private state, and a refresh keeps the resource while that record exists, also once the server is `decommissioned` or unknown to its install. The refresh gives the warning `An earlier terraform destroy of the server <id> did not finish, and the install decommissioned the server since. Finish the removal with terraform destroy, or remove the resource from the Terraform files and apply: ... To set the server up again instead, run terraform apply -replace=<address of the resource>, whose destroy does the same first.` The next destroy finds the server decommissioned, starts no drain, and goes on with step 4: it stops `hopboxd` and removes the secrets of the install. A destroy that succeeds drops the record. A stranded machine keeps its disk on the server. Fix each reason, such as a node with room for the machine, and run `terraform destroy` again. The next delete starts the drain again, and the drain tries each stranded machine again ([Drain a node](/guide/drain-a-node/#fix-a-stranded-machine)).

Each server goes out through the admin API when the provider block has `install_url` and `admin_api_key`, the first server too. If the provider cannot log in to the server, the drain and the decommission still happen, and the delete fails as step 4 says, so the next destroy stops `hopboxd`. Without the admin API, the first server goes out through `hopboxd admin` over SSH, so it needs SSH with the pinned host key for each step.

The host stays with its provider, and its disks stay as they are (plan question Q43). A destroy never ends a rental. End it at the provider. To use the host again, create a `hopbox_server` for it: the destroy removed the identity of the server, so the host takes a new create ([Create](#create)).

### Read

A create can fail before the enrollment. Its state then has no `server_id`. The refresh keeps such a state as it is, so Terraform can destroy the server and create it again.

Otherwise the refresh reads the server from the install. It uses SSH on the first server and the admin API on the others. It sets `labels`, `pool`, and `version` from the install. On the first server, it also sets `domain` from `hopboxd admin config get`. So the plan shows a real change of the domain. It keeps `roles` as the configuration orders them, when the server has the same roles. On a control server, it sets `internal_url` from the live control process of the server. On an edge server with `floating_addresses`, it logs in to the server and keeps only the addresses that the server holds on a network interface. The refresh changes nothing on the server. If the install does not answer, the refresh keeps the state as it was, with a warning.

The install can lose a server that is not the first one, or decommission it. The refresh then removes that server from the state, unless a failed destroy started its drain ([Drain of a server](#drain-of-a-server)). Then the resource stays, and the next destroy finishes the removal. The first server never leaves the state this way, because a new create would make a new install on it. So the refresh fails with `the first server <id> is decommissioned or unknown to its install, but Terraform did not destroy it`. To make a new install on it, run `terraform state rm` on the resource, remove the install from the host, and apply.

### Import

```sh
terraform import hopbox_server.node1 203.0.113.21
```

The import takes the peer address of the server alone (plan question Q96). The refresh after it logs in at that address with `ssh_private_key` as `root`, then as `debian`, through the jump host when the provider block has one. It reads the release in `/opt/hopbox/current`, the roles, and `edge.public_ipv6` of `/etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml`, and the server ID from the certificate of the server. It reads `edge.public_ipv6` only when the value has no prefix length. The address of the IPv6 block of a release before N29 reads as none, as `hopboxd` ignores it. It reads only the certificate, never the private key. A server with the role `control` and the bundled Postgres cluster of the first install, `/var/lib/hopbox/pg/data/PG_VERSION`, imports with `bootstrap = true`, and the refresh reads its `domain` from the install. Another control server never makes that cluster, so it imports without `bootstrap`.

The import checks the server before it keeps it:

* The server holds the address on a network interface. Otherwise the import fails with `the server at <address> holds no address <address> on a network interface, ...`.
* The install knows the server, through the admin API at `install_url`, or over SSH on a first server without it. A server of another install fails with `the install knows no server <id>, the server at <address>, so it belongs to another install`.
* The install records the address as the peer address of the server. Another address fails with `the install knows the server <id> with the peer address <peer address>, not <address>. Import it by its peer address`. A first server without a peer address imports, and its next update sets it. Another server without a peer address fails with `the install knows the server <id> at <address> without a peer address, so the import cannot tell it by its address`. Such a server enrolled before peer addresses (plan milestone N26). Set its peer address with `hopboxd admin server set-peer-address` on a control server ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-server-set-peer-address)), and import it again.

The import has no pinned host key yet, so it keeps the key that the server shows at this login, with the login user. It asks the server for its ed25519 key first. That is the key of `/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub`, which the guide copies from the console ([Install hopbox on your servers with Terraform](/guide/install-with-terraform/#1-set-up-the-hosts)). The next plan compares that key with `ssh_host_key`, and fails with `The SSH host key of a server cannot change` when they differ, before any change of the server. Make sure that the key in the console of the provider of the server is the key of `ssh_host_key`.

An import cannot recover `bundle`, `host_kernel`, or `admin_api_key`. The next plan shows an update of `bundle` from your Terraform files. If the file name of the bundle names the version that the server runs, the apply does not upgrade. The state of an imported first server has no `admin_api_key`.

### Host key trust

The provider never trusts a server on its first use (plan question Q95). The operator copies the SSH host key of each host from the console of its provider into `ssh_host_key`, and the provider pins that key before its first login. A server that shows another key fails each step with `remote: the host key of the server is not the pinned one`, and the create changes nothing on it. It asks the server for the key type of the pin.

The jump host has its own pin, `ssh_jump_host.host_key`, from the start. To read the files of a live control server for a new control server ([Control servers](#control-servers)), the provider pins the host key of `copy_control_from`. The provider then checks the fingerprint of each key file against the admin API, which runs over TLS, before it writes anything. So a machine that plays the control server at its address cannot plant its own keys, or a Postgres that would accept them, on the new server.

An import is the one login without a pin. The plan after it refuses a key other than `ssh_host_key` ([Import](#import)).

### A state of an earlier release

The provider of phase 1 named each server by the OVHcloud API, with a state of schema version 0. This release names a host by its peer address, with schema version 1. The first refresh with this release moves a state of version 0 to version 1, with no change on the server, as for ks:

| Attribute of version 1                                                                                                                                        | Value from the state of version 0                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`, `address`                                                                                                                                               | The `ipv4` of the old state, the public IPv4 address of the server. A state without `ipv4`, or with an address that cannot be a peer address, fails the upgrade, and says to import the server by its peer address. |
| `ssh_host_key`                                                                                                                                                | The pinned host key of the old state. A state without one fails the upgrade.                                                                                                                                        |
| `ssh_user`                                                                                                                                                    | The login user of the old state, such as `debian` with `sudo` on ks.                                                                                                                                                |
| `server_id`, `admin_api_key`, `version`, `pool`, `labels`, `roles`, `bootstrap`, `domain`, `bundle`, `host_kernel`, `floating_addresses`, `copy_control_from` | The same values.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `public_ipv6`                                                                                                                                                 | The same floating IPv6 address. The address of the IPv6 block of a release before N29, with its prefix length, becomes null, as `hopboxd` ignores it.                                                               |
| `internal_url`                                                                                                                                                | Null. The refresh reads it from the server.                                                                                                                                                                         |

The attributes of OVHcloud and of the vRack go, with the order of a server, and so does `public_ipv6_gateway`. The private state keeps the cordon of the provider and the record of a drain. Before the first plan, give the resource `address`, `ssh_host_key`, and `ssh_user` with the values of the state, so the plan changes nothing that the server keeps. On a first server from before peer addresses, the plan then shows the move of its internal listener ([The internal listener](#the-internal-listener)). The guide for ks shows the steps for ks.

### Timeouts

| Step                                                                               | Limit                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| The login after the reboot into the host kernel                                    | 30 minutes, tried every 10 s                      |
| The reboot into the host kernel                                                    | 20 minutes                                        |
| The wait after the make of an enrollment token, for the set `registered`           | 3 s                                               |
| A listener on a peer address, for the create of a server that is not the first one | 5 minutes, polled every 2 s                       |
| `ready` after the install                                                          | 5 minutes, polled every 2 s                       |
| `ready` on the new version after an upgrade                                        | 5 minutes, polled every 2 s                       |
| The wait of the first upgrade of an apply for the others                           | 3 s                                               |
| The proof that another control server runs, at the destroy of a control server     | about 6 s, the renewal period of 5 s and 1 s more |
| The decommission by a drain                                                        | 6 hours, polled every 10 s                        |

Nothing changed on the server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `read the servers of the install for their peer addresses: ...`                                                                                                                                                                            | The admin API did not answer the list of the servers. Nothing changed on the server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `the install records the peer address <peer address> for the first server <id>, not its address <address>. ...`                                                                                                                            | The `address` of the first server differs from the peer address in its install.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `the hopboxd of the server <id> runs no internal listener on a peer address: its version names no feature peer-address. ...`                                                                                                               | The move of the listener on a release from before N28. Upgrade the server first.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `move the internal listener to <address>:7443: ...`                                                                                                                                                                                        | `hopboxd install --internal-listen` failed on the server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `the server <id> runs <release> and holds <n> machines. The install of the host kernel reboots it, so delete the machines first`                                                                                                           | A change of `host_kernel` on a server with machines that does not run the tested kernel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `the first server <id> is decommissioned or unknown to its install, but Terraform did not destroy it. ...`                                                                                                                                 | Someone decommissioned the first server outside Terraform. A `terraform destroy` can also decommission the server and then lose the answer. Then the next destroy fails on this error at its refresh. Run `terraform destroy -refresh=false` to finish the destroy, or `terraform state rm` on the resource.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `log in to the first server to decommission it: remote: the host key of the server is not the pinned one: ... run terraform state rm on the resource`                                                                                      | A delete of a first server that someone reinstalled outside Terraform. Its install is gone.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `The server keeps its host firewall` with `the server <id> keeps its host firewall, because ...`                                                                                                                                           | A delete of a server without the role `edge` whose stop of `hopboxd` or removal of the table failed. Fix the cause, and run `terraform destroy` again.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `the install knows no server <id>, the server at <address>, so it belongs to another install`                                                                                                                                              | An import of a server of another install.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `the install knows the server <id> with the peer address <peer address>, not <address>. Import it by its peer address`                                                                                                                     | An import by an address that is not the peer address of the server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `The state of the server cannot move to this release`                                                                                                                                                                                      | A state of version 0 without `ipv4` or without a pinned host key. Run `terraform state rm` on the resource, and import the server by its peer address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `/var/lib/hopbox-provider is not a dir of root with mode 0700. Remove it`                                                                                                                                                                  | Another user made the work dir of the provider.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

A failed script on the server gives `the script exited with status <n>:` and the end of its error output. A connection that breaks during a script gives `remote: the connection broke: ...`. The provider resumes an upload after it ([Uploads](#uploads)), and fails every other step.

## Resource hopbox_pool

A `hopbox_pool` is one pool of servers of an install ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#poolservice)). All servers of a pool have identical hardware. The first server that enrolls into the pool records its hardware, and a new server with other hardware fails to enroll ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#hardware-of-a-pool)). So give each server model its own pool. A `hopbox_server` joins the pool with `pool = hopbox_pool.<name>.name`, which also makes Terraform create the pool first.

```hcl
resource "hopbox_pool" "big" {
  name = "big"
}
```

The resource calls the admin API at `install_url` with `admin_api_key` ([Provider block](#provider-block)). So it needs both, as a server that is not the first one does. The first server joins the pool `default`, because no other pool exists before it. A plan that gives the first server another pool fails.

| Attribute | Type   | Default             | Change   | Description                                                                  |
| --------- | ------ | ------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`    | string | none, required      | replaces | The name of the pool, a lowercase DNS label. No other live pool can have it. |
| `id`      | string | set by the provider |          | The ID of the pool, a UUID.                                                  |

The create calls `CreatePool` with a new idempotency key. The delete calls `DeletePool`. The install refuses the delete of a pool that holds a server that is not decommissioned, or that a live size names, so destroy the servers and the sizes of the pool first. Terraform orders the destroys that way for the servers and the sizes that name the pool by `hopbox_pool.<name>.name`. A delete of a pool that is gone already succeeds.

A refresh calls `GetPool`. A pool that is gone leaves the state, so the next apply creates it again. A pool of the same name with another ID also leaves the state, after someone deleted the pool and created it again outside Terraform. The next create then fails with `already_exists`, so import that pool instead. A state of an earlier release with `ovh_plan` loses the attribute at the next refresh, and nothing changes in the install. Import a pool by its name:

```sh
terraform import hopbox_pool.big big
```

## Resource hopbox_size

A `hopbox_size` is one size of machine of an install ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#sizeservice)). A user picks a size for a new machine, never a pool. The pool and the labels of the size are the placement filters of its machines ([Placement](/reference/placement/#hard-filters)).

```hcl
resource "hopbox_size" "large" {
  name       = "large"
  vcpus      = 8
  memory_gib = 32
  disk_gb    = 200
  pool       = hopbox_pool.big.name
  labels     = { disk = "nvme" }
}
```

The resource needs `install_url` and `admin_api_key`, as `hopbox_pool` does.

| Attribute    | Type          | Default             | Change   | Description                                                                                                 |
| ------------ | ------------- | ------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`       | string        | none, required      | replaces | The name of the size, a lowercase DNS label. No other size can have it, also no retired one.                |
| `vcpus`      | number        | none, required      | refused  | The count of vCPUs, 1 to 32.                                                                                |
| `memory_gib` | number        | none, required      | refused  | The RAM, in GiB.                                                                                            |
| `disk_gb`    | number        | none, required      | refused  | The size of the sparse disk, in GB.                                                                         |
| `pool`       | string        | `""`                | refused  | The pool of the machines of the size, such as `hopbox_pool.big.name`. Leave it out for any pool.            |
| `labels`     | map of string | `{}`                | refused  | The labels that a node must have to take a machine of the size. The rules of the labels of a server apply.  |
| `id`         | string        | set by the provider |          | The name of the size.                                                                                       |
| `retired`    | bool          | set by the provider |          | `true` once the size takes no new machine, for example after `hopboxd admin size retire` outside Terraform. |

A size never changes ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#sizeservice)). A destroy retires the size: it takes no new machine, its machines keep it, and its name stays taken. So a replace that keeps the name cannot work. The plan refuses a change of `vcpus`, `memory_gib`, `disk_gb`, `pool`, or `labels` that keeps `name`, with `A size never changes`. To change a size, give it a new name too. Terraform then retires the old size, and creates the new one.

The create calls `CreateSize` with a new idempotency key. The delete calls `RetireSize`. A delete of a size that is gone already succeeds. A refresh calls `GetSize`. A size that is gone leaves the state. A size whose RAM is not a whole number of GiB, or whose disk is not a whole number of GB, fails the refresh, because the resource cannot show it. Import a size by its name:

```sh
terraform import hopbox_size.large large
```

### Errors of hopbox_pool and hopbox_size

| Error                                                                                                                                                     | Cause                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `hopbox_pool and hopbox_size need the admin API: set install_url and admin_api_key in the provider block, or HOPBOX_INSTALL_URL and HOPBOX_ADMIN_API_KEY` | The provider has no admin API.                                                       |
| `invalid name: the pool name ...`                                                                                                                         | A `name` of a pool that is not a lowercase DNS label.                                |
| `vcpus must be from 1 to 32, not <n>`, `memory_gib must be from 1 to <max>, not <n>`, `disk_gb must be from 1 to <max>, not <n>`                          | A size out of bounds.                                                                |
| `invalid label: ...`                                                                                                                                      | A label of a size that breaks a rule.                                                |
| `The size <name> keeps its name after its retirement, so a replace with the same name fails. ...`                                                         | A change of a size that keeps its name.                                              |
| `The first server of an install (bootstrap = true) joins the pool default, because the install has no other pool before it.`                              | A first server with another `pool`.                                                  |
| `the admin API: already_exists: ...`                                                                                                                      | A pool or a size of the same name exists already. Import it, or pick another name.   |
| `the admin API: failed_precondition: ...`                                                                                                                 | The install refuses the delete of a pool that holds servers or that live sizes name. |

## Commands of the binary

Terraform starts the binary without arguments. So `serve` is the default command.

```sh
terraform-provider-hopbox [serve] [--debug]
terraform-provider-hopbox version [--json]
```

| Command   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `serve`   | Serves the provider to Terraform over the plugin protocol. It is the default command. When a person starts it outside Terraform, it prints a note that the binary is a plugin, and exits with status 1. |
| `version` | Prints the version of the provider. See [the version command](/reference/version/).                                                                                                                     |

### Flags of serve

| Flag           | Type | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------- | ---- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--debug`      | bool | `false` | Serves the provider in debug mode, for a Go debugger such as `dlv`. The provider prints a `TF_REATTACH_PROVIDERS` value. Set that value in the environment of Terraform, and Terraform then uses the running provider. |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | Prints the help and exits.                                                                                                                                                                                             |

Example:

```sh
terraform-provider-hopbox --debug
```

The provider reports the version from the `version` command to Terraform.

## Exit status

| Status | Meaning                                                                |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0      | The command succeeded.                                                 |
| 1      | The command failed, or `serve` ran outside Terraform.                  |
| 80     | The command line is not valid, for example an unknown command or flag. |

# TypeScript SDK

> The TypeScript SDK @hopbox/sdk for Node.js and browsers: its options, retries, idempotency keys, typed errors, credentials, exec, file copy, and tests.

`@hopbox/sdk` in `web/packages/sdk` is the TypeScript SDK of the public API `hopbox.v1`. It runs in Node.js and in a browser. It is the generated code of protoc-gen-es plus a small hand-written facade. The facade follows the rules of the Go client ([Go client](/reference/go-client/)): retries with backoff, idempotency keys on create calls, typed errors, and the bearer credential of the caller. The console uses it. [Call the API from TypeScript](/guide/typescript-sdk/) shows a script that uses it.

The SDK never holds the admin API. `buf.gen.yaml` keeps `hopbox.admin.v1` out of its generated code ([API definitions](/reference/api-definitions/#generators-and-outputs)).

## Package

| Item                 | Value                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name                 | `@hopbox/sdk`                                                                                                                                                             |
| Folder               | `web/packages/sdk`                                                                                                                                                        |
| Published            | No. The package is `private`. The owner decides on the npm scope `@hopbox` before a release to npm (plan item 13). The console takes the package from the pnpm workspace. |
| Module format        | ES modules only (`"type": "module"`)                                                                                                                                      |
| Node.js              | 24 or later, the version that CI tests                                                                                                                                    |
| Runtime dependencies | `@bufbuild/protobuf` 2.16.0, `@connectrpc/connect` 2.2.0, `@connectrpc/connect-node` 2.2.0, `@connectrpc/connect-web` 2.2.0, all pinned to an exact version               |
| Build output         | `dist/`, which git ignores. Build it with `corepack pnpm --filter @hopbox/sdk build`.                                                                                     |

### Entry points

| Import           | Condition | File              | What it holds                                                                                                  |
| ---------------- | --------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@hopbox/sdk`    | `browser` | `dist/browser.js` | `createClient` for a browser, and every export of the facade                                                   |
| `@hopbox/sdk`    | `node`    | `dist/node.js`    | `createClient` for Node.js, and every export of the facade                                                     |
| `@hopbox/sdk`    | `default` | `dist/browser.js` | the same as `browser`                                                                                          |
| `@hopbox/sdk/v1` | none      | `dist/v1.js`      | every generated message, enum, service, and schema of `hopbox.v1`, such as `MachineState` and `MachineService` |

Node.js picks the `node` condition, and a bundler for the browser, such as Vite, picks `browser`. Both entry points export the same names with the same types: the names on this page. A test checks it.

| Runtime | Unary calls and server streams                                                                                            | `Exec`                                                          | `Upload`                                    |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Node.js | Connect protocol, binary protobuf, over HTTP/2. Plain `http://` to a loopback install starts HTTP/2 with prior knowledge. | the bidi stream `Exec` over HTTP/2 by default, or the WebSocket | yes                                         |
| Browser | Connect protocol, binary protobuf, `POST` requests over `fetch`                                                           | the WebSocket `/api/ws/exec` only                               | no. A browser cannot stream a request body. |

The browser client passes the check of the session cookie ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#calls-with-the-cookie)). Each call is a Connect `POST` request with `Connect-Protocol-Version: 1`, and the browser adds the `Origin` header itself. The client never uses a Connect `GET` request.

## Make a client

```ts
import { bearerToken, createClient, NotFoundError } from "@hopbox/sdk";


const hb = createClient({
  url: "https://example.com",
  credentials: bearerToken(process.env.HOPBOX_API_KEY ?? ""),
});
try {
  const { machine } = await hb.machines.getMachine({ machine: { case: "name", value: "box1" } });
  console.log(machine?.state);
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof NotFoundError) {
    console.log("no machine box1");
  }
} finally {
  hb.close();
}
```

`createClient(options)` checks `options.url` with `parseURL` and returns a `HopboxClient`. A bad URL throws a `BadURLError`. A browser client with `execTransport: "stream"` throws an `Error`.

| `ClientOptions` field | Type                        | Default                                                                                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`                 | string                      | required                                                                                     | The URL of the install, such as `https://example.com` ([Install URLs](#install-urls)).                                                                                                                                                                |
| `credentials`         | `Credentials`               | none                                                                                         | Gives the bearer token of each call ([Credentials](#credentials)). Without it, the calls carry no `Authorization` header. The console leaves it out, so the session cookie of the browser authenticates each call. The device flow leaves it out too. |
| `userAgent`           | string                      | `hopbox-ts-client (<platform>/<arch>)` in Node.js, such as `hopbox-ts-client (darwin/arm64)` | The `User-Agent` header of each call. A browser sends its own and ignores this field.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `attemptTimeoutMs`    | number                      | `DEFAULT_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS`, 90000                                                          | The deadline of one try of a unary call, in milliseconds. The server gives a call 30 s, and a lifecycle call of a machine 60 s.                                                                                                                       |
| `maxRetryAfterMs`     | number                      | none, no cap                                                                                 | The longest `Retry-After` that the client waits for, in milliseconds. A longer one ends the call with its error, and `retryAfterMs` of the error holds the wanted wait. Without it, the client waits as long as the server asks, up to 24 hours.      |
| `logger`              | `Logger`                    | no logs                                                                                      | Gets a record for each retry ([Retries](#retries)). `console` works.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `execTransport`       | `"stream"` or `"websocket"` | `"stream"` in Node.js, `"websocket"` in a browser                                            | How `exec` reaches the machine ([Exec](#exec)).                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `fetch`               | `typeof fetch`              | `globalThis.fetch`                                                                           | The `fetch` function of a browser client. Node.js ignores it.                                                                                                                                                                                         |

`Logger` has two methods, `debug(message, fields)` and `warn(message, fields)`.

### `HopboxClient`

| Field or method                 | Type                            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `baseUrl`                       | string                          | The URL of the install, as `parseURL` returned it.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `transport`                     | `Transport`                     | The Connect transport of the client, with steps 2 to 5 of [The steps of a call](#the-steps-of-a-call). A tool such as connect-query takes it, so its calls get the same retries, keys, and credential ([The transport](#the-transport)). |
| `install`                       | `Client<typeof InstallService>` | `GetInstallInfo` ([the API server](/reference/api/#installservice))                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `auth`                          | `Client<typeof AuthService>`    | sign-in links, the device flow, and CLI tokens ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/))                                                                                                                             |
| `account`                       | `Client<typeof AccountService>` | the account of the caller ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/))                                                                                                                                                  |
| `audit`                         | `Client<typeof AuditService>`   | the audit log ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/))                                                                                                                                                              |
| `orgs`                          | `Client<typeof OrgService>`     | orgs, members, and invitations ([the org API](/reference/org-api/))                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `apiKeys`                       | `Client<typeof APIKeyService>`  | API keys ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/))                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `sshKeys`                       | `Client<typeof SSHKeyService>`  | SSH keys ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/))                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `machines`                      | `Client<typeof MachineService>` | machines, their lifecycle, and the access calls ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/))                                                                                                                                             |
| `vars`                          | `Client<typeof VarService>`     | env vars and secrets ([the env var API](/reference/vars-api/))                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `exec(start, options?)`         | `ExecSession`                   | Runs a command in a running machine ([Exec](#exec)).                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `upload(start, data, options?)` | `Promise<UploadResponse>`       | Writes a file, or a tar stream into a directory, in a running machine ([Upload](#upload)). Node.js only.                                                                                                                                 |
| `download(request, options?)`   | `Promise<Download>`             | Reads a file, or a directory as a tar stream, from a running machine ([Download](#download)).                                                                                                                                            |
| `close()`                       | `void`                          | Ends the HTTP/2 connection of a Node.js client. A later call opens a new one. In a browser, it does nothing.                                                                                                                             |

Each service field is the generated Connect client of that service, `Client<S>` of `@connectrpc/connect`. A method takes the request message as a plain object, and an optional `CallOptions` of Connect: `timeoutMs`, `headers`, `signal`, `onHeader`, `onTrailer`, and `contextValues`. A unary method returns a `Promise` of the response message. A server stream, such as `watchMachines` or `streamMachineLogs`, returns an `AsyncIterable` of messages. Each method name is the name of the RPC with a small first letter, such as `listMachines` for `ListMachines`.

`timeoutMs` and an `AbortSignal.timeout()` in `signal` both end a call in time. Only `timeoutMs` also sends the deadline to the server in the header `Connect-Timeout-Ms`, so the server stops its work too. A unary call without `timeoutMs` has no deadline of its own. Then each try has the deadline `attemptTimeoutMs`. The helpers `exec`, `upload`, and `download` set no deadline, because a stream can run for hours.

### The transport

`transport` is the Connect transport under the service fields. Its calls get the user agent, the idempotency keys, the retries, and the credential. They do not get the typed errors, because that step wraps the service fields. So a call through the transport throws the `ConnectError` of `@connectrpc/connect`. The console gives it to connect-query:

```tsx
import { TransportProvider } from "@connectrpc/connect-query";


<TransportProvider transport={hb.transport}>{children}</TransportProvider>
```

The transport already retries a call ([Retries](#retries)). So set `retry: false` in the options of TanStack Query, or the query tries each call up to 3 times more on top:

```ts
const queryClient = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false }, mutations: { retry: false } } });
```

## Install URLs

`parseURL(raw)` returns the base URL of an install, such as `https://example.com`. It follows `ParseURL` of the Go client:

* A bare domain gets `https://`.
* The host is in lower case, and a `/` at the end goes. A default port goes too.
* `http://` works only for a loopback host: `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, or `[::1]`.
* A path, a query, a fragment, a user name, or a password throws a `BadURLError`.

The message of a `BadURLError` hides the user info of the URL. It shows `xxxxx` in place of all text between `://` and the last `@`, such as `https://xxxxx@example.com`. A password with a `/` or a `?` in it stays hidden too. A URL without an `@` shows as it is.

## The steps of a call

Each unary call passes these steps in order:

1. **Typed errors.** The error of the call becomes a `HopboxError` ([Errors](#errors)).
2. **User agent.** The step sets `User-Agent`, in Node.js only.
3. **Idempotency key.** See [Idempotency keys](#idempotency-keys).
4. **Retries.** See [Retries](#retries). The steps after this one run again on each try.
5. **Credential.** See [Credentials](#credentials).

A stream gets the steps 1, 2, and 5, without retries. The typed errors also cover each message of a stream.

## Idempotency keys

A method with the option `(hopbox.v1.idempotent)` needs an `Idempotency-Key` header ([the API server](/reference/api/#idempotency-keys)). Today these are `CreateMachine`, `CreateOrg`, `CreateAPIKey`, and `AddSSHKey`. The client puts a new UUIDv7 in the header of each such call that has no key yet. The step runs before the retries, so each try of one call sends the same key. A key that the caller sets in `CallOptions.headers` stays:

```ts
await hb.machines.createMachine({ name: "box1" }, { headers: { "Idempotency-Key": "deploy-42" } });
```

A replay of a known key returns the first result. Its response has the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, which `onHeader` can read.

## Retries

The client tries a unary call at most 3 times: the first try and `MAX_RETRIES`, 2, retries.

| Code of the failed try | Retried                                                |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `unavailable`          | Only for a call that is safe to run again.             |
| `resource_exhausted`   | Only for a call that is safe to run again.             |
| `deadline_exceeded`    | Only for a call that is safe to run again.             |
| Any other code         | No. An auth error or a bad request never gets a retry. |

A call is safe to run again in these cases, as for the Go client ([Go client](/reference/go-client/#retries)):

| Case                                     | How the client knows it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| The call only reads.                     | Its method has the option `(hopbox.v1.read_only)`, or `idempotency_level` `NO_SIDE_EFFECTS` or `IDEMPOTENT` ([API definitions](/reference/api-definitions/#hopboxv1read_only)). Examples are `listOrgs` and `getMachine`.                                                                                          |
| The call carries an idempotency key.     | Its method has the option `(hopbox.v1.idempotent)`, such as `createMachine` ([Idempotency keys](#idempotency-keys)).                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| The try surely did not reach the server. | The answer of the try has the header `NOT_RUN_HEADER`, `Hopbox-Not-Run`, with the value `1` ([the API server](/reference/api/#answers-of-calls-that-changed-nothing)). In Node.js, the try also counts when it got no connection: the cause of its error has the code `ECONNREFUSED`, `ENOTFOUND`, or `EAI_AGAIN`. |

Each other call changes state and has no key, such as `createInvitation`. The client does not retry it after a lost answer, because the server can have run it. A second run can then act twice, for example with a second invitation. The check holds for each try. A refusal with `Hopbox-Not-Run` on the first try, then a lost answer on the second try, ends the call with the error of the second try.

A network error fails a call with `unavailable`. In a browser, `fetch` then rejects with a `TypeError`, both for a connection that never opened and for a lost answer. So a browser client retries a change without a key only after an answer with `Hopbox-Not-Run`. A read call and a call with a key get their retries in both runtimes. A timeout of the connection, `ETIMEDOUT` in Node.js, can come after the request went out, so it does not count as a try that did not reach the server.

The wait before a retry has full jitter: a random time from 0 up to 500 ms before the first retry, and up to 1 s before the second (`BACKOFF_MS`). If the error has a `Retry-After` header, the client waits that time instead. The client reads the header as the Go client does. It takes a count of seconds that fits in a signed 64-bit number, such as `5` or `+5`. It also takes an HTTP date in one of the three forms of RFC 9110: `Wed, 21 Oct 2026 12:00:10 GMT`, `Wednesday, 21-Oct-26 12:00:10 GMT`, or `Wed Oct 21 12:00:10 2026`. Any other value counts as no header. The client reads at most `MAX_RETRY_AFTER_HEADER_MS`, 24 hours, from either form. The client calls `logger.debug("retrying a call", fields)` before each retry. A wait of `LONG_WAIT_MS`, 10 s, or more calls `logger.warn` instead. `fields` has `procedure`, `code`, `retry`, and `waitMs`. `code` is the name of the code, such as `unavailable`.

The client does not retry in these cases:

* `maxRetryAfterMs` is set, and `Retry-After` is longer.
* The wait ends after the deadline of the call, from `timeoutMs`.
* The `signal` of the call aborts.

Each try has its own deadline. It is `attemptTimeoutMs`, or the rest of the deadline of the call, whichever ends first. The client sends it in the header `Connect-Timeout-Ms`. A try that runs out of time fails with `deadline_exceeded`, and the table above applies.

## Errors

Each error of a call is a `HopboxError`, or one of its subclasses. The errors of the SDK itself, `SignedOutError` and `BadURLError`, stay as they are.

| `HopboxError` field | Type        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`              | `Code`      | The Connect code, such as `Code.NotFound`. The SDK exports `Code`.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `codeName`          | string      | The name of the code, such as `not_found`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `message`           | string      | `<code name>: <message of the server>`, such as `not_found: not found: no machine has the name "box9"`.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `rawMessage`        | string      | The message of the server, without the code.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `procedure`         | string      | The call, such as `/hopbox.v1.MachineService/GetMachine`. For the WebSocket of exec, it is `/api/ws/exec`.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `requestId`         | string      | The `Hopbox-Request-Id` of the response ([the API server](/reference/api/#the-chain-of-a-call)). For a call that did not reach the server, it is empty. For an error of the WebSocket, it is empty too, because a browser cannot read the headers of a WebSocket. |
| `retryAfterMs`      | number      | The `Retry-After` of the response in milliseconds, or 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `details`           | `Message[]` | The typed details of the error, decoded with the messages of `hopbox.v1`, such as a `MachineNameTaken` with `$typeName` `hopbox.v1.MachineNameTaken`. A detail of an unknown type is left out.                                                                    |
| `cause`             | unknown     | The `ConnectError` of `@connectrpc/connect`, or undefined.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

`instanceof` tells the kinds apart. The codes are those of [the API server](/reference/api/#errors).

| Class                     | Code                  |
| ------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `CanceledError`           | `canceled`            |
| `UnknownError`            | `unknown`             |
| `InvalidArgumentError`    | `invalid_argument`    |
| `DeadlineExceededError`   | `deadline_exceeded`   |
| `NotFoundError`           | `not_found`           |
| `AlreadyExistsError`      | `already_exists`      |
| `PermissionDeniedError`   | `permission_denied`   |
| `ResourceExhaustedError`  | `resource_exhausted`  |
| `FailedPreconditionError` | `failed_precondition` |
| `AbortedError`            | `aborted`             |
| `UnimplementedError`      | `unimplemented`       |
| `InternalError`           | `internal`            |
| `UnavailableError`        | `unavailable`         |
| `UnauthenticatedError`    | `unauthenticated`     |

Another code, such as `out_of_range` or `data_loss`, gives a plain `HopboxError`. hopboxd sends neither.

| Other error      | Meaning                                                                          |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SignedOutError` | The credential has no token, for example `bearerToken("")`. No request goes out. |
| `BadURLError`    | `parseURL` or `createClient` refused the URL.                                    |

The SDK makes some errors itself:

| Error                                                                                                 | When                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `UnknownError`, `the exec ended without its exit chunk`                                               | An exec ended with no `exit` chunk.                                                                                                          |
| `UnknownError`, `the download did not start with its info`                                            | The first message of a download held no `info`.                                                                                              |
| `UnknownError`, `the WebSocket of exec sent a text message`                                           | The WebSocket sent a text message. The client then closes the socket.                                                                        |
| `FailedPreconditionError`, `the exec ended, so it takes no more input`                                | A write to an exec after its end.                                                                                                            |
| `CanceledError`, `the exec was canceled`                                                              | `cancel()`, a `break` out of the `for await` loop, or an abort of the `signal` of `ExecOptions`. This holds also before the WebSocket opens. |
| `ResourceExhaustedError`, `the reader of the exec fell more than 16777216 bytes behind the WebSocket` | More than 16 MiB of output of the WebSocket waits for the reader. The client then closes the socket.                                         |
| `UnimplementedError`, `a browser cannot stream an upload. ...`                                        | `upload` in a browser.                                                                                                                       |

## Credentials

```ts
interface Credentials {
  token(signal: AbortSignal): string | Promise<string>;
  rejected?(token: string): boolean | Promise<boolean>;
}
```

The client puts the token of `credentials` in the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` of each try, and of each stream. If `token` throws, the call fails with that error, and no request goes out.

Sometimes the server refuses the token of a unary call with `unauthenticated`, and the credential has `rejected`. Then the client calls `rejected` with the token. If `rejected` returns true, the client gets a token again. If the new token differs, the client sends the call once more with it. If getting the token throws a `SignedOutError`, the call fails with that error. A credential with `rejected` fits a token that a program renews, such as a CLI access token. A stream gets no second try.

`bearerToken(token)` is a token that never changes, such as an API key in the form `hbx_<key>` ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/)). An empty token throws a `SignedOutError`.

The SDK does not refresh CLI tokens. The hopbox CLI keeps them in its own files ([hopbox CLI](/reference/cli/#files)).

## Machine names

A request names a machine in the oneof field `machine`, with `id` or `name` ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#naming-a-machine)). Two helpers make the value of the field:

| Function       | Returns                         |
| -------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `byName(name)` | `{ case: "name", value: name }` |
| `byId(id)`     | `{ case: "id", value: id }`     |

```ts
await hb.machines.stopMachine({ machine: byName("box1") });
```

## Exec

`exec(start, options?)` runs a command in a running machine, with an optional terminal. `start` is an `ExecStart` as a plain object ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#exec)): `machine`, `argv`, `env`, `user`, `dir`, `tty`, `size`, `term`, and `timeout`. The session starts at once and returns an `ExecSession`.

| Transport     | Used by                                                          | Credential                                                                                | Wire                                                                                                                           |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `"stream"`    | Node.js, by default                                              | the `Authorization` header                                                                | the bidi stream `/hopbox.v1.MachineService/Exec` over HTTP/2                                                                   |
| `"websocket"` | a browser, always, and Node.js with `execTransport: "websocket"` | the session cookie in a browser. In Node.js, the `Authorization` header of `credentials`. | `GET /api/ws/exec`, one `ExecChunk` in each binary message ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#the-websocket-endpoint)) |

A browser cannot add a header to a WebSocket. So in a browser, the WebSocket carries only the session cookie, also with `credentials` set. The page must have the origin of the install.

| `ExecOptions` field | Type                                                 | Description                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stdin`             | `Uint8Array`, string, or `AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>` | Input for the command. The session sends it, then the end of the input. Without it, send input with `write` and `closeStdin`. |
| `signal`            | `AbortSignal`                                        | An abort of this signal ends the exec and the command, as `cancel()` does.                                                    |

| `ExecSession` member       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `write(data)`              | Sends input, a `Uint8Array` or a string in UTF-8. The session splits it into `stdin` chunks of at most 256 KiB (`MAX_STDIN_CHUNK`). The promise resolves after the transport took the input. |
| `closeStdin()`             | Sends `stdin_eof`. With a terminal, the command reads Ctrl-D.                                                                                                                                |
| `resize(rows, cols)`       | Sends a new terminal size.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `sendSignal(name)`         | Sends a signal, such as `SIGINT`, to the process group of the command.                                                                                                                       |
| `cancel()`                 | Ends the exec and the command. A read then throws a `CanceledError`.                                                                                                                         |
| `output()`                 | Reads the whole output, and returns `{ stdout, stderr, exit }`. `stdout` and `stderr` are `Uint8Array`. `exit` is the `ExecExit`: `code`, `signal`, `error`, and `timedOut`.                 |
| `[Symbol.asyncIterator]()` | Reads the output one `ExecEvent` at a time, with `for await`.                                                                                                                                |

`ExecEvent` is one of these:

| `kind`     | Other field        | Description                                                             |
| ---------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"stdout"` | `data: Uint8Array` | Output of the command. With a terminal, all output arrives as `stdout`. |
| `"stderr"` | `data: Uint8Array` | Error output of the command.                                            |
| `"exit"`   | `exit: ExecExit`   | How the command ended. It is the last event.                            |

Read the output of a session once, with `for await` or with `output()`. A second read throws an `Error`. A `break` out of the `for await` loop cancels the exec, as `cancel()` does.

Only the stream transport has backpressure. Over the stream, the session reads the next message only after the reader took the last event. So a slow reader slows the command down ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#how-a-stream-ends)). If nobody reads the output, the command stops once the window is full. A WebSocket has no backpressure, so the session keeps the output that waits for the reader in memory. At most `MAX_WEBSOCKET_BACKLOG`, 16 MiB, can wait. Past that, the exec fails with a `ResourceExhaustedError`, and the session closes the socket. The reader gets the event that it waits for, then the error. The rest of the output that waited is lost.

A write waits until the transport takes the input. If the exec ends first, each waiting write rejects with a `FailedPreconditionError`.

A failed exec throws its `HopboxError` from the read, such as a `FailedPreconditionError` for a machine that does not run. The close of the WebSocket maps to an error like this:

| Close code                             | Result                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1000 after the `exit` chunk            | The read ends.                                                                                   |
| 1000 without the `exit` chunk          | `UnknownError`, `the exec ended without its exit chunk`                                          |
| 1001                                   | `UnavailableError` with the reason of the server                                                 |
| 4000 plus a Connect code, such as 4009 | The error class of that code, such as `FailedPreconditionError`, with the reason as `rawMessage` |
| any other code, such as 1006           | `UnavailableError`, `the WebSocket of exec closed with the code <code>`                          |

A browser reports a refused upgrade, such as HTTP status 403 for another origin, as the close code 1006.

After the `exit` chunk, both transports ignore an end that loses nothing. Over the stream, that is a reset of the stream or a cancel. Over the WebSocket, it is the close code 1000, 1005, or 1006. Any other error after the `exit` chunk still throws, such as the close code 4013 for `internal`.

## Upload

`upload(start, data, options?)` sends `start`, an `UploadStart` as a plain object ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#upload)), then `data` in messages of at most 256 KiB (`MAX_UPLOAD_CHUNK`). It returns the `UploadResponse`, whose `bytes` is a `bigint`.

`UploadData` is one of these: a `Uint8Array`, a string in UTF-8, a `Blob`, an `Iterable<Uint8Array>`, an `AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>`, or a `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>`. In Node.js, a file read stream of `node:fs` is an `AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>`.

```ts
import { createReadStream } from "node:fs";


const { bytes } = await hb.upload({ machine: byName("box1"), path: "app.tar", mode: 0o644 }, createReadStream("app.tar"));
```

## Download

`download(request, options?)` reads the first message, the `DownloadInfo`, and returns a `Download` ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#download)).

| `Download` member          | Description                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `info`                     | The `DownloadInfo`: `archive`, `mode`, and `size` as a `bigint`. |
| `bytes()`                  | Reads the rest of the data into one `Uint8Array`.                |
| `[Symbol.asyncIterator]()` | Reads the data in parts of at most 32 KiB, with `for await`.     |

Read the data once. A download to a laptop holds at most 4 MiB ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#limits)).

## Logs and other streams

The log of a machine and the watch of machines have no helper. Call the generated methods, which carry the credential and the typed errors:

```ts
const ctl = new AbortController();
for await (const res of hb.machines.streamMachineLogs({ machine: byName("box1"), tail: 20, follow: true }, { signal: ctl.signal })) {
  if (res.event.case === "entry") {
    process.stdout.write(new TextDecoder().decode(res.event.value.data) + "\n");
  }
}
```

To stop a stream, abort its `signal`, or leave the `for await` loop.

| `MAX_RETRY_AFTER_HEADER_MS`  | 86400000, 24 hours  |

| `RETRY_AFTER_HEADER`         | `Retry-After`       |
| `NOT_RUN_HEADER`             | `Hopbox-Not-Run`    |
| `WEBSOCKET_EXEC_PATH`        | `/api/ws/exec`      |
| `MAX_WEBSOCKET_BACKLOG`      | 16777216, 16 MiB    |
| `MAX_STDIN_CHUNK`            | 262144, 256 KiB     |
| `MAX_UPLOAD_CHUNK`           | 262144, 256 KiB     |

## Build and tests

The scripts of `web/packages/sdk/package.json`:

| Script      | What it does                                                                                      |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
