| `build`     | `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`, which writes `dist/` with the `.d.ts` files                         |
| `typecheck` | `tsc -p tsconfig.json`, over the code and the tests                                               |
| `test`      | `vitest run --project unit`                                                                       |
| `test:e2e`  | `vitest run --project e2e`. It needs the env of `TestTypeScriptSDK`, so run that Go test instead. |

`make test-sdk` runs the type check, the build, and the unit tests. Then it runs `TestTypeScriptSDK` of `internal/control` with `HOPBOX_TEST_SDK=1`. It needs `corepack pnpm install` first.

* The unit tests in `web/packages/sdk/test/*.test.ts` run the client against a fake Connect server over HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1. They check the retries, the waits, `Retry-After`, and the idempotency keys. The table of retries covers a read call, a call with a key, and `createInvitation`, after a lost answer, an error code, an answer with `Hopbox-Not-Run`, and a refused connection, in Node.js and in the browser client. They also check the typed errors, the credentials, and the user agent. Then they check exec over the stream and over a fake WebSocket, upload, download, and the browser client.
* `TestTypeScriptSDK` serves the real public API of a control role. Its node runs a machine `box1` with the real guest agent and the test VMM driver. The test makes an API key, then runs `test/e2e/sdk.test.ts` with vitest. The suite checks exec over the stream and over the WebSocket, and a terminal with a resize. It also checks upload, download, and the log. Then it checks an idempotent replay, the details of a taken name, and a call with the session cookie of the console. It runs exec over the WebSocket with the session cookie and the `Origin` of the console, and checks that another `Origin` is refused.

The test reads each file of the SDK and of its tests first. So `go test` runs it again after a change of the SDK, instead of a result from its cache. Without `web/packages/sdk/node_modules`, `TestTypeScriptSDK` skips, so `make test` passes without Node.js. With `HOPBOX_TEST_SDK` set, it fails instead.

| Env var                                                                                            | Description                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `HOPBOX_TEST_SDK`                                                                                  | Without the node_modules of the SDK, `TestTypeScriptSDK` fails instead of a skip.                                                                        |
| `HOPBOX_E2E_URL`, `HOPBOX_E2E_KEY`, `HOPBOX_E2E_COOKIE`, `HOPBOX_E2E_ORIGIN`, `HOPBOX_E2E_MACHINE` | The install, API key, session cookie, origin, and machine of the end-to-end suite. `TestTypeScriptSDK` sets them. Without them, the suite fails at once. |

# The env var API

> The env var and secret calls of the public API, VarService: scopes, who can set each one, the name rules and the reserved names, the limits, the env of a machine, sealing, and their audit entries.

The service `hopbox.v1.VarService` of the public API manages the env vars and secrets of an org. hopbox puts both into the machines of the org at boot and into every login shell. A user can read an env var back. A secret is sealed, and no call returns its value. The scope of each value says which machines it reaches.

[The API server](/reference/api/) covers the parts that every call shares: the request gate, the policy check, and the error codes. The generated reference is [Public API](/api/public/). The code is in `internal/service/vars.go`, `internal/api/handlers_vars.go`, and `internal/domain/envvar.go`. [Set env vars and secrets](/guide/env-vars/) runs the calls on a laptop.

| Call                      | What it does                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`SetVar`](#setvar)       | Sets an env var or a secret, and replaces the value with the same name and scope. |
| [`ListVars`](#listvars)   | Lists the values that the caller sees, without the values of the secrets.         |
| [`DeleteVar`](#deletevar) | Deletes an env var or a secret.                                                   |

The examples on this page use the shell function `browser` of [First sign-in on a new install](/guide/first-sign-in/#sign-in-with-the-link), with the session cookie of the caller, and `API=http://127.0.0.1:7080`.

## The org of a request

Each request has the field `org_id`, an optional string. Leave it out to act in the org of the API key, or else in the personal org of the caller ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#the-org-of-a-request)). The service layer reads the role of the caller in the org before the policy check. So an org that does not exist gets the same `permission_denied` as an org of others.

## Scopes

The enum `VarScope` holds the scope of a value ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#scopes-of-env-vars-and-secrets)).

| Value                   | Scope                                       | Reaches                                                 | Who sets it                      |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `VAR_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED` | `shared` in a request. Never in a response. |                                                         |                                  |
| `VAR_SCOPE_SHARED`      | `shared`                                    | The shared machines of the org.                         | org admins and org owners        |
| `VAR_SCOPE_PRIVATE`     | `private`                                   | The private machines of the account that set the value. | any member, for its own machines |
| `VAR_SCOPE_ALL`         | `all`                                       | Every machine of the org, shared or private.            | org admins and org owners        |

A value that is not in the enum gets `invalid_argument`, after the policy check.

These rules hold for the names in one org:

* A shared value or an all value belongs to the org. Its name has one scope. So a shared value and an all value never share a name. A set with the other scope fails with `already_exists`. Delete the value first to change its scope.
* A private value belongs to one account. Two members can each have a private value with the same name. A member can also have a private value with the name of an org value. In the private machines of the member, the private value wins ([Env of a machine](#env-of-a-machine)).
* A personal org has no shared machines. So a shared value in a personal org fails with `invalid_argument`. Use the scope `all` or `private` there.

## Who can call

| Caller                                           | `ListVars`                            | `SetVar` and `DeleteVar` of a shared or an all value | `SetVar` and `DeleteVar` of a private value |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `session`, `cli_token` of a member               | yes                                   | no                                                   | its own values                              |
| `session`, `cli_token` of an admin or an owner   | yes                                   | yes                                                  | its own values                              |
| `member_key`                                     | in the org of the key, as its account | in the org of the key, as its account                | in the org of the key, its own values       |
| `org_key`                                        | the shared and all values of its org  | no                                                   | no                                          |
| `admin_key`, `local_root`, `server`, `anonymous` | no                                    | no                                                   | no                                          |

Nobody sees, sets, or deletes the private values of another account, also not an org owner. The audit log, which org admins read, names a private value only by its ID ([Audit entries](#audit-entries)). An org key has the rights of a member without personal resources, so it has no private values ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#api-keys)). An instance admin cannot read secrets, so a session of an instance admin has only the rights of its org roles.

## Names and values

A name has 1 to 128 characters. Each character is a letter, a digit, or `_`, and the first character is not a digit. A POSIX shell takes such names. The rules match case, as the shell does. So `path` is a valid name.

No value of any scope takes these names. The guest agent or the login shell sets them, or they can make the shell or the dynamic loader run code. The guest agent checks these rules too. It leaves a value with such a name out of the machine, and logs it. So a wrong push of the control role cannot set it:

| Reserved                                                                     | Why                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `PATH`, `PWD`, `OLDPWD`, `SHLVL`, `TERM` | The guest agent or the login shell sets them ([Guest link](/reference/guest-link/#exec)).            |
| `ENV`, `PROMPT_COMMAND`, `PS0`, `PS1`, `PS2`, `PS4`, `SHELLOPTS`, `IFS`      | A shell runs code from them, or they change how it reads commands.                                   |
| `GCONV_PATH`                                                                 | glibc loads code from it.                                                                            |
| every name that starts with `LD_`                                            | The dynamic loader loads code from them, for example `LD_PRELOAD` and `LD_AUDIT`.                    |
| every name that starts with `BASH_`                                          | bash runs or loads code from them, for example `BASH_ENV`, `BASH_FUNC_*`, and `BASH_LOADABLES_PATH`. |
| every name that starts with `HOPBOX_`                                        | hopbox keeps these names for the values that it sets itself.                                         |

A shared or an all value comes from an org admin. An all value reaches the private machines of every member. So a shared or an all value also cannot take the names below. A program loads or runs code from them, or finds its code through them. A member can still set them as private values, for its own machines:

| Reserved for shared and all values                                                                                                                                    | Program                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `BASHOPTS`, `ZDOTDIR`, `FPATH`, `PS3`                                                                                                                                 | bash, zsh                                                    |
| `NODE_OPTIONS`, `NODE_PATH`                                                                                                                                           | Node.js                                                      |
| `PYTHONSTARTUP`, `PYTHONPATH`, `PYTHONHOME`, `PYTHONWARNINGS`, `PYTHONBREAKPOINT`                                                                                     | Python                                                       |
| `PERL5OPT`, `PERL5LIB`, `PERLLIB`, `PERL5DB`                                                                                                                          | Perl                                                         |
| `RUBYOPT`, `RUBYLIB`                                                                                                                                                  | Ruby                                                         |
| `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`, `_JAVA_OPTIONS`, `JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS`, `CLASSPATH`                                                                                                 | Java                                                         |
| `LUA_PATH`, `LUA_CPATH`, and every name that starts with `LUA_INIT`                                                                                                   | Lua                                                          |
| `DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS`, and every name that starts with `CORECLR_`                                                                                                    | .NET                                                         |
| `PHPRC`, `PHP_INI_SCAN_DIR`                                                                                                                                           | PHP                                                          |
| `GOFLAGS`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, `RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER`                                                                                                                 | Go, Rust                                                     |
| every name that starts with `npm_config_`, in any case, for example `NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX`                                                                               | npm. It reads these names in any case.                       |
| every name that starts with `GIT_`                                                                                                                                    | git, for example `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`                           |
| every name that starts with `SSH_`                                                                                                                                    | ssh and sshd, for example `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`                    |
| `PAGER`, `MANPAGER`, `EDITOR`, `VISUAL`, `BROWSER`, `LESS`, `LESSOPEN`, `LESSCLOSE`                                                                                   | Tools that start the program in the value.                   |
| `GLIBC_TUNABLES`, `GETCONF_DIR`, `HOSTALIASES`, `LOCALDOMAIN`, `LOCPATH`, `MALLOC_TRACE`, `NIS_PATH`, `NLSPATH`, `RESOLV_HOST_CONF`, `RES_OPTIONS`, `TMPDIR`, `TZDIR` | glibc. This is the set that glibc drops for setuid programs. |

`LANG` and the `LC_*` names stay open for every scope.

These lists reduce the risk that an org admin runs code in the private machine of a member. They do not remove it. Any env var can change what a program does, and a program can read a name that no list holds. The members of an org trust its org admins and org owners. So the scope `private` does not protect a machine from the all values of its org.

A name is never sealed. It is in the table `env_vars`, in its backups, in `ListVars`, in logged errors, and in `/etc/hopbox/env`. So no value of any scope takes a name that looks like a credential. The check uses the patterns of the audit log ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#audit_log)), in `domain.LooksLikeCredential`. Examples are a name that starts with `hbx_` and a GitHub token, such as `ghp_` with 36 more characters. A name in the form of an AWS access key ID is another example. Put the credential in the value of a secret.

A value is valid UTF-8 without a NUL byte, at most 16 KiB (16384 bytes). It can be empty, and it can hold newlines and quotes.

## Limits

| Limit                                                                      | Value                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| Shared and all values in one org                                           | 100                    |
| Names and values of the shared and all values of one org, together         | 256 KiB (262144 bytes) |
| Private values of one account in one org                                   | 50                     |
| Names and values of the private values of one account in one org, together | 128 KiB (131072 bytes) |

A set that replaces a value counts the new value in place of the old one. So at the limit, a set that replaces a value works. A set over a limit fails with `resource_exhausted`. With these limits, the env of a machine stays below 384 KiB. Linux allows 2 MiB for the arguments and the env of one exec. The Go constants are `domain.MaxOrgEnvVars`, `MaxOrgEnvVarBytes`, `MaxPrivateEnvVars`, `MaxPrivateEnvVarBytes`, and `MaxEnvVarValueBytes`.

## Env of a machine

The env of a machine is the list of names and values that reach it, sorted by name:

| Machine           | Gets                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A shared machine  | the shared values and the all values of its org                                                                                          |
| A private machine | the all values of its org, and the private values of its creator in that org. A private value wins over an all value with the same name. |

A shared value never reaches a private machine, and a private value never reaches a shared machine. The private values of a member never reach the private machines of another member.

For example, an org has these values:

| Name           | Scope     | Owner | Value     |
| -------------- | --------- | ----- | --------- |
| `REGION`       | `all`     |       | `eu-west` |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `shared`  |       | a secret  |
| `LOG_LEVEL`    | `all`     |       | `info`    |
| `LOG_LEVEL`    | `private` | Ann   | `debug`   |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | `private` | Ann   | a secret  |

Then a shared machine gets `DATABASE_URL`, `LOG_LEVEL=info`, and `REGION=eu-west`. A private machine of Ann gets `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `LOG_LEVEL=debug`, and `REGION=eu-west`. A private machine of Bob gets `LOG_LEVEL=info` and `REGION=eu-west`.

The control role builds this list with the Go method `Service.ResolveEnv(ctx, MachineEnv)`. It opens each secret at that time. It also checks the name of each stored value again with the rules of its scope. A value that someone saved before a name joined the reserved lists thus never reaches a machine. `ResolveEnv` leaves such a value out. It logs `left a stored env var out of a machine, because its name no longer passes the rules` at level warn. The fields are `component=service`, `org`, `var`, `scope`, and `reason` (`invalid` or `reserved`). `var` is the ID of the value, not its name. No entry point of the API serves it. So it takes no caller, and the policy of the call that changed the machine has already run. `MachineEnv` has these fields:

| Field     | Type | Description                                                                                                                                           |
| --------- | ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Org`     | UUID | The org of the machine. It must not be the nil UUID.                                                                                                  |
| `Shared`  | bool | `true` for a machine that is shared with the org.                                                                                                     |
| `Creator` | UUID | The account that made the machine. A private machine needs it. A shared machine ignores it. A machine that an org key makes is shared from the start. |

The node sends the list to the guest agent as the field `env` of the guest-link configuration ([Guest link](/reference/guest-link/#configuration)). The guest agent writes it to `/etc/hopbox/env`, which every login shell reads. Exec and the start command get the same values ([hopbox-guest](/reference/hopbox-guest/)). The control role sends the env in the spec of each machine to its executor ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#machinespec)). A machine whose env does not resolve, for example without a key-encryption key, gets no spec while its target is `running`. A stop or a delete of it still goes on ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#a-machine-whose-env-does-not-resolve)).

A share or an unshare changes which values reach a machine. A private machine holds the private values of its creator, and the guest agent wrote them to the disk of the machine. So after `ShareMachine` and `UnshareMachine`, the control role resolves the env again. The executor then pushes it to the guest agent of a running machine ([the node executor](/reference/executor/#the-guest-link)). The guest agent then writes the new list in place of the old one. `SetVar` and `DeleteVar` do the same for each machine that the value reaches: they publish the event `machine.updated` for it, with the action `var.set` or `var.delete`. They lock those machine rows in the order of their IDs, add 1 to their version, and publish the events in their transaction. The new env does not remove a value from a copy that a program in the machine made already.

A private machine of a member of the org can thus get an all value that an org admin set. The [reserved names](#names-and-values) keep the known ways to run code out of the org values, such as `LD_PRELOAD`, `BASH_ENV`, and `NODE_OPTIONS`. They reduce the risk, and they do not remove it. Treat the scope `all` as a way to change what runs in the private machines of members.

A share fails closed: `ShareMachine` first resolves the env of the machine as a shared machine in its transaction. If that env does not resolve, the share fails with `failed_precondition`, and the machine stays private ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#sharemachine)).

## Messages

### Var

| Field                | Type       | Description                                                                              |
| -------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                 | string     | The UUID of the value. A set that replaces the value keeps it.                           |
| `org_id`             | string     | The UUID of the org of the value.                                                        |
| `name`               | string     | The name of the env var in the machine, for example `DATABASE_URL`.                      |
| `scope`              | `VarScope` | The scope of the value.                                                                  |
| `secret`             | bool       | `true` for a sealed value.                                                               |
| `value`              | string     | The value of an env var. Empty for a secret.                                             |
| `owner_account_id`   | string     | The UUID of the account of a private value. Empty for a shared or an all value.          |
| `updater_account_id` | string     | The UUID of the account that set the value last. Empty after the delete of that account. |
| `create_time`        | timestamp  | The time of the first set of the value.                                                  |
| `update_time`        | timestamp  | The time of the last set of the value.                                                   |

## Calls

### SetVar

Sets a value, and replaces the value with the same name and scope. A replace can turn an env var into a secret, or a secret into an env var. The value of a secret is sealed in the transaction of the call. A retry gives the same end state, so it needs no idempotency key. A retry still adds one to the version of the row, and writes an audit entry.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.VarService/SetVar`                                                                                                                                                         |
| Policy action     | `var.set`: a shared or an all value needs the role `admin` or `owner`. A private value needs the role `member` or more, and the account of the caller as its owner.                    |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Audit entry       | action `var.set`, target kind `var`. The details are `scope`, `kind` (`env_var` or `secret`), and `replaced` (`true` or `false`). A shared or an all value also has the detail `name`. |

| Field of `SetVarRequest` | Type            | Default                                     | Description                                                                           |
| ------------------------ | --------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `org_id`                 | optional string | the org of the API key, or the personal org | The UUID of the org.                                                                  |
| `name`                   | string          | required                                    | The name, as in [Names and values](#names-and-values).                                |
| `value`                  | string          | empty                                       | The value. The field is marked `debug_redact`, so a printed request does not show it. |
| `secret`                 | bool            | `false`                                     | Seals the value, so that no call returns it.                                          |
| `scope`                  | `VarScope`      | `shared`                                    | The scope.                                                                            |

The response `SetVarResponse` holds the value in `var`, without the value of a secret.

```sh
browser -d '{"name":"APP_ENV","value":"staging","scope":"VAR_SCOPE_ALL"}' $API/hopbox.v1.VarService/SetVar
```

```json
{"var":{"id":"01a14940-ce48-7a24-bc79-e34809e47653","orgId":"01a14940-b457-7ae9-a014-b1dd06363447","name":"APP_ENV","scope":"VAR_SCOPE_ALL","value":"staging","updaterAccountId":"01a14940-b457-7ae5-8232-30378b548d68","createTime":"2026-10-17T09:45:46.309819Z","updateTime":"2026-10-17T09:45:46.309819Z"}}
```

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Code                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| The caller cannot set this scope: `permission denied: a caller of kind session may not do var.set`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `permission_denied`   |
| An unknown scope: `invalid argument: the scope "<n>" is not shared, private, or all`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `invalid_argument`    |
| A bad name: `invalid argument: invalid env var: the name must hold only letters, digits, and underscores, and must not start with a digit`. The message never repeats a refused name. A name can be a pasted token. An empty name and a name of more than 128 characters get their own message.                                                | `invalid_argument`    |
| A reserved name: `invalid argument: reserved env var name: LD_PRELOAD. No name can start with LD_`, or `... reserved env var name: PATH. The guest agent or the shell sets it, or it can make the shell or the loader run code`                                                                                                                | `invalid_argument`    |
| A name that only a private value can take, in a shared or an all value: `invalid argument: reserved env var name: NODE_OPTIONS. A program can load or run code from it, so only a private value can take it`, or `... reserved env var name: GIT_SSH_COMMAND. No shared or all value can start with GIT_, so only a private value can take it` | `invalid_argument`    |
| A name that looks like a credential: `invalid argument: invalid env var: the name looks like a credential, and a name is never sealed. Put the credential in the value of a secret`                                                                                                                                                            | `invalid_argument`    |
| A bad value: `invalid argument: invalid env var: the value has <n> bytes, more than 16384`, `... the value is not valid UTF-8`, or `... the value holds a NUL byte`                                                                                                                                                                            | `invalid_argument`    |
| A shared value in a personal org: `invalid argument: a personal org has no shared machines, so a shared value reaches no machine. Use the scope all or private`                                                                                                                                                                                | `invalid_argument`    |
| The org has the name with the other org scope: `already exists: the org has a value REGION with the scope all. Set it with that scope, or delete it first`                                                                                                                                                                                     | `already_exists`      |
| A count limit: `usage limit exceeded: the shared and all values of an org are at most 100. Delete one first`, or `... the private values of an account in an org are at most 50. Delete one first`                                                                                                                                             | `resource_exhausted`  |
| A byte limit: `usage limit exceeded: the names and values of the shared and all values of an org hold at most 262144 bytes together, and this value would make <n>`                                                                                                                                                                            | `resource_exhausted`  |
| A suspended org: `failed precondition: org suspended: an instance admin suspended the org, so its env vars and secrets do not change until the suspension ends`                                                                                                                                                                                | `failed_precondition` |
| A secret on an install without a key-encryption key: `failed precondition: the keyring has no key-encryption key to seal or open the value. Run hopboxd admin kek rotate to make the first one`                                                                                                                                                | `failed_precondition` |

### ListVars

Lists the shared and all values of the org and the private values of the caller, sorted by name. A private value comes after the org value with the same name. The call returns the value of each env var, and no value of a secret.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.VarService/ListVars`                                                                         |
| Policy action     | `var.list`: a `session`, `cli_token`, or `member_key` with a role in the org, or an `org_key` of the org |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                       |
| Audit entry       | none                                                                                                     |

The request `ListVarsRequest` has the field `org_id`. The response `ListVarsResponse` holds the values in `vars`.

```sh
browser -d '{}' $API/hopbox.v1.VarService/ListVars
```

```json
{"vars":[{"id":"01a14940-ce48-7a24-bc79-e34809e47653","orgId":"01a14940-b457-7ae9-a014-b1dd06363447","name":"APP_ENV","scope":"VAR_SCOPE_ALL","value":"staging","updaterAccountId":"01a14940-b457-7ae5-8232-30378b548d68","createTime":"2026-10-17T09:45:46.309819Z","updateTime":"2026-10-17T09:45:46.309819Z"},{"id":"01a14940-ce58-776c-90ff-b6dd427564c2","orgId":"01a14940-b457-7ae9-a014-b1dd06363447","name":"GITHUB_TOKEN","scope":"VAR_SCOPE_PRIVATE","secret":true,"ownerAccountId":"01a14940-b457-7ae5-8232-30378b548d68","updaterAccountId":"01a14940-b457-7ae5-8232-30378b548d68","createTime":"2026-10-17T09:45:46.328096Z","updateTime":"2026-10-17T09:45:46.328096Z"}]}
```

The JSON leaves out the fields with their default value, such as `value` of a secret and `secret` of an env var.

### DeleteVar

Deletes one value. The rules of `SetVar` say who can delete it.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.VarService/DeleteVar`                                                                        |
| Policy action     | `var.delete`: as `var.set`                                                                               |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                       |
| Audit entry       | action `var.delete`, target kind `var`, details `scope`, `kind`, and `name` for a shared or an all value |

| Field of `DeleteVarRequest` | Type            | Default                                     | Description                                                              |
| --------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `org_id`                    | optional string | the org of the API key, or the personal org | The UUID of the org.                                                     |
| `name`                      | string          | required                                    | The name of the value.                                                   |
| `scope`                     | `VarScope`      | `shared`                                    | The scope of the value. A private value is always a value of the caller. |

The response `DeleteVarResponse` has no fields.

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Code                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| A name that no rule allows, with the message of `SetVar`. Examples are an empty name and a name that looks like a credential. A reserved name is allowed. A value can be older than the reservation of its name, and it can still go. | `invalid_argument`    |
| No value with this name and scope: `not found: the org has no value REGION with the scope all`                                                                                                                                        | `not_found`           |
| A suspended org, with the message of `SetVar`                                                                                                                                                                                         | `failed_precondition` |

## What a member leaves behind

A leave, a removal, and the delete of an account take the account out of an org. They also delete the private values of the account in that org. Each value gets a `var.delete` entry with the detail `reason` `owner left` and no name ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#what-a-member-leaves-behind)). The delete of an org deletes every value of the org.

## Suspension

While an instance admin suspends an org, its values do not change ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#suspension)). `SetVar` and `DeleteVar` fail with `failed_precondition`. `ListVars` still works.

## Sealing

A secret is sealed with the place `OrgSecret` of its org, scope, owner, and name ([Sealing](/reference/sealing/#places)). So a sealed value that someone copies into another row does not open there. The column `env_vars.sealed_value` is in the list of sealed columns, so `hopboxd admin kek rewrap` moves the secrets to the current key-encryption key ([Sealing](/reference/sealing/#rewrap)). The control store keeps the values in the table `env_vars` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#env_vars)).

## Audit entries

The calls write these entries in the transaction of the change. Their org is the org of the value, so the owners and admins of the org read them with `ListAuditEntries` ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/#listauditentries)). No entry holds a value. The entry of a private value also holds no name: the private values of a member are not for the org admins to see. Its target ID names the value. No new name looks like a credential. A name that someone stored before this rule never blocks a change of its value. The audit entry of that change then goes without the name.

| Action       | Call                                                                                   | Target    | Details                                                                                                           |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `var.set`    | `SetVar`                                                                               | the value | `scope`, `kind`, `replaced`, and `name` for a shared or an all value                                              |
| `var.delete` | `DeleteVar`, and the leave, removal, or account delete of the owner of a private value | the value | `scope`, `kind`, `name` for a shared or an all value, and `reason` `owner left` for a value of a member that left |

# The version command

> The version command of every hopbox binary, its output, and where its values come from.

Every hopbox binary has a `version` command: `hopboxd`, `hopbox`, `terraform-provider-hopbox`, and `hopbox-guest`. The command prints the build identity of the binary and exits.

## Usage

```sh
hopboxd version [--json]
hopbox version [--json]
terraform-provider-hopbox version [--json]
hopbox-guest version [--json]
```

## Flags

| Flag           | Type | Default | Description                                         |
| -------------- | ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json`       | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object instead of one line of text. |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | Prints the help of the command and exits.           |

## Text output

The text output is one line:

```text
<binary> <version> (commit <commit>, built <date>, <go> <os>/<arch>)
```

Example:

```sh
$ hopboxd version
hopboxd v0.1.0 (commit 1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b, built 2026-10-16T09:00:00Z, go1.27.1 linux/amd64)
```

If the binary has no commit or no date, the line leaves out that part.

## JSON output

The JSON output is one object on one line, with these fields:

| Field      | Type             | Always present | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------- | ---------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `binary`   | string           | yes            | The name of the binary, for example `hopboxd`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `version`  | string           | yes            | The version of the build. See [Where the values come from](#where-the-values-come-from).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `commit`   | string           | no             | The full hash of the git commit of the build.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `date`     | string           | no             | The time of that commit, in RFC 3339 format.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `go`       | string           | yes            | The Go version that built the binary, for example `go1.27.1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `os`       | string           | yes            | The operating system of the build, for example `linux`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `arch`     | string           | yes            | The CPU architecture of the build, for example `amd64`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `features` | array of strings | no             | The capabilities that a tool reads from the version. Only `hopboxd` has the field. `host-firewall` comes from the release with the host firewall on ([the host firewall](/reference/host-firewall/)). `egress` comes from the release with the egress tunnels on ([the egress of the machines](/reference/egress/)). `peer-address` comes from the release that runs the mesh and the control channel on the peer addresses ([the mesh](/reference/mesh/)). `floating-ipv6` comes from the release that takes `edge.public_ipv6` as a floating address, and translates the IPv6 egress to the uplink ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#the-public-ipv6-address)). `floating-addresses` comes from the release that takes `edge.floating_addresses`, and puts the floating addresses back on the uplink ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#the-check-of-the-uplink)). `remove-role` comes from the release that runs a server through the removal of one of its roles ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#removeserverroles)). `give-back` comes from the release whose executor answers the give-back of a failed move ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/#give-back)). Each heartbeat of `hopboxd` reports the list too ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#heartbeat)). The Terraform provider reads it after each move of a server to another release, and from the `hopboxd` of a bundle before its install. |

Example:

```sh
$ hopbox version --json
{"binary":"hopbox","version":"v0.1.0","commit":"1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b","date":"2026-10-16T09:00:00Z","go":"go1.27.1","os":"darwin","arch":"arm64"}
```

## Where the values come from

`make build` sets the version, the commit, and the date at link time:

* `version` comes from `go run ./tools/gitversion`. It is always a semver version, so versions sort in commit order. The rules are in the next section.
* `commit` is the full hash of `HEAD`.
* `date` is the commit time of `HEAD`, not the time of the build. So two builds of the same commit print the same date.

A binary from `go build` or `go install` gets the values from the build information that the Go toolchain writes into the binary. The version is then the module version, for example `v0.0.0-20261016090000-1a2b3c4d5e6f+dirty`. When the toolchain gives no version, as with `go run`, the version is `v0.0.0-0.unknown`, and the commit and the date are absent. This version sorts below every other version.

## Version format

The version follows the rules of Go module pseudo-versions. Only tags that match `v[0-9]*` count. The time is the commit time of `HEAD` in UTC, as `yyyymmddhhmmss`. The hash is the first 12 characters of the commit hash.

| State of the checkout                              | Version                        | Example                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `HEAD` has the tag `vX.Y.Z`                        | `vX.Y.Z`                       | `v0.1.0`                                    |
| `HEAD` is after the release tag `vX.Y.Z`           | `vX.Y.(Z+1)-0.<time>-<hash>`   | `v0.1.1-0.20261017101112-1a2b3c4d5e6f`      |
| `HEAD` is after the pre-release tag `vX.Y.Z-<pre>` | `vX.Y.Z-<pre>.0.<time>-<hash>` | `v0.2.0-rc.1.0.20261017101112-1a2b3c4d5e6f` |
| The history has no `v*` tag                        | `v0.0.0-<time>-<hash>`         | `v0.0.0-20261016090807-1a2b3c4d5e6f`        |

If a tracked file holds changes that are not committed, the version ends in `+dirty`, for example `v0.1.0+dirty`. Files that git does not track do not count.

A version after a tag sorts above that tag and below the next patch release. For example, `v0.1.0` < `v0.1.1-0.20261017101112-1a2b3c4d5e6f` < `v0.1.1`.

If the nearest tag is not a full semver version, such as `v1.2` or `v1.2.3+build`, `make build` fails. In a shallow clone, `make build` also fails, because the nearest tag is unknown. Run `git fetch --unshallow --tags` first. Outside a git checkout, `make build` also fails. In these cases, you can set the version yourself:

```sh
make build VERSION=v0.1.0
```

# The VMM driver interface

> The VMM driver interface of the executor, its capabilities, its drivers, and the test driver.

The VMM driver is the layer between the executor of a machine and the VMM that runs its microVM. The executor is the only code that calls a driver ([the node executor](/reference/executor/)). Placement and the API never call a driver. Each driver declares its capabilities. For a feature that the driver does not declare, the executor does nothing. The code is in `internal/node/vmm`.

This release has two drivers. The Firecracker driver of `internal/node/vmm/firecracker` runs the machines of a node ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/)). The test driver of `internal/node/vmm/vmmtest` lives in a test package and never ships.

## Capabilities

`Driver.Capabilities()` returns the capabilities of a driver. A driver can always boot, stop, attach to, and delete a machine.

| Capability | Go value          | What it allows                              | Interface         |
| ---------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| pause      | `vmm.CapPause`    | standby: the microVM pauses in RAM          | none yet          |
| snapshot   | `vmm.CapSnapshot` | hibernate: the memory goes to a memory file | `vmm.Snapshotter` |
| restore    | `vmm.CapRestore`  | wake: a boot from the memory file           | `vmm.Restorer`    |
| fork       | `vmm.CapFork`     | a new microVM from the state of another     | none yet          |
| migrate    | `vmm.CapMigrate`  | a move of a microVM to another node         | none yet          |

The Firecracker driver of phase 1 declares none.

## Driver

A driver runs the microVMs of one node. Its microVMs run apart from `hopboxd`, so they survive a restart and an upgrade of `hopboxd`. The executor of a machine calls the driver for that machine one call at a time. Calls for different machines can run at once.

| Method                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Name()`              | The name of the driver in logs, such as `firecracker`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Capabilities()`      | The capabilities of the driver.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `SnapshotFormat(ctx)` | The format version of the snapshots that the VMM writes, such as `v12.0.0`. The compatibility class of the node holds it ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#compatibility-class)). Each saved memory state records it. The test driver returns `vmmtest-1`.                                            |
| `LinkSocket(id)`      | The unix socket of the guest link of the machine: its path, its mode, and its owner. It is the same for each boot of the machine ([Guest link](/reference/guest-link/#transport)). The Firecracker driver keeps the socket in the jail of the machine. So before it listens, the executor makes the dir of the socket. |
| `Inspect(ctx, id)`    | What the node holds of the machine, as a `Status`. A machine that the node never saw has the zero `Status`.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `Boot(ctx, Boot)`     | Boots a machine that does not run. For a machine without a disk, it makes the disk from the image first. It returns once the microVM runs, before the guest booted. On an error, no microVM of the machine runs. After a failed boot, the executor asks `Inspect` again before its next action.                        |
| `Attach(ctx, id)`     | Returns the microVM of a machine that runs, for example after a restart of `hopboxd`. It fails with `vmm.ErrNotRunning` for a machine that does not run.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `Delete(ctx, id)`     | Removes the disk, the memory file, and every other file of a machine that does not run. A machine without files succeeds.                                                                                                                                                                                              |

| `Status` field | Description                                                   |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Disk`         | The disk of the machine exists.                               |
| `Running`      | The microVM runs.                                             |
| `Memory`       | A memory file of a hibernate is kept. Only `Delete` drops it. |

`Boot` holds the `Machine` and the link key of the boot:

| Field                               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ID`                                | The ID of the machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `VCPUs`, `MemoryBytes`, `DiskBytes` | The size of the machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `Image`                             | The image: its digest, its URL, and the SHA-256 of its kernel and of its disk ([the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/#machinespec)).                                                                                                                            |
| `Address`                           | The IPv4 address of the machine on its node, from the network of the spec, or the zero `netip.Addr` for a machine without one. A driver with a network device for each machine connects the device to the node network with it ([the node network](/reference/node-network/)). |
| `LinkKey`                           | The link key of this boot, 32 random bytes. The driver puts it in the metadata service of the microVM, never on the kernel command line.                                                                                                                                       |

## Instance

`Boot`, `Attach`, and `Restore` return an `Instance`: one running microVM.

| Method                 | Description                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Done()`               | A channel that closes once the microVM stopped, for any reason.                                                                                                        |
| `Exit()`               | Why the microVM stopped, once `Done` closed.                                                                                                                           |
| `Stop(ctx)`            | Stops the microVM, and returns once `Done` closed. The driver first asks the guest to shut down. At the end of `ctx`, it ends the microVM. A stopped microVM succeeds. |
| `SetLinkKey(ctx, key)` | Puts a new link key in the metadata service. The executor calls it after an attach, because the key of a boot lives only in memory.                                    |

| Exit reason | Go value           | Meaning                                                                                    |
| ----------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `stopped`   | `vmm.ExitStopped`  | The end of `Stop`.                                                                         |
| `shutdown`  | `vmm.ExitShutdown` | A shutdown or a reboot from inside the machine.                                            |
| `crash`     | `vmm.ExitCrash`    | An end that nobody asked for, such as a crash of the VMM. `Exit.Err` says what went wrong. |
| `snapshot`  | `vmm.ExitSnapshot` | The end of `Snapshot`. The memory is in the memory file.                                   |

## Snapshotter and Restorer

| Interface         | Method                | Description                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vmm.Snapshotter` | `Snapshot(ctx, inst)` | Saves the memory and the state of a running microVM to the memory file of the machine, and stops the microVM.                                                              |
| `vmm.Restorer`    | `Restore(ctx, Boot)`  | Boots a machine from its memory file, with a new link key. A failure keeps the memory file, and leaves no microVM of the machine running. A success drops the memory file. |

## Mover

A driver that keeps the disk of each machine in one file is a `vmm.Mover`. A cold move copies that file to another node ([Cold move](/reference/cold-move/)). A node whose driver is not a `Mover` takes part in no move.

| Interface   | Method         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vmm.Mover` | `DiskPath(id)` | The path of the disk file of a machine. The file exists from the first boot of the machine until `Delete`. A boot keeps a disk that it finds there, such as a pulled one. `Delete` also removes the partial copy of a pull beside the file. |

## The test driver

`vmmtest.New(dir, logger, capabilities...)` returns a driver for tests. Its microVM is the real guest agent of `internal/guest`, run in the test process. It connects to the guest link socket over a unix socket. So an executor goes through the same steps as on a real node, without KVM. Its microVMs live as long as the driver, so they outlive the `Manager` that booted them. This is how a microVM outlives `hopboxd`.

| Method                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Crash(id)`, `Shutdown(id)`           | Ends the running microVM of a machine as a crash, or as a shutdown from inside.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `FailBoots(err)`, `FailWakes(err)`    | Makes each boot or wake fail with `err`, until the next call with nil.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `SetDelay(d)`                         | Makes each call wait `d` before it acts. A call whose context ends during the wait fails with the cause of the end. A stop then kills the microVM.                                                                                                       |
| `Ops()`                               | The calls so far, in order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Overlaps()`                          | Each call that ran while another call of the same machine ran. An executor must never cause one.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Guarded(id, pgid)`                   | Whether a watchdog of the running microVM of a machine guards the process group `pgid` (see below).                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Boots(id)`, `Status(id)`, `Root(id)` | How many times a machine booted, what the driver holds of it, and the dir of the `/etc` of its guest.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `DiskPath(id)`                        | The disk file of a machine, `<dir>/disks/<id>/disk.raw`: a sparse file of the disk size that the first boot makes, at least 1 MiB. The guest agent of the driver never writes to it, so a test of a cold move writes its data. `Delete` removes its dir. |
| `Close()`                             | Ends every microVM, at the end of a test.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

The guest agent starts each command, exec or start command, in a process group of its own. So a Ctrl-C in the terminal does not reach the command. A killed test binary also skips `Close()`.

To keep such commands from running on, the driver starts a watchdog for each command (`internal/watchdog`). A watchdog is a `/bin/sh` that waits on a pipe whose write end only the test binary holds. When the test binary dies, for any reason, the kernel closes that end, and the watchdog sends `SIGKILL` to the process group of the command. On macOS, a child that a process of the group forks during the kill can miss the signal. So the watchdog sends `SIGKILL` to the group again every 0.1 s while the group exists, for 2 s at most. A `SIGKILL` to the `go` command alone does not end the test binary. So the watchdog fires at the end of the test binary. At the latest, `-test.timeout` ends it.

After a command exits, its background children stay in its process group. So the driver keeps the watchdog until the process group is empty, or until the microVM stops. A real stop ends each process of the microVM. So when the microVM stops, the driver sends `SIGKILL` to each process group that it still keeps, and stops its watchdog. As the watchdog does, the driver sends `SIGKILL` to a group again every 0.1 s while the group exists, for 2 s at most. Both take this rule from the same constants of `internal/watchdog`, and the driver calls `watchdog.KillGroups`.

The guest agent reports each command to the driver through `guest.Options.Started`. A real guest leaves that option empty. The agent reports a command after the command starts. So a test binary that dies before the driver starts the watchdog leaves the command running. The test `TestGuestCommandsEndWithTheTestProcess` in `internal/node/executor` kills a test binary with `SIGKILL` after `Guarded` reports the group of the command. It checks that the start command of its machine and the children of that command exit within 5 s. It also checks this for a child that outlives its start command, and for an exec of `yes`.

The dir of the driver must have a short path. A unix socket path has at most 104 bytes on macOS.

# hopbox v0.1.0

> The release notes of v0.1.0, the pre-release at the end of phase 1: what it delivers by area, its known limits, the upgrade, and the acceptance on the dev install.

v0.1.0 is the first pre-release of hopbox. It ends phase 1, the foundation on one server. Each phase ends with a tagged pre-release, and version 1.0 is the end of phase 5.

The release has one server bundle for `linux/amd64`, the hopbox CLI, the hopbox Terraform provider, and the tested host kernel package `linux-image-6.18.57-hopbox1_6.18.57-1_amd64.deb`. At the adoption of a server, the provider installs that package ([Host kernel](/reference/host-kernel/)). The release files are not public yet. The hopbox team gives them on request.

## What phase 1 delivers

Phase 1 runs every role of hopbox on one server. The dev install, which is the preview install at <https://dev.hopbox.dev>, ran this release at its acceptance ([Try hopbox](/guide/quickstart/)). The sections below follow the parts of phase 1.

### Identity and sign-in

* A person signs in with GitHub, with Google, or with a magic link by email ([Sign in with GitHub and Google](/guide/github-google-sign-in/)).
* A new account gets a personal org at its first sign-in.
* The first instance admin of a new install signs in with a one-time login link ([First sign-in on a new install](/guide/first-sign-in/)).
* The audit log records each sign-in and each security action. Org owners and org admins read the entries of their org.
* [Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/), [Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/), and [the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/) give the rules and the calls.

### Orgs and keys

* An org has members with the roles owner, admin, and member. Invitations bring new members in ([Work in a team org](/guide/orgs/)).
* Each org has usage limits, because sign-up is open. The defaults are 3 machines, 6 vCPUs, 24 GiB of RAM, and 300 GB of disk.
* An instance admin can change the limits of an org, and suspend an org.
* The CLI signs in with the device flow, and gets CLI tokens. People also make API keys and add SSH keys ([Use the hopbox CLI](/guide/cli/), [CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/)).
* An org holds env vars and secrets with scopes. hopbox seals each secret with envelope encryption ([Set env vars and secrets](/guide/env-vars/), [Sealing](/reference/sealing/)).
* [The org API](/reference/org-api/), [CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/), and [the env var API](/reference/vars-api/) give the details.

### API and admin API

* The public API `hopbox.v1` uses Connect, with idempotency keys for changes ([the API server](/reference/api/)).
